question_html: As per Section 70, when a person enjoys the benefit of another’s non-gratuitous act, the beneficiary —

options.C: A person who is usually of unsound mind can contract when he is, at the time of contracting, of sound mind
options.D: An occasionally unsound mind person can contract even when he is unsound at the time of contracting

answer_html: Answer: (C)

options.B: Fraud or misrepresentation
options.C: Mistake (subject to Sec 20, 21, 22)

options.B: Section 15
options.C: Section 16
options.D: Section 17

options.A: Section 14
options.B: Section 15
options.C: Section 16
options.D: Section 17

answer_html: Answer: (C)

question_html: “Fraud” is defined under —

options.A: Section 16
options.B: Section 17
options.C: Section 18
options.D: Section 19

answer_html: Answer: (B)

question_html: “Misrepresentation” is defined under —

options.A: Section 16
options.B: Section 17
options.C: Section 18
options.D: Section 19

answer_html: Answer: (C)

options.A: Voidable due to undue influence
options.B: Voidable due to coercion
options.C: Void (immoral)
options.D: Void (forbidden by law)

options.A: Void
options.B: Voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so obtained
options.C: Illegal
options.D: Always enforceable

answer_html: Answer: (B)

options.A: Voidable
options.B: Void
options.C: Valid
options.D: Illegal

options.A: A mistake of Indian law (no relief)
options.B: A mistake of fact (gives relief)
options.C: Not relevant at all
options.D: Always voidable

answer_html: Answer: (B)

options.A: The party has a duty to speak, OR silence is equivalent to speech
options.B: Both parties are silent
options.C: Always (silence is fraud)
options.D: Never (silence is never fraud)

answer_html: Answer: (A)

options.A: Fraud
options.B: Misrepresentation
options.C: Undue influence
options.D: Mistake of fact

options.A: Necessaries supplied to him (his estate is liable, not he personally)

options.C: Trade contracts
options.D: All contracts equally

options.C: Created by court order
options.D: Created by minor

options.B: Sections 68–72
options.C: Sections 73–75
options.D: Sections 124–238

options.A: Liability of person enjoying benefit of non-gratuitous act
options.B: Claim for necessaries supplied to a person incapable of contracting
options.C: Reimbursement of money paid by mistake
options.D: Responsibility of finder of goods

options.A: A finder of goods
options.B: A bailee
options.C: A pledger
options.D: A surety

answer_html: Answer: (A)

question_html: A “Contingent Contract” is defined under —

options.A: Section 30
options.B: Section 31
options.C: Section 32
options.D: Section 56

answer_html: Answer: (B)

options.A: A void agreement
options.B: A wagering agreement
options.C: A contingent contract
options.D: An illegal contract

answer_html: Answer: (C)

options.A: The contingency must be the future of an UNCERTAIN event collateral to the contract
options.B: The contract has no consideration
options.C: Both parties are minors
options.D: The contract is in writing

answer_html: Answer: (A)

options.A: A contract of insurance has insurable interest of the insured; in wagering there is no interest
options.B: Both are exactly the same
options.C: Insurance has no consideration
options.D: Wagering involves more money

answer_html: Answer: (A)

options.A: Valid
options.B: Voidable
options.C: Void
options.D: Enforceable

answer_html: Answer: (C)

options.A: Section 70
options.B: Section 71
options.C: Section 72
options.D: Section 73

answer_html: Answer: (C)

options.A: Bailee
options.B: Pledger
options.C: Pawnee
options.D: Agent

answer_html: Answer: (A)

options.A: Bound to compensate the other
options.B: Not bound to compensate
options.C: Required to return the benefit
options.D: Bound only if a contract exists

answer_html: Answer: (A)

question_html: Quasi-contracts are based on the principle of —

options.A: Pacta sunt servanda
options.B: Equity (no man should enrich himself at another’s cost)
options.C: Caveat emptor
options.D: Stare decisis

answer_html: Answer: (B)

options.A: When the event happens
options.B: When the contract is made
options.C: If the event becomes impossible
options.D: When the parties agree

options.D: Based on equity and good conscience

options.D: Any of the above

options.C: Made to the proper person
options.D: All of the above

options.A: Immediately
options.B: Within the shortest time possible
options.C: Within a reasonable time
options.D: Within 21 days

options.A: Randomly
options.B: In alphabetical order
options.C: In the order of time (oldest debt first)
options.D: In alpha-numeric order

answer_html: Answer: (C)

options.A: Reciprocal promises
options.B: Quasi promises
options.C: Illusory promises
options.D: Cross promises

options.A: Done in any order
options.B: Done in the order expressly fixed by the contract; if not, in the order required by the nature of the transaction
options.C: Done by the promisee first
options.D: Done by the promisor first

answer_html: Answer: (B)

options.A: Section 25
options.B: Section 31
options.C: Section 56
options.D: Section 73

answer_html: Answer: (C)

options.A: Voidable
options.B: Void
options.C: Valid
options.D: Enforceable

options.A: The contract is void
options.B: The contract becomes voidable at the option of the promisee
options.C: The promisor must perform later
options.D: The promisee must wait reasonably

answer_html: Answer: (B)

options.B: A must refund the ₹1,000 advance, but is NOT bound to pay damages for loss of profit
options.C: A is liable for both refund and loss
options.D: A is not bound to refund anything

answer_html: Answer: (B)

question_html: In an EXECUTED contract, the obligations of —

options.A: Both parties have been fulfilled
options.B: Both parties are outstanding
options.C: Only one party’s obligation is outstanding
options.D: No obligation existed

answer_html: Answer: (A)

options.A: Severally only
options.B: Jointly only
options.C: Jointly and severally
options.D: Only one of them is liable

answer_html: Answer: (C)

options.A: Must perform their respective promises unless excused under any provision of the Act
options.B: Are not bound to perform
options.C: Can refuse performance any time
options.D: Need to perform only if convenient

options.A: Always

options.C: Never
options.D: Only if minor

answer_html: Answer: (B)

options.A: Section 59
options.B: Section 60

options.D: Section 62

options.A: Section 124
options.B: Section 125
options.C: Section 126
options.D: Section 148

options.B: Section 125
options.C: Section 126
options.D: Section 148

options.D: Five

answer_html: Answer: (B)

options.A: Two (Indemnifier and Indemnity-holder)
options.B: Three
options.C: Four
options.D: Five

answer_html: Answer: (A)

options.A: Primary
options.B: Secondary (co-extensive with that of principal debtor unless otherwise provided)
options.C: Joint and several
options.D: Independent

options.A: Section 124
options.B: Section 126
options.C: Section 148
options.D: Section 172

answer_html: Answer: (C)

question_html: A “Pledge” is defined under —

options.A: Section 124
options.B: Section 148
options.C: Section 172
options.D: Section 182

answer_html: Answer: (C)

options.D: Surety

options.A: Section 172
options.B: Section 182
options.C: Section 192
options.D: Section 226

answer_html: Answer: (B)

options.A: “Qui facit per alium facit per se” + No man can delegate to another which he has no authority himself

options.C: Stare decisis
options.D: Equity

options.A: A series of transactions
options.B: One single transaction only
options.C: Past transactions only
options.D: Family transactions only

answer_html: Answer: (A)

options.A: Reasonable man would in his own affairs

question_html: Under Section 2(31) of the Companies Act, 2013, 'deposit' means:

options.A: Only fixed deposits accepted by a company from the public for a specified period
options.B: Any receipt of money by way of DEPOSIT OR LOAN or in ANY OTHER FORM by a company, but does not include such categories of amount as may be prescribed in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: Only money accepted from members of the company in the form of a fixed deposit
options.D: Only money received from banks and financial institutions under a secured loan arrangement

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Any receipt of money by way of DEPOSIT OR LOAN or in ANY OTHER FORM by a company, but does not include such categories of amount as may be prescribed in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India

Section 2(31): DEPOSIT includes any receipt of money BY WAY OF DEPOSIT OR LOAN or IN ANY OTHER FORM by a company, but does NOT include such categories of amount as may be PRESCRIBED IN CONSULTATION WITH THE RESERVE BANK OF INDIA. Rule 2(c) of the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014 provides a detailed list of exclusions. The definition is wide enough to cover most forms of money received by a company but the extensive exclusions narrow it considerably.

question_html: Under Rule 2(c), which of the following amounts received by a company is EXCLUDED from the definition of 'deposit'?

options.A: Amount received from individual members of the general public who are not shareholders
options.B: Amount received from private investors through an oral agreement
options.C: Amount received from the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT, STATE GOVERNMENT, or any amount GUARANTEED BY THE CENTRAL OR STATE GOVERNMENT for repayment; amount from LOCAL AUTHORITY or STATUTORY AUTHORITY; and any amount from FOREIGN GOVERNMENTS, FOREIGN BANKS, MULTILATERAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS per FEMA provisions
options.D: Amount received from a company's customers as advance for future supplies of goods

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Amount received from the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT, STATE GOVERNMENT, or any amount GUARANTEED BY THE CENTRAL OR STATE GOVERNMENT for repayment; amount from LOCAL AUTHORITY or STATUTORY AUTHORITY; and any amount from FOREIGN GOVERNMENTS, FOREIGN BANKS, MULTILATERAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS per FEMA provisions

Rule 2(c) EXCLUSIONS from deposit: (1) Amount from CENTRAL/STATE GOVERNMENT or amounts whose REPAYMENT IS GUARANTEED by Central/State Government; (2) Amount from LOCAL AUTHORITY or STATUTORY AUTHORITY; (3) Amount from FOREIGN GOVERNMENTS, FOREIGN OR INTERNATIONAL BANKS, MULTILATERAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS, FOREIGN GOVERNMENT-OWNED DEVELOPMENT FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS, FOREIGN EXPORT CREDIT AGENCIES, FOREIGN COLLABORATORS, FOREIGN BODIES CORPORATE, FOREIGN CITIZENS, FOREIGN AUTHORITIES, PERSONS RESIDENT OUTSIDE INDIA — subject to FEMA, 1999 and rules thereunder.

question_html: Under Rule 2(c), which of the following amounts is EXCLUDED from the definition of 'deposit'?

options.A: Any amount received as a loan or facility from any bank; any amount received as a loan or financial assistance from Public Financial Institutions notified by the Central Government; and any amount received by a company from another company
options.B: Any amount received from the general public under a fixed deposit scheme
options.C: Any amount received from shareholders under a deposit scheme
options.D: Any amount received from employees as salary advances

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Any amount received as a loan or facility from any bank; any amount received as a loan or financial assistance from Public Financial Institutions notified by the Central Government; and any amount received by a company from another company

Rule 2(c) EXCLUSIONS: (1) Any amount received as a LOAN OR FACILITY FROM ANY BANK; (2) Any amount received as LOAN OR FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE from PUBLIC FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS notified by CG in consultation with RBI; (3) Any amount received by a company FROM ANOTHER COMPANY — inter-company deposits are excluded. These exclusions recognise that institutional lending and inter-corporate borrowings are subject to separate regulatory frameworks and should not be treated as public deposits under the Companies Act.
topic_text: Rule 2(c) — Exclusions: Bank Loans & Financial Assistance

question_html: Under Rule 2(c), which of the following amounts received from a DIRECTOR is EXCLUDED from the definition of deposit?

options.A: Amount received from the director only if he is also a shareholder of the company
options.B: Any amount received from a DIRECTOR OF THE COMPANY (whether as a loan or otherwise); provided that the director from whom money is received shall furnish a declaration in writing to the company to the effect that the amount is not being given out of funds acquired by him by borrowing or accepting loans or deposits from others
options.C: Amount from the director only if the board passes a resolution approving such receipt
options.D: All amounts from directors are treated as deposits under the Act

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Any amount received from a DIRECTOR OF THE COMPANY (whether as a loan or otherwise); provided that the director from whom money is received shall furnish a declaration in writing to the company to the effect that the amount is not being given out of funds acquired by him by borrowing or accepting loans or deposits from others

Rule 2(c): Amount received from a DIRECTOR OF THE COMPANY is excluded from deposit. KEY CONDITION: The DIRECTOR FROM WHOM MONEY IS RECEIVED shall furnish a DECLARATION IN WRITING to the company to the effect that the AMOUNT IS NOT BEING GIVEN OUT OF FUNDS ACQUIRED BY HIM BY BORROWING OR ACCEPTING LOANS OR DEPOSITS FROM OTHERS. This ensures that the director's own funds are being deposited — not borrowed money being 'laundered' through the director to circumvent the deposit rules.

question_html: Under Rule 2(c), when does money received towards an OFFER OF SECURITIES become a 'deposit'?

options.A: It always constitutes a deposit regardless of allotment
options.B: It never constitutes a deposit — securities money is always excluded
options.C: Amount received towards an OFFER OF SECURITIES is excluded from deposit; HOWEVER, if the SECURITIES CANNOT BE ALLOTTED and the amount received has NOT BEEN REFUNDED WITHIN 60 DAYS — it shall be treated as a DEPOSIT from the date of expiry of 60 days
options.D: It becomes a deposit only if the offer fails and refund is delayed beyond 90 days

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Amount received towards an OFFER OF SECURITIES is excluded from deposit; HOWEVER, if the SECURITIES CANNOT BE ALLOTTED and the amount received has NOT BEEN REFUNDED WITHIN 60 DAYS — it shall be treated as a DEPOSIT from the date of expiry of 60 days

Rule 2(c): Amount received towards an OFFER OF SECURITIES is EXCLUDED from deposit. EXCEPTION/CONVERSION TO DEPOSIT: If the SECURITIES CANNOT BE ALLOTTED and the said amount has NOT BEEN REFUNDED WITHIN 60 DAYS — it WOULD AMOUNT TO A DEPOSIT. This provision ensures that companies cannot indefinitely hold investor application money under the pretext of an unallotted securities offer, thereby circumventing deposit regulations. The 60-day window aligns with refund obligations under Section 39.

question_html: Under Rule 2(c), which of the following amounts from employees are EXCLUDED from the definition of 'deposit'?

options.A: Any amount received from an employee as salary advance — both interest-bearing and non-interest-bearing
options.B: Any amount received from employees is always a deposit regardless of conditions
options.C: Any amount received in the NATURE OF NON-INTEREST BEARING SECURITY DEPOSIT from an employee
options.D: Any amount received from employees through a gratuity fund scheme

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Any amount received from an employee as salary advance — both interest-bearing and non-interest-bearing

Rule 2(c): Amount received from an employee in the NATURE OF NON-INTEREST BEARING SECURITY DEPOSIT is EXCLUDED from deposit. ALSO EXCLUDED: Any NON-INTEREST BEARING AMOUNT received and held IN TRUST. INCLUDED AS DEPOSIT: Interest-bearing security deposits from employees, or amounts that are not security deposits in nature. These exclusions recognise that non-interest-bearing security deposits from employees (e.g., for rented company accommodation) are essentially contractual security arrangements and not investment deposits.

question_html: Under Rule 2(c), which of the following amounts are EXCLUDED from the definition of 'deposit'?

options.A: Amount received from promoters is always a deposit
options.B: Any amount brought in by the PROMOTERS OF THE COMPANY by way of unsecured loan (if it is brought pursuant to a requirement by the lending financial institution or bank or as per the stipulation of terms of the loan agreement or as per the CG direction); and any amount ACCEPTED BY A NIDHI COMPANY in accordance with rules under Section 406
options.C: Only amounts from promoters exceeding Rs. 10 lakhs
options.D: Amounts from promoters only if received as equity capital

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Any amount brought in by the PROMOTERS OF THE COMPANY by way of unsecured loan (if it is brought pursuant to a requirement by the lending financial institution or bank or as per the stipulation of terms of the loan agreement or as per the CG direction); and any amount ACCEPTED BY A NIDHI COMPANY in accordance with rules under Section 406

Rule 2(c) EXCLUDED from deposit: (1) Any amount BROUGHT IN BY THE PROMOTERS OF THE COMPANY by way of unsecured loan, provided: (a) it is brought pursuant to REQUIREMENT BY LENDING FINANCIAL INSTITUTION OR BANK; or (b) AS PER STIPULATION OF TERMS OF THE LOAN AGREEMENT; or (c) AS PER DIRECTION OF THE CG; and (d) it is EXEMPT FROM REPAYMENT until repayment of the bank/FI borrowings. (2) Any amount ACCEPTED BY A NIDHI COMPANY in accordance with rules under Section 406. Nidhi companies operate under a different deposit framework specific to their mutual benefit nature.

question_html: Under Rule 2(c), which of the following amounts received in the ordinary course of business are EXCLUDED from deposits?

options.A: Any amount received as advance under a loan agreement
options.B: Any amounts received as advance for purely speculative transactions
options.C: Any amount received in the COURSE OF, or for the purposes of, the BUSINESS OF THE COMPANY as an advance against orders for supply of goods/services, recognised as REVENUE as per applicable accounting standards
options.D: Any amount received as advance for research and development only

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Any amount received in the COURSE OF, or for the purposes of, the BUSINESS OF THE COMPANY as an advance against orders for supply of goods/services, recognised as REVENUE as per applicable accounting standards

Rule 2(c): Amount received in the COURSE OF, or for the PURPOSES OF, the BUSINESS OF THE COMPANY is EXCLUDED from deposit — this includes: (a) Amount received as ADVANCE against ORDERS FOR SUPPLY OF GOODS OR PROVISION OF SERVICES (recognised as REVENUE as per applicable accounting standards); (b) SECURITY DEPOSIT for performance of a contract; (c) ADVANCE received under an AGREEMENT or ARRANGEMENT (if such advance becomes a deposit if not completed within 365 days); (d) Amount received as ADVANCE under LONG TERM PROJECTS for supply of capital goods; (e) Amount received as ADVANCE against PROPERTY PURCHASE. Key: These must be recognised as REVENUE per accounting standards.

question_html: Under Rule 2(c), is an amount received by issue of BONDS OR DEBENTURES treated as a deposit?

options.A: YES — all bonds and debentures constitute deposits
options.B: NO — any amount received by ISSUE OF BONDS OR DEBENTURES SECURED BY FIRST CHARGE on assets is EXCLUDED from deposit; however, UNSECURED BONDS or DEBENTURES issued to public may be treated as deposits unless secured or compulsorily convertible within 5 years
options.C: Only government bonds are excluded; corporate bonds are always deposits
options.D: Bonds are excluded but debentures are always deposits

answer_html:
Answer: (A) YES — all bonds and debentures constitute deposits

Rule 2(c): Any amount received by a company by ISSUE OF BONDS OR DEBENTURES is EXCLUDED from 'deposit' provided such bonds/debentures are: SECURED BY A FIRST CHARGE OR CHARGE RANKING PARI PASSU WITH FIRST CHARGE on any of the assets referred to in Schedule III (excluding intangible assets); or COMPULSORILY CONVERTIBLE INTO EQUITY SHARES WITHIN 10 YEARS. However, if a company issues UNSECURED BONDS or UNSECURED DEBENTURES convertible after 10 years to the PUBLIC — such amounts could be treated as deposits. This distinction is critical for distinguishing public borrowings from deposits.

question_html: Under Rule 2(d) of the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014, who is a 'DEPOSITOR'?

options.A: Any creditor of the company including banks and financial institutions
options.B: Any MEMBER who has made a deposit with the company under Section 73(2); OR any PERSON who has made a deposit with a PUBLIC COMPANY under Section 76
options.C: Only fixed deposit holders regardless of whether they are members or not
options.D: Only institutional investors who have made fixed deposits with the company

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Any MEMBER who has made a deposit with the company under Section 73(2); OR any PERSON who has made a deposit with a PUBLIC COMPANY under Section 76

Rule 2(d): DEPOSITOR means: (a) Any MEMBER OF THE COMPANY who has made a deposit with the company in accordance with Section 73(2) of the Act; or (b) Any PERSON WHO HAS MADE A DEPOSIT with a PUBLIC COMPANY in accordance with Section 76 of the Act. This definition is important because different rules apply to deposits from members (Section 73) versus deposits from public (Section 76). The depositor has specific rights including the right to approach the Tribunal for repayment and payment of interest [Section 73(3)].

question_html: Under Rule 2(c), which of the following is CORRECTLY stated as an exclusion from the definition of 'deposit'?

options.A: Amount received from shareholders in general meetings is always a deposit
options.B: Amount from Central Government — always treated as deposit
options.C: Amount received from debenture holder on conversion of debentures into shares
options.D: Amount received from a RELATIVE OF A DIRECTOR — PROVIDED the relative furnishes a declaration in writing that the amount is not being given out of funds acquired by him by borrowing or accepting loans or deposits from others; AND the company discloses this in its Board's report

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Amount received from debenture holder on conversion of debentures into shares

Rule 2(c) RELATIVE OF DIRECTOR: Amount received from a RELATIVE OF A DIRECTOR is EXCLUDED from deposit if: (a) The RELATIVE FURNISHES A DECLARATION IN WRITING that the amount is NOT BEING GIVEN OUT OF FUNDS ACQUIRED BY BORROWING OR ACCEPTING LOANS OR DEPOSITS FROM OTHERS; and (b) The COMPANY DISCLOSES in its BOARD'S REPORT the amount so accepted from the relative, the relationship, the purpose and such other particulars. This is distinct from the director's own money — relatives are allowed to invest personal funds in the company without it being treated as a public deposit.
topic_text: Rule 2(c) — Complete List of Key Exclusions

question_html: Under Rule 2(c), if a company receives SHARE APPLICATION MONEY and is unable to allot shares, when does this amount become a DEPOSIT?

options.A: Immediately upon dishonour of the application cheque
options.B: If securities NOT ALLOTTED and amount not refunded WITHIN 60 DAYS — it becomes a deposit from the date of expiry of 60 days
options.C: After 90 days from closure of subscription list
options.D: Only if SEBI issues a specific direction

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Immediately upon dishonour of the application cheque

Rule 2(c): Amount received TOWARDS AN OFFER OF SECURITIES is EXCLUDED from deposit. EXCEPTION: If SECURITIES CANNOT BE ALLOTTED and the amount received has NOT BEEN REFUNDED WITHIN 60 DAYS — it SHALL BE TREATED AS A DEPOSIT from the date of EXPIRY OF THE SAID 60 DAYS. This is consistent with Section 39's requirement that application money for unallotted shares must be refunded within 15 days from closure of issue (within 30 days of prospectus). The 60-day period here acts as a backstop — if not refunded even after 60 days, the regulatory treatment escalates to deposit rules. PROHIBITION ON ACCEPTING PUBLIC DEPOSITS — SECTION 73(1)
topic_text: Rule 2(c) — Share Application Money Converted to Deposit

question_html: Under Section 73(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, what is the general rule regarding acceptance of deposits from the public?

options.A: Any company may accept deposits from the public at any time without restrictions
options.B: NO COMPANY shall INVITE, ACCEPT OR RENEW DEPOSITS from the public EXCEPT in a manner provided under CHAPTER V — NOT APPLICABLE to banking companies, NBFCs (under RBI Act, 1934), and companies as CG may specify after consultation with RBI
options.C: Only private companies are prohibited from accepting public deposits
options.D: All companies may accept public deposits with SEBI approval

answer_html:
Answer: (B) NO COMPANY shall INVITE, ACCEPT OR RENEW DEPOSITS from the public EXCEPT in a manner provided under CHAPTER V — NOT APPLICABLE to banking companies, NBFCs (under RBI Act, 1934), and companies as CG may specify after consultation with RBI

Section 73(1): On and after commencement of this Act, NO COMPANY shall INVITE, ACCEPT OR RENEW DEPOSITS from the PUBLIC except in a MANNER PROVIDED UNDER CHAPTER V (Acceptance of Deposits by Companies). EXCEPTIONS — NOT APPLICABLE TO: (1) A BANKING COMPANY; (2) A NON-BANKING FINANCIAL COMPANY as defined under the RESERVE BANK OF INDIA ACT, 1934; and (3) SUCH OTHER COMPANY as the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT MAY, AFTER CONSULTATION WITH THE RBI, SPECIFY. These entities are regulated by different frameworks (Banking Regulation Act, RBI NBFC regulations).

question_html: Under the Companies Act, 2013, which of the following companies can accept deposits?

options.A: Any company including private companies from the general public
options.B: Only banking companies and NBFCs
options.C: A company may accept deposits FROM ITS MEMBERS (Section 73(2)) after passing a general meeting resolution; a PUBLIC COMPANY with prescribed net worth/turnover (ELIGIBLE COMPANY) may accept deposits FROM PUBLIC (Section 76); private companies generally cannot accept public deposits
options.D: All listed companies can accept deposits from the public without restrictions

answer_html:
Answer: (C) A company may accept deposits FROM ITS MEMBERS (Section 73(2)) after passing a general meeting resolution; a PUBLIC COMPANY with prescribed net worth/turnover (ELIGIBLE COMPANY) may accept deposits FROM PUBLIC (Section 76); private companies generally cannot accept public deposits

TYPES OF DEPOSIT ACCEPTANCE: (1) FROM MEMBERS [Section 73(2)]: Any company (subject to conditions) may accept deposits from its OWN MEMBERS after passing a RESOLUTION IN GENERAL MEETING and complying with prescribed conditions; (2) FROM PUBLIC [Section 76]: Only a PUBLIC COMPANY with NET WORTH ≥ RS. 100 CRORE OR TURNOVER ≥ RS. 500 CRORES (ELIGIBLE COMPANY) may accept deposits from PERSONS OTHER THAN MEMBERS subject to additional conditions including credit rating and charge creation. PRIVATE COMPANIES cannot accept deposits from the public. ACCEPTANCE OF DEPOSITS FROM MEMBERS — SECTION 73(2)

question_html: Under Section 73(2), a company may accept deposits from its members subject to various conditions. Which of the following is NOT a mandatory condition?

options.A: Passing a resolution in general meeting
options.B: Issuance of a circular to members containing financial position, credit rating, total depositors, amount due on previous deposits
options.C: Filing of circular with the Registrar 30 days BEFORE date of issue of circular
options.D: Obtaining prior approval of SEBI before inviting deposits from members

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Passing a resolution in general meeting

Section 73(2) CONDITIONS for accepting deposits from members: (1) PASSING OF RESOLUTION IN GENERAL MEETING; (2) CIRCULAR TO MEMBERS containing: financial position, credit rating obtained, total depositors, amount due towards deposits on previous deposits, and other prescribed particulars; (3) FILE COPY OF CIRCULAR with Registrar WITHIN 30 DAYS BEFORE DATE OF ISSUE; (4) DEPOSIT NOT LESS THAN 20% of deposits maturing during following financial year in DEPOSIT REPAYMENT RESERVE ACCOUNT in scheduled bank by 30TH APRIL; (5) CERTIFY NO DEFAULT in repayment of deposits or interest, or 5 YEARS ELAPSED; (6) Provide SECURITY (if any). SEBI APPROVAL IS NOT A CONDITION for member deposits — it is required only for public company securities issues.
topic_text: Section 73(2) — Conditions for Accepting Member Deposits

question_html: Under Section 73(2), a company must deposit what percentage of its maturing deposits in the DEPOSIT REPAYMENT RESERVE ACCOUNT, and by when?

options.A: 15% of deposits maturing during current financial year by 31st March
options.B: NOT LESS THAN 20% of the amount of deposits MATURING DURING THE FOLLOWING FINANCIAL YEAR — deposited in a SCHEDULED BANK IN A SEPARATE BANK ACCOUNT called the DEPOSIT REPAYMENT RESERVE ACCOUNT — by 30TH APRIL EACH YEAR
options.C: 25% of total deposits outstanding by 30th June each year
options.D: 10% of deposits maturing in the next quarter by end of each quarter

answer_html:
Answer: (B) NOT LESS THAN 20% of the amount of deposits MATURING DURING THE FOLLOWING FINANCIAL YEAR — deposited in a SCHEDULED BANK IN A SEPARATE BANK ACCOUNT called the DEPOSIT REPAYMENT RESERVE ACCOUNT — by 30TH APRIL EACH YEAR

Section 73(2): A company accepting deposits from members must ON OR BEFORE 30TH APRIL EACH YEAR deposit or invest — in a SCHEDULED BANK in a separate bank account to be called the DEPOSIT REPAYMENT RESERVE ACCOUNT — a sum NOT LESS THAN 20% OF THE AMOUNT OF ITS DEPOSITS MATURING DURING THE FOLLOWING FINANCIAL YEAR. This is a liquidity requirement to ensure the company has funds readily available to repay maturing deposits. Compare with Debenture Redemption Reserve: invest 15% by 30th April.

question_html: Under Section 73(2), a company seeking to accept deposits from members must certify which condition regarding prior defaults?

options.A: That no default has occurred in the last 1 year
options.B: That the company has NOT COMMITTED ANY DEFAULT in repayment of deposits or interest thereon; OR where a default occurred — company MADE GOOD THE DEFAULT and 5 YEARS HAD ELAPSED since the date of making good the default
options.C: That no default has occurred in the last 3 years
options.D: That only 50% of total deposits have been repaid in the current year

answer_html:
Answer: (C) That no default has occurred in the last 3 years

Section 73(2): The company must CERTIFY that: the company HAS NOT COMMITTED ANY DEFAULT IN THE REPAYMENT OF DEPOSITS ACCEPTED EITHER BEFORE OR AFTER COMMENCEMENT OF THIS ACT or PAYMENT OF INTEREST on such deposits. AND WHERE A DEFAULT HAD OCCURRED — the company MADE GOOD THE DEFAULT AND A PERIOD OF 5 YEARS HAS ELAPSED SINCE THE DATE OF MAKING GOOD THE DEFAULT. This 5-year 'cooling period' after a remedied default is a significant safeguard — companies with recent repayment defaults are not permitted to accept fresh deposits even if the default has been cured.

question_html: Under Section 73(2), the CIRCULAR issued to members before accepting deposits must contain which information?

options.A: Only the deposit amount, interest rate, and tenure
options.B: Only the company's audited financial statements for the last 3 years
options.C: Only names of directors and promoters along with their shareholding
options.D: FINANCIAL POSITION of the company; CREDIT RATING OBTAINED; TOTAL NUMBER OF DEPOSITORS; AMOUNT DUE TOWARDS DEPOSITS in respect of any previous deposits accepted and remaining unpaid; and such OTHER PARTICULARS as may be prescribed

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only the deposit amount, interest rate, and tenure

Section 73(2): The CIRCULAR TO MEMBERS must include: (a) FINANCIAL POSITION of the company (to help members assess creditworthiness); (b) CREDIT RATING OBTAINED (the company's external credit assessment); (c) TOTAL NUMBER OF DEPOSITORS currently depositing with the company; (d) AMOUNT DUE TOWARDS DEPOSITS in respect of any PREVIOUS DEPOSITS accepted by the company; and (e) SUCH OTHER PARTICULARS AS MAY BE PRESCRIBED. The circular must be filed with the Registrar at least 30 DAYS BEFORE the date of its issue.
topic_text: Section 73(2) — Contents of Circular to Members

question_html: Under Section 73(2), a company must file a copy of the circular with the Registrar BEFORE issuing it to members. What is the time period?

options.A: At least 7 days before the date of issue of circular
options.B: File a copy of the circular along with the statement with the Registrar WITHIN 30 DAYS BEFORE THE DATE OF ISSUE OF CIRCULAR to members
options.C: At least 60 days before the date of issue of circular
options.D: Same day as the date of issue — simultaneous filing

answer_html:
Answer: (B) File a copy of the circular along with the statement with the Registrar WITHIN 30 DAYS BEFORE THE DATE OF ISSUE OF CIRCULAR to members

Section 73(2): The company must FILE A COPY OF THE CIRCULAR, along with the statement showing the financial position and other required information, with the REGISTRAR WITHIN 30 DAYS BEFORE THE DATE OF ISSUE of such circular. This advance filing with the Registrar provides a regulatory check — the Registrar can potentially review the circular before it reaches members. The 30-day gap ensures there is a meaningful opportunity for regulatory scrutiny.
topic_text: Section 73(2) — Filing of Circular with Registrar

question_html: Under Section 73(3), if a company FAILS TO REPAY a deposit from a member or any interest thereon, what remedy is available to the depositor?

options.A: The depositor can only send a legal notice to the company — no other remedy
options.B: The depositor can directly attach the company's assets
options.C: The depositor can only approach a civil court for recovery
options.D: The depositor may APPLY TO THE TRIBUNAL for an order directing the company to PAY THE SUM DUE or for any LOSS OR DAMAGE incurred, and for such OTHER ORDERS as the Tribunal may deem fit

answer_html:
Answer: (C) The depositor can only approach a civil court for recovery

Section 73(3): Every deposit accepted by the company shall be REPAID WITH INTEREST IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF THE AGREEMENT. If a company FAILS TO REPAY the deposit or part thereof or any INTEREST thereon, the DEPOSITOR MAY APPLY TO THE TRIBUNAL for an order directing the company to PAY THE SUM DUE or for any LOSS OR DAMAGE incurred by him as a result of such non-payment, and for such OTHER ORDERS as the Tribunal MAY DEEM FIT. This Tribunal remedy provides a faster route for depositors than a civil court suit.

question_html: Under Section 73(2), what is the requirement regarding SECURITY for deposits accepted from members?

options.A: Security must always be provided — it is mandatory in all cases
options.B: Provide SECURITY, IF ANY, for the DUE REPAYMENT of the amount of deposit or the interest thereon, including the creation of such CHARGE on the property or assets of the company
options.C: No security can be provided — all member deposits must be unsecured
options.D: Security is required only for deposits exceeding Rs. 10 lakhs

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Security must always be provided — it is mandatory in all cases

Section 73(2): The company must, subject to fulfilling all other conditions, PROVIDE SECURITY, IF ANY, for the DUE REPAYMENT OF THE AMOUNT OF DEPOSIT or the INTEREST THEREON, INCLUDING THE CREATION OF SUCH CHARGE ON THE PROPERTY OR ASSETS OF THE COMPANY. The words 'if any' indicate that providing security is CONDITIONAL — it is required only if the terms of the deposit include security. It is not mandatory in all cases. However, where secured deposits are accepted from the PUBLIC under Section 76, creation of charge within 30 days IS mandatory.

question_html: Under the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014, which of the following correctly describes the position of PRIVATE COMPANIES regarding acceptance of deposits?

options.A: Private companies can freely accept deposits from any person without any compliance
options.B: Private companies can accept deposits from its MEMBERS up to a maximum of 100% of paid-up share capital and free reserves subject to Section 73(2) conditions; also from directors under declaration conditions; but CANNOT ACCEPT DEPOSITS FROM THE PUBLIC (Section 76 is only for public companies)
options.C: Private companies are fully exempt from all deposit regulations
options.D: Private companies can only accept deposits from their holding company

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Private companies can accept deposits from its MEMBERS up to a maximum of 100% of paid-up share capital and free reserves subject to Section 73(2) conditions; also from directors under declaration conditions; but CANNOT ACCEPT DEPOSITS FROM THE PUBLIC (Section 76 is only for public companies)

PRIVATE COMPANY POSITION: Private companies may accept deposits FROM MEMBERS subject to the conditions of Section 73(2) (including general meeting resolution, circular to members, DRR 20% by 30th April, no subsisting default or 5-year gap). They may also accept deposits from DIRECTORS (not treated as deposit if director gives required declaration). However, PRIVATE COMPANIES CANNOT ACCEPT DEPOSITS FROM THE PUBLIC under Section 76 — that provision is exclusively for PUBLIC ELIGIBLE COMPANIES. Maximum limit for private companies accepting member deposits = 100% of paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium. ELIGIBLE COMPANY & PUBLIC DEPOSITS — SECTION 76, RULE 2(E)

question_html: Under Rule 2(e) of the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014, an 'ELIGIBLE COMPANY' means:

options.A: Any public company that has obtained SEBI approval
options.B: Any listed company with more than 500 shareholders
options.C: A PUBLIC COMPANY as referred to in Section 76(1) having NET WORTH NOT LESS THAN RS. 100 CRORE OR TURNOVER NOT LESS THAN RS. 500 CRORES; obtained PRIOR CONSENT of company in general meeting by SPECIAL RESOLUTION; FILED SAID RESOLUTION WITH REGISTRAR BEFORE MAKING ANY INVITATION TO THE PUBLIC FOR ACCEPTANCE OF DEPOSITS
options.D: Any company with paid-up capital of at least Rs. 50 crores and 5 years of profitable operations

answer_html:
Answer: (C) A PUBLIC COMPANY as referred to in Section 76(1) having NET WORTH NOT LESS THAN RS. 100 CRORE OR TURNOVER NOT LESS THAN RS. 500 CRORES; obtained PRIOR CONSENT of company in general meeting by SPECIAL RESOLUTION; FILED SAID RESOLUTION WITH REGISTRAR BEFORE MAKING ANY INVITATION TO THE PUBLIC FOR ACCEPTANCE OF DEPOSITS

Rule 2(e): ELIGIBLE COMPANY = a PUBLIC COMPANY as referred to in Section 76(1) having: (1) A NET WORTH OF NOT LESS THAN RS. 100 CRORE; OR (2) A TURNOVER OF NOT LESS THAN RS. 500 CRORES; AND which has obtained: (3) PRIOR CONSENT OF THE COMPANY IN GENERAL MEETING BY MEANS OF A SPECIAL RESOLUTION; and (4) FILED THE SAID RESOLUTION WITH THE REGISTRAR before making any invitation to the public. EXCEPTION: An eligible company accepting deposits within limits under Section 180(1)(c) may accept by ORDINARY RESOLUTION instead of special resolution.

question_html: Under Section 76, an eligible company accepting deposits from the PUBLIC must comply with which additional requirements NOT applicable to member deposits?

options.A: No additional requirements — same conditions as member deposits
options.B: Only SEBI approval is additionally required
options.C: Only filing of circular with SEBI is required additionally
options.D: Must obtain RATING FROM A RECOGNISED RATING AGENCY ensuring adequate safety — EVERY YEAR during tenure; and companies accepting SECURED DEPOSITS shall within 30 DAYS of acceptance CREATE A CHARGE on assets of amount NOT LESS THAN deposits accepted in favour of deposit holders

answer_html:
Answer: (A) No additional requirements — same conditions as member deposits

Section 76 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS for public deposits by eligible companies: (1) Must obtain RATING from a RECOGNISED RATING AGENCY for informing the public the rating ENSURING ADEQUATE SAFETY — obtained EVERY YEAR DURING THE TENURE OF DEPOSITS; (2) Every company accepting SECURED DEPOSITS from the public shall WITHIN 30 DAYS OF SUCH ACCEPTANCE CREATE A CHARGE on its assets of an amount NOT LESS THAN THE AMOUNT OF DEPOSITS ACCEPTED in favour of the deposit holders. These requirements protect public depositors by ensuring the company maintains a minimum creditworthiness assessment and adequate security backing.
topic_text: Section 76 — Additional Requirements for Public Deposits

question_html: Under Section 76(1), when may an eligible company accept public deposits by means of an ORDINARY RESOLUTION instead of a special resolution?

options.A: Always — both ordinary and special resolution are interchangeable
options.B: When the amount of deposits is within the limits specified under Section 180(1)(c) of the Act — within 60% of paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium
options.C: When the company has a credit rating of AAA or equivalent
options.D: When the deposits are secured by a first charge on company assets

answer_html:
Answer: (B) When the amount of deposits is within the limits specified under Section 180(1)(c) of the Act — within 60% of paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium

Section 76(1): An eligible company ordinarily needs to obtain prior consent by SPECIAL RESOLUTION in general meeting. EXCEPTION: An ELIGIBLE COMPANY which is accepting deposits WITHIN THE LIMITS SPECIFIED UNDER SECTION 180(1)(c) of the Act may accept deposits by means of an ORDINARY RESOLUTION. Section 180(1)(c) relates to the limit of borrowing — typically the company's paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium unless shareholders have authorised more via special resolution. This exception recognises lower-risk deposit acceptance within prudent borrowing limits.

question_html: Under Section 76A, if a company accepts deposits or invites or allows any other person to accept deposits in CONTRAVENTION of Section 73 or Section 76, or FAILS TO REPAY, what is the penalty?

options.A: Fine up to Rs. 10 lakhs; officers: fine up to Rs. 1 lakh
options.B: COMPANY: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 1 CRORE OR TWICE THE AMOUNT OF DEPOSIT (WHICHEVER IS LOWER) but may extend to RS. 10 CRORES; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER: imprisonment up to 7 YEARS AND fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25 LAKHS but may extend to RS. 2 CRORES
options.C: Company: fine up to Rs. 5 crores; officers: imprisonment up to 3 years
options.D: Company: fine equal to the deposit amount; officers: fine up to Rs. 5 lakhs

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Company: fine up to Rs. 5 crores; officers: imprisonment up to 3 years

Section 76A: Where a company ACCEPTS DEPOSITS or INVITES or ALLOWS OR CAUSES any person to accept/invite deposits in CONTRAVENTION of Section 73 or Section 76 or rules thereunder, OR FAILS TO REPAY within specified time or extended time: COMPANY = fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 1 CRORE OR TWICE THE AMOUNT OF DEPOSIT ACCEPTED — whichever is LOWER — but may extend to RS. 10 CRORES (in addition to payment of deposit amount and interest); EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER = imprisonment which may extend to 7 YEARS AND fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25 LAKHS but may extend to RS. 2 CRORES. Compare with Section 74(3) (old deposits): same penalty structure.

question_html: Both Section 74(3) and Section 76A prescribe penalties for failure to repay deposits. Which of the following CORRECTLY compares these two provisions?

options.A: They are identical in both penalty amounts and applicability
options.B: Section 74(3): DEPOSITS ACCEPTED BEFORE COMMENCEMENT (old deposits); Sec.76A: CONTRAVENTIONS OF Sec.73 or 76 (new deposits); BOTH have SAME penalty structure: Company — Rs. 1 CRORE to Rs. 10 CRORES (plus repayment); Officers — imprisonment up to 7 YEARS AND/OR fine Rs. 25 LAKHS to Rs. 2 CRORES
options.C: Section 74(3) has lower penalties than Section 76A
options.D: Section 76A applies to old deposits only; Section 74(3) applies to new deposits

answer_html:
Answer: (A) They are identical in both penalty amounts and applicability

COMPARISON: SECTION 74(3): Applies to DEPOSITS ACCEPTED BEFORE COMMENCEMENT OF THE COMPANIES ACT, 2013; penalty for FAILURE TO REPAY within specified/extended time: COMPANY = fine Rs. 1 CRORE to Rs. 10 CRORES (in addition to repayment); OFFICER = imprisonment up to 7 YEARS or fine Rs. 25 LAKHS to Rs. 2 CRORES or BOTH. SECTION 76A: Applies to CONTRAVENTIONS OF SECTION 73 OR 76 (new deposits accepted after commencement); COMPANY = fine Rs. 1 CRORE or TWICE THE DEPOSIT AMOUNT (lower) but up to Rs. 10 CRORES; OFFICER = imprisonment up to 7 YEARS AND fine Rs. 25 LAKHS to Rs. 2 CRORES. Key distinction: Section 76A uses 'AND' (both imprisonment and fine) while Section 74(3) uses 'OR'.

question_html: Under Section 75, when a company fails to repay deposits and the deposits were accepted WITH INTENT TO DEFRAUD, what is the liability of the officers responsible?

options.A: Officers are shielded by limited liability — only the company is liable
options.B: Officers PERSONALLY RESPONSIBLE WITHOUT ANY LIMITATION OF LIABILITY for ALL OR ANY LOSSES AND DAMAGES incurred by depositors; any person/group/association who incurred loss may file a suit or proceed against such officers
options.C: Officers are liable only up to their salary received in the year of the fraud
options.D: Officers are liable for a fixed penalty of Rs. 5 crores

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Officers PERSONALLY RESPONSIBLE WITHOUT ANY LIMITATION OF LIABILITY for ALL OR ANY LOSSES AND DAMAGES incurred by depositors; any person/group/association who incurred loss may file a suit or proceed against such officers

Section 75: Where a company FAILS TO REPAY deposits and it is PROVED THAT THE DEPOSITS HAD BEEN ACCEPTED WITH INTENT TO DEFRAUD THE DEPOSITORS or for ANY FRAUDULENT PURPOSE — every OFFICER OF THE COMPANY WHO WAS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE ACCEPTANCE OF SUCH DEPOSIT shall be: PERSONALLY RESPONSIBLE, WITHOUT ANY LIMITATION OF LIABILITY, for ALL OR ANY OF THE LOSSES OR DAMAGES incurred by the depositors. Any SUIT, PROCEEDINGS OR OTHER ACTION may be taken by: any PERSON, GROUP OF PERSONS or ASSOCIATION OF PERSONS who had incurred any loss. This unlimited personal liability pierces the corporate veil to protect defrauded depositors.

question_html: Under Section 74, what must a company do regarding deposits accepted BEFORE COMMENCEMENT of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: No obligation — old deposits are governed only by the Companies Act, 1956
options.B: WITHIN 3 MONTHS from commencement: FILE WITH REGISTRAR a statement of all deposits and sums remaining unpaid with interest and arrangements for repayment; REPAY WITHIN 3 YEARS from commencement OR on/before expiry of period for which deposits were accepted — WHICHEVER IS EARLIER; Tribunal may allow further time after considering company's financial condition
options.C: Within 1 year: file statement with ROC and repay all deposits
options.D: Within 6 months: apply to SEBI for direction

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Within 1 year: file statement with ROC and repay all deposits

Section 74(1): For deposits accepted BEFORE COMMENCEMENT of the Act — company must WITHIN 3 MONTHS from commencement: (a) FILE WITH REGISTRAR a statement of ALL DEPOSITS and sums remaining unpaid along with interest and ARRANGEMENTS MADE FOR REPAYMENT; AND (b) REPAY WITHIN 3 YEARS FROM COMMENCEMENT or on/before EXPIRY OF THE PERIOD FOR WHICH DEPOSITS WERE ACCEPTED — WHICHEVER IS EARLIER. Section 74(2): Tribunal may, on application by company, considering FINANCIAL CONDITION OF THE COMPANY, the amount of deposits and interest, ALLOW FURTHER TIME as considered REASONABLE for repayment. REGISTRATION OF CHARGES — SECTIONS 77–87, RULE 3, 4, 6, 8
topic_text: Section 74 — Old Deposits: Repayment and Tribunal Role

question_html: Under Section 2(16) of the Companies Act, 2013, a 'CHARGE' is defined as:

options.A: Only a mortgage created on the company's immovable property
options.B: INTEREST OR LIEN CREATED ON PROPERTY OR ASSETS OF A COMPANY or its UNDERTAKINGS AS SECURITY, INCLUDING A MORTGAGE; Section 77(1): company must register within 30 DAYS from creation; Form CHG-1 (non-debenture) and CHG-9 (debentures); certificate of registration in Form CHG-2
options.C: Only a floating charge on all assets of the company
options.D: Only a pledge on moveable property of the company

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only a mortgage created on the company's immovable property

Section 2(16): CHARGE = an INTEREST OR LIEN CREATED ON THE PROPERTY OR ASSETS OF A COMPANY OR ANY OF ITS UNDERTAKINGS OR BOTH AS SECURITY AND INCLUDING A MORTGAGE. Section 77(1): Company must REGISTER the charge with the Registrar WITHIN 30 DAYS from the date of creation; charge may be within or OUTSIDE INDIA on tangible or intangible properties; particulars signed by company and charge holder filed in FORM CHG-1 (other than debentures) or FORM CHG-9 (for debentures). Section 77(2): Registrar issues CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION in FORM CHG-2. CERTIFICATE = CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE of compliance [Rule 6(3)].

question_html: Under Section 77(3), what is the consequence if a charge created by a company is NOT DULY REGISTERED with the Registrar?

options.A: The charge becomes void only against the company's directors
options.B: NO CHARGE created by a company shall be taken into account by the LIQUIDATOR or any other CREDITOR unless it is DULY REGISTERED and a CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION is given; however, this does NOT prejudice any contract for REPAYMENT OF THE MONEY SECURED by the charge
options.C: The charge is automatically cancelled and the loan becomes unsecured
options.D: The company incurs a penalty but the charge remains valid

answer_html:
Answer: (B) NO CHARGE created by a company shall be taken into account by the LIQUIDATOR or any other CREDITOR unless it is DULY REGISTERED and a CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION is given; however, this does NOT prejudice any contract for REPAYMENT OF THE MONEY SECURED by the charge

Section 77(3): NO CHARGE CREATED BY A COMPANY shall be taken into account by the LIQUIDATOR OR ANY OTHER CREDITOR unless it is DULY REGISTERED AND A CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION IS GIVEN BY THE REGISTRAR. This means an unregistered charge is VOID against the liquidator and other creditors — it loses its security status upon winding up. Section 77(4): However, Section 77(3) shall NOT PREJUDICE ANY CONTRACT OR OBLIGATION FOR THE REPAYMENT OF THE MONEY SECURED BY A CHARGE — meaning the debt itself remains enforceable even if the security (charge) is void.

question_html: Under Rule 4(1) and Section 77, if a company fails to register a charge within 30 days of creation, what are the available time windows for late registration?

options.A: Extension can be granted for up to 60 days beyond the initial 30-day period
options.B: 30-DAY CONDONATION: Registrar may allow registration for another 30 days (total up to 120 days from creation) with declaration that belated filing won't adversely affect intervening creditors; FURTHER EXTENSION: Registrar may allow within 300 DAYS on payment of additional fees; BEYOND 300 DAYS: seek extension from CG in Form CHG-8
options.C: Extension can be granted indefinitely by the Registrar if additional fee is paid
options.D: Only one extension of 60 days is available

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Extension can be granted indefinitely by the Registrar if additional fee is paid

Rule 4(1): If Registrar is satisfied the company had sufficient cause for not filing within 30 days — FIRST CONDONATION: allow registration for ANOTHER 30 DAYS but WITHIN 120 DAYS of creation (on payment of additional fee + declaration from CS/Director that belated filing shall NOT ADVERSELY AFFECT RIGHTS OF ANY INTERVENING CREDITORS). FURTHER EXTENSION [Section 77]: Registrar may allow registration within 300 DAYS of creation on payment of additional fees. BEYOND 300 DAYS: Company shall seek EXTENSION OF TIME from CENTRAL GOVERNMENT; application in Form CHG-8 (Rule 12). Any subsequent registration shall NOT PREJUDICE rights acquired in respect of property BEFORE the charge is actually registered.
topic_text: Rule 4 — Condonation of Delay in Registration

question_html: Under Section 78, if a COMPANY FAILS TO REGISTER a charge within the prescribed period, what right does the PERSON IN WHOSE FAVOUR THE CHARGE WAS CREATED have?

options.A: No right — only the company can register the charge
options.B: The CHARGE HOLDER may APPLY TO THE REGISTRAR for registration; Registrar issues NOTICE TO COMPANY giving 14 DAYS; unless company registers or shows sufficient cause, Registrar may allow registration; charge holder entitled to RECOVER FEES PAID from the company
options.C: The charge holder can only file a complaint with SEBI
options.D: The charge holder must wait 6 months before applying

answer_html:
Answer: (A) No right — only the company can register the charge

Section 78: If a company FAILS TO REGISTER the charge within the PRESCRIBED PERIOD, the PERSON IN WHOSE FAVOUR THE CHARGE IS CREATED (charge holder) may APPLY TO THE REGISTRAR for registration of the charge along with the INSTRUMENT CREATED FOR THE CHARGE. Registrar on receipt: ISSUE NOTICE TO THE COMPANY giving 14 DAYS TIME — stating that unless company itself registers or shows SUFFICIENT CAUSE why the charge should not be registered, the Registrar may allow such registration on payment of PRESCRIBED FEES. RECOVERY: The charge holder who registered the charge is entitled to RECOVER the amount of any FEES OR ADDITIONAL FEES PAID by him for registration FROM THE COMPANY.
topic_text: Section 78 — Registration by Holder of Charge

question_html: Under Section 80, when a charge on any property or assets of a company is registered, what constructive notice does it provide?

options.A: Notice only to persons who have searched the Register of Charges
options.B: Any person ACQUIRING such property, assets, undertakings, part thereof, or any SHARE OR INTEREST THEREIN shall be DEEMED TO HAVE NOTICE OF THE CHARGE from the date of SUCH REGISTRATION
options.C: Notice only to the company's existing shareholders
options.D: Notice only to the liquidator if the company is wound up

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Any person ACQUIRING such property, assets, undertakings, part thereof, or any SHARE OR INTEREST THEREIN shall be DEEMED TO HAVE NOTICE OF THE CHARGE from the date of SUCH REGISTRATION

Section 80: Where any CHARGE on any property or assets of a company is REGISTERED, any person ACQUIRING SUCH PROPERTY, ASSETS, UNDERTAKINGS or part thereof, or any SHARE OR INTEREST THEREIN shall be DEEMED TO HAVE NOTICE OF THE CHARGE from the DATE OF SUCH REGISTRATION. This CONSTRUCTIVE NOTICE provision is fundamental to the charge registration system — it ensures that all subsequent purchasers and encumbrancers are deemed to know about registered charges, protecting the charge holder's security interests.

question_html: Under Section 81, who maintains the Register of Charges, and how is it accessible?

options.A: The company maintains the Register — only members can inspect
options.B: The REGISTRAR maintains register containing PARTICULARS OF CHARGES; OPEN TO INSPECTION BY ANY PERSON on payment of fees; particulars maintained on MCA PORTAL (www.mca.gov.in) DEEMED TO BE REGISTER OF CHARGES for Sec.81(1)
options.C: SEBI maintains the Register — open only with court order
options.D: The company maintains the Register — open during AGM only

answer_html:
Answer: (C) SEBI maintains the Register — open only with court order

Section 81(1): The REGISTRAR shall, in respect of every company, keep a REGISTER CONTAINING PARTICULARS OF THE CHARGES REGISTERED in such form and manner as may be prescribed. Section 81(2): The register kept by the REGISTRAR shall be OPEN TO INSPECTION BY ANY PERSON on payment of such fees as may be prescribed. IMPORTANT: Rule 7(1) provides that PARTICULARS OF CHARGES MAINTAINED ON THE MCA PORTAL (www.mca.gov.in) shall be DEEMED TO BE THE REGISTER OF CHARGES for purposes of Section 81(1). ALSO: Section 85 — Every company must also keep its OWN REGISTER OF CHARGES at its registered office in Form CHG-7, open to members/creditors without fee and to others on payment.

question_html: Under Rule 8(1), within what period must a company or charge holder give INTIMATION OF SATISFACTION OF A CHARGE to the Registrar?

options.A: Within 30 days from date of payment or satisfaction in full
options.B: Within 60 days from date of satisfaction
options.C: Within 300 DAYS from the date of PAYMENT OR SATISFACTION IN FULL — in FORM CHG-4 along with fee; Registrar notifies charge holder (14-day show cause notice); if no cause shown, Registrar enters MEMORANDUM OF SATISFACTION in Register of Charges and informs company in FORM CHG-5
options.D: Within 15 days from date of satisfaction

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Within 30 days from date of payment or satisfaction in full

Rule 8(1): A COMPANY OR CHARGE HOLDER shall, within 300 DAYS from the date of PAYMENT OR SATISFACTION IN FULL of any registered charge, give intimation to the REGISTRAR in FORM CHG-4 along with fee. Section 82(2): Registrar gives NOTICE TO THE HOLDER OF THE CHARGE to SHOW CAUSE within such time NOT EXCEEDING 14 DAYS why payment/satisfaction should not be recorded. If NO CAUSE SHOWN: Registrar shall order that a MEMORANDUM OF SATISFACTION be entered in Register of Charges and inform the company in FORM CHG-5. If CAUSE IS SHOWN: Registrar records a NOTE to that effect and informs the company. NOTE: If charge holder has already SIGNED THE INTIMATION to the Registrar — no separate notice to charge holder is needed.

question_html: Under Section 83, the Registrar may suo motu (on his own motion) enter a MEMORANDUM OF SATISFACTION in the register of charges. On what evidence may he do this?

options.A: Only on evidence that the company has been wound up
options.B: On EVIDENCE TO HIS SATISFACTION that: (a) DEBT for which charge was given has been PAID OR SATISFIED in whole or in part; OR (b) PART OF PROPERTY HAS BEEN RELEASED from the charge or ceased to be company's property — notwithstanding NO INTIMATION from company; inform affected parties within 30 DAYS
options.C: Only on a court order directing such entry
options.D: Only on receipt of intimation from the company

answer_html:
Answer: (B) On EVIDENCE TO HIS SATISFACTION that: (a) DEBT for which charge was given has been PAID OR SATISFIED in whole or in part; OR (b) PART OF PROPERTY HAS BEEN RELEASED from the charge or ceased to be company's property — notwithstanding NO INTIMATION from company; inform affected parties within 30 DAYS

Section 83(1): The REGISTRAR MAY, on evidence given to HIS SATISFACTION, enter a MEMORANDUM OF SATISFACTION in the register of charges with respect to any REGISTERED CHARGE — that: (a) the DEBT FOR WHICH THE CHARGE WAS GIVEN HAS BEEN PAID OR SATISFIED in whole or in part; OR (b) PART OF THE PROPERTY OR UNDERTAKING CHARGED HAS BEEN RELEASED from the charge or HAS CEASED TO FORM PART OF THE COMPANY'S PROPERTY OR UNDERTAKING. This power exists NOTWITHSTANDING THAT NO INTIMATION HAS BEEN RECEIVED by him from the company. Section 83(2): Registrar shall INFORM THE AFFECTED PARTIES within 30 DAYS of making the entry.
topic_text: Section 83 — Registrar's Own Power to Enter Satisfaction

question_html: Under Section 84, when a person obtains an order for APPOINTMENT OF A RECEIVER OR MANAGER of property subject to a charge, what must he do?

options.A: No obligation to notify anyone
options.B: Give notice to the company only
options.C: Give notice WITHIN 30 DAYS from date of passing of order: to the COMPANY and to the REGISTRAR along with a copy of the order/instrument in FORM CHG-6; person APPOINTING receiver shall also give notice within 30 DAYS; Registrar registers particulars; receiver gives notice on CEASING TO HOLD appointment
options.D: Give notice to SEBI within 15 days

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Give notice WITHIN 30 DAYS from date of passing of order: to the COMPANY and to the REGISTRAR along with a copy of the order/instrument in FORM CHG-6; person APPOINTING receiver shall also give notice within 30 DAYS; Registrar registers particulars; receiver gives notice on CEASING TO HOLD appointment

Section 84: If any person obtains an ORDER FOR APPOINTMENT OF A RECEIVER or manager of property subject to a charge: (1) SHALL GIVE NOTICE WITHIN 30 DAYS from date of order to the COMPANY AND REGISTRAR along with copy of order/instrument; (2) The person who APPOINTS a receiver or authorized person shall ALSO GIVE NOTICE WITHIN 30 DAYS to COMPANY AND REGISTRAR with copy of order; (3) Required FORM: FORM CHG-6; (4) Registrar shall REGISTER THE PARTICULARS of the receiver/person/instrument in Register of Charges on payment of fees; (5) The receiver/manager shall, on CEASING TO HOLD SUCH APPOINTMENT, give notice to COMPANY AND REGISTRAR; Registrar shall register such notice.
topic_text: Section 84 — Appointment of Receiver or Manager

question_html: Under Section 85, every company must keep its own REGISTER OF CHARGES at its registered office. What are the inspection rights?

options.A: Only the directors can inspect the company's register of charges
options.B: OPEN FOR INSPECTION by: (a) any MEMBER OR CREDITOR — WITHOUT PAYMENT OF ANY FEES; (b) any OTHER PERSON — on payment of such fees subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by articles; maintained in FORM CHG-7; includes ALL CHARGES AND FLOATING CHARGES; copy of instrument creating charge kept at registered office
options.C: Inspection only with board approval
options.D: Register is confidential — no inspection rights

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only the directors can inspect the company's register of charges

Section 85: Every company shall keep at its REGISTERED OFFICE a REGISTER OF CHARGES in FORM CHG-7 in such manner as prescribed. The register shall include ALL CHARGES AND FLOATING CHARGES affecting any property or assets of the company or its undertakings, with prescribed particulars. A COPY OF THE INSTRUMENT CREATING THE CHARGE shall also be kept at the registered office. INSPECTION RIGHTS: OPEN during BUSINESS HOURS to: (a) any MEMBER OR CREDITOR — WITHOUT ANY PAYMENT OF FEES; (b) any OTHER PERSON — on payment of such fees as prescribed, SUBJECT TO SUCH REASONABLE RESTRICTIONS as the company may, by its ARTICLES IMPOSE. COMPARE: Registrar's Register (Section 81) is open to ANY PERSON on payment of fees.
topic_text: Section 85 — Company's Own Register of Charges

question_html: Under Section 86, what is the penalty if any company CONTRAVENES any provisions of Chapter VI (Registration of Charges)?

options.A: Fine up to Rs. 5,000 only
options.B: COMPANY: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 1 LAKH but may extend to RS. 10 LAKHS; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER: imprisonment up to 6 MONTHS or fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25,000 but may extend to RS. 1 LAKH or BOTH
options.C: Company: fine up to Rs. 1 crore; officers: imprisonment up to 3 years
options.D: No penalty — charges violations are civil matters only

answer_html:
Answer: (B) COMPANY: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 1 LAKH but may extend to RS. 10 LAKHS; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER: imprisonment up to 6 MONTHS or fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25,000 but may extend to RS. 1 LAKH or BOTH

Section 86: If any company CONTRAVENES any provisions of CHAPTER VI (Sections 77–87 — REGISTRATION OF CHARGES): COMPANY = fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 1 LAKH but which may extend to RS. 10 LAKHS. EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER = punishable with IMPRISONMENT for a term which may extend to 6 MONTHS or with fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25,000 but which may extend to RS. 1 LAKH or WITH BOTH. Compare with deposits penalty: Section 76A (deposits contravention): Rs. 1 Crore–10 Crores for company; 7 years imprisonment for officers. The charge registration penalty is significantly lower than deposits penalties. REGISTERS OF MEMBERS & RELATED REGISTERS — SECTIONS 88–95
topic_text: Section 86 — Penalty for Non-Compliance with Charge Provisions

question_html: Under Section 88 of the Companies Act, 2013, every company must maintain which of the following registers?

options.A: Only a register of equity shareholders
options.B: Only registers required by SEBI
options.C: REGISTER OF MEMBERS for each class of EQUITY AND PREFERENCE SHARES separately; REGISTER OF DEBENTURE HOLDERS; REGISTER OF ANY OTHER SECURITY HOLDERS; and FOREIGN REGISTER of members/debenture holders (for members residing outside India); FORM MGT-1 (members); FORM MGT-2 (debenture holders/other security holders)
options.D: Only one combined register of all securities holders

answer_html:
Answer: (C) REGISTER OF MEMBERS for each class of EQUITY AND PREFERENCE SHARES separately; REGISTER OF DEBENTURE HOLDERS; REGISTER OF ANY OTHER SECURITY HOLDERS; and FOREIGN REGISTER of members/debenture holders (for members residing outside India); FORM MGT-1 (members); FORM MGT-2 (debenture holders/other security holders)

Section 88: Every company must keep and maintain: (a) REGISTER OF MEMBERS for each class of EQUITY SHARES AND PREFERENCE SHARES SEPARATELY; (b) REGISTER OF DEBENTURE HOLDERS; (c) REGISTER OF ANY OTHER SECURITY HOLDERS; and (d) FOREIGN REGISTER of members, debenture holders, other security holders or beneficial owners (containing names and particulars of those RESIDING OUTSIDE INDIA — if authorized by articles). Forms: REGISTER OF MEMBERS in FORM MGT-1 [Rule 3(1)]; REGISTER OF DEBENTURE HOLDERS and other security holders in FORM MGT-2 [Rule 4]. Section 88(2): Every register shall include an INDEX of names.

question_html: Under Rule 5, where must the Register of Members be maintained, and under what circumstances may it be kept elsewhere?

options.A: Always at the registered office — no exceptions
options.B: At the REGISTERED OFFICE unless a SPECIAL RESOLUTION authorises keeping at another place WITHIN THE CITY/TOWN/VILLAGE of registered office, or any place in India where MORE THAN ONE-TENTH OF TOTAL MEMBERS RESIDE
options.C: Registers can be maintained at any place in India at the company's discretion
options.D: Registers must be maintained at the ROC's office

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Always at the registered office — no exceptions

Rule 5: Registers shall be maintained at the REGISTERED OFFICE of the company UNLESS a SPECIAL RESOLUTION IS PASSED IN A GENERAL MEETING authorizing the keeping of the register at any other place within: (a) the CITY, TOWN OR VILLAGE in which the REGISTERED OFFICE IS SITUATED; or (b) any other place in INDIA in which MORE THAN ONE-TENTH OF THE TOTAL MEMBERS ENTERED IN THE REGISTER OF MEMBERS RESIDE. ENTRIES: must be made within 7 DAYS after the Board or its authorized committee approves allotment or transfer. Entries following buy-back, reduction, sub-division, consolidation, sweat equity, transmission — also within 7 DAYS of Board approval.
topic_text: Rule 5 — Maintenance of Register: Where to Keep

question_html: Under Rule 14, what are the inspection rights for the register of members and what is the MAXIMUM INSPECTION FEE for other persons?

options.A: All persons pay a uniform fee of Rs. 100 per inspection
options.B: MEMBERS/DEBENTURE HOLDERS/SECURITY HOLDERS/BENEFICIAL OWNERS — WITHOUT FEE; OTHER PERSONS — fee not exceeding RS. 50 FOR EACH INSPECTION; at least 2 HOURS on every working day; copies: not exceeding RS. 10 PER PAGE — within 7 DAYS of deposit of fee
options.C: Only members can inspect — others have no right
options.D: Inspection fee is Rs. 500 per inspection for all persons

answer_html:
Answer: (B) MEMBERS/DEBENTURE HOLDERS/SECURITY HOLDERS/BENEFICIAL OWNERS — WITHOUT FEE; OTHER PERSONS — fee not exceeding RS. 50 FOR EACH INSPECTION; at least 2 HOURS on every working day; copies: not exceeding RS. 10 PER PAGE — within 7 DAYS of deposit of fee

Rule 14: INSPECTION RIGHTS: Registers maintained under Section 88 shall be OPEN FOR INSPECTION during business hours for such reasonable time (NOT LESS THAN 2 HOURS) on every working day as the Board may decide: (1) By any MEMBER, DEBENTURE HOLDER, OTHER SECURITY HOLDER OR BENEFICIAL OWNER — WITHOUT PAYMENT OF FEE; (2) By any OTHER PERSON — on payment of fee as specified by Articles but NOT EXCEEDING RS. 50 FOR EACH INSPECTION. COPIES: Person may require a COPY OF REGISTER OR ENTRIES on payment of fee as specified in Articles but NOT EXCEEDING RS. 10 FOR EACH PAGE. SUPPLIED WITHIN 7 DAYS of deposit of such fee.
topic_text: Rule 14 — Inspection of Registers: Rights and Fees

question_html: Under Rule 15, for what period must the REGISTER OF MEMBERS and the REGISTER OF DEBENTURE HOLDERS be PRESERVED?

options.A: Both registers must be preserved for 10 years
options.B: Both registers must be preserved permanently
options.C: REGISTER OF MEMBERS (with index): PRESERVED PERMANENTLY — in custody of CS or authorized person; REGISTER OF DEBENTURE HOLDERS or other security holders: PRESERVED FOR 8 YEARS from date of REDEMPTION OF DEBENTURES OR SECURITIES; FOREIGN REGISTERS: members = permanently; debenture holders = 8 years from redemption
options.D: Both registers must be preserved for 30 years

answer_html:
Answer: (C) REGISTER OF MEMBERS (with index): PRESERVED PERMANENTLY — in custody of CS or authorized person; REGISTER OF DEBENTURE HOLDERS or other security holders: PRESERVED FOR 8 YEARS from date of REDEMPTION OF DEBENTURES OR SECURITIES; FOREIGN REGISTERS: members = permanently; debenture holders = 8 years from redemption

Rule 15 PRESERVATION OF REGISTERS: (1) REGISTER OF MEMBERS (with INDEX): preserved PERMANENTLY; kept in custody of COMPANY SECRETARY or authorized person; (2) REGISTER OF DEBENTURE HOLDERS or other SECURITY HOLDERS (with INDEX): preserved for 8 YEARS from the date of REDEMPTION OF DEBENTURES or SECURITIES; kept in custody of CS or authorized person; (3) FOREIGN REGISTER OF MEMBERS: preserved PERMANENTLY unless discontinued and transferred; (4) FOREIGN REGISTER OF DEBENTURE HOLDERS or other security holders: preserved for 8 YEARS from date of redemption. Foreign registers kept in custody of CS or authorized person.

question_html: Under Section 88(5), what is the penalty if a company FAILS TO MAINTAIN a register of members, debenture holders, or other security holders?

options.A: Fine up to Rs. 5,000 for the company only
options.B: COMPANY AND EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 50,000 but may extend to RS. 3 LAKHS; CONTINUING FAILURE — further fine up to RS. 1,000 FOR EVERY DAY after the first
options.C: Company: fine up to Rs. 1 lakh; no liability on officers
options.D: Company: fine up to Rs. 5 lakhs; officers: imprisonment up to 1 year

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Fine up to Rs. 5,000 for the company only

Section 88(5): If a company does NOT MAINTAIN a register of members/debenture holders/other security holders, or FAILS TO MAINTAIN THEM IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PROVISIONS of the Act and Rules: COMPANY AND EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER = fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 50,000 but may extend to RS. 3 LAKHS; where the FAILURE IS A CONTINUING ONE = with a FURTHER FINE which may extend to RS. 1,000 FOR EVERY DAY after its first during which the failure continues. Compare with Section 89(5): failure to make beneficial interest declaration = fine up to RS. 50,000 + RS. 1,000 per day (no minimum fine).
topic_text: Section 88(5) — Penalty for Non-Maintenance of Registers

question_html: Under Section 89, if a person's name is entered in the REGISTER OF MEMBERS but he does NOT HOLD THE BENEFICIAL INTEREST in such shares, what must he do?

options.A: No obligation to disclose — register entries are conclusive
options.B: FILE WITH THE COMPANY a declaration in FORM MGT-4 WITHIN 30 DAYS from date on which his name is entered in register; change in beneficial interest — registered owner makes FRESH DECLARATION in FORM MGT-4 within 30 DAYS; COMPANY files RETURN IN FORM MGT-6 with Registrar within 30 DAYS of receipt
options.C: File with the Registrar directly in Form MGT-4 within 60 days
options.D: No filing requirement — the beneficial owner handles all disclosures

answer_html:
Answer: (B) FILE WITH THE COMPANY a declaration in FORM MGT-4 WITHIN 30 DAYS from date on which his name is entered in register; change in beneficial interest — registered owner makes FRESH DECLARATION in FORM MGT-4 within 30 DAYS; COMPANY files RETURN IN FORM MGT-6 with Registrar within 30 DAYS of receipt

Section 89: REGISTERED OWNER (person in register but NOT BENEFICIAL OWNER): FILE WITH COMPANY a declaration in FORM MGT-4 WITHIN 30 DAYS from entry in register; if change occurs — fresh declaration within 30 DAYS. BENEFICIAL OWNER (person holding beneficial interest but not registered): File with company a declaration in FORM MGT-5 WITHIN 30 DAYS after ACQUIRING such beneficial interest; if change — fresh declaration in FORM MGT-5 within 30 DAYS. COMPANY: Make a NOTE IN REGISTER OF MEMBERS and FILE RETURN IN FORM MGT-6 with Registrar WITHIN 30 DAYS of receipt. No right in relation to shares shall be enforceable by the beneficial owner if declaration is not made by him.

question_html: Under Section 90(1), who is a 'SIGNIFICANT BENEFICIAL OWNER' and what must he do?

options.A: Any shareholder holding more than 10% shares
options.B: Every INDIVIDUAL holding BENEFICIAL INTERESTS OF NOT LESS THAN 25% (or other prescribed percentage) in shares of a company shall make a DECLARATION to the company specifying the NATURE OF HIS INTEREST and other particulars
options.C: Any director of the company regardless of shareholding
options.D: Only institutional investors holding more than 5% shares

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Any director of the company regardless of shareholding

Section 90(1): Every INDIVIDUAL who holds BENEFICIAL INTERESTS of not less than 25 PER CENT or such other percentage as may be prescribed, in shares of a company ('SIGNIFICANT BENEFICIAL OWNER') shall make a DECLARATION to the company, specifying the NATURE OF HIS INTEREST and other particulars in such MANNER AND WITHIN SUCH PERIOD as may be prescribed. CG may prescribe CLASS OR CLASSES OF PERSONS who shall NOT be required to make such declaration. Section 90(2): Every company shall maintain a REGISTER of the INTEREST DECLARED by individuals under Subsection (1) and CHANGES THEREIN — including name, date of birth, address, details of ownership.

question_html: Under Section 91, a company may CLOSE its register of members. What are the maximum closure periods?

options.A: Not exceeding 90 days in aggregate; not exceeding 60 days at any one time
options.B: NOT EXCEEDING 45 DAYS IN AGGREGATE IN EACH YEAR, but NOT EXCEEDING 30 DAYS AT ANY ONE TIME — with PREVIOUS NOTICE OF AT LEAST 7 DAYS (SEBI may specify lesser period for listed companies); PRIVATE COMPANIES: not applicable if notice served on ALL MEMBERS at least 7 DAYS prior
options.C: Not exceeding 30 days in aggregate; not exceeding 15 days at any one time
options.D: Not exceeding 60 days per year; not exceeding 45 days at any one time

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Not exceeding 90 days in aggregate; not exceeding 60 days at any one time

Section 91: A company may close the REGISTER OF MEMBERS or register of DEBENTURE HOLDERS or other security holders for any period NOT EXCEEDING IN THE AGGREGATE 45 DAYS IN EACH YEAR, but NOT EXCEEDING 30 DAYS AT ANY ONE TIME — subject to giving PREVIOUS NOTICE OF AT LEAST 7 DAYS or such LESSER PERIOD AS MAY BE SPECIFIED BY SEBI, if the company is a LISTED COMPANY. PRIVATE COMPANIES: These provisions shall not be applicable provided the NOTICE HAS BEEN SERVED ON ALL THE MEMBERS NOT LESS THAN 7 DAYS PRIOR to the closure of the registers.
topic_text: Section 91 — Closure of Register of Members

question_html: Under Section 95 of the Companies Act, 2013, what is the EVIDENTIARY VALUE of registers maintained under the Companies Act?

options.A: Registers are conclusive evidence of all entries therein
options.B: The REGISTER, THEIR INDICES AND ANY DOCUMENT required to be kept by the Act shall be PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE of any matter directed or authorized to be inserted therein by or under the Act
options.C: Registers are only internal documents with no evidentiary value
options.D: Registers are secondary evidence and require corroboration

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The REGISTER, THEIR INDICES AND ANY DOCUMENT required to be kept by the Act shall be PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE of any matter directed or authorized to be inserted therein by or under the Act

Section 95: The REGISTERS, THEIR INDICES AND ANY DOCUMENT REQUIRED TO BE KEPT BY OR UNDER THIS ACT shall be PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE of any matter DIRECTED OR AUTHORISED TO BE INSERTED THEREIN by or under the Act. PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE means it is presumed true unless the contrary is proved — not conclusive. Compare: CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION OF CHARGE (Form CHG-2) [Rule 6(3)] = CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE of compliance with charge registration requirements. The distinction between PRIMA FACIE (rebuttable) and CONCLUSIVE (irrebuttable) evidence is frequently tested.
topic_text: Section 95 — Registers as Prima Facie Evidence

question_html: Under Section 89(7), if a company FAILS TO FILE the return with the Registrar in respect of declarations regarding beneficial interest in shares, within the time specified, the penalty is:

options.A: Company: fine up to Rs. 5 lakhs; officers: imprisonment up to 1 year
options.B: Company: fine up to Rs. 1 lakh; no officer liability
options.C: COMPANY AND EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 500 but may extend to RS. 1,000; CONTINUING FAILURE — further fine up to RS. 1,000 FOR EVERY DAY after the first
options.D: Company: fine up to Rs. 50,000 only

answer_html:
Answer: (C) COMPANY AND EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 500 but may extend to RS. 1,000; CONTINUING FAILURE — further fine up to RS. 1,000 FOR EVERY DAY after the first

Section 89(7): If a company required to file the DECLARATION WITH THE REGISTRAR (Form MGT-6) in respect of beneficial interest in shares FAILS TO DO SO BEFORE EXPIRY OF THE TIME SPECIFIED: COMPANY AND EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER = fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 500 but may extend to RS. 1,000; and where the failure is a CONTINUING ONE = further fine which may extend to RS. 1,000 FOR EVERY DAY after the first during which the failure continues. Compare: Section 89(5): failure by individual to make beneficial interest declaration = fine up to RS. 50,000 + RS. 1,000 per day. The company's liability (Rs. 500–1,000) is much lower than the individual's liability (up to Rs. 50,000). CONSOLIDATED ANSWER KEY — ALL 50 QUESTIONS — END OF QUESTION PAPER — Prepared from ICMAI Study Module | Acceptance of Deposits, Charges & Registers | Companies Act, 2013 | Module 12.1 | Syllabus 2022 | CMA Inter June 2026
topic_text: Section 89(7) — Penalty for Non-Filing by Company

question_html: Under Section 92(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, every company shall prepare an Annual Return in which Form?

options.A: Form MGT-8 — signed by a Company Secretary in practice
options.B: Form MGT-7 — which shall contain particulars as they stood at the END OF THE FINANCIAL YEAR, including registered office, principal business activities, shareholding pattern, indebtedness, members and debenture holders, promoters, directors and KMP, meetings, remuneration, penalty details, FII holdings, and other prescribed matters
options.C: Form MGT-6 — signed by a director and the Company Secretary
options.D: Form MGT-14 — which records special resolutions passed during the year

answer_html:
