Answer: (B) Form MGT-7 — which shall contain particulars as they stood at the END OF THE FINANCIAL YEAR, including registered office, principal business activities, shareholding pattern, indebtedness, members and debenture holders, promoters, directors and KMP, meetings, remuneration, penalty details, FII holdings, and other prescribed matters

Section 92(1): Every company shall prepare an Annual Return in FORM MGT-7. The Annual Return shall contain the following particulars as they stood at the END OF THE FINANCIAL YEAR: (1) Registered office, principal business activities, particulars of HOLDING, SUBSIDIARY AND ASSOCIATE COMPANIES; (2) Shares, debentures and other securities and SHAREHOLDING PATTERN; (3) INDEBTEDNESS; (4) Members and debenture holders with CHANGES since close of previous financial year; (5) Promoters, directors, KMP with CHANGES; (6) MEETINGS of members/class/Board/committees with attendance details; (7) Remuneration paid to Directors and KMP; (8) PENALTY AND PUNISHMENT and compounding details; (9) Certification matters and disclosures; (10) Details in respect of SHARES HELD BY FIIs; and (11) Such other matters as may be prescribed.

question_html: Under Section 92(1), who must SIGN the Annual Return in the case of a REGULAR COMPANY (not OPC or small company)?

options.A: Only the Managing Director — no other signatory is required
options.B: Signed by any TWO directors of the company
options.C: Signed by A DIRECTOR AND THE COMPANY SECRETARY — where there is NO COMPANY SECRETARY, it shall be signed by a COMPANY SECRETARY IN PRACTICE; for OPC and small company — signed by the Company Secretary or where there is no Company Secretary by the DIRECTOR of the company
options.D: Signed by the Company Secretary only — no director's signature is required

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Signed by A DIRECTOR AND THE COMPANY SECRETARY — where there is NO COMPANY SECRETARY, it shall be signed by a COMPANY SECRETARY IN PRACTICE; for OPC and small company — signed by the Company Secretary or where there is no Company Secretary by the DIRECTOR of the company

Section 92(1): The Annual Return shall be SIGNED BY A DIRECTOR AND THE COMPANY SECRETARY. WHERE THERE IS NO COMPANY SECRETARY: it shall be signed by a COMPANY SECRETARY IN PRACTICE (an external professional CS). SPECIAL RULE FOR OPC AND SMALL COMPANY [proviso to Section 92(1)]: Annual return of an OPC and small company shall be signed by the COMPANY SECRETARY OR WHERE THERE IS NO COMPANY SECRETARY, BY THE DIRECTOR OF THE COMPANY. Key distinction: for OPC/small company, a director can sign even if there's no CS — the CS in practice route is only for regular companies.

question_html: The Annual Return under Section 92(1) shall contain particulars as they stood at the END OF THE FINANCIAL YEAR. In which specific areas must CHANGES since the close of the PREVIOUS FINANCIAL YEAR be mentioned?

options.A: Changes in members and debenture holders; AND changes in promoters, directors and key managerial personnel since the close of the previous financial year — both categories require disclosure of changes
options.B: Only changes in share capital need to be disclosed
options.C: Only changes in the Board of Directors need to be disclosed
options.D: Changes in registered office address only

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Changes in members and debenture holders; AND changes in promoters, directors and key managerial personnel since the close of the previous financial year — both categories require disclosure of changes

Section 92(1): The Annual Return must contain TWO CATEGORIES WHERE CHANGES ARE SPECIFICALLY DISCLOSED: (a) MEMBERS AND DEBENTURE HOLDERS along with CHANGES THEREIN SINCE THE CLOSE OF THE PREVIOUS FINANCIAL YEAR; AND (b) PROMOTERS, DIRECTORS, KEY MANAGERIAL PERSONNEL along with CHANGES THEREIN SINCE THE CLOSE OF THE PREVIOUS FINANCIAL YEAR. All other contents (registered office, shareholding pattern, indebtedness, etc.) are reported as at the END OF THE FINANCIAL YEAR. This distinction — snapshot vs. movement — is frequently tested.
topic_text: Section 92(1) — Contents: Changes Since Previous Year

question_html: Under Section 92(1), which specific investment-related details must a company disclose in its Annual Return?

options.A: Only the names and addresses of all shareholders must be disclosed
options.B: Details in respect of SHARES HELD BY OR ON BEHALF OF FOREIGN INSTITUTIONAL INVESTORS (FIIs), along with such other matters as may be prescribed
options.C: Only the details of promoters' shareholding need to be disclosed
options.D: Only the shareholding of directors and KMP is required

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Details in respect of SHARES HELD BY OR ON BEHALF OF FOREIGN INSTITUTIONAL INVESTORS (FIIs), along with such other matters as may be prescribed

Section 92(1): The Annual Return must include — among other matters — DETAILS IN RESPECT OF SHARES HELD BY OR ON BEHALF OF THE FOREIGN INSTITUTIONAL INVESTORS (FIIs), including names of FIIs, countries of incorporation, registration numbers, addresses and percentages of shareholding. This reflects the importance of FII investments in Indian companies and the regulatory need for transparency regarding foreign ownership. The section also requires disclosure of the overall SHAREHOLDING PATTERN of the company.
topic_text: Section 92(1) — FII Holdings in Annual Return

question_html: Under Section 92(1), a company's Annual Return must disclose which legal proceedings-related information?

options.A: Only cases pending before the Supreme Court
options.B: Only cases where the company has been convicted
options.C: PENALTY AND PUNISHMENT IMPOSED on the company, its directors or officers; DETAILS OF COMPOUNDING OF OFFENCES; and APPEALS MADE AGAINST SUCH PENALTY OR PUNISHMENT during the relevant financial year
options.D: Only income tax penalty and assessments

answer_html:
Answer: (C) PENALTY AND PUNISHMENT IMPOSED on the company, its directors or officers; DETAILS OF COMPOUNDING OF OFFENCES; and APPEALS MADE AGAINST SUCH PENALTY OR PUNISHMENT during the relevant financial year

Section 92(1): The Annual Return must contain: PENALTY AND PUNISHMENT IMPOSED ON THE COMPANY, ITS DIRECTORS OR OFFICERS AND DETAILS OF COMPOUNDING OF OFFENCES AND APPEALS MADE AGAINST SUCH PENALTY OR PUNISHMENT. This disclosure requirement ensures transparency about regulatory non-compliance. It covers penalties under the Companies Act as well as other legislation. The disclosure helps shareholders, investors and regulators assess the legal risk profile and compliance culture of the company.

question_html: Under Section 92(1), the Annual Return must contain information about which meetings?

options.A: Meetings of members or a class thereof, Board and its various committees — along with ATTENDANCE DETAILS at each meeting
options.B: Only the Annual General Meeting details
options.C: Only Board of Directors meetings
options.D: Only audit committee meetings

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Meetings of members or a class thereof, Board and its various committees — along with ATTENDANCE DETAILS at each meeting

Section 92(1): The Annual Return must contain: MEETINGS OF MEMBERS OR A CLASS THEREOF, BOARD AND ITS VARIOUS COMMITTEES along with ATTENDANCE DETAILS. This covers: (a) GENERAL MEETINGS (AGM and EGM); (b) MEETINGS OF ANY CLASS OF MEMBERS (e.g., preference shareholders); (c) BOARD MEETINGS; and (d) COMMITTEE MEETINGS (audit committee, nomination committee, etc.) along with ATTENDANCE DETAILS at each meeting. This comprehensive disclosure helps shareholders assess the engagement level of directors with the company's governance.

question_html: With effect from Financial Year 2020-2021, what is the NEW form introduced for OPCs and SMALL COMPANIES to file their Annual Return?

options.A: Form MGT-7 — the same form used by all companies
options.B: New e-FORM MGT-7A — introduced vide the Companies (Management and Administration) Amendment Rules, 2021; filed within 60 DAYS from the date of AGM (same as regular companies); signed by the Company Secretary or by the director if there is no CS
options.C: Form MGT-8 — the form for certification by CS in practice
options.D: Form MGT-14 — the form for filing special resolutions

answer_html:
Answer: (B) New e-FORM MGT-7A — introduced vide the Companies (Management and Administration) Amendment Rules, 2021; filed within 60 DAYS from the date of AGM (same as regular companies); signed by the Company Secretary or by the director if there is no CS

Companies (Management and Administration) Amendment Rules, 2021: A new e-FORM MGT-7A was introduced. From FINANCIAL YEAR 2020-2021, OPC AND SMALL COMPANIES shall file their Annual Return in NEW e-FORM MGT-7A. DUE DATE: 60 DAYS from the date of AGM (same as regular companies — Section 92(4)). SIGNING: By Company Secretary or where there is no CS, by the DIRECTOR OF THE COMPANY (proviso to Section 92(1)). This separate form recognises that OPCs and small companies have simpler structures and need a shorter, more focused return form compared to larger companies.
topic_text: MGT-7A — Small Company & OPC Annual Return

question_html: Under Section 92(1), which remuneration-related information must be disclosed in the Annual Return?

options.A: Only the total salary bill of all employees
options.B: Remuneration paid to DIRECTORS AND KEY MANAGERIAL PERSONNEL (KMP) — disclosed in the Annual Return as particulars as at the end of the financial year
options.C: Only the remuneration of the Managing Director and Whole-time Directors
options.D: Only the remuneration of Independent Directors and other Non-Executive Directors

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Only the remuneration of the Managing Director and Whole-time Directors

Section 92(1): The Annual Return must contain REMUNERATION PAID TO DIRECTORS AND KEY MANAGERIAL PERSONNEL. KEY MANAGERIAL PERSONNEL [Section 2(51)] include: (a) Chief Executive Officer or Managing Director or Manager; (b) Company Secretary; (c) Chief Financial Officer; and (d) Whole-time Director. This disclosure ensures shareholders are aware of what their company is paying to its top management and key professionals. The remuneration details in the Annual Return complement the disclosures in the Directors' Remuneration Report. CERTIFICATE, FILING & PENALTIES — SECTIONS 92(2)(3)(4)(5)(6)

question_html: Under Section 92(2), which companies are required to have their Annual Return CERTIFIED BY A COMPANY SECRETARY IN PRACTICE in Form MGT-8?

options.A: All companies without exception must obtain Form MGT-8 certification
options.B: LISTED COMPANIES or companies having PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL OF RS. 10 CRORES OR MORE or TURNOVER OF RS. 50 CRORES OR MORE — CS in practice certifies: annual return discloses facts CORRECTLY AND ADEQUATELY and company has COMPLIED WITH ALL PROVISIONS OF THE ACT
options.C: Only government companies and public sector undertakings
options.D: Only companies with more than 500 shareholders

answer_html:
Answer: (A) All companies without exception must obtain Form MGT-8 certification

Section 92(2): The Annual Return filed by: (a) A LISTED COMPANY; or (b) A company having PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL OF RS. 10 CRORES OR MORE; or (c) A company having TURNOVER OF RS. 50 CRORES OR MORE — shall be CERTIFIED BY A COMPANY SECRETARY IN PRACTICE in FORM MGT-8. The certification states that: (1) the annual return DISCLOSES THE FACTS CORRECTLY AND ADEQUATELY; and (2) the company has COMPLIED WITH ALL THE PROVISIONS OF THIS ACT. This certification by an independent professional provides assurance to stakeholders about the reliability of the Annual Return.
topic_text: Section 92(2) — Certificate by CS in Practice: Threshold

question_html: Under Section 92(3), what must a company do with its Annual Return in relation to its WEBSITE and BOARD'S REPORT?

options.A: The Annual Return must be physically distributed to all shareholders
options.B: Every company shall PLACE A COPY OF THE ANNUAL RETURN ON THE WEBSITE OF THE COMPANY (if any); and the WEB-LINK OF SUCH ANNUAL RETURN shall be DISCLOSED IN THE BOARD'S REPORT
options.C: The Annual Return must be emailed to all shareholders within 30 days
options.D: Only listed companies need to place the Annual Return on their website

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Every company shall PLACE A COPY OF THE ANNUAL RETURN ON THE WEBSITE OF THE COMPANY (if any); and the WEB-LINK OF SUCH ANNUAL RETURN shall be DISCLOSED IN THE BOARD'S REPORT

Section 92(3): Every company shall: (1) PLACE A COPY OF THE ANNUAL RETURN ON THE WEBSITE OF THE COMPANY, if any; AND (2) The WEB-LINK of such annual return shall be DISCLOSED IN THE BOARD'S REPORT. The phrase 'if any' means this obligation applies only to companies that HAVE A WEBSITE — companies without websites are not required to create one for this purpose. The web-link disclosure in the Board's Report ensures shareholders can easily access the full Annual Return when they receive the Annual Report.
topic_text: Section 92(3) — Annual Return on Company Website

question_html: Under Section 92(4), within what period must every company file its Annual Return with the Registrar?

options.A: Within 30 days from the date of Annual General Meeting
options.B: Within 45 days from the date of Annual General Meeting
options.C: Within 60 DAYS from the date on which the AGM IS HELD — OR — where NO AGM IS HELD in any year, within 60 days from the date on which the AGM SHOULD HAVE BEEN HELD, together with a STATEMENT SPECIFYING THE REASONS FOR NOT HOLDING THE AGM
options.D: Within 90 days from the date of Annual General Meeting

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Within 60 DAYS from the date on which the AGM IS HELD — OR — where NO AGM IS HELD in any year, within 60 days from the date on which the AGM SHOULD HAVE BEEN HELD, together with a STATEMENT SPECIFYING THE REASONS FOR NOT HOLDING THE AGM

Section 92(4): Every company shall file with the Registrar a copy of the annual return WITHIN 60 DAYS from the date on which the AGM IS HELD. WHERE NO AGM IS HELD in any year: file within 60 DAYS from the date on which the AGM SHOULD HAVE BEEN HELD, TOGETHER WITH A STATEMENT SPECIFYING THE REASONS FOR NOT HOLDING THE AGM. The 60-day period provides reasonable time for companies to finalise and file the return after the meeting. EXCEPTION for OPC: OPC does not hold AGM (Section 96 exemption) but still files annual return within 60 days from close of financial year under Section 137 (financial statements).
topic_text: Section 92(4) — Filing Period for Annual Return

question_html: Under Section 92(5), what is the penalty if a company FAILS TO FILE its Annual Return before the expiry of the specified period?

options.A: Company: fine up to Rs. 1 lakh; officers: fine up to Rs. 10,000
options.B: COMPANY: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 50,000 but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER: imprisonment up to 6 MONTHS or fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 50,000 but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS or BOTH
options.C: Company: fine up to Rs. 10 lakhs; officers: imprisonment up to 1 year
options.D: Company and officers: fine up to Rs. 25,000 each

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Company: fine up to Rs. 1 lakh; officers: fine up to Rs. 10,000

Section 92(5): PENALTY for failure to file Annual Return before expiry of specified period: COMPANY = fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 50,000 but which may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS. EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER = punishable with IMPRISONMENT for a term which may extend to 6 MONTHS or with fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 50,000 but which may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS or WITH BOTH. Note: Both the COMPANY and the OFFICER can be penalised. The minimum fine of Rs. 50,000 for both company and officer reflects the importance of timely filing of the Annual Return.
topic_text: Section 92(5) — Penalty for Non-Filing of Annual Return

question_html: Under Section 92(6), what is the penalty for a COMPANY SECRETARY IN PRACTICE who certifies the Annual Return OTHERWISE THAN IN CONFORMITY with the requirements of Section 92?

options.A: Cancellation of Certificate of Practice only — no monetary penalty
options.B: Fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 50,000 but which may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS — CS in practice is personally liable for incorrect/non-conforming certification under Form MGT-8
options.C: Imprisonment up to 6 months — no fine option
options.D: Fine up to Rs. 10,000 only

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 50,000 but which may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS — CS in practice is personally liable for incorrect/non-conforming certification under Form MGT-8

Section 92(6): If a COMPANY SECRETARY IN PRACTICE certifies the Annual Return OTHERWISE THAN IN CONFORMITY WITH THE REQUIREMENTS OF SECTION 92 or the rules made thereunder — he shall be punishable with fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 50,000 but which may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS. Notable features: (1) The penalty is the SAME as the company's penalty (Rs. 50,000–5 lakhs); (2) Only FINE — no imprisonment option for the CS in practice; (3) Unlike the officer's penalty (which includes imprisonment), the CS in practice faces only monetary penalty; (4) This personal liability encourages CS professionals to exercise due diligence in certification. PLACE OF KEEPING, PRESERVATION & INSPECTION — SECTIONS 94, 95, RULES 14, 15, 16
topic_text: Section 92(6) — Penalty for CS in Practice: Incorrect Certification

question_html: Under Section 94, where must copies of the Annual Return be kept, and when may they be kept at another location?

options.A: Annual returns must always be kept at the Registrar's office
options.B: Copies kept at the REGISTERED OFFICE; may ALSO be kept at any other place in India where MORE THAN ONE-TENTH OF TOTAL MEMBERS reside — if approved by SPECIAL RESOLUTION at a general meeting
options.C: Annual returns may be kept anywhere in India at the company's discretion
options.D: Annual returns must be kept at the CG's office after filing

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Annual returns may be kept anywhere in India at the company's discretion

Section 94: COPIES OF ANNUAL RETURN shall be kept at the REGISTERED OFFICE of the company. ALTERNATE LOCATION: They may also be kept at any other place in India in which MORE THAN ONE-TENTH OF THE TOTAL NUMBER OF MEMBERS entered in the Register of Members reside — if APPROVED BY A SPECIAL RESOLUTION passed at a general meeting of the company. This provision mirrors the similar rule for the Register of Members — both allow alternative locations based on where the majority of members reside, but both require special resolution for the alternate location.
topic_text: Section 94 — Place of Keeping Annual Returns

question_html: Under Section 94 read with Rule 15(3), for what period must copies of Annual Returns and their annexures be PRESERVED?

options.A: For 5 years from the date of filing with the Registrar
options.B: For 10 years from the date of filing with the Registrar
options.C: For 3 years from the date of filing with the Registrar
options.D: For 8 YEARS from the date of filing with the Registrar — copies of annual returns AND all CERTIFICATES AND DOCUMENTS required to be annexed thereto shall be preserved for 8 years

answer_html:
Answer: (A) For 5 years from the date of filing with the Registrar

Section 94 read with Rule 15(3): Copies of Annual Returns prepared and COPIES OF ALL CERTIFICATES AND DOCUMENTS required to be annexed thereto shall be PRESERVED FOR A PERIOD OF 8 YEARS from the date of filing with the Registrar. Compare with: REGISTER OF MEMBERS — preserved PERMANENTLY; REGISTER OF DEBENTURE HOLDERS — preserved for 8 YEARS from date of redemption. The 8-year period for Annual Returns aligns with the general period for which most corporate records are preserved and allows for examination by regulatory authorities during investigations.
topic_text: Rule 15(3) — Preservation Period for Annual Returns

question_html: Under Rule 14(1), what are the INSPECTION RIGHTS for annual returns and what fees are applicable?

options.A: Annual returns are confidential — inspection allowed only by directors
options.B: OPEN FOR INSPECTION during business hours (NOT LESS THAN 2 HOURS on every working day as Board decides); BY ANY MEMBER — WITHOUT FEE; BY ANY OTHER PERSON — on payment of fee NOT EXCEEDING RS. 50 FOR EACH INSPECTION; CG may direct immediate inspection
options.C: Only members can inspect — non-members have no right
options.D: Inspection fee is Rs. 500 per inspection for all persons

answer_html:
Answer: (B) OPEN FOR INSPECTION during business hours (NOT LESS THAN 2 HOURS on every working day as Board decides); BY ANY MEMBER — WITHOUT FEE; BY ANY OTHER PERSON — on payment of fee NOT EXCEEDING RS. 50 FOR EACH INSPECTION; CG may direct immediate inspection

Rule 14(1): Copies of Annual Returns prepared under Section 92 shall be OPEN FOR INSPECTION during business hours at such REASONABLE TIME (not less than 2 HOURS) on every working day as the Board may decide: (1) BY ANY MEMBER — WITHOUT PAYMENT OF FEE; (2) BY ANY OTHER PERSON — on payment of fee as specified in articles but NOT EXCEEDING RS. 50 FOR EACH INSPECTION. Section 94(5): The CENTRAL GOVERNMENT may also, BY ORDER, direct an IMMEDIATE INSPECTION of the document, or direct that the extract required shall FORTHWITH BE ALLOWED to be taken by the person requiring it. This CG power is extraordinary and overrides normal inspection procedures.

question_html: Under Rule 16, within what period must a company supply a COPY OF THE ANNUAL RETURN to any member or other person requesting it, and what is the maximum fee per page?

options.A: Within 14 days; fee not exceeding Rs. 50 per page
options.B: Within 30 days; fee not exceeding Rs. 5 per page
options.C: Within 21 days; fee not exceeding Rs. 20 per page
options.D: Within 7 DAYS from the date of DEPOSIT OF FEE; fee not exceeding RS. 10 FOR EACH PAGE as specified in the Articles of Association

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Within 21 days; fee not exceeding Rs. 20 per page

Rule 16: Copies of Annual Return filed under Section 92 shall be FURNISHED TO ANY MEMBER OR ANY OTHER PERSON on payment of such fees as specified in the Articles of Association BUT NOT EXCEEDING RS. 10 FOR EACH PAGE. The company shall SUPPLY such copy WITHIN A PERIOD OF 7 DAYS FROM THE DATE OF DEPOSIT OF FEE to the company. Compare: INSPECTION FEE (Rule 14) = not exceeding RS. 50 PER INSPECTION; COPY FEE (Rule 16) = not exceeding RS. 10 PER PAGE. The 7-day supply obligation ensures timely access to corporate records.
topic_text: Rule 16 — Copies of Annual Return to Members

question_html: Under Section 94(4), if a company REFUSES INSPECTION or making of extracts/copies of the Annual Return, what is the penalty?

options.A: A single fine of Rs. 25,000 for the company and each officer
options.B: Imprisonment only — no financial penalty
options.C: No penalty — refusal of inspection is at the company's discretion
options.D: The COMPANY AND EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER shall be liable to a PENALTY OF RS. 1,000 FOR EVERY DAY subject to a MAXIMUM OF RS. 1 LAKH during which the default continues

answer_html:
Answer: (A) A single fine of Rs. 25,000 for the company and each officer

Section 94(4): If any INSPECTION or the making of any EXTRACT OR COPY REQUIRED IS REFUSED — the COMPANY AND EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER shall be liable for each such default: PENALTY OF RS. 1,000 FOR EVERY DAY during which the default continues, SUBJECT TO A MAXIMUM OF RS. 1 LAKH. This daily penalty with a cap structure ensures that prolonged refusals are penalised proportionately. Note: The maximum cap (Rs. 1 lakh) means that even a 100-day or longer refusal is capped at Rs. 1 lakh penalty per default. EVIDENTIARY VALUE, COMPARISONS & MISCELLANEOUS
topic_text: Section 94(4) — Penalty for Refusal to Allow Inspection

question_html: Under Section 95, copies of Annual Returns maintained under Section 94 are:

options.A: CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE of all matters inserted therein — irrebuttable
options.B: PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE of any matter directed or authorized to be inserted therein by or under this Act — presumed true unless the contrary is proved
options.C: Not admissible as evidence in any legal proceedings
options.D: Secondary evidence which requires corroboration from other documents

answer_html:
Answer: (B) PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE of any matter directed or authorized to be inserted therein by or under this Act — presumed true unless the contrary is proved

Section 95: Copies of Annual Returns maintained under Section 94 shall be PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE of any matter DIRECTED OR AUTHORISED TO BE INSERTED THEREIN by or under the Act. PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE = REBUTTABLE — it is presumed to be true and admissible as evidence unless the CONTRARY IS PROVED. Compare with: CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION OF CHARGE (Form CHG-2) = CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE (IRREBUTTABLE). REGISTERS [Section 95] = PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE (rebuttable). This distinction between conclusive and prima facie evidence is a classic examination question.
topic_text: Section 95 — Annual Return as Prima Facie Evidence

question_html: Under the Companies Act, 2013, which of the following is CORRECT regarding the Annual Return of a ONE PERSON COMPANY (OPC)?

options.A: OPC need not file any Annual Return
options.B: OPC files Annual Return in FORM MGT-7A (w.e.f. FY 2020-21); signed by CS or where no CS by the DIRECTOR; no CS in practice certification required; no AGM held; filing within 60 days from close of financial year
options.C: OPC files Annual Return in Form MGT-7 with full CS in practice certification
options.D: OPC files Annual Return within 30 days from close of financial year

answer_html:
Answer: (C) OPC files Annual Return in Form MGT-7 with full CS in practice certification

OPC ANNUAL RETURN: (1) FORM: New e-FORM MGT-7A (w.e.f. FY 2020-21); (2) SIGNING: Company Secretary or where no CS, the DIRECTOR OF THE COMPANY (Proviso to Section 92(1)); (3) NO CS IN PRACTICE CERTIFICATION required (threshold under Section 92(2) does not typically apply to OPCs); (4) NO AGM: OPC is exempt from holding AGM [Section 96]; (5) FILING: Within 60 days from the date of AGM — but since OPC has no AGM, effectively within 60 days from date on which AGM SHOULD have been held, or as per Section 92(4); (6) OPC is also exempt from requirement of cash flow statement [Section 2(40)].

question_html: Which of the following correctly compares the ANNUAL RETURN requirements for a REGULAR COMPANY versus an OPC/SMALL COMPANY?

options.A: REGULAR COMPANY: Form MGT-7, signed by director + CS (or CS in practice if no CS), CS in practice certification (Form MGT-8) if paid-up capital ≥ Rs.10Cr or turnover ≥ Rs.50Cr or listed, filed within 60 days of AGM, preserved 8 years; OPC/SMALL COMPANY: Form MGT-7A (w.e.f. FY 2020-21), signed by CS or director (if no CS), filed within 60 days of AGM
options.B: Both use Form MGT-7 — no distinction
options.C: OPC files Annual Return in Form MGT-7 and regular companies use MGT-7A
options.D: Regular companies file within 30 days; OPC files within 60 days

answer_html:
Answer: (A) REGULAR COMPANY: Form MGT-7, signed by director + CS (or CS in practice if no CS), CS in practice certification (Form MGT-8) if paid-up capital ≥ Rs.10Cr or turnover ≥ Rs.50Cr or listed, filed within 60 days of AGM, preserved 8 years; OPC/SMALL COMPANY: Form MGT-7A (w.e.f. FY 2020-21), signed by CS or director (if no CS), filed within 60 days of AGM

COMPARISON TABLE: REGULAR COMPANY: Form MGT-7; Signed by DIRECTOR + CS (or CS in practice if no CS); CS in practice CERTIFICATION (Form MGT-8) required if: (a) LISTED; or (b) Paid-up capital ≥ RS. 10 CRORES; or (c) Turnover ≥ RS. 50 CRORES; Filed WITHIN 60 DAYS of AGM; Preserved for 8 YEARS. OPC/SMALL COMPANY: Form MGT-7A (w.e.f. FY 2020-21); Signed by CS or DIRECTOR (if no CS) — no CS in practice route; No mandatory MGT-8 certification; Filed within 60 DAYS of AGM; Preserved for 8 YEARS. Both: Website disclosure + weblink in Board's Report (Section 92(3)).
topic_text: Section 92 — Comparison: Regular vs OPC/Small Company

question_html: Under Section 92(3), what is the specific obligation regarding the Annual Return and the BOARD'S REPORT?

options.A: The Board's Report must summarise all contents of the Annual Return
options.B: The WEB-LINK OF THE ANNUAL RETURN placed on the company's website shall be DISCLOSED IN THE BOARD'S REPORT
options.C: The Annual Return must be approved by the Board before it is filed
options.D: The Board's Report must certify the accuracy of the Annual Return

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The WEB-LINK OF THE ANNUAL RETURN placed on the company's website shall be DISCLOSED IN THE BOARD'S REPORT

Section 92(3): Two linked obligations: (1) Place a copy of the Annual Return on the COMPANY'S WEBSITE (if any); AND (2) The WEB-LINK of such annual return shall be DISCLOSED IN THE BOARD'S REPORT. The Board's Report (prepared under Section 134) is the primary annual communication to shareholders. By requiring the web-link to be in the Board's Report, shareholders receiving the annual report will know exactly where to find the full Annual Return. Note: This obligation is on ALL COMPANIES that have a website — not just listed companies.
topic_text: Section 92 — Annual Return vs Board's Report

question_html: Under Section 92(4), when NO ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING is held in any year, what must the company do when filing the Annual Return?

options.A: The company is exempt from filing if no AGM was held
options.B: The company must file a revised annual return within 30 days
options.C: Along with the Annual Return: A STATEMENT SPECIFYING THE REASONS FOR NOT HOLDING THE AGM — filed within 60 DAYS from the date on which the AGM SHOULD HAVE BEEN HELD
options.D: The company must obtain NCLT approval before filing

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Along with the Annual Return: A STATEMENT SPECIFYING THE REASONS FOR NOT HOLDING THE AGM — filed within 60 DAYS from the date on which the AGM SHOULD HAVE BEEN HELD

Section 92(4): Where NO AGM IS HELD IN ANY YEAR — the company shall file the Annual Return WITHIN 60 DAYS from the date on which the AGM SHOULD HAVE BEEN HELD — TOGETHER WITH A STATEMENT SPECIFYING THE REASONS FOR NOT HOLDING THE ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING, along with such fees or additional fees as may be prescribed. The 'reasons for not holding AGM' statement provides regulatory transparency about companies that are unable to comply with AGM requirements. Not holding an AGM is itself a violation and the reasons statement helps regulators assess whether enforcement action is needed.
topic_text: Section 92(4) — No AGM Held: Statement of Reasons

question_html: Under Section 94(5), the Central Government has an extraordinary power regarding inspection of Annual Returns. What is this power?

options.A: The CG may order the company to destroy its Annual Returns
options.B: The CG may, BY ORDER, direct AN IMMEDIATE INSPECTION of the document, OR direct that the EXTRACT REQUIRED shall FORTHWITH BE ALLOWED to be taken by the person requiring it — overriding normal inspection hours and procedures
options.C: The CG may order the company to re-file its Annual Return with corrections
options.D: The CG may only direct inspection during regular business hours

answer_html:
Answer: (A) The CG may order the company to destroy its Annual Returns

Section 94(5): The CENTRAL GOVERNMENT MAY ALSO, BY ORDER, DIRECT: (a) AN IMMEDIATE INSPECTION of the document; or (b) That the EXTRACT REQUIRED shall FORTHWITH BE ALLOWED TO BE TAKEN by the person requiring it. This EXTRAORDINARY POWER allows the CG to override: (1) Normal business hours restriction; (2) Normal notice requirements for inspection; (3) Any reasonable restrictions imposed by the company's Articles. This power is used in regulatory investigations, enforcement proceedings, or situations where immediate access to corporate records is needed in the public interest.
topic_text: Section 94 — CG Power for Immediate Inspection

question_html: Which of the following correctly summarises the KEY NUMBERS associated with the Annual Return under Section 92?

options.A: Form MGT-7 (regular) / MGT-7A (OPC/small co.); MGT-8 certification if listed/paid-up ≥ Rs.10Cr/turnover ≥ Rs.50Cr; file within 60 DAYS of AGM; penalty Rs.50K–5L (company and officer); CS in practice penalty Rs.50K–5L; preserved 8 YEARS; inspection: members FREE, others ≤ Rs.50; copies ≤ Rs.10/page within 7 DAYS; refusal penalty Rs.1,000/day max Rs.1 LAKH
options.B: Form MGT-7 for all companies; filed within 30 days; penalty Rs.10K–1L
options.C: Form MGT-7A for all companies; filed within 45 days; penalty Rs.1L–5L
options.D: Form MGT-8 for all companies; filed within 90 days; penalty Rs.25K–2.5L

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Form MGT-7 for all companies; filed within 30 days; penalty Rs.10K–1L

ANNUAL RETURN — COMPLETE KEY NUMBERS SUMMARY: FORM: MGT-7 (regular companies); MGT-7A (OPC and small companies, w.e.f. FY 2020-21). CERTIFICATION: MGT-8 (CS in practice) if LISTED or paid-up ≥ RS. 10 CRORES or turnover ≥ RS. 50 CRORES. FILING: Within 60 DAYS of AGM. PENALTY (non-filing): COMPANY = Rs. 50,000–5 LAKHS; OFFICER = 6 months imprisonment or Rs. 50,000–5 LAKHS or both. PENALTY (CS in practice incorrect certification): Rs. 50,000–5 LAKHS (fine only). PRESERVATION: 8 YEARS from filing. INSPECTION: Members FREE; Others ≤ RS. 50 per inspection (not less than 2 hours daily). COPIES: ≤ RS. 10 per page within 7 DAYS. REFUSAL PENALTY: RS. 1,000 per day max RS. 1 LAKH. CONSOLIDATED ANSWER KEY — ALL 25 QUESTIONS — END OF QUESTION PAPER — Prepared from ICMAI Study Module | Annual Return — Section 92, 94, 95 | Companies Act, 2013 | Module 12.1 | Syllabus 2022 | CMA Inter June 2026

question_html: The Code on Wages, 2019 subsumed four Central labour legislations under Section 69. Which of the following correctly lists ALL FOUR Acts repealed?

options.A: Payment of Wages Act 1936, Minimum Wages Act 1948, Maternity Benefit Act 1961, Equal Remuneration Act 1976
options.B: Payment of Wages Act 1936, Minimum Wages Act 1948, Workmen's Compensation Act 1923, Equal Remuneration Act 1976
options.C: Payment of Wages Act 1936, Minimum Wages Act 1948, Payment of Bonus Act 1965, Equal Remuneration Act 1976
options.D: Minimum Wages Act 1948, Payment of Bonus Act 1965, Industrial Disputes Act 1947, Equal Remuneration Act 1976

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Payment of Wages Act 1936, Minimum Wages Act 1948, Payment of Bonus Act 1965, Equal Remuneration Act 1976

Section 69: The Code on Wages, 2019 (enacted 2020) expressly REPEALS: (1) Payment of Wages Act, 1936; (2) Minimum Wages Act, 1948; (3) Payment of Bonus Act, 1965; and (4) Equal Remuneration Act, 1976. These four Acts have been consolidated into a single comprehensive Code to bring uniformity and ease of compliance.

question_html: Under Section 68 of the Code on Wages, the Central Government may notify provisions for removing difficulties. What is the maximum time period within which such notifications can be issued?

options.A: One year from commencement of the Code
options.B: Three years from commencement of the Code
options.C: Five years from commencement of the Code
options.D: Ten years from commencement of the Code

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Three years from commencement of the Code

Section 68: In case of any difficulty, the Central Government shall notify provisions not inconsistent with the Code, as may appear necessary for REMOVING THE DIFFICULTY, within a period of THREE YEARS from the commencement of the Code. The Code was enacted in 2019 and came into force in 2020.

question_html: The Code on Wages, 2019 seeks to regulate wage and bonus payments in which sectors?

options.A: All sectors — industry, trade, business, or manufacture, wherever employees are appointed
options.B: Only factories and mines employing more than 20 workers
options.C: Only Central Government establishments and public sector undertakings
options.D: Only unorganised sector workers earning below minimum wage

answer_html:
Answer: (A) All sectors — industry, trade, business, or manufacture, wherever employees are appointed

The Code on Wages, 2019 is a WELCOME CHANGE to the existing labour law regime as it seeks to regulate wage and bonus payments in ALL SECTORS such as industry, trade, business, or manufacture, WHEREVER EMPLOYEES ARE APPOINTED. Through this Code, the Central Government gets power to regulate wages for railways, mines and oil fields, while State Governments reserve power for all other employments.

question_html: Which of the following Codes was enacted simultaneously alongside the Code on Wages, 2019 as part of India's comprehensive labour law consolidation?

options.A: Code on Employment Benefits, 2020
options.B: Code on Social Welfare, 2019
options.C: Code on Social Security 2020, Industrial Relations Code 2020, and Occupational Safety Health and Working Conditions Code 2020
options.D: Code on Retirement Benefits 2021 and Code on Industrial Relations 2019

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Code on Social Security 2020, Industrial Relations Code 2020, and Occupational Safety Health and Working Conditions Code 2020

Simultaneously with the Code on Wages, the Government also enacted: (1) The Code on Social Security, 2020; (2) The Industrial Relations Code, 2020; and (3) The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. Together, these four Codes comprehensively consolidate most provisions from numerous scattered labour legislations.

question_html: Compared to the earlier legislations, a significant feature of the Code on Wages, 2019 is that it regulates wages of:

options.A: Only workmen doing manual or unskilled work
options.B: Both workmen AND employees performing managerial or supervisory functions
options.C: Only employees of establishments employing more than 100 persons
options.D: Only employees in scheduled employments notified by the Central Government

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Both workmen AND employees performing managerial or supervisory functions

The Code not only regulates the wages of WORKMEN but also the wages of EMPLOYEES PERFORMING MANAGERIAL AND SUPERVISORY FUNCTIONS. This broader coverage brings uniformity in the definition of various terms overlapping in various pieces of legislation and eases the burden of documentation — a significant improvement over the earlier fragmented regime. DEFINITIONS — WAGES, EMPLOYEE, WORKMAN — SECTIONS 2(K), 2(Y), 2(Z)

question_html: Under Section 2(y) of the Code on Wages, 2019, which of the following components are INCLUDED in the definition of 'wages'?

options.A: Basic pay, dearness allowance, retaining allowance, house rent allowance, and overtime allowance
options.B: Basic pay, dearness allowance, and retaining allowance (if any)
options.C: Basic pay, bonus, dearness allowance, commission, and gratuity
options.D: All remuneration including PF contribution and conveyance allowance

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Basic pay, dearness allowance, retaining allowance, house rent allowance, and overtime allowance

Section 2(y): Wages INCLUDES: (i) BASIC PAY; (ii) DEARNESS ALLOWANCE; and (iii) RETAINING ALLOWANCE (if any). The definition does NOT include bonus, HRA, PF contribution, conveyance allowance, overtime allowance, commission, gratuity, retrenchment compensation, or ex gratia payments. Only these three components form the core of 'wages'.

question_html: Which of the following is correctly EXCLUDED from the definition of 'wages' under Section 2(y) of the Code on Wages?

options.A: Dearness allowance forming part of remuneration
options.B: Retaining allowance paid during off-season
options.C: Conveyance allowance or the value of any travelling concession
options.D: Basic pay forming the base salary under the employment contract

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Conveyance allowance or the value of any travelling concession

Section 2(y): EXCLUDED from wages are: (a) bonus; (b) house accommodation or amenity value; (c) PF/pension contribution and interest; (d) CONVEYANCE ALLOWANCE or travelling concession; (e) sum for special expenses; (f) HRA; (g) remuneration under court/tribunal order; (h) overtime allowance; (i) commission; (j) gratuity; (k) retrenchment compensation/ex gratia. Basic pay, DA and retaining allowance are INCLUDED.

question_html: Under the proviso to Section 2(y) of the Code on Wages, if the excluded payments (clauses (a) to (i)) together exceed what proportion of total remuneration, the excess shall be deemed as wages?

options.A: One-third of total remuneration
options.B: One-half (50%) of total remuneration
options.C: Two-thirds of total remuneration
options.D: Three-fourths of total remuneration

answer_html:
Answer: (B) One-half (50%) of total remuneration

Proviso to Section 2(y): If payments made under clauses (a) to (i) (the excluded items) TOGETHER EXCEED ONE-HALF (50%) of all remuneration calculated under that clause, the amount which EXCEEDS SUCH ONE-HALF shall be DEEMED AS REMUNERATION and shall be accordingly ADDED IN WAGES. The Central Government may notify a different percentage. This proviso prevents wage structuring to avoid statutory obligations.

question_html: Under the Explanation to Section 2(y), if an employee is given remuneration in kind in lieu of part of wages, what portion is deemed to form part of wages?

options.A: The value which does not exceed fifteen per cent. of total wages payable shall be deemed as wages
options.B: The entire value of remuneration in kind is always deemed as wages
options.C: Only if the remuneration in kind exceeds twenty-five per cent. of wages
options.D: Remuneration in kind is never treated as wages under the Code

answer_html:
Answer: (A) The value which does not exceed fifteen per cent. of total wages payable shall be deemed as wages

Explanation to Section 2(y): Where an employee is given remuneration IN KIND in lieu of the whole or part of wages, the value of such remuneration in kind which does NOT EXCEED FIFTEEN PER CENT. of the TOTAL WAGES PAYABLE to him, shall be deemed to form part of the wages of such employee. The 15% cap prevents employers from fully replacing cash wages with kind.

question_html: Under Section 2(k) of the Code on Wages, which person is EXCLUDED from the definition of 'employee'?

options.A: A person performing supervisory work for hire or reward
options.B: A person performing clerical work in an establishment
options.C: A member of the Armed Forces of the Union
options.D: A person performing managerial work in an establishment

answer_html:
Answer: (C) A member of the Armed Forces of the Union

Section 2(k): Employee means any person (other than an APPRENTICE under the Apprentices Act, 1961) employed on wages by an establishment to do any skilled, semi-skilled, unskilled, manual, operational, supervisory, managerial, administrative, technical or clerical work for hire or reward. It does NOT include any MEMBER OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE UNION. Both apprentices and armed forces members are excluded.

question_html: Under Section 2(z), a person employed in a SUPERVISORY capacity is excluded from the definition of 'workman' if he draws wages exceeding:

options.A: Rs. 10,000 per month
options.B: Rs. 15,000 per month (or as notified by CG)
options.C: Rs. 21,000 per month
options.D: Rs. 25,000 per month

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Rs. 15,000 per month (or as notified by CG)

Section 2(z): A workman does NOT include a person employed in a SUPERVISORY CAPACITY drawing wages EXCEEDING RS. 15,000 PER MONTH or such amount as may be notified by the Central Government from time to time. Also excluded are persons subject to the Air Force/Army/Navy Acts, police service employees, prison officers, and those employed mainly in managerial or administrative capacity.

question_html: Which of the following persons is specifically INCLUDED in the definition of 'workman' under Section 2(z) of the Code on Wages?

options.A: Working journalists as defined under the Working Journalists and other Newspaper Employees Act, 1955, AND sales promotion employees under the Sales Promotion Employees Act, 1976
options.B: Members of the Armed Forces of the Union
options.C: Employees mainly in managerial or administrative capacity
options.D: Police service officers and prison employees

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Working journalists as defined under the Working Journalists and other Newspaper Employees Act, 1955, AND sales promotion employees under the Sales Promotion Employees Act, 1976

Section 2(z): Workman INCLUDES: (i) WORKING JOURNALISTS as defined in the Working Journalists and other Newspaper Employees (Conditions of Service) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1955; and (ii) SALES PROMOTION EMPLOYEES as defined in the Sales Promotion Employees (Conditions of Service) Act, 1976. For the purpose of industrial dispute proceedings, it also includes persons dismissed/discharged/retrenched in connection with a dispute.

question_html: The second proviso to Section 2(y) of the Code on Wages states that for the purpose of EQUAL WAGES TO ALL GENDERS and for the purpose of PAYMENT OF WAGES, which emoluments from the exclusion list shall be taken for computation?

options.A: All excluded items (a) to (k) shall be included
options.B: Only house rent allowance and commission
options.C: Emoluments specified in clauses (d) conveyance, (f) HRA, (g) tribunal/award remuneration, and (h) overtime allowance
options.D: Only overtime allowance and commission

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Emoluments specified in clauses (d) conveyance, (f) HRA, (g) tribunal/award remuneration, and (h) overtime allowance

Second Proviso to Section 2(y): For the purpose of EQUAL WAGES TO ALL GENDERS and for the purpose of PAYMENT OF WAGES, the emoluments specified in clauses (d) [conveyance allowance], (f) [HRA], (g) [remuneration under award/settlement/court order], and (h) [overtime allowance] shall be taken for computation of wage. This ensures gender wage parity is calculated on a comprehensive basis. GENDER NON-DISCRIMINATION — SECTION 3
topic_text: Section 2(y) — Second Proviso: Equal Wages Computation

question_html: Section 3(1) of the Code on Wages prohibits gender discrimination in which specific matter?

options.A: Only in matters relating to promotion and seniority
options.B: In matters relating to wages for the same work or work of a similar nature done by any employee
options.C: Only in recruitment and selection of employees
options.D: Only in matters of leave and working hours

answer_html:
Answer: (B) In matters relating to wages for the same work or work of a similar nature done by any employee

Section 3(1): There shall be NO DISCRIMINATION in an establishment or any unit thereof among employees on the GROUND OF GENDER in matters relating to WAGES, by the same employer, in respect of THE SAME WORK OR WORK OF A SIMILAR NATURE done by any employee. The Code seeks to put an end to all gender-based discriminations in wages — illustrated by the Sita-Mahesh example in the module where paying half wages to a female worker for the same work is illegal.
topic_text: Section 3 — No Gender Discrimination in Wages

question_html: Under Section 3(2) of the Code, which of the following actions by an employer is PROHIBITED?

options.A: Reducing the rate of wages of any employee for the purpose of complying with Section 3(1), AND making gender-based discrimination while recruiting for the same or similar work
options.B: Only reducing wages of male employees to match female wages
options.C: Providing separate facilities for male and female employees
options.D: Offering higher salary to a more qualified employee regardless of gender

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Reducing the rate of wages of any employee for the purpose of complying with Section 3(1), AND making gender-based discrimination while recruiting for the same or similar work

Section 3(2): No employer shall: (a) for the purpose of complying with Section 3(1), REDUCE THE RATE OF WAGES OF ANY EMPLOYEE; and (b) MAKE ANY DISCRIMINATION ON THE GROUND OF SEX WHILE RECRUITING any employee for the same work or work of similar nature, except where employment of women in such work is prohibited or restricted by or under any law. Both wage-reduction and recruitment discrimination are prohibited. MINIMUM WAGES — SECTIONS 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12

question_html: Under Section 6 of the Code, the appropriate Government shall fix minimum wages. What types of work are covered for fixing minimum rates?

options.A: Only time work — not piece work
options.B: Only piece work — not time work
options.C: Both time work and piece work; and for piece-work, a minimum time rate shall also be fixed
options.D: Only work in scheduled employments notified by the Central Government

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Both time work and piece work; and for piece-work, a minimum time rate shall also be fixed

Section 6: The appropriate Government shall fix minimum wages: (a) for TIME WORK; or (b) for PIECE WORK. Section 6(3): Where employees are on PIECE WORK, the appropriate Government shall ALSO fix a MINIMUM TIME RATE for securing them a minimum income. Time work rates may be fixed by the hour, day, or month [Section 6(4)]. The number of minimum wage categories should be kept to a minimum [Section 6(7)].

question_html: Under Section 6(6)(a), while fixing minimum wages, the appropriate Government shall PRIMARILY take into account:

options.A: Profitability of the establishment and national economic conditions
options.B: Skill of workers — unskilled, skilled, semi-skilled and highly-skilled — or geographical area or both
options.C: Number of workers employed and their length of service
options.D: Wage rates prevailing in comparable establishments in neighbouring states

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Skill of workers — unskilled, skilled, semi-skilled and highly-skilled — or geographical area or both

Section 6(6)(a): The appropriate Government shall PRIMARILY take into account the SKILL OF WORKERS REQUIRED for working under the categories of UNSKILLED, SKILLED, SEMI-SKILLED and HIGHLY-SKILLED, or GEOGRAPHICAL AREA, or BOTH. Section 6(6)(b): Additionally, ARDUOUSNESS of work (temperature, humidity, hazardous occupations, underground work) may also be considered. The number of minimum wage categories should be kept to a minimum.
topic_text: Section 6(6) — Skill Categories for Wage Fixation

question_html: Under Section 7, minimum wages fixed by the appropriate Government may consist of which of the following?

options.A: Only a basic rate of wages and a dearness allowance linked to CPI
options.B: Only an all-inclusive rate — no separate DA component is permitted
options.C: (i) Basic rate + cost of living allowance (COLA); OR (ii) Basic rate with/without COLA + cash value of concessions; OR (iii) All-inclusive rate covering basic rate + COLA + concessions
options.D: Only basic rate plus productivity-linked incentive

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only a basic rate of wages and a dearness allowance linked to CPI

Section 7: Minimum wages may consist of: (a) a BASIC RATE + COST OF LIVING ALLOWANCE (COLA) adjusted to cost of living index; OR (b) a BASIC RATE with/without COLA + CASH VALUE OF CONCESSIONS on essential commodities where authorised; OR (c) an ALL-INCLUSIVE RATE covering basic rate + COLA + cash value of concessions. All three methods are valid and interchangeable at the appropriate Government's choice.

question_html: Under Section 8(2), every committee appointed to fix/revise minimum wages shall consist of persons representing employers and employees (equal in number), plus:

options.A: Majority of government officials and five state representatives
options.B: Five representatives of the Central Government plus independent economists
options.C: Independent persons not exceeding ONE-THIRD of the total members of the committee
options.D: Only independent persons — employer and employee representatives are optional

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Independent persons not exceeding ONE-THIRD of the total members of the committee

Section 8(2): Every committee shall consist of: (a) persons REPRESENTING EMPLOYERS; (b) persons REPRESENTING EMPLOYEES — equal in number to employer representatives; and (c) INDEPENDENT PERSONS, not exceeding ONE-THIRD of the total members of the committee. After considering recommendations, the appropriate Government fixes minimum wages by notification, coming into force on EXPIRY OF THREE MONTHS from date of issue.

question_html: Under Section 8(4) of the Code, the appropriate Government shall review or revise minimum rates of wages at an interval ordinarily NOT EXCEEDING:

options.A: Two years
options.B: Five years
options.C: Three years
options.D: One year

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Five years

Section 8(4): The appropriate Government shall REVIEW OR REVISE minimum rates of wages ORDINARILY AT AN INTERVAL NOT EXCEEDING FIVE YEARS. Additionally, where the appropriate Government proposes to revise minimum wages by the notification method [Section 8(1)(b)], it shall also CONSULT THE CONCERNED ADVISORY BOARD constituted under Section 42. The minimum wage notification must specify a date not less than TWO MONTHS from the notification date.

question_html: Under Section 9(1) of the Code on Wages, the power to fix the 'floor wage' (taking into account minimum living standards of a worker) vests with:

options.A: The Central Government, which may fix different floor wages for different geographical areas
options.B: The State Government for all establishments within the State
options.C: The Central Advisory Board constituted under Section 42
options.D: The appropriate Government in consultation with the Chief Labour Commissioner

answer_html:
Answer: (A) The Central Government, which may fix different floor wages for different geographical areas

Section 9(1): The CENTRAL GOVERNMENT shall fix the FLOOR WAGE taking into account minimum living standards of a worker in such manner as may be prescribed. DIFFERENT FLOOR WAGES may be fixed for DIFFERENT GEOGRAPHICAL AREAS. Section 9(2): Minimum wages fixed by appropriate Governments under Section 6 SHALL NOT BE LESS THAN THE FLOOR WAGE. If existing minimum wages are already HIGHER, the appropriate Government SHALL NOT REDUCE them.
topic_text: Section 9 — Floor Wage by Central Government

question_html: Under Section 9(3), before fixing the floor wage, the Central Government may obtain advice from which body and also consult State Governments?

options.A: The National Labour Commission
options.B: The Planning Commission of India
options.C: The Central Advisory Board constituted under Section 42(1)
options.D: The Ministry of Finance

answer_html:
Answer: (C) The Central Advisory Board constituted under Section 42(1)

Section 9(3): The Central Government MAY, BEFORE FIXING THE FLOOR WAGE, OBTAIN THE ADVICE OF THE CENTRAL ADVISORY BOARD constituted under Section 42(1) and CONSULT STATE GOVERNMENTS in such manner as may be prescribed. This consultation is permissive ('may') not mandatory — the Central Government has the final power to fix the floor wage.

question_html: Under Section 10, if an employee whose minimum wage is fixed 'by the day' works for LESS than the normal working hours, he is entitled to:

options.A: Wages only for the actual hours worked on that day
options.B: Half wages regardless of hours worked
options.C: Full normal day wages — UNLESS the failure to work is caused by his own unwillingness (not employer's failure to provide work)
options.D: No wages if he works less than half the normal hours

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Half wages regardless of hours worked

Section 10: An employee whose minimum rate is fixed BY THE DAY and who works for less than the requisite number of hours shall be entitled to receive wages AS IF HE HAD WORKED FOR A FULL NORMAL WORKING DAY, EXCEPT: (i) where his failure to work is caused by HIS OWN UNWILLINGNESS — not by the employer's failure to provide work; and (ii) in such other cases as may be prescribed. The employer's obligation to pay for a full day is the default. PAYMENT OF WAGES, OVERTIME, DEDUCTIONS & FINES — SECTIONS 14–20
topic_text: Section 10 — Less Than Normal Working Day

question_html: Under Section 14 of the Code on Wages, the overtime rate for work done in excess of the normal working day shall be:

options.A: One and a half times the normal rate of wages
options.B: Three times the normal rate of wages
options.C: Not less than TWICE the normal rate of wages
options.D: The same as the normal rate of wages

answer_html:
Answer: (A) One and a half times the normal rate of wages

Section 14: Where an employee works on any day in excess of the number of hours constituting a NORMAL WORKING DAY, the employer shall pay for every hour (or part thereof) so worked in excess, at the OVERTIME RATE which shall NOT BE LESS THAN TWICE THE NORMAL RATE OF WAGES. The appropriate Government may fix the number of hours constituting a normal working day, including rest intervals, day of rest per week, and payment for work on rest days at not less than overtime rate.

question_html: Under Section 15 of the Code on Wages, wages may be paid in which of the following modes?

options.A: Only in cash — cheque payments are prohibited under the Code
options.B: Only by cheque or bank transfer for establishments with more than 10 employees
options.C: Current coin or currency notes, OR by cheque, OR by crediting in bank account, OR by electronic mode
options.D: Only by electronic mode — cash payment is prohibited for all establishments

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Current coin or currency notes, OR by cheque, OR by crediting in bank account, OR by electronic mode

Section 15: All wages shall be paid in: (i) CURRENT COIN OR CURRENCY NOTES; OR (ii) by CHEQUE; OR (iii) by CREDITING THE WAGES IN THE BANK ACCOUNT of the employee; OR (iv) by ELECTRONIC MODE. The appropriate Government may, by notification, specify establishments where wages shall be paid ONLY BY CHEQUE OR BY CREDITING TO BANK ACCOUNT (compulsory non-cash payment for specified establishments).

question_html: Under Section 16 of the Code on Wages, the maximum permissible wage period that an employer can fix for any employee is:

options.A: Weekly
options.B: Fortnightly
options.C: No wage period shall be more than ONE MONTH
options.D: Quarterly

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Fortnightly

Section 16: The employer shall fix the wage period as DAILY, WEEKLY, FORTNIGHTLY, or MONTHLY, subject to the condition that NO WAGE PERIOD IN RESPECT OF ANY EMPLOYEE SHALL BE MORE THAN A MONTH. Different wage periods may be fixed for different establishments. The monthly cap ensures workers receive wages at least once a month.

question_html: Under Section 17(1)(d), wages of employees on a MONTHLY basis shall be paid before the expiry of:

options.A: The last day of the same month
options.B: The third day of the succeeding month
options.C: The seventh day of the succeeding month
options.D: The fifteenth day of the succeeding month

answer_html:
Answer: (A) The last day of the same month

Section 17(1): Wages shall be paid — (a) DAILY BASIS: at end of shift; (b) WEEKLY BASIS: on last working day before weekly holiday; (c) FORTNIGHTLY BASIS: before end of second day after the fortnight ends; (d) MONTHLY BASIS: before expiry of the SEVENTH DAY of the succeeding month. Section 17(2): On removal/dismissal/retrenchment/resignation/closure — within TWO WORKING DAYS.

question_html: Under Section 17(2), when an employee is removed, dismissed, retrenched, or has resigned, the wages payable must be paid within:

options.A: Seven working days from the date of separation
options.B: Thirty days from date of separation
options.C: Two working days of removal, dismissal, retrenchment, or resignation
options.D: The next regular wage payment date for that establishment

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Two working days of removal, dismissal, retrenchment, or resignation

Section 17(2): Where an employee has been (a) REMOVED OR DISMISSED FROM SERVICE; or (b) RETRENCHED or has RESIGNED FROM SERVICE, or became unemployed due to CLOSURE OF THE ESTABLISHMENT — the wages payable to him shall be paid within TWO WORKING DAYS of such removal, dismissal, retrenchment or resignation. This protects departing workers from delayed payment.

question_html: Under Section 18(2)(p) of the Code on Wages, the total amount of all deductions from wages in any wage period shall NOT EXCEED:

options.A: 25% of wages in that wage period
options.B: 50% of wages in that wage period
options.C: 33.33% of wages in that wage period
options.D: 75% of wages in that wage period

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 50% of wages in that wage period

Section 18(2)(p): The TOTAL AMOUNT OF DEDUCTIONS from wages in any wage period shall NOT EXCEED FIFTY PER CENT (50%) of such wages. Where total deductions exceed 50% of wages, the excess may be recovered in such manner as may be prescribed [Section 18(3)]. Section 18(4): If an employer makes a deduction but does not deposit it in the prescribed fund/account, the EMPLOYEE SHALL NOT BE HELD RESPONSIBLE for the employer's default.

question_html: Under Section 19 of the Code on Wages, which of the following statements about FINES is CORRECT?

options.A: Total fines in any wage period can be up to 10% of wages; fines can be imposed on children under 15
options.B: Fines can be recovered by instalments within 60 days of imposition
options.C: Total fines shall not exceed 3% of wages; no fine on employee under 15 years; fine cannot be recovered after 90 days from imposition
options.D: All fine realisations are retained by the employer for administrative purposes

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Total fines in any wage period can be up to 10% of wages; fines can be imposed on children under 15

Section 19: (4) Total fines in any one WAGE PERIOD shall NOT EXCEED 3% OF WAGES payable; (5) NO FINE shall be imposed on an employee UNDER 15 YEARS OF AGE; (6) No fine shall be recovered by instalments or after NINETY DAYS from the day it was imposed; (7) every fine is deemed imposed on day of the act/omission; (8) All fine realisations shall be applied ONLY TO PURPOSES BENEFICIAL TO EMPLOYEES as approved by prescribed authority. PAYMENT OF BONUS — SECTIONS 26–41

question_html: Under Section 26(1) of the Code on Wages, every eligible employee is entitled to a minimum annual bonus of:

options.A: 10% of wages or Rs. 100, whichever is higher
options.B: 5% of wages or Rs. 50, whichever is higher
options.C: 8.33% of wages or Rs. 100 (whichever is higher), whether or not the employer has any allocable surplus
options.D: 15% of wages or Rs. 200, whichever is higher

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 8.33% of wages or Rs. 100 (whichever is higher), whether or not the employer has any allocable surplus

Section 26(1): Annual MINIMUM BONUS = 8.33% OF WAGES EARNED or RS. 100, WHICHEVER IS HIGHER — whether or not the employer has any allocable surplus in the previous accounting year. Eligibility: employee must have put in at least THIRTY DAYS of work in an accounting year. This minimum is payable even in a loss-making year.

question_html: Under Section 26(3), where the allocable surplus exceeds the minimum bonus, the employer shall pay bonus not exceeding:

options.A: 15% of wages earned in the accounting year
options.B: 20% of wages earned in the accounting year
options.C: 25% of wages earned in the accounting year
options.D: 30% of wages earned in the accounting year

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 20% of wages earned in the accounting year

Section 26(3): Where allocable surplus EXCEEDS the minimum bonus payable, the employer shall pay bonus in proportion to wages, subject to a MAXIMUM OF TWENTY PER CENT (20%) of wages earned in the accounting year. Any demand for production/productivity-based bonus exceeding 20% must be determined by agreement or settlement between employer and employees [Section 26(5)].

question_html: To be eligible for minimum annual bonus under Section 26(1), an employee must have put in at least how many days of work in an accounting year?

options.A: Thirty days
options.B: Sixty days
options.C: Ninety days
options.D: One hundred and twenty days

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Thirty days

Section 26(1): An employee must have put in AT LEAST THIRTY DAYS OF WORK in an accounting year to be eligible for bonus. Section 27: Where an employee has not worked for all working days, the minimum bonus shall be PROPORTIONATELY REDUCED if such bonus is higher than 8.33% of wages of days actually worked. Section 28 defines which days count as days worked (lay-off, leave with pay, accident absence, maternity leave).

question_html: For a new establishment, in the FIRST FIVE ACCOUNTING YEARS following the year in which the employer first sells goods/renders services, bonus is payable:

options.A: From the very first accounting year at the standard minimum rate
options.B: At a fixed rate of 5% without any allocable surplus calculation
options.C: Only in respect of the accounting year in which the employer derives PROFIT, calculated without applying Section 36 (set on/set off)
options.D: Not at all for the first five years — new establishments are completely exempt

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Only in respect of the accounting year in which the employer derives PROFIT, calculated without applying Section 36 (set on/set off)

Section 26(6): In the FIRST FIVE ACCOUNTING YEARS after first sale/service, bonus shall be payable ONLY IN RESPECT OF THE ACCOUNTING YEAR IN WHICH THE EMPLOYER DERIVES PROFIT. For those profit years, bonus is calculated per the Code but WITHOUT APPLYING SECTION 36 (set on/set off). From the 8th accounting year, Section 36 applies fully. This provision protects new establishments from the set-on/set-off mechanism during initial years.

question_html: Under Section 28, for computing the number of working days to determine proportionate bonus, an employee is DEEMED TO HAVE WORKED on which of the following days?

options.A: Days of wilful absence and unpaid leave without reason
options.B: Days of lay-off under agreement/law, leave with salary, absence due to employment accident, and maternity leave with salary
options.C: Days of illegal strike and lockout caused by the employer's misconduct
options.D: Days of suspension pending disciplinary enquiry

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Days of lay-off under agreement/law, leave with salary, absence due to employment accident, and maternity leave with salary

Section 28: An employee is deemed to have worked on days when: (a) he has been LAID OFF under agreement or as permitted by Standing Orders/ID Act/other law; (b) he has been on LEAVE WITH SALARY OR WAGES; (c) he has been ABSENT DUE TO TEMPORARY DISABLEMENT caused by accident arising out of and in the course of employment; and (d) the employee has been on MATERNITY LEAVE WITH SALARY OR WAGES. These count as working days for bonus.

question_html: Under Section 29 of the Code on Wages, an employee is DISQUALIFIED from receiving bonus if dismissed from service for which of the following?

options.A: Fraud, riotous/violent behaviour on premises, theft/misappropriation/sabotage of establishment property, OR conviction for sexual harassment
options.B: Unauthorised absence for more than 30 consecutive days
options.C: Poor performance as assessed in annual performance review
options.D: Refusal to work overtime when required by the employer

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Fraud, riotous/violent behaviour on premises, theft/misappropriation/sabotage of establishment property, OR conviction for sexual harassment

Section 29: An employee is DISQUALIFIED from bonus if DISMISSED FROM SERVICE FOR: (a) FRAUD; (b) RIOTOUS OR VIOLENT BEHAVIOUR while on the premises; (c) THEFT, MISAPPROPRIATION OR SABOTAGE of any property of the establishment; or (d) CONVICTION FOR SEXUAL HARASSMENT. Note: The disqualification is linked to dismissal for these specific serious misconduct — routine disciplinary matters do not attract bonus disqualification.

question_html: Under Section 31(1) of the Code on Wages, the allocable surplus for payment of bonus is:

options.A: 50% of available surplus for banking companies; 67% for all others
options.B: 60% of available surplus for banking companies; 75% for all others
options.C: 60% of available surplus for banking companies; 67% for all other establishments
options.D: 67% of available surplus for banking companies; 60% for all others

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 60% of available surplus for banking companies; 67% for all other establishments

Section 31(1): Bonus shall be paid out of the ALLOCABLE SURPLUS which is: 60% of AVAILABLE SURPLUS for a BANKING COMPANY; and 67% of AVAILABLE SURPLUS for ALL OTHER ESTABLISHMENTS. Available surplus = Gross profits minus sums deductible under Section 34 (depreciation, direct tax, and prescribed further sums). Section 32 provides how gross profits shall be computed.

question_html: Under Section 36 of the Code on Wages, where allocable surplus EXCEEDS maximum bonus payable, the excess is carried forward for 'set on'. What is the maximum period for which set on/set off applies?

options.A: Up to and inclusive of the second accounting year
options.B: Up to and inclusive of the fourth accounting year
options.C: Up to and inclusive of the sixth accounting year
options.D: Indefinitely until the surplus or deficiency is exhausted

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Up to and inclusive of the fourth accounting year

Section 36: Where allocable surplus exceeds maximum bonus, the EXCESS (subject to 20% of total salary/wages) shall be carried forward for SET ON in succeeding accounting years UP TO AND INCLUSIVE OF THE FOURTH ACCOUNTING YEAR. Section 36(2): Where there is no/insufficient surplus, the deficiency is carried forward for SET OFF likewise up to and inclusive of the FOURTH ACCOUNTING YEAR. When calculating bonus for a succeeding year, amount set on/off from the EARLIEST accounting year is first taken into account.
topic_text: Section 36 — Set On and Set Off

question_html: Under Section 37, if an employer has paid a PUJA BONUS or other CUSTOMARY BONUS to an employee during an accounting year, the employer is entitled to:

options.A: Deduct the amount so paid from the statutory bonus payable — the employee receives only the balance
options.B: Pay the customary bonus in addition to the full statutory bonus without any deduction
options.C: Claim a tax refund for the customary bonus paid
options.D: Seek prior approval from the appropriate Government before making such payment

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Deduct the amount so paid from the statutory bonus payable — the employee receives only the balance

Section 37: Where an employer has paid any PUJA BONUS or other CUSTOMARY BONUS (or an interim advance against bonus), the employer is entitled to DEDUCT THE AMOUNT SO PAID from the statutory bonus payable under the Code, and the employee shall be entitled to receive ONLY THE BALANCE. Section 38: Similarly, where an employee is found guilty of misconduct causing FINANCIAL LOSS, the employer may deduct the loss from bonus payable for that year only — the employee gets the balance, if any.

question_html: Under Section 39(1), all bonus amounts shall be paid by crediting to the employee's bank account within what period from the close of the accounting year?

options.A: Three months (extendable to six months)
options.B: Six months (extendable to one year)
options.C: Eight months (extendable — total period not exceeding two years in any case)
options.D: Twelve months (not extendable)

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Eight months (extendable — total period not exceeding two years in any case)

Section 39(1): All bonus amounts shall be paid by CREDITING TO THE EMPLOYEE'S BANK ACCOUNT within EIGHT MONTHS from the close of the accounting year. The appropriate Government may, on application by employer and for sufficient reasons, extend this period — but the TOTAL PERIOD SHALL NOT IN ANY CASE EXCEED TWO YEARS. Section 39(2): Where bonus is in dispute, it shall be paid within ONE MONTH from the date the award becomes enforceable. BONUS EXEMPTIONS & APPLICABILITY — SECTIONS 40, 41
topic_text: Section 39 — Time Limit for Bonus Payment

question_html: Under Section 41 of the Code on Wages, the bonus provisions (Chapter IV) apply to establishments in which how many persons are employed?

options.A: 10 or more persons on any day during an accounting year
options.B: Twenty or more persons employed or were employed on any day during an accounting year
options.C: 50 or more persons regularly employed throughout the year
options.D: 100 or more persons employed on the first day of the accounting year

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Twenty or more persons employed or were employed on any day during an accounting year

Section 41: Notwithstanding the exemptions in Section 41(1), bonus provisions apply to establishments in which TWENTY OR MORE PERSONS ARE EMPLOYED OR WERE EMPLOYED ON ANY DAY DURING AN ACCOUNTING YEAR. The phrase 'were employed' is crucial — even if current headcount is below 20, past employment during the year maintains coverage.

question_html: Under Section 40(1), a PUBLIC SECTOR establishment is covered by bonus provisions if:

options.A: It sells goods or renders services in competition with private sector AND income from such sales is not less than 20% of its gross income for that year
options.B: It employs more than 100 persons regardless of its income from competitive activities
options.C: The Central Government specifically notifies it as a bonus-applicable establishment
options.D: Its employees have passed a resolution demanding bonus under the Industrial Disputes Act

answer_html:
Answer: (A) It sells goods or renders services in competition with private sector AND income from such sales is not less than 20% of its gross income for that year

Section 40(1): If a public sector establishment SELLS GOODS OR RENDERS SERVICES IN COMPETITION WITH A PRIVATE SECTOR ESTABLISHMENT and the INCOME FROM SUCH SALE OR SERVICES is NOT LESS THAN TWENTY PER CENT (20%) of its GROSS INCOME for that year, the bonus provisions apply to it as they apply to a private sector establishment. Section 40(2): Otherwise, employees of public sector establishments are EXEMPT from bonus provisions. ADVISORY BOARDS — SECTION 42

question_html: Under Section 42(1), the Central Advisory Board shall consist of persons representing employers, equal number representing employees, independent persons (not exceeding 1/3rd of total), AND:

options.A: Three representatives of the Central Government ministries
options.B: Representatives of the Supreme Court and High Courts
options.C: Five representatives of such State Governments as nominated by the Central Government
options.D: Ten representatives from major industry associations

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Five representatives of such State Governments as nominated by the Central Government

Section 42(1): Central Advisory Board consists of: (a) EMPLOYER representatives; (b) EMPLOYEE representatives (equal in number); (c) INDEPENDENT PERSONS (not exceeding 1/3rd of total); and (d) FIVE REPRESENTATIVES OF SUCH STATE GOVERNMENTS as nominated by the Central Government. Section 42(2): ONE-THIRD of all members shall be WOMEN; and a member from the independent persons category shall be appointed as CHAIRPERSON by the Central Government.

question_html: Regarding composition of the Central Advisory Board AND the State Advisory Board under Section 42, which of the following is CORRECT about the mandatory gender representation?

options.A: At least one-fourth (25%) of total members shall be women
options.B: One-third (1/3rd) of total members of both the Central Advisory Board and State Advisory Board shall be women
options.C: One-half (50%) of total members shall be women
options.D: Women membership is recommended but not mandatory

answer_html:
Answer: (B) One-third (1/3rd) of total members of both the Central Advisory Board and State Advisory Board shall be women

Section 42(2): ONE-THIRD of the members of the CENTRAL ADVISORY BOARD shall be WOMEN. Section 42(7): ONE-THIRD of the members referred to in Section 42(6) (State Advisory Board, committees and sub-committees) shall also be WOMEN. The Chairperson of the Central Advisory Board shall be an independent member appointed by the Central Government; and the Chairperson of the State Advisory Board shall be appointed by the State Government from independent members.

question_html: Under Section 42(3), the Central Advisory Board shall advise the Central Government on which of the following matters?

options.A: Fixation/revision of minimum wages, increasing employment opportunities for women, extent to which women may be employed in specified establishments, and any other matter relating to the Code
options.B: Only on wage disputes between employers and employees in specific industries
options.C: Only on fixation of floor wage — no other functions
options.D: Setting interest rates for EPF contributions and determining bonus rates

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Fixation/revision of minimum wages, increasing employment opportunities for women, extent to which women may be employed in specified establishments, and any other matter relating to the Code

Section 42(3): The Central Advisory Board shall advise the Central Government on: (i) FIXATION OR REVISION OF MINIMUM WAGES and connected matters; (ii) INCREASING EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR WOMEN; (iii) the EXTENT TO WHICH WOMEN may be employed in specified establishments; and (iv) ANY OTHER MATTER RELATING TO THE CODE. On such advice, the Central Government may issue DIRECTIONS TO STATE GOVERNMENTS as it deems fit. INSPECTOR-CUM-FACILITATOR, CLAIMS & PENALTIES — SECTIONS 45, 49–55

question_html: Under Section 51(4) of the Code on Wages, every Inspector-cum-Facilitator shall be deemed to be:

options.A: A judicial officer with powers to impose fines and imprisonment
options.B: A quasi-judicial authority with powers of a Sessions Court
options.C: A PUBLIC SERVANT within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code
options.D: A government servant with the status of a gazetted officer

answer_html:
Answer: (C) A PUBLIC SERVANT within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code

Section 51(4): Every Inspector-cum-Facilitator appointed under Section 51(1) shall be deemed to be a PUBLIC SERVANT within the meaning of Section 21 of the INDIAN PENAL CODE, 1860. Section 51(5): The Inspector-cum-Facilitator may (a) ADVISE employers and workers on compliance; and (b) INSPECT establishments as assigned. Section 51(6): Powers include examining persons, requiring information, searching/seizing records, and bringing deficiencies to the appropriate Government's notice.

question_html: Under Section 45(2), when deciding a claim under the Code, the authority may order payment of compensation in addition to the claim. The compensation may extend to how much of the claim determined?

options.A: Five times the claim determined
options.B: Ten times the claim determined
options.C: Twice the claim determined
options.D: Twenty times the claim determined

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Ten times the claim determined

Section 45(2): While deciding claims, the authority may order, having regard to circumstances, the payment of COMPENSATION IN ADDITION TO THE CLAIM DETERMINED, which may EXTEND TO TEN TIMES of the claim determined. The authority shall endeavour to decide the claim within THREE MONTHS. Recovery of unpaid dues and compensation is effected through CERTIFICATE OF RECOVERY issued to the Collector/District Magistrate who recovers as ARREARS OF LAND REVENUE.

question_html: Under Section 45(6), an application for claim under the Code must be filed within what period from the date the claim arises?

options.A: Three years from the date the claim arises
options.B: One year from the date the claim arises
options.C: Six months from the date the claim arises
options.D: Five years from the date the claim arises

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Three years from the date the claim arises
