Section 45(6): The application for claim must be filed within THREE YEARS from the date on which the claim arises. However, the authority may entertain the application AFTER THREE YEARS on SUFFICIENT CAUSE being shown by the applicant for the delay. Section 45(4): Applications may be filed by: (a) the EMPLOYEE concerned; (b) any TRADE UNION of which the employee is a member; or (c) the INSPECTOR-CUM-FACILITATOR.

question_html: Under Section 49(1), any person aggrieved by an order of the claims authority may prefer an appeal to the appellate authority within:

options.A: Sixty days from date of order
options.B: Thirty days from date of order
options.C: Ninety days from the date of such order
options.D: One hundred and twenty days from date of order

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Ninety days from the date of such order

Section 49(1): An appeal against an order of the Section 45 authority shall be preferred within NINETY DAYS from the date of such order. The appellate authority may entertain a delayed appeal if SUFFICIENT CAUSE for delay is shown. Section 49(2): The appellate authority shall be from officers holding a post at least ONE RANK HIGHER than the Section 45 authority. The appellate authority shall endeavour to dispose of the appeal within THREE MONTHS.

question_html: Under Section 54(1) of the Code on Wages, what is the penalty for an employer who PAYS LESS than the amount due to an employee (FIRST offence)?

options.A: Imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to Rs. 1 lakh or both
options.B: Fine which may extend to FIFTY THOUSAND RUPEES (Rs. 50,000)
options.C: Fine only up to Rs. 20,000 for any contravention
options.D: Imprisonment up to one year and fine up to Rs. 5 lakhs

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Fine which may extend to FIFTY THOUSAND RUPEES (Rs. 50,000)

Section 54(1): FIRST OFFENCE of underpayment: FINE UP TO RS. 50,000. SECOND/SUBSEQUENT underpayment offence (within 5 years): IMPRISONMENT UP TO 3 MONTHS or FINE UP TO RS. 1 LAKH or BOTH. Contravention of OTHER PROVISIONS (first offence): FINE UP TO RS. 20,000; repeat within 5 years: IMPRISONMENT UP TO 1 MONTH or FINE UP TO RS. 40,000 or BOTH. Non-maintenance of records: FINE UP TO RS. 10,000. Section 52: Offences triable only by METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE OR JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE OF THE FIRST CLASS. CONSOLIDATED ANSWER KEY — ALL 50 QUESTIONS — END OF QUESTION PAPER — Prepared from ICMAI Study Module | Code on Wages, 2019 | Module 11 | Syllabus 2022 | CMA Inter June 2026

question_html: Under Section 1(3) of the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, the Act applies to every factory engaged in any industry specified in Schedule I and employing how many or more persons?

options.A: 10 or more persons
options.B: 20 or more persons
options.C: 50 or more persons
options.D: 100 or more persons

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 20 or more persons

Section 1(3): The EPF Act applies to every factory in a Schedule I industry employing 20 OR MORE PERSONS, and to any other establishment employing 20 or more persons as the Central Government may notify. The Central Government may also extend coverage to establishments with fewer than 20 persons (with at least 2 months' notice).
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Once an establishment becomes covered under the EPF Act, what happens if the number of persons employed subsequently falls below 20?

options.A: The Act ceases to apply automatically after 6 months
options.B: The Act ceases to apply, and the employer must seek fresh registration if headcount rises again
options.C: The Act continues to apply notwithstanding that the number falls below 20
options.D: The Central Government must issue a fresh notification to maintain coverage

answer_html:
Answer: (C) The Act continues to apply notwithstanding that the number falls below 20

Section 1(3) Proviso: Once the EPF Act is applied to any establishment, it SHALL CONTINUE TO APPLY notwithstanding that the number of persons employed therein at any time FALLS BELOW 20. This was affirmed in Annamma Iype v. Regional PF Commissioner (1993): a fall in strength does not remove the establishment from the Act's purview.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 16(1) of the EPF Act, the Act does NOT apply to which of the following establishments?

options.A: A co-operative society registered under the Co-operative Societies Act, 1912, employing less than 50 persons and working WITHOUT the aid of power
options.B: A manufacturing factory in Schedule I employing exactly 20 persons
options.C: A coal mine employing 25 workers
options.D: A private bank with 30 employees

answer_html:
Answer: (A) A co-operative society registered under the Co-operative Societies Act, 1912, employing less than 50 persons and working WITHOUT the aid of power

Section 16(1)(a): The Act is NOT applicable to any establishment registered under the Co-operative Societies Act, 1912 (or any State law on co-operatives), employing LESS THAN 50 PERSONS and working WITHOUT THE AID OF POWER. Both conditions — fewer than 50 persons AND no power — must be met for this exemption.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 1(4) of the EPF Act, an establishment employing FEWER than 20 persons may be brought under the Act if:

options.A: The employee union files a petition with the High Court
options.B: The Central Provident Fund Commissioner notifies coverage based on employer-employee agreement
options.C: The State Government issues a mandatory coverage order
options.D: The employer unilaterally registers the establishment

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The Central Provident Fund Commissioner notifies coverage based on employer-employee agreement

Section 1(4): Where it appears to the CENTRAL PROVIDENT FUND COMMISSIONER that the EMPLOYER AND THE MAJORITY OF EMPLOYEES HAVE AGREED that the Act should apply, he may, by notification, apply the provisions to that establishment from the date of such agreement or a subsequent date specified in the agreement. This is voluntary coverage by mutual consent.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 16(1)(b), which government establishment is exempt from the EPF Act?

options.A: Any government establishment regardless of the benefits it provides
options.B: Any private establishment owned by a public sector undertaking
options.C: Establishments belonging to or under control of Central/State Government whose employees are entitled to contributory provident fund or old age pension under a government scheme
options.D: Only Central Government establishments with more than 500 employees

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Establishments belonging to or under control of Central/State Government whose employees are entitled to contributory provident fund or old age pension under a government scheme

Section 16(1)(b): The Act does NOT apply to any establishment belonging to or under the CONTROL OF THE CENTRAL OR STATE GOVERNMENT whose employees are entitled to the benefit of CONTRIBUTORY PROVIDENT FUND or OLD AGE PENSION in accordance with any scheme or rule framed by the Central/State Government. The key condition is that such employees already enjoy equivalent benefits.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Which of the following correctly lists ALL THREE schemes framed under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952?

options.A: Employees' Provident Fund Scheme 1952; Employees' Pension Scheme 1995; Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme 1976
options.B: Employees' Provident Fund Scheme 1952; Employees' Gratuity Scheme 1972; Employees' Insurance Scheme 1948
options.C: Employees' Provident Fund Scheme 1952; Employees' Pension Scheme 2004; Employees' Health Insurance Scheme 1976
options.D: Employees' Provident Fund Scheme 1952; Employees' State Insurance Scheme 1948; Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme 1976

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Employees' Provident Fund Scheme 1952; Employees' Pension Scheme 1995; Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme 1976

The EPF Act provides THREE schemes: (a) Employees' Provident Fund Scheme, 1952 [Section 5]; (b) Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995 [Section 6A]; and (c) Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976 [Section 6C]. These three together provide old-age security, survivorship benefits, and life insurance cover to employees.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: The EPF Act is now applicable to employees drawing pay (basic wages + DA + retaining allowance + cash value of food concession) not exceeding:

options.A: Rs. 6,500 per month
options.B: Rs. 15,000 per month
options.C: Rs. 21,000 per month
options.D: Rs. 25,000 per month

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Rs. 15,000 per month

The EPF Act applies to employees drawing pay not exceeding RS. 15,000 PER MONTH (with effect from 01.09.2014). The term 'pay' for this purpose includes basic wages, dearness allowance, retaining allowance (if any), and cash value of food concession. For international workers, the wage ceiling of Rs. 15,000 is NOT applicable.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: To which of the following establishments do the EPF Scheme, 1952 and the EDLI Scheme, 1976 specifically NOT apply?

options.A: Coal mines in Jharkhand
options.B: Jute mills in West Bengal
options.C: Tea factories in the State of Assam
options.D: Textile mills in Tamil Nadu

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Tea factories in the State of Assam

The EPF Scheme, 1952 and the Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976 specifically do NOT apply to TEA FACTORIES IN THE STATE OF ASSAM. This is an established exception. All other Schedule I industries and notified establishments are covered, subject to the 20-person threshold. IMPORTANT DEFINITIONS — SECTION 2
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 2(b) of the EPF Act, 'basic wages' includes which of the following?

options.A: All emoluments earned by an employee while on duty, on leave, or on holidays with wages paid in cash under the contract of employment
options.B: Dearness allowance, house rent allowance, overtime allowance, and commission
options.C: Any presents made by the employer and cash value of food concessions
options.D: Bonus, commission, and any other similar allowance

answer_html:
Answer: (A) All emoluments earned by an employee while on duty, on leave, or on holidays with wages paid in cash under the contract of employment

Section 2(b): Basic wages = ALL EMOLUMENTS earned while on duty, on leave or on holidays WITH WAGES in cash per contract. It EXCLUDES: cash value of any consideration, dearness allowance, HRA, overtime allowance, bonus, commission, and any similar allowance, and any presents made by the employer. DA is expressly excluded from basic wages under the EPF Act definition.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 2(f) of the EPF Act, which of the following persons is INCLUDED in the definition of 'employee'?

options.A: A member of the Armed Forces of the Union
options.B: A person employed through a contractor in connection with the work of the establishment
options.C: An apprentice engaged under the Apprentices Act, 1961
options.D: A partner of a firm having status of a beneficiary

answer_html:
Answer: (B) A person employed through a contractor in connection with the work of the establishment

Section 2(f): Employee includes any person employed for wages in any kind of work (manual or otherwise) in or in connection with the work of an establishment who gets wages directly or indirectly from the employer. INCLUDED: persons employed THROUGH A CONTRACTOR, and apprentices NOT under the Apprentices Act 1961. EXCLUDED: apprentices under Apprentices Act 1961, Armed Forces members. (Prakash D. Shah v. Union of India: partners are not employees.)
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: For an establishment having departments or branches in MORE THAN ONE STATE, the 'appropriate Government' under Section 2(a) of the EPF Act is:

options.A: Each individual State Government for its respective territorial jurisdiction
options.B: The State Government where the registered office of the establishment is located
options.C: The Central Government
options.D: Both Central and State Governments jointly

answer_html:
Answer: (C) The Central Government

Section 2(a): The CENTRAL GOVERNMENT is the appropriate government for: (i) establishments belonging to or under control of the Central Government; (ii) establishments connected with railways, major ports, mines, oil fields, or controlled industries; and (iii) establishments HAVING DEPARTMENTS OR BRANCHES IN MORE THAN ONE STATE. For all other establishments, the STATE GOVERNMENT is appropriate.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 2(aa), which of the following is NOT included in the definition of 'authorised officer' under the EPF Act?

options.A: Central Provident Fund Commissioner
options.B: Additional Central Provident Fund Commissioner
options.C: Inspector General of Factories
options.D: Regional Provident Fund Commissioner

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Central Provident Fund Commissioner

Section 2(aa): Authorised officer means the Central Provident Fund Commissioner, Additional Central Provident Fund Commissioner, Deputy Provident Fund Commissioner, Regional Provident Fund Commissioner, or such other officer as the Central Government may authorise. Inspector General of Factories is NOT an authorised officer under the EPF Act — that is a position under the Factories Act.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 2(e) of the EPF Act, in relation to an establishment which is a factory, 'employer' means:

options.A: Only the registered owner of the factory building
options.B: The owner or occupier of the factory, including the agent of such owner/occupier, the legal representative of a deceased owner/occupier, and where a person has been named as manager, that person
options.C: Only the managing director of the company
options.D: Any senior officer nominated by the Board of Directors

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The owner or occupier of the factory, including the agent of such owner/occupier, the legal representative of a deceased owner/occupier, and where a person has been named as manager, that person

Section 2(e): In relation to a factory, employer means the OWNER OR OCCUPIER of the factory, including: (a) the AGENT of such owner/occupier; (b) the LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE of a deceased owner/occupier; and (c) where a person has been named as MANAGER, that person. For other establishments, employer means the person having ultimate control or the managing director/agent entrusted with affairs.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 2(g) of the EPF Act, 'factory' is defined as any premises in any part of which a manufacturing process is being carried on:

options.A: Only with the aid of power and employing 10 or more workers
options.B: Only without the aid of power in certain scheduled industries
options.C: Whether with the aid of power or without the aid of power
options.D: With the aid of power only, employing 20 or more workers

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Whether with the aid of power or without the aid of power

Section 2(g): Under the EPF Act, 'factory' means any premises including its precincts in any part of which a manufacturing process is being carried on or is ordinarily so carried on, WHETHER WITH THE AID OF POWER OR WITHOUT THE AID OF POWER. This is broader than the Factories Act definition which requires 10+ workers with power and 20+ without power. CONTRIBUTIONS — SECTION 6, 6A, 6C
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 6 of the EPF Act, the basic rate of contribution payable by the employer to the Provident Fund is:

options.A: 10% of basic wages, dearness allowance and retaining allowance
options.B: 8.33% of basic wages only
options.C: 12% of basic wages, dearness allowance and retaining allowance (enhanced rate, specially notified)
options.D: 15% of total wages including all allowances

answer_html:
Answer: (A) 10% of basic wages, dearness allowance and retaining allowance

Section 6: The basic statutory rate is 10% of basic wages, DA and retaining allowance. The Government has raised the rate to 12% (from 10%) for establishments specially notified — effective September 22, 1997. Both rates apply in different contexts. Employee contribution = same as employer contribution. Both the 10% standard rate and the enhanced 12% rate are tested by examiners.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 6, if an employee desires to contribute to the Provident Fund at a rate HIGHER than the prescribed rate, which of the following is correct?

options.A: The employer is obligated to match the higher contribution in full
options.B: The employee may contribute at a higher rate, but the employer is NOT obligated to contribute over and above the prescribed rate
options.C: The employee can only contribute at the prescribed rate — no higher contribution is allowed
options.D: Higher contribution by the employee requires prior approval of the Regional PF Commissioner

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The employee may contribute at a higher rate, but the employer is NOT obligated to contribute over and above the prescribed rate

Section 6 Proviso: Employees, if they desire, may make contribution EXCEEDING the prescribed rate. However, the employer shall NOT BE UNDER ANY OBLIGATION to contribute over and above the contribution payable as prescribed by the Government. This is the Voluntary Provident Fund (VPF) arrangement — only the employee bears the excess.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: With effect from 01.09.2014, the maximum wage limit up to which PF contribution is calculated (employer and employee) is:

options.A: Rs. 6,500 per month
options.B: Rs. 10,000 per month
options.C: Rs. 15,000 per month
options.D: Rs. 25,000 per month

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Rs. 15,000 per month

Contribution is paid on a maximum of RS. 15,000 PER MONTH by both employer and employee (w.e.f. 01.09.2014). To contribute on higher wages, a JOINT REQUEST from both employee and employer is required. In such cases the employer must also pay administrative charges on the higher wages. For INTERNATIONAL WORKERS, the Rs. 15,000 ceiling is NOT applicable.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Each PF contribution shall be calculated to the nearest rupee. How are fractions treated?

options.A: 50 paise or more is rounded up to the next higher rupee; fraction less than 50 paise is ignored
options.B: All fractions are always rounded up to the next rupee
options.C: All fractions are always rounded down and ignored
options.D: Fractions are carried forward to the next month's calculation

answer_html:
Answer: (A) 50 paise or more is rounded up to the next higher rupee; fraction less than 50 paise is ignored

Section 6: Each contribution shall be calculated to the NEAREST RUPEE — 50 PAISE OR MORE is counted as the NEXT HIGHER RUPEE; a FRACTION OF A RUPEE LESS THAN 50 PAISE IS IGNORED. This standard rounding rule is frequently tested in MCQs and fill-in-the-blank questions.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under the Employees' Pension Scheme (Section 6A), the employer's contribution to the Pension Fund is:

options.A: Equal to the employee's contribution to EPS
options.B: 8.33% of basic wages, dearness allowance and retaining allowance of the employee
options.C: 10% of basic wages plus special allowance
options.D: 12% of total wages drawn by the employee

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 8.33% of basic wages, dearness allowance and retaining allowance of the employee

Section 6A / EPS 1995: The employer contributes 8.33% of the basic wages, DA and retaining allowance to the Employees' Pension Scheme. Critically, there is NO CONTRIBUTION FROM THE EMPLOYEE to the EPS — only the employer contributes. Contribution to EPS is NOT payable once the employee crosses 58 YEARS OF AGE, as the scheme ceases on completion of 58 years.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Regarding the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS, 1995), which of the following statements is CORRECT?

options.A: Both employer and employee contribute equally to EPS
options.B: Only the employee contributes to EPS — the employer's contribution goes entirely to the PF
options.C: There is NO contribution from the employee to EPS; only the employer contributes 8.33%
options.D: Contributions to EPS continue until retirement regardless of age

answer_html:
Answer: (C) There is NO contribution from the employee to EPS; only the employer contributes 8.33%

EPS 1995: There is ABSOLUTELY NO CONTRIBUTION from the employee to the Pension Scheme. The employer contributes 8.33% of the basic wages + DA + retaining allowance to EPS. Contribution is NOT payable once the employee CROSSES 58 YEARS OF AGE since the scheme ceases on completion of 58 years. This is one of the most tested facts about EPS.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: The Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI) under Section 6C came into effect on:

options.A: 1st September 1976
options.B: 2nd September 1952
options.C: 1st January 1995
options.D: 1st September 2014

answer_html:
Answer: (A) 1st September 1976

Section 6C: The Central Government made the EMPLOYEES' DEPOSIT-LINKED INSURANCE SCHEME, 1976 which came into effect from 01.09.1976. (The EPF Scheme, 1952 came into effect from 2nd September 1952; EPS, 1995 came into effect from 1995.) Note: The EDLI Scheme, like the EPF Scheme, does NOT apply to tea factories in the State of Assam.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under the Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance (EDLI) Scheme, the employer's contribution to the Insurance Fund shall not exceed:

options.A: 0.5% of aggregate of basic wages, DA and retaining allowance
options.B: 1% of aggregate of basic wages, DA and retaining allowance
options.C: 2% of basic wages only
options.D: 8.33% of basic wages and DA

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 1% of aggregate of basic wages, DA and retaining allowance

Section 6C: The employer shall pay to the Insurance Fund an amount NOT BEING MORE THAN 1% of the aggregate of basic wages, DA and retaining allowance of every employee. Additionally, the employer pays a further amount (not exceeding one-fourth of the contribution) to meet administration expenses of the scheme. EDLI insurance benefit ranges from Rs. 2.5 lakhs to Rs. 6 lakhs. CENTRAL BOARD, STATE BOARD & GOVERNANCE — SECTIONS 5A, 5AA, 5B
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 5A of the EPF Act, who is the ex-officio member of the Central Board?

options.A: The Union Minister of Labour
options.B: The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
options.C: The Central Provident Fund Commissioner
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

answer_html:
Answer: (C) The Central Provident Fund Commissioner

Section 5A: The Central Board is established by the Central Government. It consists of a Chairman and Vice Chairman appointed by the Central Government. The CENTRAL PROVIDENT FUND COMMISSIONER is an EX-OFFICIO member of the Central Board. Other members are appointed by the Central Government as per the provisions of Section 5A.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Section 5AA of the EPF Act provides for the appointment of which body to assist the Central Board in the performance of its functions?

options.A: An Executive Committee appointed by the Central Government
options.B: A Standing Sub-Committee appointed by Parliament
options.C: A Technical Advisory Committee appointed by the Regional PF Commissioner
options.D: A Management Committee appointed by the State Government

answer_html:
Answer: (A) An Executive Committee appointed by the Central Government

Section 5AA: The Central Government shall appoint an EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE to assist the Central Board in the performance of its functions. Members of the Executive Committee are also appointed by the Central Government. (Fill-in-blank from module: Section 5AA provides for the appointment of EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE.)
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 7 of the EPF Act, the power to add, amend or vary the EPF Scheme, Pension Scheme or Insurance Scheme vests with:

options.A: The Central Government, either prospectively or retrospectively
options.B: The Regional Provident Fund Commissioner with Central Board approval
options.C: The State Government in consultation with the Central Board
options.D: The EPF Appellate Tribunal on application by workers

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The Regional Provident Fund Commissioner with Central Board approval

Section 7: The CENTRAL GOVERNMENT may, by notification in the Official Gazette, ADD TO, AMEND OR VARY, either PROSPECTIVELY OR RETROSPECTIVELY, the Scheme, the Pension Scheme or the Insurance Scheme. The power to modify schemes rests solely with the Central Government — no other authority can amend these schemes.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under which body does the Pension Fund vest and by whom is it administered?

options.A: The Regional Provident Fund Commissioner in each State
options.B: The State Government in consultation with Central Board
options.C: The Central Board constituted under Section 5A of the EPF Act
options.D: The Life Insurance Corporation of India

answer_html:
Answer: (C) The Central Board constituted under Section 5A of the EPF Act

The PENSION FUND shall VEST IN AND BE ADMINISTERED BY THE CENTRAL BOARD. The Central Board constituted under Section 5A also administers the Provident Fund. The Pension Fund is kept and invested by the Central Board subject to the pattern of investment determined by the Central Government.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Section 12 of the EPF Act prohibits an employer from doing which of the following?

options.A: Reducing wages of any employee by reason only of the employer's liability to pay contribution to the Fund or under any charges under the scheme
options.B: Increasing wages of employees without prior intimation to the PF Commissioner
options.C: Employing additional workers after contributing to the Fund
options.D: Paying wages in kind instead of cash

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Reducing wages of any employee by reason only of the employer's liability to pay contribution to the Fund or under any charges under the scheme

Section 12: No employer in relation to an establishment to which any scheme or insurance scheme applies shall, BY REASON ONLY OF HIS LIABILITY for payment of any contribution to the fund or any charges under the scheme, REDUCE — WHETHER DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY — THE WAGES of any employee to whom the scheme applies. This prevents employers from shifting the burden of PF contributions to employees by wage cuts.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
topic_text: Section 12 — Employer Not to Reduce Wages
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 17A of the EPF Act, if an employee leaves employment in a covered establishment and joins an establishment NOT covered by the Act, what happens to his PF accumulations?

options.A: The accumulations are automatically forfeited after 3 years
options.B: The accumulations may be transferred to the PF of the new establishment if the employee desires and the new fund's rules permit
options.C: The accumulations must remain in the old fund until the employee reaches retirement age
options.D: The employee receives the accumulations as a lump sum immediately upon leaving

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The accumulations may be transferred to the PF of the new establishment if the employee desires and the new fund's rules permit

Section 17A: Where an employee employed in a covered establishment leaves and obtains re-employment in an establishment to which the Act does NOT apply, the AMOUNT OF ACCUMULATIONS TO HIS CREDIT shall be TRANSFERRED to his account in the provident fund of the new establishment — IF (a) the EMPLOYEE SO DESIRES and (b) the RULES of that provident fund PERMIT SUCH TRANSFER. WITHDRAWALS, ADVANCES & PROTECTION — SECTIONS 10, 12, 17A
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 10 of the EPF Act, the amount standing to the credit of a member of the Fund:

options.A: May be attached by a court decree if the member has defaulted on a bank loan
options.B: May be assigned by the member to his creditors with prior written consent
options.C: Shall NOT be capable of being assigned or charged, and shall NOT be liable to attachment under any court decree in respect of any debt or liability incurred by the member
options.D: May be attached if ordered by a Tribunal in an industrial dispute

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Shall NOT be capable of being assigned or charged, and shall NOT be liable to attachment under any court decree in respect of any debt or liability incurred by the member

Section 10: The amount standing to the credit of any member of the Fund shall NOT in any way be capable of being ASSIGNED OR CHARGED and shall NOT be LIABLE TO ATTACHMENT under any decree of any court in respect of ANY DEBT OR LIABILITY incurred by the member. Neither the Official Assignee nor any receiver shall be entitled to or have any claim on such amount.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Withdrawal from the Provident Fund is permitted for which of the following purposes?

options.A: Purchase/construction of a dwelling house including acquisition of a suitable site
options.B: Purchase of a motor vehicle
options.C: Payment of credit card dues or personal loans
options.D: Funding a business venture or trade

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Purchase/construction of a dwelling house including acquisition of a suitable site

Withdrawal from PF is allowed for: (i) Purchase of a DWELLING HOUSE/FLAT or CONSTRUCTION of a dwelling house including acquisition of a suitable site; (ii) Repayment of loans in special cases; (iii) Withdrawal within one year BEFORE RETIREMENT; and (iv) WITHDRAWAL UP TO 75% of balance if not employed for one month or more (subject to PF Commissioner approval). Such withdrawals need NOT be repaid.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under the EPF Scheme, which of the following is a correct ground for obtaining an advance (not a withdrawal) from the Provident Fund?

options.A: For illness in certain cases and for marriage or post-matriculation education of children
options.B: For foreign travel for leisure purposes
options.C: For purchase of a car or motorcycle
options.D: For repayment of personal loans from private lenders

answer_html:
Answer: (B) For foreign travel for leisure purposes

ADVANCES from the PF Fund are granted for: (a) ILLNESS in certain cases; (b) MARRIAGES or POST-MATRICULATION EDUCATION of children; (c) Abnormal conditions (calamity — floods, earthquakes, riots) — non-refundable; (d) Cut in electricity supply — non-refundable; (e) Physically handicapped members — non-refundable. These are advances and are refundable (except those noted as non-refundable).
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under the EPF Scheme, a member who has not been employed for one month or more may withdraw up to what percentage of the balance in the Fund, subject to approval?

options.A: 50% of the PF balance
options.B: 60% of the PF balance
options.C: 75% of the PF balance
options.D: 100% of the PF balance

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 75% of the PF balance

Under the EPF Scheme, a member who has been UNEMPLOYED FOR ONE MONTH OR MORE may withdraw UP TO 75% of the balance standing to his credit in the PF, subject to the approval of the PF Commissioner or any officer authorised by him. This is a partial withdrawal to tide over unemployment and does not require repayment.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under the Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976, the insurance benefit payable shall be an amount between:

options.A: Rs. 50,000 and Rs. 1 lakh
options.B: Rs. 2.5 lakhs and Rs. 6 lakhs
options.C: Rs. 1 lakh and Rs. 3 lakhs
options.D: Rs. 5 lakhs and Rs. 10 lakhs

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Rs. 50,000 and Rs. 1 lakh

Section 6C / EDLI Scheme 1976: The INSURANCE BENEFIT under the EDLI Scheme shall be an amount BETWEEN RS. 2.5 LAKHS AND RS. 6 LAKHS. The wage ceiling under EDLI has been increased from Rs. 6,500 to Rs. 15,000. This lump sum is payable to the nominee/legal heir on the death of the member while in service. DETERMINATION, REVIEW & APPELLATE TRIBUNAL — SECTIONS 7A, 7B, 7C, 7D
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 7A of the EPF Act, who has the authority to conduct an inquiry and determine the amount due from an employer where a dispute arises regarding the applicability of the Act?

options.A: The Authorised Officer (e.g., Regional PF Commissioner) who may conduct inquiry and determine dues
options.B: The High Court on a writ petition by the employer
options.C: The Industrial Tribunal constituted under the Industrial Disputes Act
options.D: The Chief Labour Commissioner in consultation with State Government

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The High Court on a writ petition by the employer

Section 7A: The AUTHORITY CONCERNED (i.e., the authorised officer) may conduct such inquiry as deemed necessary, determine the dispute about applicability, and DETERMINE THE AMOUNT DUE from the employer. Before passing an order, the employer must be given a REASONABLE OPPORTUNITY to present his case. The authority has the powers of a civil court under CPC for the inquiry.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 7A, if the employer fails to attend the inquiry, the authority passes an ex-parte order. The employer may apply to set aside this ex-parte order within how many months?

options.A: One month from the date of communication of order
options.B: Six months from the date of communication of order
options.C: Three months from the date of communication of order
options.D: Twelve months from the date of communication of order

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Three months from the date of communication of order

Section 7A: If an ex-parte order is passed due to the employer's failure to attend, the employer may apply to the Authority to SET ASIDE the ex-parte order within THREE MONTHS from the date of COMMUNICATION of such order, showing sufficient causes for non-attendance. If satisfied, the Authority may set aside the ex-parte order and fix a fresh date for inquiry.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 7B of the EPF Act, a person aggrieved by an order under Section 7A may apply for REVIEW of that order on which of the following grounds?

options.A: Discovery of new and important evidence not within his knowledge earlier (after due diligence), mistake or error apparent on the face of the record, or any other sufficient reason
options.B: Only if the order was passed without giving him an opportunity to be heard
options.C: Only if there is a change in law after the original order
options.D: Mere disagreement with the quantum of dues determined

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Discovery of new and important evidence not within his knowledge earlier (after due diligence), mistake or error apparent on the face of the record, or any other sufficient reason

Section 7B: Review may be applied on grounds of: (i) DISCOVERY OF NEW AND IMPORTANT MATTER OR EVIDENCE which after exercise of due diligence was not within knowledge or could not be produced at time of order; (ii) MISTAKE or ERROR APPARENT ON THE FACE OF THE RECORD; or (iii) ANY OTHER SUFFICIENT REASON. The officer may also REVIEW HIS OWN ORDER on his own motion if satisfied it is necessary to do so.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 7C of the EPF Act, the officer can re-open a case to determine 'escaped amounts' within how many years from the date of the order under Section 7A or 7B?

options.A: Two years from the date of the order
options.B: Five years from the date of the order
options.C: Three years from the date of the order
options.D: Ten years from the date of the order

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Five years from the date of the order

Section 7C: The officer can re-open the case within FIVE YEARS from the date of the order passed under Section 7A or 7B, if he has reason to believe that, due to the employer's omission or failure to make documents available or to disclose all material facts, any amount due from the employer for any period HAS ESCAPED NOTICE. The officer may pass orders re-determining the escaped amount.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: The EPF Appellate Tribunal under Section 7D hears appeals against orders passed under which sections of the EPF Act?

options.A: Section 5A and Section 5B only
options.B: Section 6, 6A and 6C only
options.C: Section 7A, 7B or 7C, or under the Central Government
options.D: Section 14 and Section 14A only

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Section 7A, 7B or 7C, or under the Central Government

Section 7D: The EPF Appellate Tribunal is appointed to hear appeals against orders passed by the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT OR ANY AUTHORITY UNDER SECTIONS 7A, 7B OR 7C. After giving reasonable opportunity to parties, the Tribunal may CONFIRM, MODIFY, OR ANNUL the order, or remit the case back with directions. The Tribunal may rectify mistakes within FIVE YEARS of its order.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 7D of the EPF Act, no appeal by the employer shall be entertained by the Appellate Tribunal unless the employer has deposited what percentage of the amount due from him?

options.A: 75% of the amount due
options.B: 25% of the amount due
options.C: 50% of the amount due
options.D: 100% of the amount due

answer_html:
Answer: (A) 75% of the amount due

Section 7D: No appeal by the EMPLOYER shall be entertained by the EPF Appellate Tribunal UNLESS THE EMPLOYER HAS DEPOSITED 75% of the amount due from him as determined under Section 7A/7B/7C. However, the Tribunal may, FOR REASONS TO BE RECORDED IN WRITING, WAIVE OR REDUCE the amount to be deposited under this section.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: The EPF Appellate Tribunal may rectify any mistake apparent from the record in its own order within:

options.A: Three years from the date of its appeal order
options.B: Five years from the date of its appeal order
options.C: One year from the date of its appeal order
options.D: Two years from the date of its appeal order

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Five years from the date of its appeal order

Section 7D: The EPF Appellate Tribunal may rectify any MISTAKE APPARENT FROM THE RECORD within FIVE YEARS from the date of its appeal order. This rectification power is similar to the inherent power of courts to correct obvious errors and ensures finality with fairness in the appellate process. PENALTIES & OFFENCES — SECTIONS 14, 14A
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 14(1) of the EPF Act, any person who knowingly makes or causes to be made any false statement or false representation (to avoid payment) shall be punishable with:

options.A: Fine only up to Rs. 10,000
options.B: Imprisonment up to 6 months only
options.C: Imprisonment up to one year OR fine of Rs. 5,000 OR both
options.D: Imprisonment up to two years and fine of Rs. 1 lakh

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Imprisonment up to one year OR fine of Rs. 5,000 OR both

Section 14(1): For the purpose of AVOIDING ANY PAYMENT, whoever knowingly makes or causes to be made any FALSE STATEMENT OR FALSE REPRESENTATION shall be punishable with IMPRISONMENT UP TO ONE YEAR, or a FINE OF RS. 5,000, or BOTH. This is the penalty for fraudulent evasion of PF contributions.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 14(1A) of the EPF Act, an employer who defaults in paying employees' PF contributions (deducted from employees' wages) shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall NOT BE LESS THAN:

options.A: One year (with fine of Rs. 10,000)
options.B: Six months
options.C: Three months
options.D: Two years

answer_html:
Answer: (A) One year (with fine of Rs. 10,000)

Section 14(1A): An employer who defaults in payment of EMPLOYEES' CONTRIBUTION (deducted but not deposited) — imprisonment for a term which may extend to THREE YEARS but shall NOT BE LESS THAN ONE YEAR, with fine of RS. 10,000. For default in payment of INSPECTION/ADMINISTRATIVE CHARGES — not less than SIX MONTHS with fine of Rs. 5,000. These are mandatory minimum sentences.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 14(3) of the EPF Act, any person who contravenes or makes default in complying with ANY provision of the Act (where no other penalty is provided) shall be punishable with:

options.A: Fine only up to Rs. 2,000
options.B: Imprisonment which may extend to six months but not less than one month, with fine up to Rs. 5,000
options.C: Imprisonment up to three years with fine up to Rs. 10,000
options.D: Imprisonment up to one year with fine up to Rs. 4,000

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Imprisonment which may extend to six months but not less than one month, with fine up to Rs. 5,000

Section 14(3): General contravention (where no other penalty is provided elsewhere) — imprisonment which may extend to SIX MONTHS but shall NOT BE LESS THAN ONE MONTH, with fine up to RS. 5,000. Section 14(2): Contravention of scheme provisions — imprisonment up to one year OR fine up to Rs. 4,000 or both. The distinction between these penalty levels is frequently tested.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 14A(1) of the EPF Act, if a company commits an offence, who is deemed to be guilty?

options.A: Only the company as a legal entity — no individual officer is liable
options.B: Only the employee who caused the offence
options.C: Every person who was in charge of and responsible for the conduct of the company's business, as well as the company itself
options.D: Only the Managing Director and Company Secretary

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Every person who was in charge of and responsible for the conduct of the company's business, as well as the company itself

Section 14A(1): If an offence under the EPF Act is committed by a company, EVERY PERSON who at the time of the offence was IN CHARGE OF AND RESPONSIBLE to the company for conduct of its business, AS WELL AS THE COMPANY, shall be deemed guilty and liable to punishment. EXCEPTION: A person shall not be liable if he proves the offence was committed WITHOUT HIS KNOWLEDGE or that he exercised ALL DUE DILIGENCE to prevent it.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 14A(2) of the EPF Act, when can a director, manager, secretary or other officer of a company be personally liable for an offence committed by the company?

options.A: When it is proved that the offence was committed with his consent or connivance, or is attributable to neglect on his part
options.B: Automatically, as a company officer, regardless of involvement
options.C: Only when convicted separately by a special tribunal
options.D: Only when the company has been wound up

answer_html:
Answer: (A) When it is proved that the offence was committed with his consent or connivance, or is attributable to neglect on his part

Section 14A(2): A director, manager, secretary or other officer of a company is personally liable where it is PROVED that the offence was committed: (a) WITH HIS CONSENT OR CONNIVANCE; or (b) is ATTRIBUTABLE TO ANY NEGLECT on his part. This section lifts the corporate veil to hold individual officers accountable for deliberate or negligent compliance failures.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Under Section 14(1B) of the EPF Act, an employer who defaults in payment of INSPECTION CHARGES under Section 6C (EDLI Scheme) shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year but which shall NOT BE LESS THAN:

options.A: Three months
options.B: Six months
options.C: One month
options.D: Nine months

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Six months

Section 14(1B): Default in payment of inspection charges under Section 6C (EDLI Scheme) — imprisonment up to ONE YEAR but not less than SIX MONTHS, with fine up to RS. 5,000. Compare with Section 14(1A): default in employees' PF contributions — imprisonment up to three years, not less than one year. The different minimum sentences reflect severity of the offence. EPS BENEFITS, EXEMPTIONS & SPECIAL PROVISIONS
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: The Employees' Pension Scheme under Section 6A provides for which of the following pension benefits?

options.A: Only superannuation pension for employees above 60 years
options.B: Only widow's pension payable on death of the employee
options.C: Superannuation pension, retiring pension/permanent total disablement pension, widow/widower's pension, children's pension, and orphan's pension
options.D: Only retirement pension and medical benefit for dependents

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Superannuation pension, retiring pension/permanent total disablement pension, widow/widower's pension, children's pension, and orphan's pension

Section 6A: The EPS, 1995 provides for: (i) SUPERANNUATION PENSION; (ii) RETIRING PENSION or PERMANENT TOTAL DISABLEMENT PENSION; (iii) WIDOW OR WIDOWER'S PENSION; (iv) CHILDREN'S PENSION; and (v) ORPHAN'S PENSION payable to beneficiaries of such employees. These five categories of pension cover the employee and his family both during service and after death.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: For the purpose of conducting an inquiry under Section 7A, the authority has the same powers as are vested in a court under the Code of Civil Procedure for which of the following?

options.A: Enforcing attendance of any person or examining him on oath, requiring discovery and production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavit, and issuing commissions for examination of witnesses
options.B: Sentencing persons to imprisonment
options.C: Ordering attachment of property before judgment
options.D: Trying summary criminal offences

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Enforcing attendance of any person or examining him on oath, requiring discovery and production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavit, and issuing commissions for examination of witnesses

Section 7A: The authority has the SAME POWERS AS A CIVIL COURT UNDER CPC for: (a) ENFORCING ATTENDANCE of any person or EXAMINING HIM ON OATH; (b) REQUIRING DISCOVERY AND PRODUCTION OF DOCUMENTS; (c) RECEIVING EVIDENCE ON AFFIDAVIT; and (d) ISSUING COMMISSIONS FOR EXAMINATION OF WITNESSES. This equips the PF authority with judicial tools to conduct effective inquiries.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: For the purpose of PF contribution under Section 6, 'dearness allowance' shall include which of the following?

options.A: Only the standard cost-of-living allowance as separately designated in the pay slip
options.B: The cash value of any food concession allowed to an employee
options.C: House rent allowance paid to employees in lieu of accommodation
options.D: Conveyance allowance or travel concession

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The cash value of any food concession allowed to an employee

Section 6: For purposes of PF contribution calculation, DEARNESS ALLOWANCE shall include the CASH VALUE OF ANY FOOD CONCESSION allowed to an employee. RETAINING ALLOWANCE is defined separately as the allowance payable for retaining the employee's services when the establishment is not working. Both are included in the contribution base.
chapter_label: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
module_title: Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

question_html: Regarding PF contribution for INTERNATIONAL WORKERS under the EPF Act, which of the following is CORRECT?

options.A: International workers must contribute at a lower rate of 8.33% only
options.B: International workers are completely exempt from EPF coverage
options.C: The wage ceiling of Rs. 15,000 per month does NOT apply to international workers — they must contribute on actual wages
options.D: International workers may opt out of EPF coverage by written application

answer_html:
Answer: (C) The wage ceiling of Rs. 15,000 per month does NOT apply to international workers — they must contribute on actual wages

For INTERNATIONAL WORKERS, the wage ceiling of RS. 15,000 (w.e.f. 01.09.2014) is NOT APPLICABLE. International workers contribute on their ACTUAL wages without any ceiling cap. When a contribution on higher wages is sought for domestic workers (above Rs. 15,000), a JOINT REQUEST from both employer and employee is required, and the employer must pay administrative charges on higher wages. question_html: The Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 is described as the first major legislation on social security for employees in India. What is the primary OBJECT of the Act?

options.A: To regulate minimum wages and overtime for all factory workers
options.B: To provide certain benefits to employees in case of sickness, maternity and employment injury, and to make provision for related matters
options.C: To establish a provident fund and pension scheme for all employees
options.D: To provide compensation to workers for accidents under the Workmen's Compensation Act

answer_html:
Answer: (B) To provide certain benefits to employees in case of sickness, maternity and employment injury, and to make provision for related matters

The ESI Act, 1948 is the FIRST MAJOR LEGISLATION on social security for employees in India, devised to provide social protection in contingencies such as illness, long-term sickness, health risks due to employment injury, or occupational hazards. The OBJECT is to provide certain benefits to employees in case of SICKNESS, MATERNITY and EMPLOYMENT INJURY and to make provision for certain other related matters.
topic_text: First Major Social Security Legislation & Object

question_html: The ESI Act, 1948 applies in the first instance to which of the following establishments?

options.A: All establishments employing 10 or more persons regardless of the nature of work
options.B: All factories (including Government factories), other than seasonal factories
options.C: Only private factories employing 20 or more persons with the aid of power
options.D: Only establishments notified by the Central Government by a gazette notification

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Only private factories employing 20 or more persons with the aid of power

Section 1: The ESI Act applies IN THE FIRST INSTANCE to ALL FACTORIES, including factories belonging to the Government, OTHER THAN SEASONAL FACTORIES. The appropriate Government may, in consultation with the Corporation (and with Central Government approval where State Government), extend provisions to any other establishment after giving ONE MONTH's notice. Once applicable, it continues even if worker numbers fall below the limit or manufacturing ceases to be carried on with power.

question_html: The Central Government has prescribed the wage limit for coverage of an employee under Section 2(9) of the ESI Act as:

options.A: Rs. 21,000 per month (excluding remuneration for overtime work)
options.B: Rs. 15,000 per month
options.C: Rs. 25,000 per month
options.D: Rs. 18,000 per month

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Rs. 21,000 per month (excluding remuneration for overtime work)

The Central Government has prescribed the WAGE LIMIT for ESI coverage at RS. 21,000 PER MONTH (excluding remuneration for overtime work). If an employee's wages exceed Rs. 21,000 at any time AFTER (and not before) the beginning of the contribution period, he shall continue to be an employee until the END OF THAT CONTRIBUTION PERIOD. An employee whose salary per day is Rs. 176 or less need not pay the EMPLOYEE'S contribution — this is paid by the Government; however, the employer must still pay the employer's share.

question_html: Once the ESI Act becomes applicable to a factory or establishment, what happens if the number of employees subsequently falls below the minimum limit?

options.A: The Act ceases to apply automatically after 6 months
options.B: The Act continues to apply notwithstanding that the number falls below the limit or manufacturing with power ceases
options.C: The employer must apply to the Corporation for deregistration
options.D: The Act ceases to apply but the Central Government may re-apply it by notification

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The Act continues to apply notwithstanding that the number falls below the limit or manufacturing with power ceases

Section 1 Proviso: A factory or establishment to which the Act applies SHALL CONTINUE TO BE GOVERNED BY THE ACT NOTWITHSTANDING that the NUMBER OF PERSONS EMPLOYED therein falls below the limit specified, or that the MANUFACTURING PROCESS CEASES TO BE CARRIED ON WITH THE AID OF POWER. This was affirmed in Kuriacose v. ESI Corporation (1988): once applicable, application is continuous.

question_html: Under Section 2(19A), a 'seasonal factory' is one exclusively engaged in which of the following manufacturing processes?

options.A: Any factory engaged in producing electronic goods for less than 6 months in a year
options.B: Any factory working less than 200 days in a year for any product
options.C: Cotton ginning, cotton or jute pressing, decortication of groundnuts, manufacture of coffee, indigo, lac, rubber, sugar or tea or incidental processes; OR engaged for not exceeding 7 months in blending, packing or repacking of tea or coffee
options.D: Any factory whose output is seasonal in nature regardless of the manufacturing process

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Cotton ginning, cotton or jute pressing, decortication of groundnuts, manufacture of coffee, indigo, lac, rubber, sugar or tea or incidental processes; OR engaged for not exceeding 7 months in blending, packing or repacking of tea or coffee

Section 2(19A): A SEASONAL FACTORY means a factory exclusively engaged in one or more of: COTTON GINNING, COTTON OR JUTE PRESSING, DECORTICATION OF GROUNDNUTS, manufacture of COFFEE, INDIGO, LAC, RUBBER, SUGAR (including gur) or TEA, or incidental processes. It also includes a factory engaged for NOT EXCEEDING SEVEN MONTHS in a year in BLENDING, PACKING OR REPACKING OF TEA OR COFFEE, or such other process as the Central Government may notify. Seasonal factories are exempt from the ESI Act's primary applicability.

question_html: Under Section 2(12) of the ESI Act, a 'factory' means any premises where a manufacturing process is being carried on and where:

options.A: Ten or more persons are employed or were employed on any day of the preceding 12 months, but does not include a mine or a railway running shed
options.B: Twenty or more persons are employed with the aid of power
options.C: Ten or more persons are employed with the aid of power only
options.D: Any number of persons are employed regardless of power usage

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Ten or more persons are employed or were employed on any day of the preceding 12 months, but does not include a mine or a railway running shed

Section 2(12): FACTORY means any premises including the precincts thereof whereon TEN OR MORE PERSONS ARE EMPLOYED OR WERE EMPLOYED ON ANY DAY OF THE PRECEDING 12 MONTHS and in any part of which a manufacturing process is being carried on or is ordinarily so carried on. It does NOT include: (a) A MINE subject to the Mines Act, 1952; or (b) a RAILWAY RUNNING SHED. IMPORTANT DEFINITIONS — SECTION 2

question_html: Under Section 2(8), 'employment injury' means a personal injury to an employee caused by accident or occupational disease arising out of and in the course of insurable employment. This definition is notable because:

options.A: It only covers accidents occurring within the territorial limits of India
options.B: It covers accidents or occupational diseases WHETHER occurring within OR outside the territorial limits of India
options.C: It only covers physical injuries, not occupational diseases
options.D: It covers only injuries sustained inside the factory premises

answer_html:
Answer: (B) It covers accidents or occupational diseases WHETHER occurring within OR outside the territorial limits of India

Section 2(8): Employment injury = a personal injury caused by ACCIDENT OR OCCUPATIONAL DISEASE arising out of and in the course of INSURABLE EMPLOYMENT, WHETHER THE ACCIDENT OCCURS OR THE OCCUPATIONAL DISEASE IS CONTRACTED WITHIN OR OUTSIDE THE TERRITORIAL LIMITS OF INDIA. The extra-territorial coverage is a critical feature — injuries sustained by insured workers even outside India are covered.

question_html: Under Section 2(9) of the ESI Act, which of the following is EXCLUDED from the definition of 'employee'?

options.A: A canteen worker employed at the factory canteen
options.B: A casual worker employed on daily rate basis
options.C: A member of the Indian naval, military or air forces
options.D: A worker whose services are temporarily lent to the principal employer

answer_html:
Answer: (C) A member of the Indian naval, military or air forces

Section 2(9): Employee EXCLUDES: (a) ANY MEMBER OF THE INDIAN NAVAL, MILITARY OR AIR FORCES; and (b) a person whose WAGES EXCEED THE PRESCRIBED LIMIT (Rs. 21,000/month). Case law includes: CANTEEN WORKERS (ESI Corp v. Shri Ram Chemical Industries, 1978), CASUAL WORKERS (AIR 1986 SC 1686), and PART-TIME EMPLOYEES (Hindu Jea Band) are all included. A PARTNER is NOT an employee (Ramanuja Match Industries). An APPRENTICE TRAINEE with a distinct purpose is also not an employee (Tata TELCO, AIR 1976 SC 66).

question_html: Under Section 2(9), an employee includes a person who is employed in or in connection with the work of a factory in which of the following categories?

options.A: (i) Directly employed by principal employer; OR (ii) employed by/through an immediate employer under supervision of principal employer; OR (iii) services temporarily lent/let on hire to principal employer
options.B: Only persons directly on the payroll of the principal employer
options.C: Only persons employed at the factory premises — not those working remotely
options.D: Only permanent employees — not contractual or temporary workers

answer_html:
Answer: (A) (i) Directly employed by principal employer; OR (ii) employed by/through an immediate employer under supervision of principal employer; OR (iii) services temporarily lent/let on hire to principal employer

Section 2(9): Three categories of employees: (i) DIRECTLY EMPLOYED by the principal employer on work of the factory/establishment (whether done in factory or elsewhere); (ii) Employed BY OR THROUGH AN IMMEDIATE EMPLOYER on the premises or under SUPERVISION of the principal employer; and (iii) Persons WHOSE SERVICES ARE TEMPORARILY LENT OR LET ON HIRE to the principal employer. All three count as employees under the Act.

question_html: Under Section 2(13), 'immediate employer' in relation to employees employed by or through him, is defined as a person who has undertaken execution of the whole or part of any work which is ordinarily part of the work of the principal employer's factory. This definition specifically includes:

options.A: Only persons directly hiring employees for administrative work at the factory
options.B: A contractor, and also a person by whom services of an employee are temporarily lent on hire to the principal employer
options.C: Only sub-contractors below the third tier
options.D: Only the managing agent of the principal employer

answer_html:
Answer: (B) A contractor, and also a person by whom services of an employee are temporarily lent on hire to the principal employer

Section 2(13): IMMEDIATE EMPLOYER means a person who has undertaken execution (on premises of the factory/establishment or under supervision of the principal employer) of the whole or any part of any work which is ordinarily part of the factory/establishment work. It INCLUDES: (a) a person by whom employee services are TEMPORARILY LENT ON HIRE to the principal employer; and (b) a CONTRACTOR. Case: ESI Corp v. T. Shankar Singh (1988) — the supplier of services is the immediate employer even if employees were employed by him.

question_html: Under Section 2(14), who is an 'insured person' under the ESI Act?

options.A: Any employee currently working in a covered factory regardless of contribution status
options.B: Only employees who have themselves paid contributions for at least 6 months
options.C: A person who IS OR WAS an employee in respect of whom contributions ARE OR WERE PAYABLE under the Act and who is thereby entitled to any of the benefits
options.D: Only the employee — not family members or dependants

answer_html:
Answer: (C) A person who IS OR WAS an employee in respect of whom contributions ARE OR WERE PAYABLE under the Act and who is thereby entitled to any of the benefits

Section 2(14): INSURED PERSON = a person who IS OR WAS an employee in respect of whom CONTRIBUTIONS ARE OR WERE PAYABLE under the Act and who is by reason thereof entitled to any of the BENEFITS provided by the Act. The definition uses the past tense ('was', 'were payable') — meaning the status can continue even after leaving employment. Medical benefits are extended even to the FAMILY of insured persons and to retired persons.

question_html: Under Section 2(22) of the ESI Act, 'wages' includes which of the following?

options.A: All remuneration paid or payable in cash including payments for periods of authorized leave, lay-off, and non-illegal strike; and additional remuneration paid at intervals not exceeding two months
options.B: Basic wages only — all allowances are excluded
options.C: Basic wages plus dearness allowance only
options.D: All remuneration including gratuity, PF contribution and travelling allowances

answer_html:
Answer: (A) All remuneration paid or payable in cash including payments for periods of authorized leave, lay-off, and non-illegal strike; and additional remuneration paid at intervals not exceeding two months

Section 2(22): WAGES = all remuneration paid or payable IN CASH if terms of employment were fulfilled, and INCLUDES payments for: authorized leave, LOCK-OUT, STRIKE (NOT ILLEGAL), LAY-OFF, and ADDITIONAL REMUNERATION paid at intervals NOT EXCEEDING TWO MONTHS. EXCLUDES: (a) PF/pension contribution; (b) travelling allowance; (c) sum for special expenses; (d) GRATUITY on discharge. Case law (SC, 1994): BONUS or ex-gratia is NOT wages. LIC premium subsidy, HRA, heat/gas/dust allowance, incentive bonus, and overtime allowance ARE treated as wages.

question_html: Under Section 2(11), the 'family' of an insured person includes which of the following persons?

options.A: Spouse; minor legitimate or adopted dependent child; child receiving education up to age 21; unmarried daughter; infirm dependent child; dependent parents (income below prescribed limit); and minor brother/sister if insured person is unmarried and parents are dead
options.B: Only the spouse and minor children below 18 years
options.C: Spouse, all children regardless of age, and all parents and siblings
options.D: Only the insured person's own parents and spouse

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Only the spouse and minor children below 18 years

Section 2(11): FAMILY includes: (a) a SPOUSE; (b) minor legitimate/adopted DEPENDENT CHILD; (c) a child RECEIVING EDUCATION up to 21 years or UNMARRIED DAUGHTER (wholly dependent); (d) INFIRM child (physical/mental abnormality) wholly dependent; (e) DEPENDENT PARENTS whose income from all sources does not exceed the prescribed limit; and (f) where the insured person is UNMARRIED and parents are NOT ALIVE, a MINOR BROTHER OR SISTER wholly dependent. The scope of 'family' for medical benefit purposes is broader than for dependants' benefit.

question_html: Under Section 2(3) of the ESI Act, 'confinement' is defined as:

options.A: Any period of hospitalisation of an insured woman during pregnancy
options.B: Only delivery of a living child at any stage of pregnancy
options.C: Labour resulting in the issue of a living child OR labour after 26 weeks of pregnancy resulting in the issue of a child, whether alive or dead
options.D: Any birth after 20 weeks of pregnancy, whether live or stillborn

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Labour resulting in the issue of a living child OR labour after 26 weeks of pregnancy resulting in the issue of a child, whether alive or dead

Section 2(3): CONFINEMENT means: (a) LABOUR RESULTING IN THE ISSUE OF A LIVING CHILD (at any gestational age); OR (b) LABOUR AFTER 26 WEEKS OF PREGNANCY resulting in the issue of a CHILD WHETHER ALIVE OR DEAD. This definition ensures that stillbirths after 26 weeks are treated as confinement for maternity benefit purposes under the ESI Act.

question_html: Under the ESI Act, which statement correctly distinguishes 'permanent partial disablement' from 'permanent total disablement'?

options.A: Permanent partial disablement reduces earning capacity in every employment; permanent total disablement incapacitates for ALL work the employee was capable of performing — the latter arises when the aggregate percentage of loss of earning capacity amounts to 100% or more
options.B: Permanent partial disablement means loss of a limb only; permanent total disablement means being bedridden
options.C: Permanent total disablement is always less severe than permanent partial disablement
options.D: Both are the same — the distinction is only relevant for compensation calculation

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Permanent partial disablement reduces earning capacity in every employment; permanent total disablement incapacitates for ALL work the employee was capable of performing — the latter arises when the aggregate percentage of loss of earning capacity amounts to 100% or more

Section 2(15A): PERMANENT PARTIAL DISABLEMENT = disablement of a permanent nature that REDUCES EARNING CAPACITY of an employee in every employment (Part II of the Second Schedule). Section 2(15B): PERMANENT TOTAL DISABLEMENT = disablement of a permanent nature that INCAPACITATES an employee for ALL WORK he was capable of performing (Part I of Second Schedule), or from a COMBINATION of Part II injuries where aggregate loss of earning capacity amounts to 100% OR MORE.

question_html: Under Section 2(6A), 'dependants' of a deceased insured person include which of the following who are entitled to dependants' benefit?

options.A: Only the widow and minor children of the deceased
options.B: Widow, legitimate/adopted son under 25, unmarried daughter, widowed mother, infirm son/daughter over 25 wholly dependent, dependent parents, minor siblings (if dependent), widowed daughter-in-law, and paternal grandparent (if no parent alive)
options.C: Only the widow and parents wholly dependent on the deceased
options.D: Only the legal heirs as determined by the personal law of the deceased

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Widow, legitimate/adopted son under 25, unmarried daughter, widowed mother, infirm son/daughter over 25 wholly dependent, dependent parents, minor siblings (if dependent), widowed daughter-in-law, and paternal grandparent (if no parent alive)

Section 2(6A): DEPENDANTS of a deceased insured person include: (i) widow, legitimate/adopted son under 25, unmarried daughter; (ii) widowed mother; (iii) infirm legitimate/adopted son/daughter over 25 (wholly dependent); (iv) if wholly or partly dependent: parent other than widowed mother, minor illegitimate/unmarried illegitimate/married minor daughter, minor brother/unmarried or widowed minor sister; (v) widowed daughter-in-law; (vi) minor child of predeceased son; (vii) minor child of predeceased daughter (no parent alive); (viii) paternal grandparent (if no parent of insured person is alive).

question_html: Under Section 2(17), who is the 'principal employer' in relation to a factory?

options.A: Only the registered owner of the factory building
options.B: The owner or occupier of the factory, including the managing agent, legal representative of deceased owner/occupier, and the person named as manager under the Factories Act
options.C: Only the Managing Director of the company
options.D: Any senior officer authorised by the Board of Directors

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Only the Managing Director of the company

Section 2(17): In relation to a FACTORY, principal employer means: the OWNER OR OCCUPIER of the factory and includes the MANAGING AGENT of such owner/occupier, the LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE OF A DECEASED owner/occupier, and where a person has been named as MANAGER of the factory under the Factories Act, 1948, THAT PERSON. For government establishments: authority appointed or the head of department. For other establishments: person responsible for supervision and control. ESI CORPORATION & GOVERNANCE — SECTIONS 3–22

question_html: Under Section 3 of the ESI Act, the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) was established with effect from which date and with what legal character?

options.A: 01.01.1948 — as a department of the Central Government
options.B: 01.10.1948 — as a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal
options.C: 15.08.1947 — as an autonomous constitutional body
options.D: 26.01.1950 — as a statutory corporation under the Constitution

answer_html:
Answer: (A) 01.01.1948 — as a department of the Central Government

Section 3: The EMPLOYEES' STATE INSURANCE CORPORATION was established with effect from 01.10.1948 (1st October 1948). The Corporation is a BODY CORPORATE having PERPETUAL SUCCESSION and a COMMON SEAL, and shall by the said name sue and be sued. All orders and decisions of the Corporation shall be authenticated by the SIGNATURE OF THE DIRECTOR GENERAL.

question_html: Under Section 4, the Constitution of the ESI Corporation includes which of the following members as ex-officio members?

options.A: The Chief Justice of India and the Labour Secretary
options.B: Three members of Parliament and the Director General of the Corporation
options.C: The Chief Ministers of all States and the Finance Minister
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General and the Attorney General

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Three members of Parliament and the Director General of the Corporation

Section 4: The Corporation shall consist of a CHAIRMAN, a VICE CHAIRMAN and other members representing the interests of employers, employees, state governments, union territories, and medical professions. THREE MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT and the DIRECTOR GENERAL OF THE CORPORATION are its EX-OFFICIO MEMBERS. The Corporation's diverse representation ensures balanced decision-making across stakeholder groups.

question_html: Under Section 8, the Standing Committee of ESIC consists of a Chairman and which other members?

options.A: Only employer and employee representatives — no parliamentary member
options.B: Only government officials and independent experts
options.C: Three Corporation members; three Corporation members representing State Governments; eight elected members (3 employer reps, 3 employee reps, 1 medical profession rep, 1 Parliament member); and the Director General (ex-officio)
options.D: Five employer representatives and five employee representatives only

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Three Corporation members; three Corporation members representing State Governments; eight elected members (3 employer reps, 3 employee reps, 1 medical profession rep, 1 Parliament member); and the Director General (ex-officio)

Section 8: STANDING COMMITTEE consists of: (i) a CHAIRMAN; (ii) 3 members of the Corporation; (iii) 3 members representing STATE GOVERNMENTS; (iv) 8 members elected by the Corporation: 3 representing EMPLOYERS, 3 representing EMPLOYEES, 1 representing MEDICAL PROFESSION, and 1 elected by PARLIAMENT; and (v) the DIRECTOR GENERAL of the Corporation, EX-OFFICIO. Total = Chairman + 14 elected/nominated + DG.

question_html: Under Section 9, the term of office of a member of the Standing Committee is:

options.A: Two years from the date on which his election is notified, and he ceases on ceasing to be a member of the Corporation
options.B: Five years from appointment
options.C: Three years from election, irrespective of membership of Corporation
options.D: Until the next general elections

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Two years from the date on which his election is notified, and he ceases on ceasing to be a member of the Corporation

Section 9: The TERM OF OFFICE of a Standing Committee member is TWO YEARS from the date on which his election is notified. A member of the Standing Committee shall CEASE TO HOLD OFFICE when he CEASES TO BE A MEMBER OF THE CORPORATION. The link between Standing Committee membership and Corporation membership ensures alignment of governance.

question_html: Under Section 10, who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Medical Benefit Council?

options.A: The Minister of Health of the Central Government
options.B: The Director General of ESI (ex-officio) as Chairman, and the Director General of Health Services (ex-officio) as Co-Chairman
options.C: The Director General of Health Services alone
options.D: The Medical Commissioner of the Corporation

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The Director General of ESI (ex-officio) as Chairman, and the Director General of Health Services (ex-officio) as Co-Chairman

Section 10: MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL consists of: (i) DIRECTOR GENERAL OF ESI — EX-OFFICIO CHAIRMAN; (ii) DIRECTOR GENERAL, HEALTH SERVICES — EX-OFFICIO CO-CHAIRMAN; (iii) Medical Commissioner of the Corporation — ex-officio; (iv) one member each representing each State (excluding UTs); (v) 3 employer reps; (vi) 3 employee reps; (vii) 3 medical profession reps (of whom ONE SHALL BE A WOMAN). Term of office for the last three categories = FOUR YEARS.

question_html: Under Section 12, a member of the Corporation, Standing Committee or Medical Benefit Council shall CEASE TO BE A MEMBER if:

options.A: He is absent from a single meeting without sufficient cause
