options.B: He is absent from a single meeting without prior notice
options.C: He fails to attend THREE CONSECUTIVE MEETINGS (restoration possible subject to government rules)
options.D: He fails to attend any two meetings in a financial year

answer_html:
Answer: (C) He fails to attend THREE CONSECUTIVE MEETINGS (restoration possible subject to government rules)

Section 12: A member shall CEASE TO BE A MEMBER if he FAILS TO ATTEND THREE CONSECUTIVE MEETINGS. However, the Corporation, the Standing Committee or the Medical Benefit Council MAY RESTORE the membership SUBJECT TO THE RULES MADE BY THE GOVERNMENT. Section 11: A member may RESIGN by notice in writing to the Central Government; his seat falls vacant on ACCEPTANCE of the resignation by the Government.

question_html: Under Section 13, which of the following is a ground for disqualification as a member of the Corporation, Standing Committee or Medical Benefit Council?

options.A: Being declared of unsound mind, being an undischarged insolvent, having a subsisting contract interest with the Corporation (other than as medical practitioner or company shareholder), or conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude
options.B: Holding a government job concurrently
options.C: Being over 70 years of age
options.D: Being a non-resident Indian

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Being declared of unsound mind, being an undischarged insolvent, having a subsisting contract interest with the Corporation (other than as medical practitioner or company shareholder), or conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude

Section 13: DISQUALIFICATION if: (a) declared to be of UNSOUND MIND by a competent court; (b) UNDISCHARGED INSOLVENT; (c) has directly or indirectly, by himself or his partner, ANY INTEREST IN A SUBSISTING CONTRACT WITH THE CORPORATION or work being done for it (EXCEPT as a medical practitioner or as a SHAREHOLDER OF A COMPANY); or (d) CONVICTED OF AN OFFENCE INVOLVING MORAL TURPITUDE (before or after commencement of the Act). ESI FUND & CONTRIBUTIONS — SECTIONS 26–45C

question_html: Under Section 26, the Employees' State Insurance Fund is held and administered by the Corporation. The Fund consists of:

options.A: Only contributions from employers and employees
options.B: Contributions under the Act AND grants, donations, and gifts from the Central Government, State Governments, local authorities, or any individual or body (incorporated or not)
options.C: Only Central Government grants and State Government subsidies
options.D: Only employer contributions — employee contributions are separate

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Contributions under the Act AND grants, donations, and gifts from the Central Government, State Governments, local authorities, or any individual or body (incorporated or not)

Section 26: The ESI FUND is held and administered by the CORPORATION. The Fund consists of: (a) ALL CONTRIBUTIONS PAID UNDER THE ACT and all other moneys received on behalf of the Corporation; and (b) GRANTS, DONATIONS AND GIFTS received from the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT, any STATE GOVERNMENT, LOCAL AUTHORITY, or any INDIVIDUAL OR BODY whether incorporated or not. The Fund is a pooled resource for all ESI expenditures.

question_html: The present rates of ESI contribution are:

options.A: 4.75% by employer and 1.75% by employee
options.B: 2.75% by employer and 1% by employee
options.C: 3.25% by employer and 0.75% by employee
options.D: 6.5% by employer and 1% by employee

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 3.25% by employer and 0.75% by employee

The PRESENT RATE of ESI contribution is: EMPLOYER = 3.25% of workers' wages; EMPLOYEE = 0.75% of workers' wages. IMPORTANT EXCEPTION: An employee whose salary per day is RS. 176 OR LESS need NOT pay the employee's contribution — it is paid by the GOVERNMENT. However, the EMPLOYER MUST STILL PAY the employer's share of contribution even in this case.

question_html: Regarding the deposit of ESI contributions online, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

options.A: Contributions can be deposited online indefinitely — there is no time limit after the contribution period ends
options.B: Nothing more than SBI can be used for payment of contribution
options.C: Contributions cannot be deposited online after 42 days from the end date of the contribution period; payment may be made at any SBI branch in cash, cheque or demand draft on generation of challan through ESIC portal
options.D: Contributions may be filed quarterly — not monthly

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Contributions can be deposited online indefinitely — there is no time limit after the contribution period ends

The employer is required to file MONTHLY CONTRIBUTIONS ONLINE through the ESIC PORTAL on a monthly basis for all registered employees. The employer files employee-wise number of days for which wages were paid and the wage amount. Contributions CANNOT BE DEPOSITED ONLINE AFTER 42 DAYS from the end date of the contribution period. Payment is made at any SBI branch in CASH, CHEQUE or DEMAND DRAFT on generation of challan, or through SBI INTERNET BANKING.

question_html: Under Section 40(1), the principal employer's obligation regarding ESI contributions is:

options.A: To pay only the employer's share — the employee must directly pay his own contribution
options.B: To pay BOTH the employer's contribution AND the employee's contribution in respect of ALL employees, whether directly employed by him OR through an immediate employer
options.C: To pay contributions only for directly employed workers — not for contractor employees
options.D: To pay contributions quarterly through the immediate employer

answer_html:
Answer: (B) To pay BOTH the employer's contribution AND the employee's contribution in respect of ALL employees, whether directly employed by him OR through an immediate employer

Section 40(1): The PRINCIPAL EMPLOYER shall PAY IN RESPECT OF ALL EMPLOYEES — whether DIRECTLY EMPLOYED BY HIM or BY OR THROUGH AN IMMEDIATE EMPLOYER — BOTH THE EMPLOYER'S CONTRIBUTION AND THE EMPLOYEE'S CONTRIBUTION. Section 40(4): Any sum DEDUCTED from wages shall be deemed to be ENTRUSTED to the principal employer by the employee for the purpose of paying the contribution. The principal employer shall bear the EXPENSES OF REMITTING contributions to the Corporation.
topic_text: Section 40 — Principal Employer: First Instance Payer

question_html: Under Section 41, after the principal employer pays ESI contributions for employees engaged through an immediate employer, the principal employer is entitled to:

options.A: Claim a tax deduction from the government for such payments
options.B: Forfeit the contributions already paid — no recovery is possible
options.C: RECOVER the amount of contribution so paid FROM THE IMMEDIATE EMPLOYER, either by deduction from any amount payable to him under any contract, or as a DEBT PAYABLE by the immediate employer
options.D: Seek direct reimbursement from the ESI Corporation

answer_html:
Answer: (C) RECOVER the amount of contribution so paid FROM THE IMMEDIATE EMPLOYER, either by deduction from any amount payable to him under any contract, or as a DEBT PAYABLE by the immediate employer

Section 41: A principal employer who has paid contribution in respect of an employee employed THROUGH AN IMMEDIATE EMPLOYER, shall be entitled to RECOVER THE AMOUNT so paid from the IMMEDIATE EMPLOYER, either: (a) by DEDUCTION FROM ANY AMOUNT PAYABLE to him by the principal employer under any contract; or (b) as a DEBT PAYABLE by the immediate employer. The immediate employer must maintain a REGISTER OF EMPLOYEES employed by or through him and submit it before settlement of any amount payable.

question_html: Under Sections 45B and 45C, how may ESI contributions in arrears be recovered?

options.A: As an arrear of land revenue; and the Recovery Officer may attach/sell moveable or immovable property, arrest the employer and detain him in prison, or appoint a receiver for his properties
options.B: Only through court proceedings with a civil suit
options.C: Only by deducting from future wage payments
options.D: Through the Central Government treasury only

answer_html:
Answer: (A) As an arrear of land revenue; and the Recovery Officer may attach/sell moveable or immovable property, arrest the employer and detain him in prison, or appoint a receiver for his properties

Section 45B: Any contribution payable may be recovered as an ARREAR OF LAND REVENUE. Section 45C: The Authorised Officer may issue a certificate to the RECOVERY OFFICER who may recover by: (a) ATTACHMENT AND SALE of moveable or immovable property of the factory/establishment or principal/immediate employer; (b) ARREST OF THE EMPLOYER and his DETENTION IN PRISON; or (c) APPOINTING A RECEIVER for management of moveable or immovable properties. Attachment first against factory/establishment properties.

question_html: Under Section 28, the ESI Fund may be expended for which of the following purposes?

options.A: Any purpose the Corporation deems fit, including investment in private companies
options.B: Payment of benefits, medical treatment, fees to members of governing bodies, salaries of Corporation officers, establishment of hospitals, and other purposes authorised by the Corporation with Central Government approval
options.C: Only for payment of direct cash benefits — not for infrastructure like hospitals
options.D: Only for administrative expenses of the Corporation

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Payment of benefits, medical treatment, fees to members of governing bodies, salaries of Corporation officers, establishment of hospitals, and other purposes authorised by the Corporation with Central Government approval

Section 28: The ESI Fund may be expended for: (i) PAYMENT OF BENEFITS and MEDICAL TREATMENT to insured persons and families; (ii) FEES AND ALLOWANCES to members of Corporation/Standing Committee/Medical Benefit Council and Regional Boards; (iii) SALARIES, GRATUITIES and PENSIONS of Corporation officers; (iv) ESTABLISHMENT OF HOSPITALS, dispensaries; (v) CONTRIBUTIONS TO STATE GOVERNMENTS, local authorities or private bodies for medical treatment costs; (vi) AUDIT COSTS; (vii) ESI Court costs; and (viii) OTHER PURPOSES authorised by the Corporation with PRIOR APPROVAL OF THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT. BENEFITS — SECTIONS 46–65

question_html: Under Section 46, insured persons and their dependants shall be entitled to which of the following benefits?

options.A: Only sickness and maternity benefits
options.B: Only medical benefits and disablement benefits
options.C: Sickness benefit, maternity benefit, disablement benefit, dependants' benefit, medical benefit, and funeral expenses
options.D: Sickness, maternity, disablement, dependants', medical, and rehabilitation benefit

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Sickness benefit, maternity benefit, disablement benefit, dependants' benefit, medical benefit, and funeral expenses

Section 46 provides SIX BENEFITS: (i) SICKNESS BENEFIT — periodical payments for sickness; (ii) MATERNITY BENEFIT — payments for confinement/miscarriage; (iii) DISABLEMENT BENEFIT — periodical payments for employment injury; (iv) DEPENDANTS' BENEFIT — periodical payments to dependants on death from employment injury; (v) MEDICAL BENEFIT — medical treatment and attendance; and (vi) FUNERAL EXPENSES — payment to eldest surviving family member (or person incurring expenses) not exceeding the prescribed amount; claim must be made within 3 MONTHS of death.

question_html: The claim for funeral expenses under Section 46 must be made within how many months of the death of the insured person?

options.A: Within 3 months of the death of the insured person (or within such extended period as the Corporation allows)
options.B: Within 6 months of death
options.C: Within 1 month of death
options.D: Within 12 months of death

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Within 3 months of the death of the insured person (or within such extended period as the Corporation allows)

Section 46: The FUNERAL EXPENSES shall be paid to the ELDEST SURVIVING MEMBER OF THE FAMILY, or where the insured person at death has NO FAMILY, to the PERSON WHO ACTUALLY INCURS THE EXPENDITURE. The amount shall not exceed such amount as may be PRESCRIBED BY THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT. The CLAIM MUST BE MADE WITHIN THREE MONTHS of the death of the insured person or such extended period as the Corporation allows.

question_html: Under Section 53, if an insured person sustains an employment injury, which of the following is CORRECT?

options.A: The insured person can claim ESI benefits AND also claim compensation under the Workmen Compensation Act from the employer
options.B: The insured person or his dependants shall NOT be entitled to receive or recover, whether from the employer or any other person, any compensation or damages under the Workmen Compensation Act, 1923 or any other law
options.C: The insured person can choose either ESI benefits or WCA compensation
options.D: The employer can offset ESI benefits against WCA compensation payable

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The insured person or his dependants shall NOT be entitled to receive or recover, whether from the employer or any other person, any compensation or damages under the Workmen Compensation Act, 1923 or any other law

Section 53: An INSURED PERSON or his DEPENDANTS shall NOT BE ENTITLED TO RECEIVE OR RECOVER — whether from the EMPLOYER or from ANY OTHER PERSON — any COMPENSATION OR DAMAGES under the Workmen Compensation Act, 1923 or any other law for the time being in force or otherwise in respect of an EMPLOYMENT INJURY sustained by the insured person. ESI benefits and WCA compensation are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — no double recovery.

question_html: Under Section 56, medical benefit may be provided in which of the following forms?

options.A: Only in-patient treatment in hospitals — no out-patient treatment
options.B: Only out-patient treatment at ESIC dispensaries
options.C: Out-patient treatment at hospital/dispensary/clinic; OR by visits to the home of the insured person; OR as in-patient treatment in a hospital
options.D: Only as medical allowance payable in cash

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Out-patient treatment at hospital/dispensary/clinic; OR by visits to the home of the insured person; OR as in-patient treatment in a hospital

Section 56: Medical benefit may be given either: (a) in the form of OUT-PATIENT TREATMENT AND ATTENDANCE in a hospital, dispensary, clinic or other institution; (b) by VISITS TO THE HOME of the insured person; or (c) as IN-PATIENT TREATMENT in a hospital or other institution. A person is entitled to medical benefit during any period for which contributions are payable, or while qualified to claim sickness/maternity benefit, or while in receipt of disablement benefit (that does not disentitle him to medical benefit).

question_html: Under Section 60 of the ESI Act, which of the following applies to ESI benefits?

options.A: The right to receive any payment or benefit under the Act shall NOT be transferable or assignable
options.B: Benefits may be assigned to a nominee with written consent
options.C: Benefits may be attached by a court for recovery of employee's debts
options.D: Benefits can be assigned to immediate family members by the insured person

answer_html:
Answer: (A) The right to receive any payment or benefit under the Act shall NOT be transferable or assignable

Section 60: The RIGHT TO RECEIVE ANY PAYMENT OR ANY BENEFIT under the ESI Act shall NOT BE TRANSFERABLE OR ASSIGNABLE. This absolute protection ensures ESI benefits reach the intended recipient (the insured person or dependant) and cannot be alienated to creditors or third parties. This provision is similar to Section 13 of the Gratuity Act and Section 10 of the EPF Act.

question_html: Under Section 65, an insured person is NOT entitled to receive which combination of benefits for the same period?

options.A: Medical benefit and sickness benefit simultaneously
options.B: Both sickness benefit and maternity benefit; OR both sickness benefit and disablement benefit for temporary disablement; OR both maternity benefit and disablement benefit for temporary disablement — for the same period
options.C: Disablement benefit and medical benefit simultaneously
options.D: Dependants' benefit and sickness benefit simultaneously

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Both sickness benefit and maternity benefit; OR both sickness benefit and disablement benefit for temporary disablement; OR both maternity benefit and disablement benefit for temporary disablement — for the same period

Section 65: An insured person shall NOT be entitled to receive for THE SAME PERIOD: (i) BOTH SICKNESS BENEFIT AND MATERNITY BENEFIT; OR (ii) BOTH SICKNESS BENEFIT AND DISABLEMENT BENEFIT FOR TEMPORARY DISABLEMENT; OR (iii) BOTH MATERNITY BENEFIT AND DISABLEMENT BENEFIT FOR TEMPORARY DISABLEMENT. Where a person is entitled to more than one such benefit, he shall be ENTITLED TO CHOOSE WHICH BENEFIT HE SHALL RECEIVE.
topic_text: Section 65 — Benefits Not to Be Combined

question_html: Under Section 70, if a person has received any benefit or payment under the ESI Act when not lawfully entitled to it, such person shall:

options.A: Be prosecuted under Section 84 only — no civil recovery is possible
options.B: Forfeit all future ESI benefits as punishment
options.C: Be liable to repay the value of the benefit or the amount of payment to the Corporation; in case of death, the representative shall repay from the assets of the deceased; recoverable as arrears of land revenue or by the Recovery Officer
options.D: Be disqualified from claiming any benefits for 5 years

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Be liable to repay the value of the benefit or the amount of payment to the Corporation; in case of death, the representative shall repay from the assets of the deceased; recoverable as arrears of land revenue or by the Recovery Officer

Section 70: Where any person has received any BENEFIT OR PAYMENT WHEN NOT LAWFULLY ENTITLED TO RECEIVE, he shall be LIABLE TO THE CORPORATION for the VALUE OF THE BENEFIT OR THE AMOUNT OF PAYMENT. In case of HIS DEATH, his REPRESENTATIVE shall be liable to REPAY from the ASSETS OF THE DECEASED, if any, in his hands. The amount is RECOVERABLE AS ARREARS OF LAND REVENUE or by the RECOVERY OFFICER.
topic_text: Section 70 — Repayment of Improperly Received Benefits

question_html: Under Section 72 of the ESI Act, which of the following actions by an employer is PROHIBITED?

options.A: Reducing the wages of any employee by reason only of the employer's liability for ESI contributions, or discontinuing/reducing benefits similar to ESI benefits under conditions of service
options.B: Paying wages in kind instead of cash
options.C: Employing employees in excess of the prescribed limit
options.D: Changing the place of employment of an insured employee without notice

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Reducing the wages of any employee by reason only of the employer's liability for ESI contributions, or discontinuing/reducing benefits similar to ESI benefits under conditions of service

Section 72: No employer, BY REASON ONLY OF HIS LIABILITY FOR ESI CONTRIBUTIONS, shall: (a) directly or indirectly REDUCE THE WAGES of any employee; or (b) (except as provided by regulations) DISCONTINUE OR REDUCE BENEFITS payable under the conditions of service which are similar to the benefits conferred by the Act. This prevents employers from shifting the financial burden of ESI contributions to employees through indirect wage reductions.
topic_text: Section 72 — Employer Not to Reduce Wages

question_html: Under Section 73, during which periods is an employer PROHIBITED from dismissing, discharging, reducing or otherwise punishing an employee?

options.A: Only during maternity leave — no restriction during sickness benefit period
options.B: During the period the employee is in receipt of SICKNESS BENEFIT, MATERNITY BENEFIT, DISABLEMENT BENEFIT FOR TEMPORARY DISABLEMENT, during medical treatment for sickness, or absent due to illness certified to arise out of pregnancy/confinement rendering the employee unfit for work
options.C: Only during hospitalisation of the employee
options.D: Only when the employee has filed a complaint before the ESI Court

answer_html:
Answer: (B) During the period the employee is in receipt of SICKNESS BENEFIT, MATERNITY BENEFIT, DISABLEMENT BENEFIT FOR TEMPORARY DISABLEMENT, during medical treatment for sickness, or absent due to illness certified to arise out of pregnancy/confinement rendering the employee unfit for work

Section 73: No employer shall DISMISS, DISCHARGE, REDUCE OR OTHERWISE PUNISH an employee during: (a) receipt of SICKNESS BENEFIT; (b) receipt of MATERNITY BENEFIT; (c) receipt of DISABLEMENT BENEFIT FOR TEMPORARY DISABLEMENT; (d) UNDER MEDICAL TREATMENT FOR SICKNESS; or (e) ABSENT DUE TO ILLNESS duly certified as arising out of PREGNANCY OR CONFINEMENT rendering the employee unfit for work. Violation of this section is a serious offence. ESI COURTS, APPEALS & PENALTIES — SECTIONS 74–86

question_html: Under Section 74, who constitutes the ESI Court?

options.A: The Central Government by a gazette notification for the entire country
options.B: The ESIC Corporation in consultation with the Director General
options.C: The STATE GOVERNMENT for such local area as may be specified in the notification
options.D: The appropriate Government in consultation with the High Court

answer_html:
Answer: (C) The STATE GOVERNMENT for such local area as may be specified in the notification

Section 74: The STATE GOVERNMENT shall constitute an ESI COURT for such LOCAL AREA as may be specified in the notification. Section 75(3): NO CIVIL COURT has jurisdiction to decide or deal with any question or dispute to be decided by the ESI Court, or to adjudicate on any liability which is to be decided by a medical board or medical appeal tribunal or ESI Court. The ESI Court has exclusive jurisdiction over specified matters.

question_html: Under Section 75, the ESI Court may decide which of the following disputes?

options.A: Whether any person is an employee; whether he is liable for employee's contribution; rate of wages; rate of contribution; person who is principal employer; right to benefit and its amount/duration; disputes between principal employer and Corporation/immediate employer/person/employee
options.B: Only wage disputes between employers and employees
options.C: Only criminal complaints by employees against employers
options.D: Only disputes about the quantum of medical benefit

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Whether any person is an employee; whether he is liable for employee's contribution; rate of wages; rate of contribution; person who is principal employer; right to benefit and its amount/duration; disputes between principal employer and Corporation/immediate employer/person/employee

Section 75: ESI Court may decide: (a) whether a person is an EMPLOYEE under the Act; (b) whether he is LIABLE FOR EMPLOYEE'S CONTRIBUTION; (c) RATE OF WAGES or average daily wages; (d) RATE OF CONTRIBUTION payable by principal employer; (e) person who is or was the PRINCIPAL EMPLOYER; (f) RIGHT TO BENEFIT and its AMOUNT AND DURATION; (g) directions on review of dependants' benefit; and (h) disputes between principal employer and Corporation/immediate employer/person/employee. CLAIMS decided by ESI Court include recovery of contributions and claims for recovery of benefits improperly received.
topic_text: Section 75 — Matters Decided by ESI Court

question_html: Under the ESI Act, an appeal from an order of the ESI Court lies to which court, and must be filed within what period?

options.A: To the Supreme Court within 90 days from the date of order
options.B: To the High Court within 60 days from the date of order of the ESI Court (only if it involves a substantial question of law)
options.C: To the District Court within 30 days from the date of order
options.D: To the Central Administrative Tribunal within 45 days

answer_html:
Answer: (B) To the High Court within 60 days from the date of order of the ESI Court (only if it involves a substantial question of law)

An appeal shall lie to the HIGH COURT from an order of the ESI Court — but ONLY IF THE ORDER INVOLVES A SUBSTANTIAL QUESTION OF LAW. The appeal shall be FILED WITHIN 60 DAYS from the date of the order of the ESI Court. Civil courts have NO JURISDICTION over matters to be decided by the ESI Court (ESI Corp v. Jalandhar Gymkhana Club, 1972). The High Court is the final appellate forum under the Act.
topic_text: Appeal from ESI Court — Period & Forum

question_html: Under Section 84, an insured person who makes a false statement or false representation to obtain a benefit not admissible under the Act is punishable with:

options.A: Imprisonment up to 1 year and fine up to Rs. 5,000
options.B: Fine up to Rs. 500 only
options.C: Imprisonment up to 6 months OR fine up to Rs. 2,000 OR both; and on conviction, the person may be disqualified from cash benefits for a prescribed period
options.D: Cancellation of ESI registration and fine of Rs. 10,000

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Imprisonment up to 6 months OR fine up to Rs. 2,000 OR both; and on conviction, the person may be disqualified from cash benefits for a prescribed period

Section 84: An INSURED PERSON who makes a WRONG/FALSE STATEMENT or representation to obtain a BENEFIT NOT ADMISSIBLE to him is punishable with IMPRISONMENT UP TO 6 MONTHS or FINE UP TO RS. 2,000 or BOTH. Additionally, if convicted, the insured person shall NOT BE ENTITLED TO ANY CASH BENEFITS available under the Act for SUCH PERIOD AS MAY BE PRESCRIBED by the Central Government. This dual penalty (criminal + loss of benefits) acts as a strong deterrent.
topic_text: Section 84 — Penalty for False Statement by Insured Person

question_html: Under Section 85(a) and 85(i), if an employer DEDUCTS employees' share of ESI contribution from wages but FAILS TO PAY it, the punishment is:

options.A: Imprisonment of 1 to 3 years AND fine of Rs. 10,000
options.B: Fine of Rs. 5,000 only
options.C: Imprisonment of 6 months and fine of Rs. 5,000 in any other case
options.D: Only a civil penalty — no criminal liability

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Imprisonment of 1 to 3 years AND fine of Rs. 10,000

Section 85(i)(a): If an employer FAILS TO PAY contributions where EMPLOYEES' SHARE HAS BEEN DEDUCTED from wages — IMPRISONMENT UP TO 3 YEARS (not less than 1 YEAR) AND FINE OF RS. 10,000. Section 85(i)(b): For any OTHER CASE of contribution default — IMPRISONMENT NOT LESS THAN 6 MONTHS AND FINE OF RS. 5,000. The mandatory minimum sentences reflect the seriousness of misappropriating deducted employee contributions.

question_html: Under Sections 85(b) to 85(g), an employer who commits any offence for non-compliance with provisions of the ESI Act (other than contribution default) is punishable with:

options.A: Imprisonment up to 1 year OR fine up to Rs. 4,000 OR both
options.B: Fine up to Rs. 10,000 only
options.C: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to Rs. 25,000
options.D: Imprisonment up to 6 months OR fine up to Rs. 1,000 OR both

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Fine up to Rs. 10,000 only

Sections 85(b) to 85(g): An employer who commits an offence for NON-COMPLIANCE with any OTHER provisions of the Act (not falling under Section 85(a)) is punishable with IMPRISONMENT UP TO 1 YEAR or FINE UP TO RS. 4,000 or BOTH. This is the general penalty for non-compliance — distinct from the harsher penalty for contribution default under Section 85(a).

question_html: Under Section 85-A, if an employer convicted of an ESI offence commits the SAME OFFENCE AGAIN, and the subsequent offence is for FAILURE TO PAY CONTRIBUTION, the punishment is:

options.A: Imprisonment of 1 to 2 years and fine of Rs. 5,000
options.B: Fine of Rs. 25,000 and cancellation of ESI registration
options.C: Imprisonment of 2 to 5 years AND fine of Rs. 25,000 for subsequent contribution failure; imprisonment up to 2 years with fine of Rs. 5,000 for any other subsequent offence
options.D: Imprisonment up to 6 months and fine up to Rs. 10,000

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Imprisonment of 2 to 5 years AND fine of Rs. 25,000 for subsequent contribution failure; imprisonment up to 2 years with fine of Rs. 5,000 for any other subsequent offence

Section 85-A: For ANY SUBSEQUENT OFFENCE after previous conviction — IMPRISONMENT UP TO 2 YEARS WITH FINE OF RS. 5,000. If the SUBSEQUENT OFFENCE IS FAILURE TO PAY CONTRIBUTION — IMPRISONMENT of 2 TO 5 YEARS (not less than 2 years) AND FINE OF RS. 25,000. The enhanced punishment regime under Section 85-A is designed to prevent repeat offenders from continuing to violate the Act's contribution payment obligations.
topic_text: Section 85-A — Enhanced Punishment After Previous Conviction

question_html: Under Section 85-B, the ESI Corporation may recover damages from an employer who fails to pay contributions within the prescribed time. What is the MAXIMUM amount of damages recoverable?

options.A: 200% of the contribution paid/payable
options.B: The amount of damages may NOT EXCEED the amount of contribution paid/payable; and a reasonable opportunity of being heard must be given before recovery
options.C: 50% of the contribution paid/payable
options.D: Three times the amount of contribution with compound interest

answer_html:
Answer: (A) 200% of the contribution paid/payable

Section 85-B: The Corporation may recover DAMAGES from an employer who FAILS TO PAY contributions within specified time or pays BELATEDLY. The AMOUNT OF DAMAGES SHALL NOT EXCEED the AMOUNT OF CONTRIBUTION PAID OR PAYABLE. Before recovering, the EMPLOYER shall be given a REASONABLE OPPORTUNITY OF BEING HEARD. For SICK INDUSTRIAL UNITS with a BIFR rehabilitation scheme (Regulation 31-C): (a) on change of management/transfer/merger with healthy company — damages can be WAIVED COMPLETELY; (b) in other cases — damages can be waived UP TO 50%.

question_html: Under Section 21, the Central Government may supersede the Corporation or the Standing Committee if:

options.A: The Corporation fails to hold its annual meeting for one year
options.B: In the opinion of the Central Government, the Corporation or Standing Committee persistently makes default in performing its duties or abuses its powers — after giving a reasonable opportunity to show cause
options.C: The Director General requests supersession due to administrative difficulties
options.D: A majority of employer representatives demand supersession

answer_html:
Answer: (B) In the opinion of the Central Government, the Corporation or Standing Committee persistently makes default in performing its duties or abuses its powers — after giving a reasonable opportunity to show cause

Section 21: If in the opinion of the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT, the Corporation or the Standing Committee PERSISTENTLY MAKES DEFAULT in performing duties imposed under the Act or ABUSES ITS POWERS, the Central Government may, by notification, SUPERSEDE THE STANDING COMMITTEE in consultation with the Standing Committee. BEFORE ISSUING THE NOTIFICATION, the Standing Committee shall be given a REASONABLE OPPORTUNITY TO SHOW CAUSE. On supersession, ALL MEMBERS shall be DEEMED TO VACATE OFFICE; a NEW STANDING COMMITTEE shall be IMMEDIATELY CONSTITUTED.

question_html: Under Section 22, the Medical Benefit Council is required to advise the Corporation and Standing Committee on which of the following matters?

options.A: Investment of the ESI Fund and administrative budgeting only
options.B: Appointment of the Director General and Standing Committee members
options.C: Administration of medical benefit, certification for grant of benefits, investigation of complaints against medical practitioners in connection with treatment/attendance, and medical treatment duties specified in regulations
options.D: Determination of the wage ceiling and contribution rates

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Administration of medical benefit, certification for grant of benefits, investigation of complaints against medical practitioners in connection with treatment/attendance, and medical treatment duties specified in regulations

Section 22: DUTIES OF THE MEDICAL BENEFIT COUNCIL: (a) TO ADVISE the Corporation and Standing Committee on matters relating to the ADMINISTRATION OF MEDICAL BENEFIT, the CERTIFICATION for purposes of grant of benefits, and other connected matters; (b) POWERS AND DUTIES OF INVESTIGATION in relation to COMPLAINTS AGAINST MEDICAL PRACTITIONERS in connection with MEDICAL TREATMENT AND ATTENDANCE; and (c) perform such other duties in connection with MEDICAL TREATMENT AND ATTENDANCE as may be specified in the regulations. CONSOLIDATED ANSWER KEY — ALL 50 QUESTIONS — END OF QUESTION PAPER — Prepared from ICMAI Study Module | Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 | Module 10 | Syllabus 2022 | CMA Inter June 2026

question_html: Under the Factories Act 1948, a premises is classified as a 'factory' when it uses power-assisted manufacturing and employs at least how many workers on any day of the preceding 12 months?

options.A: 5 or more workers
options.B: 10 or more workers
options.C: 20 or more workers
options.D: 50 or more workers

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 10 or more workers

Section 2(m): 10+ workers with aid of power; 20+ workers without power. Both thresholds are based on any day of the preceding 12 months.

question_html: In the case of a company owning a factory, who is deemed to be the 'Occupier' under Section 2(n) of the Factories Act?

options.A: The company secretary
options.B: The General Manager of the factory
options.C: Any one of the directors of the company
options.D: The Managing Director only

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Any one of the directors of the company

Section 2(n): In the case of a company, any one of the directors shall be deemed to be the occupier. The Container Corporation case confirmed a company cannot nominate other employees as occupier.

question_html: Which of the following persons is EXCLUDED from the definition of 'worker' under Section 2(l) of the Factories Act, 1948?

options.A: A person employed through a contractor
options.B: A person employed without remuneration
options.C: A member of the armed forces of the Union
options.D: A person cleaning machinery used in manufacturing

answer_html:
Answer: (C) A member of the armed forces of the Union

Section 2(l) explicitly excludes members of the armed forces of the Union. Workers employed through contractors, unpaid workers, and cleaning staff are all included.

question_html: Which of the following activities is NOT included in the definition of 'manufacturing process' under Section 2(k)?

options.A: Pumping oil or water
options.B: Preserving articles in cold storage
options.C: Retail sale of finished goods
options.D: Composing types for printing

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Retail sale of finished goods

Section 2(k) includes pumping, cold storage, printing, generating power, ship repairs, etc. Retail sale is not a manufacturing process — it involves no making, altering, treating, or adapting an article.

question_html: The Factories Act, 1948 came into effect on which date?
answer_html:
Answer: (C) 01.04.1949

The Act extends to the whole of India and came into effect from 1st April 1949. It applies to government-owned factories unless otherwise provided (Section 116).

question_html: The power to amend the First Schedule of the Factories Act by adding or removing industries listed as involving 'hazardous processes' vests with:

options.A: Central Government by Gazette notification
options.B: State Government by Gazette notification
options.C: Chief Inspector of Factories
options.D: Site Appraisal Committee

answer_html:
Answer: (B) State Government by Gazette notification

Section 2(cb): The State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, amend the First Schedule by addition, omission or variation of any industry specified therein.

question_html: How many days before occupying or using premises as a factory must the occupier send a written notice to the Chief Inspector?

options.A: 7 days
options.B: 15 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 45 days

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 15 days

Section 7: The occupier must send written notice to the Chief Inspector at least 15 days before beginning to occupy or use the premises as a factory. For a new manager appointment, the notice period to the Inspector is 7 days.

question_html: Which of the following is NOT a power of the Inspector of Factories under Section 9?

options.A: Enter any place believed to be used as a factory
options.B: Impose fines directly on the occupier
options.C: Take possession of any article for examination
options.D: Seize or take copies of any register or record

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Impose fines directly on the occupier

The Inspector can enter, inspect, seize documents, take possession of articles, and inquire into accidents. The power to impose fines is judicial and vests with the court, not the Inspector.

question_html: Who appoints the Certifying Surgeon under the Factories Act, 1948?

options.A: Central Government
options.B: Chief Inspector of Factories
options.C: State Government
options.D: Occupier of the factory

answer_html:
Answer: (C) State Government

Section 10: The State Government may appoint qualified medical practitioners as Certifying Surgeons within such local limits or for such factory or class of factories as it may assign.

question_html: A premises installs only a Computer/EDP unit and carries on no manufacturing process. Under Section 2(m), this premises is:

options.A: A factory if it employs 10+ workers
options.B: A factory if it employs 20+ workers
options.C: NOT a factory regardless of worker count
options.D: A factory only if it uses power

answer_html:
Answer: (C) NOT a factory regardless of worker count

Section 2(m) Explanation II: The mere installation of an EDP or computer unit shall not make the premises a factory if no manufacturing process is being carried on. Confirmed in Seelan Raj v. Presiding Officer (2001). HEALTH PROVISIONS – CHAPTER III

question_html: White-wash or colour-wash of interior walls and roofs of a factory must be carried out at least once in every period of:

options.A: 6 months
options.B: 12 months
options.C: 14 months
options.D: 5 years

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 14 months

Section 11: White-wash/colour-wash must be done at least once in every 14-month period. Painted/varnished surfaces require repainting once in 5 years; washable surfaces once in 6 months.

question_html: To prevent overcrowding, the Factories Act mandates a minimum of how many cubic metres of space per worker in every workroom?

options.A: 9.9 cubic metres
options.B: 14.2 cubic metres
options.C: 20.0 cubic metres
options.D: 11.5 cubic metres

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 14.2 cubic metres

Section 16: No workroom shall be overcrowded. At least 14.2 cubic metres of space must be provided for every worker employed in any workroom.

question_html: Cool drinking water during hot weather must be provided in a factory where more than how many workers are employed?

options.A: 100 workers
options.B: 150 workers
options.C: 200 workers
options.D: 250 workers

answer_html:
Answer: (D) 250 workers

Section 18: Where more than 250 workers are employed, provision shall be made for cool drinking water during hot weather. Water points must be at least 6 metres from any washing place, urinal, latrine, or open drain.

question_html: Where more than 250 workers are employed, latrines and urinals must be washed and cleaned at least once in every:

options.A: 3 days
options.B: 5 days
options.C: 7 days
options.D: 14 days

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 7 days

Section 19: Where more than 250 workers are employed, latrines and urinals shall be washed and cleaned at least once in every seven days with suitable detergents or disinfectants or both.

question_html: The floor of every workroom in a factory must be cleaned by washing with disinfectant or other effective method at least:

options.A: Once every day
options.B: Once every week
options.C: Once every fortnight
options.D: Once every month

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Once every week

Section 11: The floor of every workroom must be cleaned once in every week by washing with disinfectant or by some other effective method. Dates of such processes must be entered in the prescribed register.

question_html: Under Section 15, who has the power to make rules prescribing standards of humidification in factories?

options.A: Occupier of the factory
options.B: State Government
options.C: Central Government
options.D: Chief Inspector of Factories

answer_html:
Answer: (B) State Government

Section 15: Where humidity of air is artificially increased, the State Government may make rules prescribing standards of humidification, regulating methods used, directing prescribed tests, and prescribing methods for adequate ventilation.

question_html: Section 13 of the Factories Act requires every workroom to have adequate ventilation. In addition to ventilation, this section also mandates securing and maintaining:

options.A: Natural lighting only
options.B: Reasonable temperature conditions
options.C: Dust-free environment
options.D: Minimum floor space

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Reasonable temperature conditions

Section 13: Requires effective provision for securing adequate ventilation by circulation of fresh air AND such temperature as will secure reasonable conditions of comfort and prevent injury to health.

question_html: Under Section 14, where dust or fumes of an injurious nature are given off in the manufacturing process, the exhaust appliance shall be applied:

options.A: At the exit of the factory
options.B: As near as possible to the point of origin
options.C: At the centre of the workroom
options.D: At a height of not less than 3 metres

answer_html:
Answer: (B) As near as possible to the point of origin

Section 14: The exhaust appliance shall be applied as near as possible to the point of origin of dust, fume or other impurity, and such points shall be enclosed so far as possible. SAFETY & HAZARDOUS PROCESSES – CHAPTER IV/IVA

question_html: The Safety Committee under Section 41G of the Factories Act must be composed of:

options.A: Only management representatives
options.B: Only worker representatives
options.C: Equal numbers of workers and management representatives
options.D: Majority of government nominees

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Equal numbers of workers and management representatives

Section 41G: The occupier shall set up a Safety Committee consisting of equal numbers of representatives of workers and management to promote co-operation in maintaining proper safety and health at work.

question_html: Under Section 41C, which specific record must the occupier maintain in relation to hazardous processes?

options.A: Production records
options.B: Health records of employees
options.C: Financial accounts
options.D: Leave records

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Health records of employees

Section 41C: The occupier shall maintain health records of employees engaged in hazardous processes, and appoint experienced/qualified persons competent to supervise handling of hazardous substances within the factory.

question_html: The Site Appraisal Committee must make its recommendation to the State Government regarding a hazardous process factory application within how many days of receipt?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 90 days
options.D: 120 days

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 90 days

Chapter IVA: The Site Appraisal Committee shall examine applications for establishment of a factory involving hazardous process and make its recommendation to the State Government within 90 days of receipt of the application.

question_html: If workers have reasonable apprehension of imminent danger to their lives due to a hazardous process, under Section 41H they must:

options.A: Immediately stop work without notifying anyone
options.B: Bring it to the notice of the occupier/manager; Inspector must be informed
options.C: File a complaint in court directly
options.D: Contact the Central Government

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Bring it to the notice of the occupier/manager; Inspector must be informed

Section 41H: Workers may bring imminent danger to the notice of the occupier, agent, manager or person-in-charge. Immediate action shall be taken and a report made to the Inspector having jurisdiction.

question_html: Section 7A casts a general duty on the occupier to ensure the health, safety and welfare of all workers. The standard applied for this duty is:

options.A: Absolute liability in all cases
options.B: So far as is reasonably practicable
options.C: Best available technology standard
options.D: Cost-benefit analysis standard

answer_html:
Answer: (B) So far as is reasonably practicable

Section 7A: Uses the phrase 'so far as is reasonably practicable' as the standard of duty for the occupier in ensuring health, safety and welfare of workers while at work in the factory.

question_html: The power to fix maximum permissible threshold limits of exposure to chemical and toxic substances in any factory vests under Section 41F with:

options.A: State Government
options.B: Inspector of Factories
options.C: Central Government
options.D: Pollution Control Board

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Central Government

Section 41F: The Central Government has the power to fix maximum permissible threshold limits of exposure to chemical and toxic substances in manufacturing processes. Section 41D grants power to inquire into safety standards; 41E for emergency standards.

question_html: Which of the following is classified as a SAFETY measure (Chapter IV) and NOT a health or welfare measure?

options.A: Artificial humidification
options.B: Spittoons
options.C: Fencing of machinery
options.D: First aid appliances

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Fencing of machinery

Fencing of machinery is a safety measure under Chapter IV. Artificial humidification and spittoons are health measures (Chapter III). First aid appliances are welfare measures (Chapter V). This distinction is frequently tested. WELFARE MEASURES – CHAPTER V

question_html: A canteen is compulsorily required to be provided and maintained by the occupier when more than how many workers are employed?

options.A: 100 workers
options.B: 150 workers
options.C: 250 workers
options.D: 500 workers

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 250 workers

Section 46: If more than 250 workers are employed, a canteen or canteens shall be provided and maintained by the occupier. Expenditure on running (not foodstuffs) shall be borne by the employer.

question_html: Shelters/rest rooms and a lunch room with drinking water must be provided when more than how many workers are employed?

options.A: 100 workers
options.B: 150 workers
options.C: 250 workers
options.D: 500 workers

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 150 workers

Section 47: Adequate shelters/rest rooms and suitable lunch rooms are required when more than 150 workers are employed. These must be sufficiently lighted, ventilated and maintained in cool and clean condition.

question_html: A crèche (room for children under 6 years) is required to be provided when more than how many women workers are employed?

options.A: 15 women workers
options.B: 20 women workers
options.C: 30 women workers
options.D: 50 women workers

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 30 women workers

Section 48: If more than 30 women workers are employed, a suitable room (crèche) shall be provided for children under 6 years of age, maintained under charge of women trained in childcare.

question_html: Employment of welfare officers in a factory is mandatory when the number of workers employed is:

options.A: 150 or more
options.B: 250 or more
options.C: 500 or more
options.D: 1000 or more

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 500 or more

Section 49: If 500 or more workers are employed, the occupier shall employ welfare officers in such number as may be prescribed. Note: Safety Officers are required when 1000+ workers are employed.

question_html: Under Section 45, one first-aid box/cupboard must be provided for every how many workers at any one time in the factory?

options.A: 100 workers
options.B: 150 workers
options.C: 200 workers
options.D: 250 workers

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 150 workers

Section 45: Not less than one first-aid box or cupboard shall be provided for every 150 workers at any one time. Each box shall be in charge of a person holding a first-aid certificate recognised by the State Government.

question_html: An ambulance room with prescribed equipment and nursing staff is required to be provided when more than how many workers are employed?

options.A: 150 workers
options.B: 250 workers
options.C: 500 workers
options.D: 1000 workers

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 500 workers

Section 45: In a factory where more than 500 workers are employed, an ambulance room of the prescribed size containing prescribed equipment and nursing staff shall be provided and made readily available at all times.

question_html: Match the correct worker threshold: Safety Officers are required when workers are ___, and Welfare Officers when workers are ___.

options.A: Safety: 500; Welfare: 1000
options.B: Safety: 1000; Welfare: 500
options.C: Safety: 500; Welfare: 500
options.D: Safety: 1000; Welfare: 1000

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Safety: 1000; Welfare: 500

Safety Officers (Fill-in-blank answer from module) require 1000+ workers. Welfare Officers under Section 49 require 500+ workers. This comparison is a classic tricky distinction in CMA examinations.
topic_text: Threshold Comparison — Safety vs Welfare Officers

question_html: Regarding washing facilities under Section 42, which of the following statements is CORRECT?

options.A: Common washing facilities for all workers are sufficient
options.B: Separate and adequately screened facilities for male and female workers
options.C: Washing facilities are optional for factories with less than 250 workers
options.D: Only hot water supply is mandated

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Separate and adequately screened facilities for male and female workers

Section 42: Adequate and suitable washing facilities must be provided for all workers, with separate and adequately screened facilities for male and female workers, conveniently accessible and kept clean. WORKING HOURS & ANNUAL LEAVE – CHAPTER VI/VIII

question_html: An adult worker in a factory is not allowed to work more than ___ hours per day and ___ hours per week.

options.A: 8 hours per day; 44 hours per week
options.B: 9 hours per day; 48 hours per week
options.C: 10 hours per day; 60 hours per week
options.D: 8 hours per day; 40 hours per week

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 9 hours per day; 48 hours per week

Section 54: Maximum 9 hours per day. Section 51: Maximum 48 hours per week. Work beyond these limits attracts overtime at double the ordinary rate under Section 59.

question_html: Under Section 55, no adult worker shall be made to work for more than how many hours continuously without a rest interval of at least half an hour?

options.A: 4 hours
options.B: 5 hours
options.C: 6 hours
options.D: 8 hours

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 5 hours

Section 55: No period of work shall exceed 5 hours, and the worker shall not work for more than 5 hours before he has had an interval for rest of at least half an hour. Section 56 further limits the spread-over to 10.5 hours.

question_html: The spread over of duty of an adult worker (including rest intervals) under Section 56 shall not exceed:

options.A: 9 hours
options.B: 10 hours
options.C: 10.5 hours
options.D: 12 hours

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 10.5 hours

Section 56: The periods of work, inclusive of intervals for rest, shall not spread over more than ten and a half hours in any day. This is distinct from the 9-hour maximum working time under Section 54.

question_html: The overtime wages payable to a worker under Section 59 shall be at the rate of:

options.A: 1.5 times ordinary wages
options.B: Twice the ordinary rate of wages
options.C: Three times ordinary wages
options.D: Same as ordinary wages

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Twice the ordinary rate of wages

Section 59: Where a worker works more than 9 hours in any day or 48 hours in any week, he shall be entitled to wages at twice his ordinary rate of wages. 'Ordinary rate' includes basic wages + DA but excludes bonus and overtime wages.

question_html: To be eligible for annual leave with wages, an adult worker must have worked for at least how many days in a calendar year?

options.A: 180 days
options.B: 200 days
options.C: 240 days
options.D: 270 days

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 240 days

Section 79: A worker must have worked for a period of 240 days or more in a factory during a calendar year to be eligible for annual leave with wages. Days of lay-off, female maternity leave (up to 12 weeks), and previous year's leave count towards 240 days.

question_html: An adult worker earns annual leave at the rate of one day for every ___ days of work performed during the previous year.

options.A: 10 days
options.B: 15 days
options.C: 20 days
options.D: 25 days

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 20 days

Section 79: Adults earn 1 day leave for every 20 days worked in the previous calendar year. Children earn 1 day for every 15 days worked. This distinction between adult and child workers is frequently tested.

question_html: The maximum leave that can be carried forward to the next year for an adult worker is ___ days and for a child worker is ___ days.

options.A: Adult: 20 days; Child: 30 days
options.B: Adult: 30 days; Child: 40 days
options.C: Adult: 40 days; Child: 60 days
options.D: Adult: 15 days; Child: 20 days

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Adult: 30 days; Child: 40 days

Section 79: Total days of leave that may be carried forward shall not exceed 30 days for an adult or 40 days for a child. A worker refused leave may carry it forward without any limit.

question_html: A worker employed in a public utility service must apply for leave at least how many days before the intended date of commencement of leave?

options.A: 7 days
options.B: 15 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 45 days

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 30 days

Section 79: A worker in a public utility service must apply not less than 30 days before the intended date. For other workers, the notice period is 15 days. The leave application must be made in writing to the Manager. EMPLOYMENT OF WOMEN & YOUNG PERSONS – CHAPTER VII

question_html: Under Section 67, the minimum age below which a child is PROHIBITED from working in any factory is:

options.A: 12 years
options.B: 14 years
options.C: 15 years
options.D: 18 years

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 14 years

Section 67 expressly prohibits employment of any child who has not completed 14 years of age in any factory. A child who has completed 14 years may work only with a fitness certificate (Sections 68 & 69).

question_html: A certificate of fitness to work as an 'adult' in a factory may be granted by the Certifying Surgeon only if the young person has completed:

options.A: 14th year
options.B: 15th year
options.C: 16th year
options.D: 18th year

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 15th year

Section 69(2): (i) Certificate to work as a CHILD requires completion of 14th year; (ii) Certificate to work as an ADULT requires completion of the 15th year AND fitness for a full day's work. Certificate is valid for 12 months.

question_html: A child worker in a factory shall not be employed for more than ___ hours in any day, and not during night.

options.A: 3 hours
options.B: 4.5 hours
options.C: 6 hours
options.D: 8 hours

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 4.5 hours

Section 71: No child shall be employed for more than four and a half hours in any day, and not during night. The period shall be limited to two shifts which shall not overlap or spread over more than 5 hours each.

question_html: Under Section 66, no woman worker shall ordinarily be required or allowed to work in any factory except between the hours of:

options.A: 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.
options.B: 6 a.m. to 7 p.m.
options.C: 6 a.m. to 6 p.m.
options.D: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 6 a.m. to 7 p.m.

Section 66: Women shall not work except between 6 a.m. and 7 p.m. The State Government may authorize employment between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. in exceptional cases. No change of shifts except after a weekly or other holiday.

question_html: No female CHILD shall be allowed to work in any factory except between which hours?

options.A: 6 a.m. and 7 p.m.
options.B: 7 a.m. and 6 p.m.
options.C: 8 a.m. and 7 p.m.
options.D: 8 a.m. and 6 p.m.

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 8 a.m. and 7 p.m.

Section 71: No female child shall be allowed to work except between 8 a.m. and 7 p.m. This differs from adult women (6 a.m. to 7 p.m.) — a key distinction that is frequently tested in CMA examinations.

question_html: Under Section 81, advance payment of wages before leave begins is required when leave granted is not less than ___ days (for adults).

options.A: 2 days
options.B: 4 days
options.C: 7 days
options.D: 15 days

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 4 days

Section 81: A worker allowed leave for not less than 4 days (adult) or 5 days (child) shall, before leave begins, be paid the wages due for the entire period of leave allowed. PENALTIES & MISCELLANEOUS
topic_text: Section 81 — Advance Payment of Leave Wages

question_html: For a general contravention of the Factories Act under Section 92, the occupier/manager is punishable with imprisonment up to ___ and/or fine up to ___.

options.A: 1 year; Rs. 50,000
options.D: 6 months; Rs. 10,000

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 2 years; Rs. 1,00,000

Section 92: Punishable with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to Rs. 1,00,000 or both. Continuing contravention after conviction attracts further Rs. 1,000 per day. If an accident causing death occurs, minimum fine is Rs. 25,000.

question_html: Contravention of provisions relating to hazardous processes (Sections 41B, 41C or 41H) can attract imprisonment of up to ___ years and, if the contravention continues beyond 1 year after conviction, up to ___ years.

options.A: 2 years; 5 years
options.B: 5 years; 7 years
options.C: 7 years; 10 years
options.D: 3 years; 5 years

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 7 years; 10 years

Section 96A: Imprisonment up to 7 years with fine up to Rs. 2 lakhs for hazardous process violations, plus Rs. 5,000 per day for continuing violations. If failure continues beyond 1 year after conviction, the punishment extends to 10 years.

question_html: A worker who is discharged/dismissed or quits employment is entitled to wages in lieu of leave. Such payment must be made before the expiry of:

options.A: The same working day
options.B: The second working day from the date of discharge/dismissal/quitting
options.C: Within 7 days from the date of discharge
options.D: Within 30 days of the end of that calendar year

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The second working day from the date of discharge/dismissal/quitting

Section 79(3): Leave wages shall be paid before the expiry of the second working day from the date of discharge, dismissal or quitting. For superannuation or death, payment must be made within 2 months. ANSWER KEY — ALL 50 QUESTIONS — END OF QUESTION PAPER — Prepared from ICMAI Study Module | Factories Act, 1948 | Module 7 | Syllabus 2022

question_html: Under Section 2(20) of the Companies Act, 2013, a 'company' means a company incorporated under this Act or under any previous company law. Which of the following correctly describes the structure of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: 400 sections, five schedules, and 25 chapters
options.B: 470 sections, seven schedules, and 29 chapters — a rule-based legislation that aims to improve corporate governance, simplify regulations and strengthen minority investors
options.C: 500 sections, ten schedules, and 35 chapters
options.D: 356 sections, six schedules, and 20 chapters

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 470 sections, seven schedules, and 29 chapters — a rule-based legislation that aims to improve corporate governance, simplify regulations and strengthen minority investors

The Companies Act, 2013 is a RULE-BASED LEGISLATION comprising 470 SECTIONS and SEVEN SCHEDULES, divided into 29 CHAPTERS. It was enacted to CONSOLIDATE AND AMEND the law relating to companies previously existing under the Companies Act, 1956. It introduced new concepts like ONE PERSON COMPANY and aims to IMPROVE CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, SIMPLIFY REGULATIONS and STRENGTHEN MINORITY INVESTORS.
topic_text: Section 2(20) — Definition of Company & Act Structure

question_html: The principle of 'lifting of the corporate veil' means that courts will look behind the corporate entity and make members personally liable. In which of the following circumstances is lifting of the corporate veil JUSTIFIED?

options.A: When a company's profits fall below the industry average
options.B: When a company has too many shareholders
options.C: Where the company is used for tax evasion, to commit fraud (Jones v. Lipman), to avoid welfare legislation (Workmen v. Associated Rubber), or where the company is a mere sham (Gilford Motor v. Horne) or acts as agent of shareholders
options.D: Only when the company is in the process of winding up

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Where the company is used for tax evasion, to commit fraud (Jones v. Lipman), to avoid welfare legislation (Workmen v. Associated Rubber), or where the company is a mere sham (Gilford Motor v. Horne) or acts as agent of shareholders

LIFTING OF THE CORPORATE VEIL is justified in: (1) PROTECTION OF REVENUE — tax evasion; (2) DETERMINATION OF ENEMY CHARACTER — Daimler Co. v. Continental Tyre; (3) PREVENTION OF FRAUD — Jones v. Lipman; (4) PROTECTION OF PUBLIC POLICY; (5) COMPANY AS MERE SHAM — Gilford Motor v. Horne; (6) COMPANY AS AGENT OF SHAREHOLDERS with unlimited liability; (7) AVOIDANCE OF WELFARE LEGISLATION — Workmen of Associated Rubber v. Associated Rubber; (8) TO PUNISH FOR CONTEMPT OF COURT. The corporate veil is a privilege that must be used only for LEGITIMATE BUSINESS PURPOSES.
topic_text: Characteristics — Separate Legal Entity & Lifting of Corporate Veil

question_html: Under Section 3 of the Companies Act, 2013, how many persons are required to form the following types of companies — Public Company, Private Company, and One Person Company (OPC)?

options.A: Public Company: 7 or more; Private Company: 2 or more; OPC: 1 person
options.B: Public Company: 5 or more; Private Company: 3 or more; OPC: 2 persons
options.C: Public Company: 10 or more; Private Company: 2 or more; OPC: 1 person
options.D: Public Company: 7 or more; Private Company: 3 or more; OPC: 2 persons

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Public Company: 7 or more; Private Company: 2 or more; OPC: 1 person

Section 3(1): FORMATION requires: (a) SEVEN OR MORE PERSONS for a PUBLIC COMPANY; (b) TWO OR MORE PERSONS for a PRIVATE COMPANY; and (c) ONE PERSON for an OPC (which is a kind of PRIVATE COMPANY). All form a company by SUBSCRIBING THEIR NAMES TO A MEMORANDUM and complying with registration requirements. The minimum directors required: 3 for a public company and 2 for a private company [Section 149].
topic_text: Section 3 — Formation: Minimum Number of Persons

question_html: Under Section 2(68), a private company is defined as a company having a minimum paid-up share capital as may be prescribed, and which by its articles:

options.A: Restricts transfer of shares; limits members to 50; and prohibits public offers of any securities
options.B: RESTRICTS THE RIGHT TO TRANSFER ITS SHARES; LIMITS THE NUMBER OF ITS MEMBERS TO 200 (except OPC); and PROHIBITS ANY INVITATION TO THE PUBLIC TO SUBSCRIBE FOR ANY SECURITIES of the company
options.C: Restricts transfer of shares; limits members to 100; and prohibits listing on stock exchange
options.D: Restricts transfer of shares; limits members to 500; and prohibits issue of debentures

answer_html:
Answer: (B) RESTRICTS THE RIGHT TO TRANSFER ITS SHARES; LIMITS THE NUMBER OF ITS MEMBERS TO 200 (except OPC); and PROHIBITS ANY INVITATION TO THE PUBLIC TO SUBSCRIBE FOR ANY SECURITIES of the company

Section 2(68): A PRIVATE COMPANY must by its ARTICLES: (i) RESTRICT the right to TRANSFER ITS SHARES; (ii) LIMIT THE NUMBER OF MEMBERS TO 200 (except OPC) — joint holders counted as SINGLE MEMBER; PRESENT AND FORMER EMPLOYEES WHO ARE MEMBERS are NOT counted; (iii) PROHIBIT ANY INVITATION TO THE PUBLIC to subscribe for any securities. The MINIMUM PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL requirement was ABOLISHED by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2015. Name must end with 'PRIVATE LIMITED'.

question_html: Under Section 2(71), which of the following is an important provision regarding a subsidiary of a public company?

options.A: A subsidiary of a public company can maintain its private company status with no additional compliance requirements
options.B: A subsidiary of a public company may have fewer than 7 members if it was incorporated as a private company
options.C: A company which is a SUBSIDIARY OF A COMPANY NOT BEING A PRIVATE COMPANY shall be deemed to be a PUBLIC COMPANY for purposes of the Act even where such subsidiary company continues to be a private company in its articles
options.D: A subsidiary of a public company is exempt from the Companies Act requirements

answer_html:
Answer: (C) A company which is a SUBSIDIARY OF A COMPANY NOT BEING A PRIVATE COMPANY shall be deemed to be a PUBLIC COMPANY for purposes of the Act even where such subsidiary company continues to be a private company in its articles

Section 2(71): PUBLIC COMPANY means a company which: (a) is NOT a private company; (b) has minimum paid-up share capital as prescribed. KEY PROVISION: A company which is a SUBSIDIARY OF A COMPANY NOT BEING A PRIVATE COMPANY shall be deemed to be a PUBLIC COMPANY for purposes of the Act — EVEN WHERE SUCH SUBSIDIARY CONTINUES TO BE A PRIVATE COMPANY IN ITS ARTICLES. This prevents private companies from avoiding public company obligations by becoming subsidiaries of public companies.

question_html: Under Section 2(62) and Rule 3, which of the following is CORRECT regarding eligibility to incorporate an OPC?

options.A: Only a natural person who is an Indian citizen and RESIDENT IN INDIA (stayed in India for NOT LESS THAN 182 DAYS during immediately preceding one financial year) shall be eligible to incorporate an OPC and shall be a nominee for the sole member
options.B: Any Indian citizen, whether resident or non-resident, can incorporate an OPC
options.C: A foreign national can also incorporate an OPC if he holds a valid work permit
options.D: A company or LLP can incorporate an OPC on behalf of individual members

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only a natural person who is an Indian citizen and RESIDENT IN INDIA (stayed in India for NOT LESS THAN 182 DAYS during immediately preceding one financial year) shall be eligible to incorporate an OPC and shall be a nominee for the sole member

Rule 3: ELIGIBILITY FOR OPC: Only a NATURAL PERSON who is an INDIAN CITIZEN and RESIDENT IN INDIA shall be eligible to INCORPORATE an OPC and shall be a NOMINEE for the sole member. RESIDENT IN INDIA = a person who has stayed in India for NOT LESS THAN 182 DAYS during the IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING ONE FINANCIAL YEAR. Additional OPC conditions: No person can incorporate MORE THAN ONE OPC or be nominee in MORE THAN ONE OPC; NO MINOR as member or nominee; Cannot carry on NBFC activities; Cannot convert voluntarily for first 2 years (unless threshold exceeded).

question_html: Under Rule 6, an OPC is mandatorily required to convert into a private or public company when:

options.A: The number of employees exceeds 50 persons
options.B: Paid-up share capital EXCEEDS Rs. 50 LAKHS OR average annual turnover EXCEEDS Rs. 2 CRORES — within 6 months into a public company (7+ members) or private company (2+ members); notice to Registrar in Form INC-5 within 60 days
options.C: When the company completes 5 years from date of incorporation
options.D: When the OPC decides to make a public issue of shares

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Paid-up share capital EXCEEDS Rs. 50 LAKHS OR average annual turnover EXCEEDS Rs. 2 CRORES — within 6 months into a public company (7+ members) or private company (2+ members); notice to Registrar in Form INC-5 within 60 days

Rule 6: OPC MANDATORY CONVERSION: When PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL EXCEEDS RS. 50 LAKHS or AVERAGE ANNUAL TURNOVER EXCEEDS RS. 2 CRORES — the OPC ceases to be entitled to continue as OPC and must CONVERT WITHIN 6 MONTHS into: (a) PUBLIC LIMITED COMPANY with at least 7 members; or (b) PRIVATE COMPANY with minimum 2 members. Notice to Registrar in FORM INC-5 within 60 DAYS from applicability. Penalty for contravention: Fine up to Rs. 10,000 + Rs. 1,000 per day of continuing offence.

question_html: Under Section 2(85) (as amended w.e.f. 01.04.2021), a 'small company' is a company whose:

options.A: Paid-up capital does not exceed Rs. 50 lakhs AND turnover does not exceed Rs. 10 crores
options.B: Paid-up capital does not exceed Rs. 1 crore AND turnover does not exceed Rs. 10 crores
options.C: PAID-UP CAPITAL DOES NOT EXCEED RS. 2 CRORES AND TURNOVER DOES NOT EXCEED RS. 20 CRORES — but excludes public company, holding company, subsidiary company, Section 8 company, and company governed by any special act
options.D: Paid-up capital does not exceed Rs. 5 crores AND turnover does not exceed Rs. 50 crores

answer_html:
Answer: (C) PAID-UP CAPITAL DOES NOT EXCEED RS. 2 CRORES AND TURNOVER DOES NOT EXCEED RS. 20 CRORES — but excludes public company, holding company, subsidiary company, Section 8 company, and company governed by any special act

Section 2(85) (Amendment w.e.f. 01.04.2021): SMALL COMPANY = paid-up capital NOT EXCEEDING RS. 2 CRORES AND turnover NOT EXCEEDING RS. 20 CRORES. NOT ELIGIBLE TO BE SMALL COMPANY: (1) A PUBLIC COMPANY; (2) A HOLDING COMPANY; (3) A SUBSIDIARY COMPANY; (4) COMPANY REGISTERED UNDER SECTION 8; (5) A COMPANY GOVERNED BY ANY SPECIAL ACT. Small companies file Annual Return in new e-Form MGT-7A within 60 days from AGM.

question_html: Under Section 2(45), a 'Government company' means a company in which not less than what percentage of the paid-up share capital is held by the Central Government, State Government(s), or partly by both?

options.A: At least 51 per cent. of the paid-up share capital — and includes a subsidiary of such a Government company
options.B: At least 26 per cent. of the paid-up share capital
options.C: At least 74 per cent. of the paid-up share capital
options.D: 100 per cent. of the paid-up share capital — only fully government-owned companies qualify

answer_html:
Answer: (A) At least 51 per cent. of the paid-up share capital — and includes a subsidiary of such a Government company

Section 2(45): GOVERNMENT COMPANY = any company in which NOT LESS THAN 51 PER CENT. of the PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL is held by: (a) CENTRAL GOVERNMENT; OR (b) STATE GOVERNMENT(S); OR (c) PARTLY BY CENTRAL GOVERNMENT AND PARTLY BY ONE OR MORE STATE GOVERNMENTS. INCLUDES a company which is a SUBSIDIARY of such a Government company. Case: Heavy Engineering Mazdoor Union v. State of Bihar (SC): employees of a Govt. company are NOT employees of the Central or State Government. A Govt. company is NOT a department of the Government.

question_html: Under Section 2(42), a 'foreign company' means any company or body corporate incorporated OUTSIDE INDIA which:

options.A: Only a company incorporated abroad and having 100% foreign ownership qualifies as a foreign company
options.B: Has a PLACE OF BUSINESS IN INDIA (by itself or through agent, physically or through electronic mode) AND conducts any business activity in India in any other manner
options.C: Any company incorporated outside India regardless of whether it has any business activity in India
options.D: A company incorporated outside India but having majority Indian shareholders

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Has a PLACE OF BUSINESS IN INDIA (by itself or through agent, physically or through electronic mode) AND conducts any business activity in India in any other manner

Section 2(42): FOREIGN COMPANY = company or body corporate INCORPORATED OUTSIDE INDIA which: (a) HAS A PLACE OF BUSINESS IN INDIA (whether by itself or through an agent, PHYSICALLY OR THROUGH ELECTRONIC MODE); AND (b) CONDUCTS ANY BUSINESS ACTIVITY IN INDIA in any other manner. KEY: Having a SHARE TRANSFER/REGISTRATION OFFICE = place of business. But MERE HOLDING OF PROPERTY is NOT a place of business. A company incorporated in India with all foreign shareholders = INDIAN COMPANY, not a foreign company. Section 379: If 50%+ paid-up capital held by Indian citizens/Indian companies, additional compliance required.

question_html: Under Section 2(87), a 'subsidiary company' is a company in which the HOLDING COMPANY:

options.A: Holds only preference shares in excess of 25%
options.B: Holds a minority stake of at least 26% of equity shares
options.C: (i) CONTROLS THE COMPOSITION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS (power to appoint/remove all or a majority of directors); OR (ii) EXERCISES OR CONTROLS MORE THAN ONE-HALF OF THE TOTAL SHARE CAPITAL either at its own or together with one or more subsidiary companies
options.D: Provides management services or financial assistance to the other company

answer_html:
Answer: (C) (i) CONTROLS THE COMPOSITION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS (power to appoint/remove all or a majority of directors); OR (ii) EXERCISES OR CONTROLS MORE THAN ONE-HALF OF THE TOTAL SHARE CAPITAL either at its own or together with one or more subsidiary companies

Section 2(87): SUBSIDIARY COMPANY = a company in which the HOLDING COMPANY: (i) CONTROLS THE COMPOSITION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS — can appoint/remove ALL OR MAJORITY of directors at its discretion; OR (ii) EXERCISES OR CONTROLS MORE THAN ONE-HALF OF THE TOTAL SHARE CAPITAL either alone or with its subsidiaries. Section 2(6): ASSOCIATE COMPANY = company in which another company has SIGNIFICANT INFLUENCE (at least 20% of total share capital or business decisions under agreement) but is NOT a subsidiary. A joint venture is included as an associate company.

question_html: Under Section 8, the Central Government may license a company to be registered WITHOUT the word 'LIMITED' or 'PRIVATE LIMITED' in its name if it has objects for:

options.A: Any commercial activity with intention to distribute profits to members
options.B: Promotion of COMMERCE, ART, SCIENCE, SPORTS, EDUCATION, RESEARCH, SOCIAL WELFARE, RELIGION, CHARITY, or PROTECTION OF ENVIRONMENT — and intends to apply profits in promoting its objects and prohibit payment of any dividend to members
options.C: Only educational activities conducted by the government
options.D: Any charitable activity that is approved by the Income Tax authorities

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Any commercial activity with intention to distribute profits to members

Section 8: LICENCE for company WITHOUT 'LIMITED' or 'PRIVATE LIMITED': Central Government grants if: (a) Objects include PROMOTION OF COMMERCE, ART, SCIENCE, SPORTS, EDUCATION, RESEARCH, SOCIAL WELFARE, RELIGION, CHARITY, PROTECTION OF ENVIRONMENT; (b) INTENDS TO APPLY PROFITS in promoting its objects; (c) PROHIBITS PAYMENT OF ANY DIVIDEND to members. PUNISHMENT for default: Fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 10 LAKHS up to RS. 1 CRORE; Officers: imprisonment up to 3 YEARS or fine Rs. 25,000 to RS. 25 LAKHS or BOTH. Alteration of MOA/AOA requires PRIOR APPROVAL OF CENTRAL GOVERNMENT. MEMORANDUM OF ASSOCIATION — SECTIONS 4, 6, 13
topic_text: Section 8 — Companies Not for Profit (Section 8 Companies)

question_html: Under Section 4(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, the Memorandum of a limited company must contain which of the following clauses?

options.A: Name clause, object clause, liability clause, capital clause, directors clause, and auditors clause
options.B: NAME CLAUSE ('Limited'/'Private Limited'); SITUATION CLAUSE (State of registered office); OBJECTS CLAUSE (objects of proposed company); LIABILITY CLAUSE (limited or unlimited); CAPITAL CLAUSE (share capital and division); and for OPC — NOMINEE CLAUSE
options.C: Name clause, object clause, subscribers clause, capital clause, directors clause, and nominee clause
options.D: Name clause, registered office clause, objects clause, shareholders rights clause, capital clause, and audit clause

answer_html:
Answer: (B) NAME CLAUSE ('Limited'/'Private Limited'); SITUATION CLAUSE (State of registered office); OBJECTS CLAUSE (objects of proposed company); LIABILITY CLAUSE (limited or unlimited); CAPITAL CLAUSE (share capital and division); and for OPC — NOMINEE CLAUSE

Section 4(1): SIX CLAUSES of MOA: (a) NAME CLAUSE — 'Limited' as last word for public; 'Private Limited' for private (not applicable to Section 8 companies); (b) SITUATION CLAUSE — State where registered office is situated; (c) OBJECTS CLAUSE — objects for which company is proposed to be incorporated; (d) LIABILITY CLAUSE — whether limited/unlimited; for shares/guarantee specifics; (e) CAPITAL CLAUSE — amount of share capital, division into shares, subscribers' shares; (f) NOMINEE CLAUSE — for OPC only, name of person who becomes member on death/incapacity.

question_html: As per Section 4(6), the Memorandum of a company shall be in the form specified in the Tables of Schedule I. For a company limited by SHARES, the applicable Table is:

options.A: Table B — Memorandum of company limited by guarantee without share capital
options.B: Table C — Memorandum of company limited by guarantee with share capital
options.C: Table A — Memorandum of company limited by shares
options.D: Table D — Memorandum of unlimited company without share capital

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Table A — Memorandum of company limited by shares

Section 4(6): FORMS OF MOA in SCHEDULE I: TABLE A = Company LIMITED BY SHARES; TABLE B = Company LIMITED BY GUARANTEE (no share capital); TABLE C = Company LIMITED BY GUARANTEE (with share capital); TABLE D = UNLIMITED COMPANY (no share capital); TABLE E = UNLIMITED COMPANY (with share capital). For Articles of Association: TABLE F = Limited by shares; G, H, I, J for other types. These forms provide the prescribed format for drafting MOA and AOA.
topic_text: Section 4(6) — Forms of MOA in Schedule I

question_html: The doctrine of ultra vires, as applied to companies, means that any act done by a company which is beyond the powers in its Memorandum is:

options.A: WHOLLY VOID AND INOPERATIVE IN LAW — not binding on the company; cannot be ratified even by all shareholders; the company can be restrained from employing funds for purposes not sanctioned by the memorandum (Ashbury Railway Company v. Riche)
options.B: Voidable at the option of the company
options.C: Valid if subsequently ratified by shareholders in a general meeting
options.D: Invalid only if the third party had notice of the company's memorandum

answer_html:
Answer: (A) WHOLLY VOID AND INOPERATIVE IN LAW — not binding on the company; cannot be ratified even by all shareholders; the company can be restrained from employing funds for purposes not sanctioned by the memorandum (Ashbury Railway Company v. Riche)

DOCTRINE OF ULTRA VIRES [Ashbury Railway Company Ltd. v. Riche]: Any act done or contract made by a company that TRAVELS BEYOND THE POWERS NOT ONLY OF THE DIRECTORS BUT ALSO OF THE COMPANY is WHOLLY VOID AND INOPERATIVE IN LAW. It is NOT BINDING ON THE COMPANY. It CANNOT BE RATIFIED by the shareholders. The company can be RESTRAINED from employing funds for other purposes. However: (a) If ultra vires the DIRECTORS only — shareholders can RATIFY; (b) If ultra vires the ARTICLES — company can ALTER the articles; (c) If DONE IRREGULARLY — shareholders can validate. The MEMORANDUM is a PUBLIC DOCUMENT — persons dealing with company are DEEMED TO KNOW the company's powers.
topic_text: Doctrine of Ultra Vires — Ashbury Railway Case
