question_html: Section 6 of the Companies Act, 2013 provides that the provisions of the Act shall have effect NOTWITHSTANDING anything to the contrary in the MOA, AOA, or any agreement or resolution. This means:

options.A: Companies can override Act provisions by passing a special resolution
options.B: Any provision in the MOA, AOA, agreement or resolution which is REPUGNANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE ACT shall, to the extent of such repugnancy, become or be VOID
options.C: The MOA and AOA always prevail over any provisions of the Companies Act
options.D: The Act overrides only MOA provisions but not AOA provisions

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Any provision in the MOA, AOA, agreement or resolution which is REPUGNANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE ACT shall, to the extent of such repugnancy, become or be VOID

Section 6: The COMPANIES ACT, 2013 SHALL HAVE EFFECT NOTWITHSTANDING anything to the contrary in: (a) MEMORANDUM or ARTICLES of a company; (b) any AGREEMENT EXECUTED by it; or (c) any RESOLUTION passed by the company in general meeting or by the Board of Directors — whether registered, executed or passed before or after commencement of the Act. Any provision in the memorandum, articles, agreement or resolution shall, to the extent it is REPUGNANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE ACT, become or be VOID.
topic_text: Section 6 — Act Overrides Memorandum and Articles

question_html: Under Section 10 of the Companies Act, 2013, once the memorandum and articles are registered, they:

options.A: Bind only the directors and officers of the company
options.B: Bind only the company in its dealings with third parties
options.C: BIND THE COMPANY AND THE MEMBERS thereof to the SAME EXTENT as if they had respectively been SIGNED BY THE COMPANY AND BY EACH MEMBER and contained covenants on their part to observe all provisions; all monies payable by any member under MOA/AOA shall be a DEBT DUE FROM HIM TO THE COMPANY
options.D: Bind only the members who signed the memorandum as original subscribers

answer_html:
Answer: (C) BIND THE COMPANY AND THE MEMBERS thereof to the SAME EXTENT as if they had respectively been SIGNED BY THE COMPANY AND BY EACH MEMBER and contained covenants on their part to observe all provisions; all monies payable by any member under MOA/AOA shall be a DEBT DUE FROM HIM TO THE COMPANY

Section 10: Once MOA and AOA are REGISTERED, they shall BIND THE COMPANY AND THE MEMBERS to the SAME EXTENT as if: (a) SIGNED BY THE COMPANY AND BY EACH MEMBER; and (b) contained COVENANTS on their part to observe ALL PROVISIONS of the memorandum and the articles. All MONIES PAYABLE BY ANY MEMBER to the company under the memorandum or articles shall be a DEBT DUE FROM HIM TO THE COMPANY. This statutory contract (Sec.10) is enforceable by the company against members and vice-versa, but is limited to MEMBERSHIP RIGHTS — not external contracts.
topic_text: Section 10 — Effect of MOA and Articles as Contracts

question_html: Under Section 13 of the Companies Act, 2013, any change in the NAME of a company requires:

options.A: An ordinary resolution passed at an extraordinary general meeting
options.B: Approval of the Central Government in writing AND a special resolution — except where only the word 'Private' is added or deleted consequent on conversion between classes
options.C: Only a board resolution and notification to the Registrar
options.D: Court order plus shareholder approval by special resolution

answer_html:
Answer: (A) An ordinary resolution passed at an extraordinary general meeting

Section 13: ALTERATION OF MOA generally requires a SPECIAL RESOLUTION. Specifically for NAME CHANGE: (a) Requires APPROVAL OF CENTRAL GOVERNMENT IN WRITING; (b) No such approval necessary where ONLY DELETION OR ADDITION OF THE WORD 'PRIVATE' consequent on conversion between private and public company. On name change: Registrar enters new name and issues FRESH CERTIFICATE OF INCORPORATION — change is complete only on ISSUE OF SUCH CERTIFICATE. A company with defaulted annual returns/financial statements or with matured deposit defaults CANNOT change name [Rule 29].
topic_text: Section 13 — Alteration of MOA: Name Change

question_html: Under Section 13, shifting of registered office from one STATE to another requires approval from which authority, and what is the time limit for disposal?

options.A: Registrar of Companies — within 30 days
options.B: CENTRAL GOVERNMENT — within 60 DAYS; before approving, the CG may satisfy itself that alteration has consent of creditors/debenture holders or adequate provision has been made for discharge of all debts
options.C: National Company Law Tribunal — within 30 days
options.D: Both the Registrar of Companies and the NCLT — within 60 days

answer_html:
Answer: (B) CENTRAL GOVERNMENT — within 60 DAYS; before approving, the CG may satisfy itself that alteration has consent of creditors/debenture holders or adequate provision has been made for discharge of all debts

Section 13: CHANGE OF REGISTERED OFFICE ACROSS STATES: Requires approval of the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT (in prescribed form). DISPOSAL WITHIN 60 DAYS. Before approving, CG may satisfy that: (a) ALTERATION HAS CONSENT OF CREDITORS, DEBENTURE-HOLDERS AND OTHER PERSONS CONCERNED; OR (b) SUFFICIENT PROVISION HAS BEEN MADE for DISCHARGE OF ALL DEBTS AND OBLIGATIONS or adequate security has been provided. After approval: CERTIFIED COPY of order filed with Registrar of EACH STATE; Registrar of new state issues FRESH CERTIFICATE OF INCORPORATION.
topic_text: Section 13 — Change of Registered Office Across States

question_html: Under Section 13, a company which has raised money from public through prospectus and still has any UNUTILISED AMOUNT shall not change its objects UNLESS:

options.A: Approved by the board of directors by passing an ordinary resolution
options.B: Approved by a special resolution passed by the majority of shareholders in general meeting
options.C: A SPECIAL RESOLUTION IS PASSED THROUGH POSTAL BALLOT; details published in newspapers (English + vernacular); placed on website; and DISSENTING SHAREHOLDERS are given an opportunity to EXIT by the promoters and shareholders having control as per SEBI regulations
options.D: Prior approval of SEBI obtained and majority shareholders vote in favour

answer_html:
Answer: (C) A SPECIAL RESOLUTION IS PASSED THROUGH POSTAL BALLOT; details published in newspapers (English + vernacular); placed on website; and DISSENTING SHAREHOLDERS are given an opportunity to EXIT by the promoters and shareholders having control as per SEBI regulations

Section 13: CHANGE OF OBJECTS (with unutilised public funds): A company that raised money from public via prospectus and has UNUTILISED AMOUNT shall not change objects unless: (1) SPECIAL RESOLUTION THROUGH POSTAL BALLOT is passed; (2) DETAILS published in ENGLISH + VERNACULAR NEWSPAPERS at place of registered office AND placed on COMPANY WEBSITE with justification; (3) DISSENTING SHAREHOLDERS given opportunity to EXIT by PROMOTERS AND CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS per SEBI regulations. Registrar shall register and certify within 30 days of filing the special resolution.
topic_text: Section 13 — Change of Objects with Unutilised Public Funds

question_html: Under Section 16(1), the Central Government may direct a company to CHANGE ITS NAME within what period if it is registered by a name too nearly resembling an existing company's name or a registered trademark?

options.A: For resemblance with existing company name: 3 months by ordinary resolution; for trade mark conflict: 6 months by ordinary resolution — trademark application must be made within 3 years of incorporation/name change
options.B: For resemblance with existing company name: 6 months; for trade mark conflict: 1 year
options.C: Both cases: 3 months by special resolution
options.D: Both cases: 1 year by special resolution

answer_html:
Answer: (A) For resemblance with existing company name: 3 months by ordinary resolution; for trade mark conflict: 6 months by ordinary resolution — trademark application must be made within 3 years of incorporation/name change

Section 16(1): RECTIFICATION OF NAME: (1) If name RESEMBLES EXISTING COMPANY NAME — Central Government directs change within 3 MONTHS from issue of direction (by ORDINARY RESOLUTION); (2) If name RESEMBLES REGISTERED TRADE MARK — application by registered proprietor within 3 YEARS of incorporation/registration/change; CG may direct change within 6 MONTHS from direction (by ORDINARY RESOLUTION). Section 16(2): Company shall WITHIN 15 DAYS of such change give notice to Registrar. Section 16(3): Punishment for non-compliance.

question_html: Under Section 17, within what time must a company send a copy of its MOA, AOA or resolutions to a member upon request?

options.A: Within 15 days of the request
options.B: WITHIN 7 DAYS of the request on payment of fee — penalty for default: Rs. 1,000 per day or Rs. 1 lakh (whichever is less) for the company and every defaulting officer
options.C: Within 30 days of the request
options.D: Within 21 days of the request on payment of fee

answer_html:
Answer: (B) WITHIN 7 DAYS of the request on payment of fee — penalty for default: Rs. 1,000 per day or Rs. 1 lakh (whichever is less) for the company and every defaulting officer

Section 17(1) with Rule 34: On payment of fee, a company shall send to a member WITHIN 7 DAYS of the request: (a) the MEMORANDUM; (b) the ARTICLES; (c) every AGREEMENT AND RESOLUTION not embodied in the MOA/AOA. Section 17(2): Penalty for default = the company and every defaulting officer liable for EACH DEFAULT to a penalty of RS. 1,000 FOR EACH DAY during which the default continues OR RS. 1 LAKH — whichever is LESS. ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION — SECTION 5, 14, 15
topic_text: Section 17 — Copy of Documents to Members

question_html: Section 5 of the Companies Act, 2013 provides that the articles of a company shall contain REGULATIONS FOR MANAGEMENT of the company. Which table of Schedule I provides matters for a company LIMITED BY SHARES?

options.A: Table A contains regulations for a company limited by shares
options.B: Table F contains the matters that shall be contained in the Articles of a company LIMITED BY SHARES
options.C: Table B contains regulations for a company limited by shares
options.D: Table G contains Articles for a company limited by shares

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Table B contains regulations for a company limited by shares

Section 5 / Schedule I: TABLE F provides matters for ARTICLES OF A COMPANY LIMITED BY SHARES including: interpretation, share capital and variation of rights, lien, calls on shares, transfer/transmission/forfeiture of shares, alteration of capital, capitalisation of profits, buy-back, general meetings, proceedings, voting rights, proxy, Board of Directors, Board proceedings, CEO/Manager/CS/CFO, Seal (now OPTIONAL), dividends, accounts, winding up, indemnity. For other types: Table G (guarantee + share capital), Table H (guarantee, no share capital), Table I (unlimited + share capital), Table J (unlimited, no share capital).

question_html: Under Section 14, a company may alter its Articles of Association by passing a SPECIAL RESOLUTION. Which of the following is the CORRECT rule about conversion of a public company into a private company through AOA alteration?

options.A: Conversion of public to private company requires only a board resolution and Registrar approval
options.B: Conversion of private to public requires court approval; conversion of public to private is free
options.C: Conversion of private into public does not require any special approval; but alteration having effect of CONVERSION OF A PUBLIC COMPANY INTO A PRIVATE COMPANY shall NOT take effect EXCEPT WITH APPROVAL OF THE TRIBUNAL — copy of order filed with Registrar in Form INC-27 within 15 days
options.D: All conversions require Central Government approval regardless of direction

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Conversion of public to private company requires only a board resolution and Registrar approval

Section 14: ALTERATION OF ARTICLES by SPECIAL RESOLUTION. KEY RULES: (1) PRIVATE TO PUBLIC: If articles altered so they no longer contain required restrictions — company CEASES TO BE PRIVATE from the date of such alteration; (2) PUBLIC TO PRIVATE: ALTERATION HAS NO EFFECT EXCEPT WITH APPROVAL OF THE TRIBUNAL. Copy of Tribunal order filed with Registrar in FORM INC-27 (with printed altered articles) within 15 DAYS of receipt of order. Application for conversion filed in Form INC-27. Any such alteration shall be VALID AS IF ORIGINALLY IN THE ARTICLES.

question_html: Under Section 15, every alteration made in the MOA or AOA shall be noted in every copy. What is the penalty for issuing a copy WITHOUT the alteration?

options.A: Rs. 10,000 per copy issued without alteration
options.B: Rs. 500 per copy issued without alteration
options.C: Rs. 100 per copy issued without alteration
options.D: Rs. 1,000 per copy of the memorandum or articles issued without such alteration — the company and every defaulting officer are liable

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Rs. 500 per copy issued without alteration

Section 15: Every ALTERATION in MOA or AOA shall be NOTED IN EVERY COPY of the MOA/AOA. PENALTY for non-compliance: The COMPANY AND EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER shall be liable to a PENALTY OF RS. 1,000 FOR EVERY COPY of the memorandum or articles issued WITHOUT SUCH ALTERATION. This ensures all copies of the constitutional documents reflect the current position of the company.
topic_text: Section 15 — Alteration to be Noted in Every Copy

question_html: With respect to the Common Seal of a company, which of the following correctly states the position after the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2015?

options.A: Common seal remains mandatory for all documents including share certificates
options.B: Common seal is mandatory only for public companies — private companies can opt out
options.C: USE OF COMMON SEAL HAS BEEN MADE OPTIONAL as per the 2015 Amendment — documents that previously required affixing of common seal may now instead be SIGNED BY TWO DIRECTORS or ONE DIRECTOR AND A COMPANY SECRETARY of the company
options.D: Common seal is mandatory for bills of exchange and share certificates only

answer_html:
Answer: (C) USE OF COMMON SEAL HAS BEEN MADE OPTIONAL as per the 2015 Amendment — documents that previously required affixing of common seal may now instead be SIGNED BY TWO DIRECTORS or ONE DIRECTOR AND A COMPANY SECRETARY of the company

Section 5 / 2015 Amendment: The USE OF COMMON SEAL HAS BEEN MADE OPTIONAL by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2015. The Companies Act, 2013 originally required common seal on certain documents (bills of exchange, share certificates, etc.). Now, ALL such documents which required common seal may instead be SIGNED BY TWO DIRECTORS or ONE DIRECTOR AND A COMPANY SECRETARY. For an OPC without common seal, the share certificate shall be signed by one director or authorised person and the Company Secretary.

question_html: Under Rule 13, how must the Memorandum and Articles be signed when the SUBSCRIBER IS A BODY CORPORATE?

options.A: By any two directors of the body corporate
options.B: By a director, officer or employee of the body corporate duly authorised by a BOARD RESOLUTION — such person shall NOT simultaneously be a subscriber to the MOA
options.C: By the Chairman of the Board of Directors only
options.D: By the Company Secretary of the body corporate

answer_html:
Answer: (A) By any two directors of the body corporate

Rule 13: SIGNING OF MOA AND AOA: For a BODY CORPORATE SUBSCRIBER — signed by DIRECTOR, OFFICER OR EMPLOYEE of the body corporate DULY AUTHORIZED BY A BOARD RESOLUTION. If the SUBSCRIBER IS AN LLP — signed by a PARTNER authorized by a RESOLUTION APPROVED BY ALL PARTNERS. KEY: IN EITHER CASE, the person so authorised shall NOT, AT THE SAME TIME, BE A SUBSCRIBER to the MOA/AOA. For ILLITERATE SUBSCRIBER — thumb impression, described as such by person writing for him; contents to be read and explained to subscriber. INCORPORATION PROCEDURE — SECTIONS 7, 10A

question_html: Under Section 7, the promoter shall submit which of the following documents to the Registrar of Companies for registration of a company?

options.A: Only MOA and AOA signed by subscribers
options.B: MEMORANDUM AND ARTICLES signed by all subscribers; DECLARATION by an Advocate/CA/CMA/CS and person named as director/manager/secretary; DECLARATION from each SUBSCRIBER and FIRST DIRECTOR in Form INC-9; address for correspondence; particulars of every subscriber; particulars of first directors; and CONSENT TO ACT AS DIRECTORS
options.C: Only MOA, AOA and consent to act as directors
options.D: MOA, AOA, board resolution and declaration by subscribers only

answer_html:
Answer: (B) MEMORANDUM AND ARTICLES signed by all subscribers; DECLARATION by an Advocate/CA/CMA/CS and person named as director/manager/secretary; DECLARATION from each SUBSCRIBER and FIRST DIRECTOR in Form INC-9; address for correspondence; particulars of every subscriber; particulars of first directors; and CONSENT TO ACT AS DIRECTORS

Section 7: Documents for REGISTRATION: (a) MOA AND AOA signed by all subscribers; (b) DECLARATION by Advocate/CA/COST ACCOUNTANT/CS (engaged in formation) and person named as director/manager/secretary — confirming compliance; (c) DECLARATION from each subscriber and first director in FORM INC-9 stating: (i) not convicted of any offence in connection with promotion/formation/management of any company; (ii) not found guilty of fraud/misfeasance/breach of duty in last 5 years; (iii) documents filed are correct/complete; (d) Address for correspondence; (e) Particulars of every subscriber with identity proof; (f) Particulars of first directors; (g) Consent to act as directors.

question_html: Under Section 7(2) and (3), what happens when the Registrar is satisfied with the documents filed for registration?

options.A: Issues a licence to incorporate and the company can start business immediately
options.B: Registers all documents and issues a CERTIFICATE OF INCORPORATION in Form No. INC-11; allots a CORPORATE IDENTITY NUMBER (CIN) as a DISTINCT IDENTITY for the company — included in the certificate; the company shall maintain and preserve copies of all filed documents at its registered office till dissolution
options.C: Issues a provisional registration and company can apply for permanent status within 6 months
options.D: Issues only a registration number and the company must separately apply for a CIN

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Issues a provisional registration and company can apply for permanent status within 6 months

Section 7(2): On being satisfied, Registrar REGISTERS ALL DOCUMENTS and INFORMATION and issues a CERTIFICATE OF INCORPORATION in FORM NO. INC-11. Section 7(3): Registrar shall allot to the company a CORPORATE IDENTITY NUMBER (CIN) — a DISTINCT IDENTITY for the company — on and from the date mentioned in the certificate; CIN is included in the certificate. Section 7(4): Company shall MAINTAIN AND PRESERVE AT ITS REGISTERED OFFICE copies of all originally filed documents TILL ITS DISSOLUTION. Section 7(5)/(6): FALSE OR INCORRECT INFORMATION in documents = liability under SECTION 447.

question_html: Under Section 10A (introduced by Companies Amendment Ordinance), a company incorporated AFTER THE NOTIFICATION OF THE ORDINANCE shall not COMMENCE BUSINESS unless:

options.A: Directors file a declaration within 90 days of incorporation confirming receipt of subscription money and verification of registered office
options.B: Directors file a declaration within 180 DAYS of incorporation confirming that EVERY SUBSCRIBER HAS PAID FOR THE SHARES AS AGREED and the REGISTERED OFFICE HAS BEEN VERIFIED by filing necessary returns
options.C: Shareholders file a declaration within 60 days of incorporation
options.D: The company obtains a business commencement certificate from the Central Government

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Directors file a declaration within 90 days of incorporation confirming receipt of subscription money and verification of registered office

Section 10A: Every company incorporated after the notification of the COMPANIES AMENDMENT ORDINANCE shall NOT COMMENCE BUSINESS unless the DIRECTORS file a DECLARATION within 180 DAYS of incorporation stating: (a) Every SUBSCRIBER HAS PAID FOR THE SHARES as agreed upon; and (b) The REGISTERED OFFICE has been verified by filing necessary returns. Section 12A (new): Name of company may be STRUCK OFF if NO OFFICE IS FOUND ON PHYSICAL VERIFICATION.

question_html: Under Section 7(5) and (6), if any person furnishes false or incorrect information in documents filed with the Registrar for registration, he shall be liable under:

options.A: Section 299 — fines for incorrect documents
options.B: Section 447 — the provision relating to FRAUD — and where the company was got incorporated by furnishing false information, the Tribunal may pass orders including directing that liability of members shall be unlimited, removal of company name from register, or order winding up
options.C: Section 134 — provisions relating to Board's report
options.D: Section 403 — provisions relating to filing fee only

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Section 447 — the provision relating to FRAUD — and where the company was got incorporated by furnishing false information, the Tribunal may pass orders including directing that liability of members shall be unlimited, removal of company name from register, or order winding up

Section 7(5): Any person furnishing FALSE OR INCORRECT PARTICULARS or SUPPRESSING MATERIAL INFORMATION in documents filed with Registrar for registration = liable under SECTION 447 (FRAUD). Section 7(6): Where the company was incorporated by FURNISHING FALSE INFORMATION — promoters, first directors, and persons making declarations are EACH PERSONALLY LIABLE under Section 447. Section 7(7): The TRIBUNAL MAY on application: (1) Pass orders for REGULATION OF MANAGEMENT; (2) Direct LIABILITY OF MEMBERS SHALL BE UNLIMITED; (3) Direct REMOVAL OF NAME from register; (4) Order WINDING UP; or (5) Such other orders as it deems fit.

question_html: A promoter who wishes to register a company shall first reserve the name for the company. Under Rule 9, in which form is the application for RESERVATION OF NAME made?

options.A: Form INC-2 along with prescribed fee
options.B: Form INC-7 along with prescribed fee
options.C: Form INC-1 along with the prescribed fee — the promoter must comply with Rule 8 regarding undesirable names
options.D: Form DIR-12 along with prescribed fee

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Form INC-1 along with the prescribed fee — the promoter must comply with Rule 8 regarding undesirable names

Rule 9: An APPLICATION FOR RESERVATION OF NAME shall be made in FORM INC-1 along with the FEE. Rule 8: The promoter must comply with the list of UNDESIRABLE NAMES that cannot be adopted — including names identical/nearly resembling existing companies, names with prohibited words (CROWN, EMPEROR, KING, QUEEN, ROYAL, EMPIRE, IMPERIAL etc. without State Government consent), names identical to registered trademarks, etc. Where articles contain ENTRENCHMENT provisions, company shall give notice to Registrar of such provisions in Form INC-2 or Form INC-7 at time of incorporation.

question_html: Under the OPC rules, when a nominee withdraws his consent, the sole member must nominate another person within how many days, and the company must file with the Registrar within how many days?

options.A: Nominate another person within 30 days; Company to file with Registrar within 60 days
options.B: Nominate another person within 15 DAYS of notice of withdrawal; Company to file with Registrar within 30 DAYS of receipt of notice of withdrawal — in Form INC-4 with written consent of new nominee in Form INC-3
options.C: Nominate another person within 45 days; Company to file with Registrar within 45 days
options.D: Nominate another person within 7 days; Company to file with Registrar within 15 days

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Nominate another person within 30 days; Company to file with Registrar within 60 days

OPC NOMINEE RULES: When nominee WITHDRAWS CONSENT — (1) SOLE MEMBER shall nominate another person within 15 DAYS of the notice of withdrawal; (2) Send intimation to company with written consent of new nominee in FORM INC-3; (3) COMPANY shall file with Registrar within 30 DAYS of receipt of withdrawal notice — in FORM INC-4 with fee and written consent in FORM INC-3. Where a new member BECOMES MEMBER (due to death of original member) — new member shall nominate another person within 15 DAYS of becoming member; company shall file intimation within 30 DAYS in FORM INC-4.

question_html: Under Rule 7A, if an OPC or any officer of such company contravenes any provisions of the OPC rules, the penalty is:

options.A: Fine up to Rs. 10,000 only
options.B: FINE WHICH MAY EXTEND TO RS. 5,000 with a FURTHER FINE which may extend to RS. 500 FOR EVERY DAY after the first offence during which such contravention continues
options.C: Fine up to Rs. 50,000 with imprisonment up to 6 months
options.D: Fine up to Rs. 1 lakh only — no per-day continuing fine

answer_html:
Answer: (B) FINE WHICH MAY EXTEND TO RS. 5,000 with a FURTHER FINE which may extend to RS. 500 FOR EVERY DAY after the first offence during which such contravention continues

Rule 7A (w.e.f. 01.05.2015): If an OPC or any OFFICER of such company contravenes any provisions of these rules, the OPC or officer shall be punishable with: FINE which may extend to RS. 5,000 AND FURTHER FINE which may extend to RS. 500 FOR EVERY DAY after the first offence during which such contravention continues. Compare with CONVERSION CONTRAVENTION [Rule 6(5)]: Fine up to RS. 10,000 + RS. 1,000 per day. These penalty structures for OPC non-compliance are frequently tested.

question_html: Under Section 379, when shall a foreign company be required to comply with the provisions of Chapter XXII (relating to foreign companies in India) 'as if it were a company incorporated in India'?

options.A: When the foreign company has any business activity in India
options.B: When the foreign company has Indian employees working in its overseas offices
options.C: When NOT LESS THAN 50 PER CENT of the PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL (equity or preference, or partly both) of a foreign company is held by citizens of India or companies/bodies corporate incorporated in India — singly or in aggregate
options.D: When the foreign company intends to list its shares on Indian stock exchanges

answer_html:
Answer: (C) When NOT LESS THAN 50 PER CENT of the PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL (equity or preference, or partly both) of a foreign company is held by citizens of India or companies/bodies corporate incorporated in India — singly or in aggregate

Section 379: Where NOT LESS THAN 50 PER CENT of the PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL (whether equity or preference or partly equity and partly preference) of a FOREIGN COMPANY is held by: (a) one or more CITIZENS OF INDIA; or (b) one or more COMPANIES OR BODIES CORPORATE INCORPORATED IN INDIA; or (c) COMBINATION of both — whether singly or in the AGGREGATE — such foreign company must comply with CHAPTER XXII of the Companies Act (with all incidental provisions) as if it were a company INCORPORATED IN INDIA. Section 380: Documents foreign company must deliver to Registrar; Section 381: Accounts compliance.
topic_text: Section 15 and Sections 380-382 — Foreign Company Compliance

question_html: Under Rule 21(1), when does a Section 8 company wishing to convert into a company of any other kind need to pass a SPECIAL RESOLUTION?

options.A: Only when the Central Government directs conversion
options.B: When the Income Tax authority recommends conversion
options.C: Conversion requires no special resolution — only board approval is needed
options.D: The Section 8 company shall pass a SPECIAL RESOLUTION AT A GENERAL MEETING for approving such conversion — filed with Registrar in Form MGT-14; application for conversion filed in Form INC-18 with Regional Director; notice published within ONE WEEK of filing application

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only when the Central Government directs conversion

Rule 21(1): Section 8 company intending to CONVERT INTO ANOTHER KIND OF COMPANY shall pass a SPECIAL RESOLUTION at a general meeting. Certified copy filed with Registrar in FORM MGT-14. Application filed in FORM INC-18 with REGIONAL DIRECTOR. Notice published within ONE WEEK from date of filing application (vernacular + English newspaper + website). Copy sent to: Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, Charity Commissioner, Chief Secretary of State, and other relevant Govt. departments. Any of these authorities may make representations within 60 DAYS. On approval, Regional Director issues order; company files in Form INC-20 within 30 DAYS.

question_html: Under Rule 7, when may a private company convert itself into an OPC?

options.A: Any time, by passing a board resolution and filing with Registrar
options.B: A private company other than a Section 8 company, having paid-up share capital of RS. 50 LAKHS OR LESS AND average annual turnover of RS. 2 CRORES OR LESS, may convert itself into OPC by passing a SPECIAL RESOLUTION in general meeting — after obtaining NO OBJECTION CERTIFICATE from all members and creditors; file copy of resolution in Form MGT-14 within 30 DAYS; application in Form INC-6
options.C: Only if approved by the National Company Law Tribunal
options.D: Any private company with fewer than 5 shareholders can convert

answer_html:
Answer: (B) A private company other than a Section 8 company, having paid-up share capital of RS. 50 LAKHS OR LESS AND average annual turnover of RS. 2 CRORES OR LESS, may convert itself into OPC by passing a SPECIAL RESOLUTION in general meeting — after obtaining NO OBJECTION CERTIFICATE from all members and creditors; file copy of resolution in Form MGT-14 within 30 DAYS; application in Form INC-6

Rule 7: CONVERSION OF PRIVATE COMPANY INTO OPC: Conditions: (1) PRIVATE COMPANY (not Section 8 company); (2) Paid-up share capital RS. 50 LAKHS OR LESS; (3) Average annual turnover during RELEVANT PERIOD RS. 2 CRORES OR LESS. Process: (a) Pass SPECIAL RESOLUTION in general meeting; (b) BEFORE passing resolution, obtain NO OBJECTION CERTIFICATE in writing from ALL MEMBERS AND CREDITORS; (c) File copy of resolution in FORM MGT-14 within 30 DAYS; (d) Application in FORM INC-6 with: affidavit from directors, list of members/creditors, latest audited balance sheet, copy of NOC from secured creditors. Registrar issues certificate on satisfaction.
topic_text: Conversion of Private Company to OPC

question_html: Section 122 of the Companies Act, 2013 provides that various sections relating to GENERAL MEETINGS do not apply to OPC. Which section provides for an OPC to pass resolutions by simply COMMUNICATING THE RESOLUTION TO THE COMPANY?

options.A: Section 96 — Annual General Meetings not required for OPC
options.B: Section 100 — Extraordinary general meetings not required
options.C: Section 103 — Quorum requirements do not apply
options.D: Section 122(3) — Any business requiring ordinary or special resolution at AGM or EGM: it is SUFFICIENT if the MEMBER COMMUNICATES THE RESOLUTION TO THE COMPANY, it is ENTERED IN THE MINUTES BOOK and SIGNED AND DATED by the member — such date is deemed the date of the meeting

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Section 103 — Quorum requirements do not apply

Section 122: OPC EXEMPTIONS from meeting-related sections: Sec. 98 (Tribunal calling meetings), 100 (EGM), 101 (Notice), 102 (Statement to notice), 103 (Quorum), 104 (Chairman), 105 (Proxies), 106 (Voting rights restrictions), 107 (Voting by show of hands), 108 (Electronic voting), 109 (Poll), 111 (Circulation of members' resolution). Section 122(3): Member COMMUNICATES RESOLUTION to company + entered in MINUTES BOOK + SIGNED AND DATED by member = deemed resolution passed. Section 122(4): Where ONE DIRECTOR on Board — Board resolution similarly entered in minutes book and signed by director. Financial statements can be filed within 6 MONTHS from close of financial year [Sec.137]. LIABILITY STRUCTURES & SPECIAL PROVISIONS — SECTIONS 2(21)(22)(92)

question_html: Under Section 2(22), in a company LIMITED BY SHARES, what is the maximum liability of a member?

options.A: The AMOUNT UNPAID, IF ANY, ON THE SHARES HELD BY HIM — members cannot be called upon to pay more than the unpaid value of their shares; liability may be enforced during existence or during winding up
options.B: The entire amount of the company's debts without any limit
options.C: The face value of shares held regardless of what was paid
options.D: Limited to initial investment only — no calls can be made

answer_html:
Answer: (A) The AMOUNT UNPAID, IF ANY, ON THE SHARES HELD BY HIM — members cannot be called upon to pay more than the unpaid value of their shares; liability may be enforced during existence or during winding up

Section 2(22): Company LIMITED BY SHARES = company having the liability of its members LIMITED BY THE MEMORANDUM to the AMOUNT, IF ANY, UNPAID ON SHARES RESPECTIVELY HELD BY THEM. A member CANNOT BE CALLED UPON TO PAY MORE THAN THE UNPAID VALUE OF HIS SHARES. Note: COMPANY'S LIABILITY IS NEVER LIMITED — it is the LIABILITY OF SHAREHOLDERS that is limited. Liability can be enforced at any time during existence AND DURING WINDING UP. Section 2(21): Company LIMITED BY GUARANTEE = members undertake to contribute a SPECIFIED AMOUNT (not share value) on winding up or within one year of ceasing to be a member.
topic_text: Companies Limited by Shares vs Guarantee

question_html: Under Section 2(92), an UNLIMITED COMPANY has which characteristic regarding its members' liability?

options.A: Members' liability is limited to 10 times the share value
options.B: Members' liability is limited to twice the share capital contributed by each member
options.C: Members have no liability once shares are fully paid
options.D: A company having NO LIMIT on the LIABILITY OF ITS MEMBERS — each member's liability extends to the whole amount of the company's debts/liabilities; creditors must proceed through winding up and Official Liquidator; may or may not have share capital; can purchase its own shares [Section 67]

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Members' liability is limited to twice the share capital contributed by each member

Section 2(92): UNLIMITED COMPANY = company having NO LIMIT on the LIABILITY OF ITS MEMBERS. Each member's liability extends to the WHOLE AMOUNT OF THE COMPANY'S DEBTS AND LIABILITIES — similar to partnership liability. However, unlike partners, MEMBERS CANNOT BE DIRECTLY PROCEEDED AGAINST — the company (being a separate legal entity) must be wound up and the OFFICIAL LIQUIDATOR may call on members. Such companies MAY OR MAY NOT HAVE SHARE CAPITAL. NOT SUBJECT TO ANY RESTRICTIONS regarding PURCHASE OF OWN SHARES [Section 67] — may purchase own shares or advance monies to purchase shares.

question_html: Which of the following statements about the COMMON SEAL of a company after the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2015 is CORRECT?

options.A: Common seal is still mandatory for all companies incorporated after 2015
options.B: Common seal is mandatory only for public companies with more than 50 shareholders
options.C: USE OF COMMON SEAL IS OPTIONAL — documents which previously required common seal may now be SIGNED BY TWO DIRECTORS or ONE DIRECTOR AND A COMPANY SECRETARY in place of affixing the common seal
options.D: Common seal is mandatory only for documents involving immovable property transactions

answer_html:
Answer: (C) USE OF COMMON SEAL IS OPTIONAL — documents which previously required common seal may now be SIGNED BY TWO DIRECTORS or ONE DIRECTOR AND A COMPANY SECRETARY in place of affixing the common seal

Section 5 and 2015 AMENDMENT: The USE OF COMMON SEAL HAS BEEN MADE OPTIONAL by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2015. Previously, the Companies Act, 2013 required common seal on certain documents. Now, ALL such documents that required common seal may instead be SIGNED BY: (a) TWO DIRECTORS; or (b) ONE DIRECTOR AND A COMPANY SECRETARY of the company. This reduces procedural burdens. The seal, if used, must be affixed in the presence of authorized persons and signed.

question_html: Which of the following best describes the concept of 'PERPETUAL SUCCESSION' as a characteristic of a company under the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: A company can perpetually issue new shares without shareholder approval
options.B: A company continues to exist IRRESPECTIVE OF ANY CHANGE IN ITS MEMBERSHIP — MEMBERS MAY COME AND MEMBERS MAY GO BUT THE COMPANY SURVIVES from the time of incorporation to winding up; it can only be wound up by the prescribed process
options.C: A company's directors have perpetual tenure unless removed by shareholders
options.D: A company's assets perpetually belong to the shareholders who subscribed to the memorandum

answer_html:
Answer: (A) A company can perpetually issue new shares without shareholder approval

PERPETUAL SUCCESSION: A company has its existence from the TIME OF INCORPORATION TO WINDING UP. MEMBERS MAY COME AND MEMBERS MAY GO — but the company survives. Unlike a partnership, death, insolvency or retirement of members/shareholders does not affect the company's existence. The company can ONLY BE DISSOLVED BY THE WINDING UP PROCESS as ordered by the Court. This feature makes the company fundamentally different from a partnership firm.

question_html: Under Section 44, shares of any member in a company are MOVABLE PROPERTY transferable in the manner provided by the ARTICLES of the company. In a PRIVATE COMPANY, what is the position regarding transfer of shares?

options.A: Shares of a private company can be freely transferred like public company shares
options.B: Private company shares cannot be transferred at all — any transfer is void
options.C: Transfer only permitted with Reserve Bank of India approval
options.D: By definition [Section 2(68)], a private company MUST RESTRICT the right to transfer its shares through its ARTICLES — only restrictions CONTAINED IN ARTICLES are valid and binding; additional restrictions in PRIVATE AGREEMENTS between shareholders are NOT BINDING on the company or other shareholders (V.B. Nagaraj v. V.B. Gopalakrishnan, 1991 SC)

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Private company shares cannot be transferred at all — any transfer is void

Section 44 + Section 2(68): PRIVATE COMPANY: Must by its articles RESTRICT the right to TRANSFER SHARES. The only permissible restrictions are those CONTAINED IN ARTICLES — an additional restriction in a PRIVATE AGREEMENT between two shareholders is NOT BINDING either on the company or on the shareholders [V.B. Nagaraj v. V.B. Gopalakrishnan (1991) CLA 211 SC]. Articles may empower directors to DECLINE REGISTRATION OF TRANSFER. PUBLIC COMPANY: Shares are freely transferable [Section 44].

question_html: Under Section 2(6), an 'associate company' means a company in which another company has 'significant influence'. What constitutes significant influence?

options.A: Holding more than 50% of total share capital
options.B: Holding at least 26% of total share capital
options.C: The right to appoint a majority of the directors of the other company
options.D: Control of AT LEAST 20% OF TOTAL SHARE CAPITAL, or of business decisions under an AGREEMENT; includes a JOINT VENTURE COMPANY — but the company shall NOT be a subsidiary of the company having such influence

answer_html:
Answer: (C) The right to appoint a majority of the directors of the other company

Section 2(6): ASSOCIATE COMPANY = company in which another company has SIGNIFICANT INFLUENCE but which is NOT a SUBSIDIARY. SIGNIFICANT INFLUENCE = control of AT LEAST 20% OF TOTAL SHARE CAPITAL, or of BUSINESS DECISIONS UNDER AN AGREEMENT. INCLUDES A JOINT VENTURE COMPANY. JOINT VENTURE = joint arrangement whereby parties having joint control have rights to the NET ASSETS of the arrangement. Compare: Subsidiary requires more than 50% share capital control or control over Board composition. OPC RELAXATIONS, SECTION 8 COMPANY & MISCELLANEOUS — SECTIONS 92, 96, 137

question_html: Under Section 137 of the Companies Act, 2013, what is the EXTENDED TIME LIMIT available to an OPC for filing financial statements?

options.A: OPC must file financial statements within 30 days from close of financial year
options.B: OPC financial statements can be filed WITHIN SIX MONTHS from the close of the financial year — as against the normal 30 days applicable to other companies
options.C: OPC must file financial statements within 3 months from close of financial year
options.D: OPC has no special relaxation for filing financial statements

answer_html:
Answer: (A) OPC must file financial statements within 30 days from close of financial year

Section 137: OPC financial statements can be filed WITHIN SIX MONTHS from the close of the financial year (NORMAL COMPANIES: within 30 days). Other OPC RELAXATIONS: (1) No CASH FLOW STATEMENT required [Sec.2(40)]; (2) Annual Return can be signed by DIRECTOR (if no CS) [Sec.92]; (3) No AGM required [Sec.96]; (4) EGM provisions do NOT apply [Sec.100]; (5) Notice requirements, quorum, proxies, voting provisions — all inapplicable [Sec.101-111]; (6) Resolutions communicated by member and entered in minutes book = DEEMED PASSED [Sec.122(3)]; (7) No postal ballot required [Rule 22(16)].

question_html: Under Section 8(11), if a Section 8 company makes any default in complying with the requirements of Section 8, the penalty is:

options.A: Fine up to Rs. 5 lakhs only
options.B: COMPANY: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 10 LAKHS but MAY EXTEND TO RS. 1 CRORE; DIRECTORS AND EVERY OFFICER IN DEFAULT: imprisonment up to 3 YEARS or fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25,000 but MAY EXTEND TO RS. 25 LAKHS or BOTH; fraudulent conduct = Section 447 liability
options.C: Fine up to Rs. 50,000 for company and directors
options.D: Imprisonment up to 6 months and fine up to Rs. 5 lakhs for all officers

answer_html:
Answer: (B) COMPANY: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 10 LAKHS but MAY EXTEND TO RS. 1 CRORE; DIRECTORS AND EVERY OFFICER IN DEFAULT: imprisonment up to 3 YEARS or fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25,000 but MAY EXTEND TO RS. 25 LAKHS or BOTH; fraudulent conduct = Section 447 liability

Section 8(11): DEFAULT BY SECTION 8 COMPANY: COMPANY: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 10 LAKHS but which may extend to RS. 1 CRORE. DIRECTORS AND EVERY OFFICER IN DEFAULT: imprisonment for a term which MAY EXTEND TO 3 YEARS OR FINE NOT LESS THAN RS. 25,000 BUT WHICH MAY EXTEND TO RS. 25 LAKHS OR BOTH. Where affairs of the company were conducted FRAUDULENTLY — every officer in default liable under SECTION 447. Section 8(6): Licence may be revoked by the CG for non-compliance, fraudulent conduct, or violation of licence conditions.

question_html: From Financial Year 2020-2021, small companies are required to file their Annual Return in which specific e-Form, and within what period?

options.A: Form MGT-7 within 30 days from AGM
options.B: Form MGT-7 within 60 days from AGM
options.C: Form MGT-7A within 30 days from AGM
options.D: New e-FORM MGT-7A within 60 DAYS from the date of Annual General Meeting

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Form MGT-7A within 30 days from AGM

Small Company Annual Return: Vide the Companies (Management and Administration) Amendment Rules, 2021, a NEW e-FORM MGT-7A was introduced. From FINANCIAL YEAR 2020-2021, SMALL COMPANIES file Annual Return in NEW e-FORM MGT-7A. Due date = 60 DAYS from the date of AGM. Compare: OPC Annual Return is signed by CS or where no CS, by the DIRECTOR of the company [Section 92 proviso]. Regular companies use Form MGT-7.

question_html: Under Section 8(4)(ii), a company registered under Section 8 may convert itself into a company of any other kind only after:

options.A: Obtaining prior permission from the Central Government and passing an ordinary resolution
options.B: Complying with CONDITIONS AS MAY BE PRESCRIBED — under Rule 21: passing a SPECIAL RESOLUTION at a general meeting; filing application in Form INC-18 with Regional Director; publishing notice within one week; obtaining Regional Director's ORDER for conversion
options.C: Filing an application with SEBI and obtaining a no-objection certificate
options.D: Only after being wound up and re-incorporated as another type of company

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Obtaining prior permission from the Central Government and passing an ordinary resolution

Section 8(4)(ii): A Section 8 company may CONVERT INTO ANOTHER KIND of company only after COMPLYING WITH CONDITIONS AS MAY BE PRESCRIBED. Rule 21: (1) Pass SPECIAL RESOLUTION at general meeting; (2) File FORM MGT-14 with Registrar; (3) File application in FORM INC-18 with REGIONAL DIRECTOR; (4) Publish notice within ONE WEEK (vernacular + English newspapers + website); (5) Send notice to Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, Charity Commissioner, Chief Secretary, etc.; (6) Regional Director issues ORDER on satisfaction; (7) File order in FORM INC-20 within 30 DAYS; (8) Pass special resolution for altering MOA/AOA.

question_html: In the formation of a company, a 'promoter' is a person who takes the initial steps in forming the company. Which of the following documents does the PROMOTER file with the Registrar during incorporation under Section 7?

options.A: Only the MOA signed by subscribers
options.B: MEMORANDUM AND ARTICLES duly signed by subscribers; declarations in Form INC-9; consent of first directors; particulars of subscribers — and if any FALSE OR INCORRECT PARTICULARS are furnished, each PROMOTER shall be liable for action under SECTION 447 (Fraud)
options.C: Only bank statements and proof of capital
options.D: Only the Form INC-1 for name reservation

answer_html:
Answer: (B) MEMORANDUM AND ARTICLES duly signed by subscribers; declarations in Form INC-9; consent of first directors; particulars of subscribers — and if any FALSE OR INCORRECT PARTICULARS are furnished, each PROMOTER shall be liable for action under SECTION 447 (Fraud)

PROMOTER's role in incorporation: The promoter submits to the Registrar all incorporation documents under Section 7. DECLARATIONS: Every subscriber and FIRST DIRECTOR must declare in FORM INC-9 that they: (i) are not convicted of any offence in connection with promotion/formation/management of any company; (ii) not found guilty of fraud/misfeasance/breach of duty to any company in last 5 YEARS; (iii) all documents filed are CORRECT, COMPLETE AND TRUE. Section 7(6): Where company was incorporated by furnishing FALSE INFORMATION — promoters, first directors, and declarants are EACH personally liable under SECTION 447.

question_html: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a STATUTORY COMPANY from a REGISTERED COMPANY under the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Statutory companies can have unlimited liability; registered companies must have limited liability
options.B: Statutory companies always have more than 1000 shareholders; registered companies have fewer shareholders
options.C: A STATUTORY COMPANY is formed under a SPECIAL ACT of Parliament (e.g., LIC, RBI, IRDA) and does NOT require a Memorandum of Association; governed by its special Act — Companies Act applies only to the extent NOT INCONSISTENT with the special Act [Section 1(4)]. A REGISTERED COMPANY is incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 or previous laws and is registered with the Registrar
options.D: There is no distinction — both are governed identically under the Companies Act, 2013

answer_html:
Answer: (C) A STATUTORY COMPANY is formed under a SPECIAL ACT of Parliament (e.g., LIC, RBI, IRDA) and does NOT require a Memorandum of Association; governed by its special Act — Companies Act applies only to the extent NOT INCONSISTENT with the special Act [Section 1(4)]. A REGISTERED COMPANY is incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 or previous laws and is registered with the Registrar

STATUTORY COMPANY vs REGISTERED COMPANY: STATUTORY COMPANY: Formed under a SPECIAL ACT OF PARLIAMENT (e.g., Life Insurance Corporation Act, Reserve Bank of India Act, Insurance Act); does NOT REQUIRE a Memorandum of Association necessarily; governed by PROVISIONS OF ITS SPECIAL ACT; Companies Act 2013 applies only to the extent NOT INCONSISTENT WITH THE SPECIAL ACT [Section 1(4)]. REGISTERED COMPANY: A company REGISTERED UNDER THE COMPANIES ACT, 2013 or any PREVIOUS COMPANY LAW; incorporated as LIMITED or UNLIMITED; as PUBLIC or PRIVATE. REGISTRATION IS AN ESSENTIAL FEATURE of registered companies. CONSOLIDATED ANSWER KEY — ALL 50 QUESTIONS — END OF QUESTION PAPER — Prepared from ICMAI Study Module | Companies Act, 2013 – Incorporation of Company | Module 12.1 | Syllabus 2022 | CMA Inter June 2026

question_html: Under Section 96(1), every company other than an OPC must hold an AGM in each year. Which of the following correctly states the time rules for holding an AGM?

options.A: AGM must be held within 3 months from close of financial year; gap between two AGMs must not exceed 12 months
options.B: AGM must be held within 6 MONTHS from close of financial year; gap between two consecutive AGMs must NOT EXCEED 15 MONTHS; Registrar may extend time by up to 3 MONTHS for special reason — EXCEPT FOR FIRST AGM; FIRST AGM within 9 months from close of first financial year; company holding first AGM need not hold AGM in year of incorporation
options.C: AGM must be held within 12 months from close of financial year; gap between two AGMs must not exceed 18 months
options.D: AGM must be held within 6 months from date of incorporation; gap between two AGMs must not exceed 12 months

answer_html:
Answer: (B) AGM must be held within 6 MONTHS from close of financial year; gap between two consecutive AGMs must NOT EXCEED 15 MONTHS; Registrar may extend time by up to 3 MONTHS for special reason — EXCEPT FOR FIRST AGM; FIRST AGM within 9 months from close of first financial year; company holding first AGM need not hold AGM in year of incorporation

Section 96(1): (1) AGM within 6 MONTHS from close of financial year; (2) Gap between two AGMs NOT MORE THAN 15 MONTHS; (3) Registrar may extend time by a period NOT EXCEEDING 3 MONTHS for special reason — BUT NOT IN CASE OF FIRST AGM. FIRST AGM [Section 96(1)]: Within 9 MONTHS from close of FIRST FINANCIAL YEAR. If company holds its first AGM, it need NOT hold AGM in the YEAR OF INCORPORATION. NO FURTHER EXTENSION given by Registrar for First AGM.
topic_text: Section 96 — AGM: Time Limits & Key Rules

question_html: Under Section 96(2), every AGM shall be held on what day and at what time? What is the special provision for unlisted companies?

options.A: Any day including national holidays; 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.; only at registered office
options.B: On any day that is NOT A NATIONAL HOLIDAY; during BUSINESS HOURS (9 a.m. to 6 p.m.); at REGISTERED OFFICE or other place within THE SAME CITY, TOWN OR VILLAGE as the registered office; UNLISTED COMPANY: may hold at ANY PLACE IN INDIA if CONSENT IS GIVEN IN WRITING OR ELECTRONIC MODE BY ALL MEMBERS IN ADVANCE
options.C: Only on Saturdays and Sundays; 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.; anywhere in India for all companies
options.D: Only on working days; 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.; only at the registered office for all companies

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Only on Saturdays and Sundays; 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.; anywhere in India for all companies

Section 96(2): AGM shall be held: (1) On a day that is NOT A NATIONAL HOLIDAY; (2) During BUSINESS HOURS i.e., 9 A.M. TO 6 P.M.; (3) At the REGISTERED OFFICE or at some OTHER PLACE WITHIN THE CITY, TOWN OR VILLAGE in which the registered office is situated. EXCEPTION — UNLISTED COMPANY: AGM may be held at any place in India if CONSENT is given IN WRITING OR BY ELECTRONIC MODE BY ALL THE MEMBERS IN ADVANCE. CG may EXEMPT any company from Sec.96(2) subject to conditions.
topic_text: Section 96(2) — Conduct of AGM: Time, Day, Place

question_html: Under Section 97, when may the TRIBUNAL call or direct the calling of an AGM, and what is the special quorum rule for a Tribunal-directed AGM?

options.A: If default is made in holding AGM — on application of ANY MEMBER: Tribunal may call/direct calling of AGM; may direct that ONE MEMBER present in person or by proxy shall be deemed to constitute a meeting; ancillary or consequential directions may also be given; such meeting deemed to be AGM under the Act
options.B: Only SEBI can direct calling of an AGM — Tribunal has no such power
options.C: The Tribunal can only direct a meeting if more than 50% members apply
options.D: The Tribunal can only direct a meeting after 2 years of default

answer_html:
Answer: (A) If default is made in holding AGM — on application of ANY MEMBER: Tribunal may call/direct calling of AGM; may direct that ONE MEMBER present in person or by proxy shall be deemed to constitute a meeting; ancillary or consequential directions may also be given; such meeting deemed to be AGM under the Act

Section 97: If DEFAULT is made in holding AGM under Section 96 — the TRIBUNAL may, notwithstanding anything in the Act or articles, on APPLICATION OF ANY MEMBER, CALL OR DIRECT THE CALLING OF AN ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING. Directions may include a direction that ONE MEMBER OF THE COMPANY PRESENT IN PERSON OR BY PROXY SHALL BE DEEMED TO CONSTITUTE A MEETING. Such meeting deemed to be AGM. PENALTY for default [Section 99]: Company and officer fine up to RS. 1 LAKH + continuing default: RS. 5,000 per day.
topic_text: Section 97 — Tribunal's Power to Call AGM

question_html: Under Section 100, who may REQUISITION an Extraordinary General Meeting and what is the minimum threshold?

options.A: Any single shareholder regardless of shareholding may requisition an EGM
options.B: For companies with share capital: members holding NOT LESS THAN ONE-TENTH OF PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL CARRYING VOTING RIGHTS on date of requisition; for companies WITHOUT share capital: members having NOT LESS THAN ONE-TENTH OF TOTAL VOTING POWER on date of requisition; Board must call the meeting within 21 DAYS of receipt and conduct it within 45 DAYS of requisition
options.C: Members holding at least 25% of paid-up share capital
options.D: At least 10 members regardless of their shareholding

answer_html:
Answer: (B) For companies with share capital: members holding NOT LESS THAN ONE-TENTH OF PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL CARRYING VOTING RIGHTS on date of requisition; for companies WITHOUT share capital: members having NOT LESS THAN ONE-TENTH OF TOTAL VOTING POWER on date of requisition; Board must call the meeting within 21 DAYS of receipt and conduct it within 45 DAYS of requisition

Section 100: EGM may be requisitioned by: (1) COMPANY WITH SHARE CAPITAL: members holding NOT LESS THAN ONE-TENTH of paid-up share capital CARRYING VOTING RIGHTS on date of receipt of requisition; (2) COMPANY WITHOUT SHARE CAPITAL: members having NOT LESS THAN ONE-TENTH OF TOTAL VOTING POWER. BOARD'S OBLIGATION: Call meeting within 21 DAYS of receipt of valid requisition; meeting conducted within 45 DAYS from receipt. If Board fails: REQUISITIONISTS themselves may conduct meeting within THREE MONTHS from date of requisition. They have right to receive LIST OF MEMBERS with addresses (as on 21st day from receipt + changes before expiry of 45 days).

question_html: Under Section 100, an Extraordinary General Meeting of a company (other than of a wholly owned subsidiary of a company incorporated outside India) shall be held:

options.A: At any place globally where the holding company is located
options.B: Only at the registered office of the company
options.C: AT A PLACE WITHIN INDIA — Board may call EGM whenever it deems fit; EGM of wholly owned subsidiary of a company incorporated outside India may be held outside India
options.D: Only with Central Government approval for each EGM

answer_html:
Answer: (C) AT A PLACE WITHIN INDIA — Board may call EGM whenever it deems fit; EGM of wholly owned subsidiary of a company incorporated outside India may be held outside India

Section 100: The Board may, WHENEVER IT DEEMS FIT, call an Extraordinary General Meeting. An EGM of the company, OTHER THAN OF THE WHOLLY OWNED SUBSIDIARY OF A COMPANY INCORPORATED OUTSIDE INDIA, shall be held AT A PLACE WITHIN INDIA. EXCEPTION: Wholly owned subsidiary of a foreign company may hold EGM outside India. Compare with AGM: must be at registered office or same city/town/village (unlisted — anywhere in India with all-member consent). EGM location rule is broader (anywhere in India) compared to AGM.

question_html: Under Section 99, what is the penalty for DEFAULT in holding a meeting of the company or not complying with directions of the Tribunal?

options.A: Company and every defaulting officer: fine up to RS. 1 LAKH; CONTINUING DEFAULT: additional fine up to RS. 5,000 FOR EVERY DAY during which default continues
options.B: Only the company is liable — no individual officer liability
options.C: Fine up to Rs. 5 lakhs for company only
options.D: Imprisonment only — no fine option

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Company and every defaulting officer: fine up to RS. 1 LAKH; CONTINUING DEFAULT: additional fine up to RS. 5,000 FOR EVERY DAY during which default continues

Section 99: If any default is made in HOLDING A MEETING or in COMPLYING WITH ANY DIRECTIONS OF THE TRIBUNAL: COMPANY AND EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER = punishable with fine which may extend to RS. 1 LAKH. CONTINUING DEFAULT: fine which may extend to RS. 5,000 FOR EVERY DAY during which such default continues. This comparatively modest penalty (Rs.1 lakh) reflects that failure to hold AGM is primarily a procedural default, while the daily penalty for continuing defaults provides ongoing incentive for compliance. NOTICE, QUORUM & CHAIRMAN — SECTIONS 101–104
topic_text: Section 99 — Penalty for Default in Holding Meeting

question_html: Under Section 101, what is the MINIMUM NOTICE PERIOD for calling a general meeting, and when may SHORTER NOTICE be given?

options.A: 14 days clear notice; shorter notice with 50% consent
options.B: NOT LESS THAN CLEAR 21 DAYS NOTICE (written or electronic); SHORTER NOTICE PERMITTED: (a) AGM — with consent of NOT LESS THAN 95% OF MEMBERS entitled to vote; (b) OTHER GENERAL MEETING — with consent of members holding majority in number entitled to vote representing NOT LESS THAN 95% OF PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL (or 95% of total voting power for companies without share capital)
options.C: 30 days clear notice; shorter notice with unanimous consent only
options.D: 7 days clear notice; shorter notice permitted for private companies only

answer_html:
Answer: (B) NOT LESS THAN CLEAR 21 DAYS NOTICE (written or electronic); SHORTER NOTICE PERMITTED: (a) AGM — with consent of NOT LESS THAN 95% OF MEMBERS entitled to vote; (b) OTHER GENERAL MEETING — with consent of members holding majority in number entitled to vote representing NOT LESS THAN 95% OF PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL (or 95% of total voting power for companies without share capital)

Section 101: NOTICE PERIOD: Not less than CLEAR 21 DAYS (in writing or electronic mode). SHORTER NOTICE allowed if: (a) AGM: consent in writing/electronic mode by NOT LESS THAN 95% OF MEMBERS ENTITLED TO VOTE; (b) OTHER GENERAL MEETING: consent by members holding MAJORITY IN NUMBER ENTITLED TO VOTE and representing NOT LESS THAN 95% OF PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL (or 95% of total voting power if no share capital). Notice shall specify place, date, day and hour, and contain statement of business to be transacted. Recipients: every MEMBER, LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE OF DECEASED MEMBER, ASSIGNEE OF INSOLVENT, AUDITOR, and every DIRECTOR.
topic_text: Section 101 — Notice of General Meeting: Period & Shorter Notice

question_html: Under Section 103(1), what are the QUORUM requirements for general meetings of PUBLIC and PRIVATE companies?

options.A: Public company: always 5 members; Private company: always 2 members
options.B: Public company: always 10 members; Private company: always 5 members
options.C: PRIVATE COMPANY: 2 MEMBERS PERSONALLY PRESENT; PUBLIC COMPANY: (a) 5 members if members on date of meeting ≤ 1,000; (b) 15 members if members > 1,000 but ≤ 5,000; (c) 30 members if members exceed 5,000 — unless articles provide for larger quorum
options.D: Both public and private companies: 10 members regardless of total membership

answer_html:
Answer: (C) PRIVATE COMPANY: 2 MEMBERS PERSONALLY PRESENT; PUBLIC COMPANY: (a) 5 members if members on date of meeting ≤ 1,000; (b) 15 members if members > 1,000 but ≤ 5,000; (c) 30 members if members exceed 5,000 — unless articles provide for larger quorum

Section 103(1): QUORUM — unless Articles provide for LARGER NUMBER: PRIVATE COMPANY: 2 MEMBERS PERSONALLY PRESENT. PUBLIC COMPANY: (a) 5 MEMBERS personally present if total members on date of meeting ≤ 1,000; (b) 15 MEMBERS personally present if total members > 1,000 but ≤ 5,000; (c) 30 MEMBERS personally present if total members EXCEED 5,000. Only personally present members count for quorum — not proxies. If quorum not present within 30 MINUTES: meeting adjourned to same day next week (same time and place) or Board-decided date. If meeting called by requisitionists: CANCELLED.
topic_text: Section 103 — Quorum: Public vs Private Company

question_html: Under Section 103(2), if quorum is NOT PRESENT within half an hour at a meeting, what happens? What are the rules for the adjourned meeting?

options.A: Meeting is automatically cancelled regardless of how it was called
options.B: Meeting proceeds with any number of members present
options.C: Meeting proceeds only if the chairman approves
options.D: Regular meeting: adjourned to SAME DAY NEXT WEEK (same time/place) or Board-decided date; 3 DAYS NOTICE (individual or by English + vernacular newspaper at RO city); Requisitioned meeting: CANCELLED; At adjourned meeting: if quorum again not present in 30 minutes — MEMBERS PRESENT SHALL BE THE QUORUM

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Meeting is automatically cancelled regardless of how it was called

Section 103(2): Quorum not present within HALF AN HOUR: (a) REGULAR MEETING (not by requisitionists): adjourned to SAME DAY IN THE NEXT WEEK at same time and place, OR to such other date/time/place as the Board may determine; (b) REQUISITIONED MEETING: STANDS CANCELLED. ADJOURNED MEETING NOTICE: Company gives NOT LESS THAN 3 DAYS NOTICE to members INDIVIDUALLY OR by ADVERTISEMENT in NEWSPAPERS — ONE IN ENGLISH and ONE IN VERNACULAR LANGUAGE circulating at the place of registered office. ADJOURNED MEETING: If quorum again not present within half an hour — MEMBERS PRESENT SHALL BE THE QUORUM.
topic_text: Section 103(2) — Adjourned Meeting for Lack of Quorum

question_html: Under Section 104, how is the Chairman of a general meeting elected, and what happens if a poll is demanded on the election of the Chairman?

options.A: Chairman is always the Managing Director — no election is required
options.B: Unless ARTICLES otherwise provide, MEMBERS PERSONALLY PRESENT elect one of themselves as Chairman on SHOW OF HANDS; if POLL DEMANDED on this election — taken FORTHWITH; Chairman elected on show of hands CONTINUES until another is elected as a result of the poll
options.C: Chairman is elected by the Board before the meeting
options.D: The oldest member present automatically becomes Chairman

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Unless ARTICLES otherwise provide, MEMBERS PERSONALLY PRESENT elect one of themselves as Chairman on SHOW OF HANDS; if POLL DEMANDED on this election — taken FORTHWITH; Chairman elected on show of hands CONTINUES until another is elected as a result of the poll

Section 104(1): Unless the ARTICLES OF THE COMPANY provide otherwise, the MEMBERS PERSONALLY PRESENT at the meeting shall ELECT ONE OF THEMSELVES to be the CHAIRMAN on a SHOW OF HANDS. Section 104(2): If a POLL IS DEMANDED on the election of the Chairman — it shall be taken FORTHWITH (immediately) in accordance with the provisions of the Act. The Chairman elected ON A SHOW OF HANDS shall CONTINUE TO BE THE CHAIRMAN of the meeting UNTIL SOME OTHER PERSON is elected as Chairman as a result of the POLL. Such other person shall be the Chairman for the REST OF THE MEETING. PROXY, VOTING METHODS & ELECTRONIC VOTING — SECTIONS 105–110

question_html: Under Section 105, which of the following correctly states the rules for PROXY?

options.A: A proxy can vote on all matters but cannot inspect documents
options.B: A proxy can act for unlimited number of members
options.C: Member may appoint PROXY; proxy need NOT be a member (EXCEPT Section 8 company where proxy must also be a member); Form MGT-11; deposited at registered office AT LEAST 48 HOURS before meeting; ONE PERSON can be proxy for NOT MORE THAN 50 MEMBERS AND aggregate NOT MORE THAN 10% of total share capital carrying voting rights; member holding MORE THAN 10% may appoint only ONE PROXY who cannot act for any other person
options.D: Proxy must be deposited 24 hours before meeting; unlimited members can appoint same proxy

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Member may appoint PROXY; proxy need NOT be a member (EXCEPT Section 8 company where proxy must also be a member); Form MGT-11; deposited at registered office AT LEAST 48 HOURS before meeting; ONE PERSON can be proxy for NOT MORE THAN 50 MEMBERS AND aggregate NOT MORE THAN 10% of total share capital carrying voting rights; member holding MORE THAN 10% may appoint only ONE PROXY who cannot act for any other person

Section 105: KEY PROXY RULES: (1) APPOINTMENT: Member entitled to attend and vote may appoint a proxy; (2) PROXY NEED NOT BE MEMBER — exception: SECTION 8 COMPANY (proxy must also be a member); (3) FORM: MGT-11; (4) DEPOSIT: At registered office AT LEAST 48 HOURS BEFORE MEETING; (5) LIMITS: One person as proxy for NOT MORE THAN 50 MEMBERS and aggregate NOT MORE THAN 10% of total share capital carrying voting rights; (6) LARGE HOLDER: Member holding MORE THAN 10% of total voting share capital may appoint only ONE PROXY — that proxy cannot act for any other person; (7) Section 8 COMPANY: member not entitled to appoint proxy unless that person is also a member of such company.

question_html: Under Section 105(2), what statement must appear in EVERY NOTICE FOR A MEETING regarding proxies, and what is the penalty for non-compliance?

options.A: A statement about proxy rights must appear WITH REASONABLE PROMINENCE in every notice; default: EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER punishable with fine up to RS. 5,000
options.B: No mandatory proxy statement in notices is required
options.C: A proxy statement is required only for AGM notices
options.D: A proxy statement is required only in notices sent to members holding more than 1% shares

answer_html:
Answer: (A) A statement about proxy rights must appear WITH REASONABLE PROMINENCE in every notice; default: EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER punishable with fine up to RS. 5,000

Section 105(2): In EVERY NOTICE FOR A MEETING, there shall appear WITH REASONABLE PROMINENCE a statement that: (1) A member entitled to attend and vote is entitled to appoint a PROXY (or one or more proxies if allowed) to attend and vote instead of him; AND (2) A PROXY NEED NOT BE A MEMBER. PENALTY for default: EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER punishable with fine which may extend to RS. 5,000. Section 105(8): Every member entitled to vote may INSPECT PROXIES LODGED beginning 24 HOURS BEFORE the meeting until its conclusion — provided NOT LESS THAN 3 DAYS NOTICE IN WRITING of intention to inspect is given to the company.
topic_text: Section 105(2) — Notice Must State Proxy Rights

question_html: Under Section 109(1), a poll may be demanded before or on declaration of result of voting on show of hands. By whom and on what threshold?

options.A: Any single member present may demand a poll regardless of shareholding
options.B: WITH SHARE CAPITAL: Chairman (own motion) or members present in person/proxy having NOT LESS THAN 1/10TH TOTAL VOTING POWER or shares with aggregate sum paid up ≥ RS. 5 LAKHS (or higher); WITHOUT SHARE CAPITAL: Chairman or member/members present in person/proxy having NOT LESS THAN 1/10TH TOTAL VOTING POWER
options.C: Only the Chairman can demand a poll — members have no right
options.D: At least 20 members regardless of shareholding may demand a poll

answer_html:
Answer: (B) WITH SHARE CAPITAL: Chairman (own motion) or members present in person/proxy having NOT LESS THAN 1/10TH TOTAL VOTING POWER or shares with aggregate sum paid up ≥ RS. 5 LAKHS (or higher); WITHOUT SHARE CAPITAL: Chairman or member/members present in person/proxy having NOT LESS THAN 1/10TH TOTAL VOTING POWER

Section 109(1): POLL DEMAND — by: (a) CHAIRMAN on his own motion; or (b) On demand: (i) COMPANY WITH SHARE CAPITAL: members present in person or proxy having NOT LESS THAN ONE-TENTH OF TOTAL VOTING POWER or holding shares on which aggregate sum of NOT LESS THAN RS. 5 LAKHS has been paid up (or higher prescribed amount); (ii) COMPANY WITHOUT SHARE CAPITAL: any member/members present in person or proxy having NOT LESS THAN ONE-TENTH OF TOTAL VOTING POWER. TIMING [Section 109(3)]: Poll for ADJOURNMENT or CHAIRMAN APPOINTMENT — taken IMMEDIATELY. Other polls: within 48 HOURS of demand.

question_html: Under Rule 20 on ELECTRONIC VOTING (e-voting), which of the following is CORRECT?

options.A: E-voting period must be open for at least 7 days; closes at midnight on date of general meeting
options.B: Only listed companies can use e-voting; unlisted companies must use show of hands only
options.C: Any member who has cast vote by remote e-voting can cast vote again at physical meeting if they attend
options.D: E-VOTING open for NOT LESS THAN 3 DAYS; closes at 5.00 P.M. ON DATE PRECEDING the general meeting; members who remote e-voted MAY ATTEND meeting but SHALL NOT VOTE AGAIN; Scrutinizer submits consolidated report within 3 DAYS of conclusion of meeting; resolution through e-voting SHALL NOT BE WITHDRAWN

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Any member who has cast vote by remote e-voting can cast vote again at physical meeting if they attend

Rule 20 E-VOTING RULES: (1) E-voting open for NOT LESS THAN 3 DAYS; (2) CLOSES AT 5.00 P.M. ON THE DATE PRECEDING THE DATE OF GENERAL MEETING; (3) Members who voted via REMOTE E-VOTING: MAY ATTEND the meeting but SHALL NOT BE ENTITLED TO CAST THEIR VOTE AGAIN; (4) Members attending meeting who have NOT already remote e-voted: can vote at the meeting; (5) SCRUTINIZER: Appointed by Board — CA/CMA/CS in practice or Advocate or other reputable person NOT IN EMPLOYMENT of company; count votes at meeting first, then unblock remote e-votes in presence of AT LEAST TWO WITNESSES not in employment of company; submit consolidated report within 3 DAYS of conclusion of meeting; (6) A resolution through e-voting SHALL NOT BE WITHDRAWN.

question_html: Under Rule 22(16), which businesses MUST be transacted through POSTAL BALLOT (voting by postal ballot is MANDATORY)?

options.A: Alteration of OBJECTS CLAUSE of memorandum; alteration of ARTICLES (insertion/removal of private company provisions); change in REGISTERED OFFICE outside local limits; change in OBJECTS (with unutilised public funds); issue of SHARES WITH DIFFERENTIAL RIGHTS; VARIATION of class rights; BUY-BACK; ELECTION OF DIRECTOR; SALE OF WHOLE/SUBSTANTIALLY WHOLE UNDERTAKING; giving loans/guarantee/security exceeding limits — OPC and companies with UP TO 200 MEMBERS are EXEMPT from postal ballot
options.B: Only ordinary resolutions require postal ballot
options.C: Postal ballot is optional for all matters
options.D: Only AGM business requires postal ballot

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Alteration of OBJECTS CLAUSE of memorandum; alteration of ARTICLES (insertion/removal of private company provisions); change in REGISTERED OFFICE outside local limits; change in OBJECTS (with unutilised public funds); issue of SHARES WITH DIFFERENTIAL RIGHTS; VARIATION of class rights; BUY-BACK; ELECTION OF DIRECTOR; SALE OF WHOLE/SUBSTANTIALLY WHOLE UNDERTAKING; giving loans/guarantee/security exceeding limits — OPC and companies with UP TO 200 MEMBERS are EXEMPT from postal ballot

Rule 22(16): MANDATORY POSTAL BALLOT for: (1) Alteration of OBJECTS CLAUSE of memorandum; (2) Alteration of ARTICLES (re: constituting a private company — inserting/removing such provisions); (3) Change in REGISTERED OFFICE outside local limits of any city/town/village; (4) Change in OBJECTS for which money raised from public via prospectus and amount still unutilised; (5) Issue of SHARES WITH DIFFERENTIAL RIGHTS; (6) VARIATION OF RIGHTS attached to class of shares or debentures; (7) BUY-BACK; (8) ELECTION OF DIRECTOR; (9) SALE OF WHOLE/SUBSTANTIALLY WHOLE UNDERTAKING; (10) Giving LOANS/GUARANTEE/SECURITY exceeding specified limits. EXEMPT: OPC and companies having UP TO 200 MEMBERS are NOT required to transact any business through postal ballot.
topic_text: Section 110 & Rule 22 — Postal Ballot: Mandatory Items

question_html: Under Rule 22, what is the key procedure for conducting POSTAL BALLOT?

options.A: Notice sent only by registered post with 60-day response period; Scrutinizer reports within 30 days
options.B: NOTICE sent to all shareholders along with draft resolution and reasons; response time: 30 DAYS from dispatch; notice sent by REGISTERED POST/SPEED POST or ELECTRONIC MEANS or COURIER SERVICE; assent/dissent received after 30 days treated as NO REPLY from member; SCRUTINIZER submits report not later than 7 DAYS after last date of receipt of ballots; RESULTS declared on company website along with Scrutinizer's report
options.C: Notice sent only electronically; 45-day response period; Scrutinizer reports within 15 days
options.D: Notice sent only by registered post; 15-day response period; no Scrutinizer required

answer_html:
Answer: (B) NOTICE sent to all shareholders along with draft resolution and reasons; response time: 30 DAYS from dispatch; notice sent by REGISTERED POST/SPEED POST or ELECTRONIC MEANS or COURIER SERVICE; assent/dissent received after 30 days treated as NO REPLY from member; SCRUTINIZER submits report not later than 7 DAYS after last date of receipt of ballots; RESULTS declared on company website along with Scrutinizer's report

Rule 22 POSTAL BALLOT PROCEDURE: (1) Company sends NOTICE to all shareholders with DRAFT RESOLUTION and REASONS, requesting assent/dissent WITHIN 30 DAYS of dispatch; (2) Notice sent by: REGISTERED POST or SPEED POST; or ELECTRONIC MEANS (registered email); or COURIER SERVICE; (3) Advertisement in VERNACULAR language (district) and ENGLISH language; (4) Notice placed on COMPANY WEBSITE (remains till last date of receipt); (5) Board appoints ONE SCRUTINIZER; (6) Assent/dissent received AFTER 30 DAYS = NO REPLY; (7) Scrutinizer submits report NOT LATER THAN 7 DAYS after last date of receipt; (8) Results declared on company website with Scrutinizer's report. RESOLUTIONS & MINUTES — SECTIONS 114–119

question_html: Under Section 114, what is the MINIMUM VOTES RATIO required to pass a SPECIAL RESOLUTION?

options.A: Simple majority — more votes for than against
options.B: Two-thirds majority of votes cast in favour
options.C: Votes in favour must be NOT LESS THAN 3 TIMES the votes cast against; INTENTION to propose as SR must be DULY SPECIFIED IN NOTICE; REQUIRED NOTICE must have been duly given
options.D: Unanimous approval — all votes must be in favour

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Votes in favour must be NOT LESS THAN 3 TIMES the votes cast against; INTENTION to propose as SR must be DULY SPECIFIED IN NOTICE; REQUIRED NOTICE must have been duly given

Section 114: ORDINARY RESOLUTION [Sec.114(1)]: Votes in FAVOUR EXCEED votes against (simple majority — including Chairman's casting vote). SPECIAL RESOLUTION [Sec.114(2)]: Three conditions: (1) INTENTION to propose as SR DULY SPECIFIED IN NOTICE; (2) Required NOTICE under Act duly given; (3) Votes in FAVOUR are NOT LESS THAN 3 TIMES the votes cast AGAINST the resolution. Voting may be on show of hands, electronically, on poll, or by postal ballot.

question_html: Under Section 115, a resolution requiring SPECIAL NOTICE must be given to the company by members holding what threshold of voting power or paid-up shares?

options.A: Members holding NOT LESS THAN 1% OF TOTAL VOTING POWER or holding shares on which aggregate sum NOT EXCEEDING RS. 5 LAKH (as prescribed) has been paid up
options.B: Members holding at least 5% of total voting power
options.C: Members holding at least 10% of total voting power
options.D: Any single member regardless of shareholding

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Members holding NOT LESS THAN 1% OF TOTAL VOTING POWER or holding shares on which aggregate sum NOT EXCEEDING RS. 5 LAKH (as prescribed) has been paid up

Section 115: Where any provision in the Act or articles REQUIRES SPECIAL NOTICE of any resolution — notice of intention to move such resolution shall be given to the company by members holding NOT LESS THAN 1% OF TOTAL VOTING POWER or holding shares on which such AGGREGATE SUM NOT EXCEEDING RS. 5 LAKH (as may be prescribed) has been paid up. The company shall give its members notice of the resolution in the manner prescribed. COMMON EXAMPLES requiring special notice: Appointment of auditors other than retiring auditor; Removal of auditors before expiry of term; Removal of directors before expiry of term.

question_html: Under Section 117, a copy of every prescribed resolution and agreement shall be filed with the Registrar within what period and in which form?

options.A: Within 60 days in Form MGT-7
options.B: WITHIN 30 DAYS of passing in FORM MGT-14 with prescribed fee; applies to: SPECIAL RESOLUTIONS; all-member-agreed resolutions that would otherwise have been special resolutions; Board resolutions re: MANAGING DIRECTOR appointment/reappointment/renewal/variation; class member resolutions requiring special majority; resolutions for VOLUNTARY WINDING UP under IBC 2016; Board resolutions under Section 179(3); other prescribed resolutions
options.C: Within 15 days in Form MGT-8
options.D: Within 45 days in Form MGT-14

answer_html:
Answer: (B) WITHIN 30 DAYS of passing in FORM MGT-14 with prescribed fee; applies to: SPECIAL RESOLUTIONS; all-member-agreed resolutions that would otherwise have been special resolutions; Board resolutions re: MANAGING DIRECTOR appointment/reappointment/renewal/variation; class member resolutions requiring special majority; resolutions for VOLUNTARY WINDING UP under IBC 2016; Board resolutions under Section 179(3); other prescribed resolutions

Section 117: A copy of every PRESCRIBED RESOLUTION OR AGREEMENT with explanatory statement shall be filed with Registrar WITHIN 30 DAYS of passing/making in FORM MGT-14 with prescribed fee. CATEGORIES: (1) SPECIAL RESOLUTIONS; (2) Resolutions agreed by ALL MEMBERS that would otherwise have been special resolutions; (3) Board resolutions/agreements re: MANAGING DIRECTOR — appointment/reappointment/renewal/variation of terms; (4) Class member resolutions requiring special majority; (5) Resolutions for VOLUNTARY WINDING UP under Section 59 of IBC, 2016; (6) Board resolutions under SECTION 179(3); (7) Other prescribed resolutions. Copy of SR altering articles shall be embodied/annexed to every copy of articles issued after passing of the SR.
topic_text: Section 117 — Filing of Resolutions with Registrar

question_html: Under Rule 25 and Section 118, which of the following correctly states the rules about MINUTES of meetings?

options.A: Minutes of all meetings may be kept in a single minute book; entries made within 60 days
