Section 5: The appropriate Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, exempt any establishment or class of establishments from the provisions of the Act if SATISFIED that the employees in such establishment are in receipt of GRATUITY OR PENSIONARY BENEFITS NOT LESS FAVOURABLE than the benefits provided under the Act. The exemption protects employees from losing better existing benefits.

question_html: The term 'gratuity' is derived from which Latin word, and what is the nature of this payment?

options.A: 'Gratia' — a gift payable only on voluntary resignation
options.B: 'Gratuitous' — a lump-sum retiral social security benefit paid by the employer in consideration of past services rendered
options.C: 'Gratis' — a payment made only on death of the employee
options.D: 'Gratitude' — an optional payment at the discretion of the employer

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 'Gratuitous' — a lump-sum retiral social security benefit paid by the employer in consideration of past services rendered

The term 'gratuity' is derived from the Latin word 'GRATUITOUS'. It is a LUMP-SUM RETIRAL SOCIAL SECURITY BENEFIT paid by the employer at the time of termination of an employee's service (retirement, superannuation, resignation, death or disablement), IN CONSIDERATION OF PAST SERVICES RENDERED. The Supreme Court in D.S. Nakara v. Union of India described it as a social welfare measure rendering socio-economic justice. CONTINUOUS SERVICE — SECTION 2A

question_html: Under Section 2A(1), an employee is said to be in 'continuous service' for a period if his service during that period is uninterrupted. Which of the following interruptions does NOT break continuity of service?

options.A: Absence treated as break in service by standing orders after a proper order
options.B: Lay off, strike or lockout, or cessation of work not due to fault of the employee
options.C: Resignation followed by re-employment
options.D: Wilful absence for more than 30 days without leave

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Resignation followed by re-employment

Section 2A(1): Continuous service includes service INTERRUPTED on account of SICKNESS, ACCIDENT, LEAVE, ABSENCE WITHOUT LEAVE (unless an order treating it as a break in service has been passed per standing orders), LAY-OFF, STRIKE, LOCK-OUT, or CESSATION OF WORK NOT DUE TO FAULT OF THE EMPLOYEE. These do not break continuity. But absence where a formal 'break in service' order exists under standing orders DOES break continuity.
topic_text: Section 2A — Basic Rule of Continuous Service

question_html: For an employee to be deemed in continuous service for ONE YEAR (in a general establishment working 6 days a week), he must have actually worked for not less than how many days during the 12 calendar months preceding the relevant date?

options.A: 240 days
options.B: 190 days
options.C: 180 days
options.D: 120 days

answer_html:
Answer: (A) 240 days

Section 2A(2)(a)(ii): For an employee in a GENERAL ESTABLISHMENT (working 6 days a week or more), deemed continuous service for ONE YEAR requires actually working NOT LESS THAN 240 DAYS during the preceding 12 calendar months. For employees BELOW GROUND IN A MINE or establishments working LESS THAN 6 DAYS A WEEK, the requirement is 190 days. (For 6-month period: 120 days / 95 days respectively.)

question_html: For an employee working BELOW THE GROUND IN A MINE, how many days of actual work are required to be deemed in continuous service for ONE YEAR?

options.A: 240 days
options.B: 190 days
options.C: 150 days
options.D: 120 days

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 190 days

Section 2A(2)(a)(i): For an employee BELOW THE GROUND IN A MINE or in an establishment working LESS THAN 6 DAYS A WEEK, deemed continuous service for ONE YEAR requires actually working NOT LESS THAN 190 DAYS during the 12 preceding calendar months. For a 6-MONTH period, the requirement is 95 DAYS. The lower threshold reflects the inherently difficult working conditions underground.

question_html: For computing the number of 'days on which an employee has actually worked' under Section 2A, which of the following days are COUNTED?

options.A: Days of wilful absence and unpaid leave
options.B: Days of suspension pending enquiry
options.C: Days of lay-off under agreement/law, leave with full wages earned in previous year, absence due to temporary disablement from employment accident, and maternity leave (up to 26 weeks)
options.D: Days of illegal strike and lockout caused by the employer

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Days of lay-off under agreement/law, leave with full wages earned in previous year, absence due to temporary disablement from employment accident, and maternity leave (up to 26 weeks)

Section 2A Explanation: Days COUNTED as actually worked include: (i) DAYS OF LAY-OFF under agreement/Standing Orders/ID Act; (ii) LEAVE WITH FULL WAGES earned in previous year; (iii) ABSENCE DUE TO TEMPORARY DISABLEMENT caused by accident arising out of and in the course of employment; and (iv) MATERNITY LEAVE not exceeding 26 WEEKS (amended from 12 weeks by the 2009 Amendment). Wilful absence and suspension do not count.

question_html: After the Payment of Gratuity (Amendment) Act, 2009 (in tune with the Maternity Benefit Act), what is the maximum maternity leave period that counts towards continuous service under Section 2A?

options.A: Twenty-six weeks
options.B: Twelve weeks
options.C: Sixteen weeks
options.D: Thirty-six weeks

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Twenty-six weeks

The 2009 Amendment modified the maternity leave period that counts towards continuous service from TWELVE WEEKS (under the earlier Act) to TWENTY-SIX WEEKS — aligning with the amended Maternity Benefit Act. So maternity leave of up to 26 weeks is treated as days actually worked for computing continuous service for gratuity purposes.

question_html: For an employee in a SEASONAL ESTABLISHMENT, deemed continuous service for a period requires that the employee has actually worked for not less than what percentage of the number of days the establishment was in operation during such period?

options.A: 66.67% (two-thirds)
options.B: 75% of the days the establishment was in operation
options.C: 50% of the days the establishment was in operation
options.D: 80% of the days the establishment was in operation

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 75% of the days the establishment was in operation

Section 2A(3): For an employee in a SEASONAL ESTABLISHMENT, deemed continuous service for one year or six months requires actually working for NOT LESS THAN 75% of the number of days on which the establishment was in operation during such period. The rule for seasonal establishments is different from the 240/190-day rule applicable to regular establishments.

question_html: For deemed continuous service for a period of SIX MONTHS in a general establishment (working 6 days a week), an employee must have actually worked for not less than:

options.A: 95 days
options.B: 120 days
options.C: 150 days
options.D: 180 days

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 150 days

Section 2A(2)(b)(ii): For deemed continuous service for a period of SIX MONTHS in a general establishment, an employee must have actually worked for NOT LESS THAN 120 DAYS during the preceding 6 calendar months. For employees below ground in a mine or establishments working less than 6 days a week, the requirement for a 6-month period is 95 DAYS. PAYMENT OF GRATUITY — SECTION 4

question_html: Under Section 4(1), gratuity is payable to an employee on termination of employment after he has rendered continuous service for not less than FIVE YEARS on which of the following events?

options.A: Superannuation, retirement, or resignation — but NOT on death or disablement
options.B: Superannuation, retirement, resignation, death, or disablement due to accident or disease
options.C: Only on retirement or superannuation — not resignation or death
options.D: Only on termination by the employer — not on voluntary resignation

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Superannuation, retirement, or resignation — but NOT on death or disablement

Section 4(1): Gratuity is payable on TERMINATION OF EMPLOYMENT AFTER 5 YEARS OF CONTINUOUS SERVICE on: (i) SUPERANNUATION; (ii) RETIREMENT; (iii) RESIGNATION; (iv) DEATH; or (v) DISABLEMENT DUE TO ACCIDENT OR DISEASE. Critically: the 5-year minimum is NOT REQUIRED in cases of DEATH OR DISABLEMENT — gratuity is payable even without 5 years' service in those two cases.

question_html: The completion of 5 years of continuous service is NOT required for payment of gratuity in which of the following situations?

options.A: Voluntary resignation after 4 years and 10 months of service
options.B: Death or disablement of the employee due to accident or disease
options.C: Termination of service by the employer after 3 years
options.D: Early retirement on health grounds after 4 years of service

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Death or disablement of the employee due to accident or disease

Section 4(1) Proviso: The completion of FIVE YEARS of continuous service shall NOT be necessary where the termination of employment is due to DEATH OR DISABLEMENT. In case of death, gratuity payable shall be paid to the NOMINEE, or if no nomination exists, to the HEIRS. This is one of the most tested provisions of the Gratuity Act.

question_html: Under Section 4(2), the rate at which gratuity is payable for every COMPLETED YEAR of service (or part thereof in excess of six months) is:

options.A: Ten days' wages based on last drawn wages
options.B: Twelve days' wages based on average wages
options.C: Fifteen days' wages based on the rate of wages last drawn by the employee
options.D: Thirty days' wages based on the rate of wages last drawn

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Fifteen days' wages based on the rate of wages last drawn by the employee

Section 4(2): Gratuity = FIFTEEN DAYS' WAGES based on the RATE OF WAGES LAST DRAWN by the employee for every COMPLETED YEAR OF SERVICE or PART THEREOF IN EXCESS OF SIX MONTHS. For piece-rated employees, daily wages are computed on the AVERAGE of total wages for 3 months preceding termination (excluding overtime wages). For seasonal establishments: SEVEN DAYS' WAGES per season.

question_html: The standard formula for calculation of gratuity under the Payment of Gratuity Act is:

options.A: Last wage drawn × 15/26 × completed years of service
options.B: Last wage drawn × 15/30 × completed years of service
options.C: Average wage of last 3 months × 15/26 × completed years of service
options.D: Last wage drawn × 30/26 × completed years of service

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Last wage drawn × 15/26 × completed years of service

The prescribed FORMULA for calculating gratuity is: LAST WAGE DRAWN × 15/26 × COMPLETED YEARS OF SERVICE. In calculating gratuity, ONE MONTH IS TAKEN AS 26 DAYS (not 30 days). The numerator 15 represents fifteen days' wages. This formula applies to non-seasonal establishments. For seasonal establishments, the rate is 7 days' wages per season.

question_html: An employee completes 10 years and 8 months of continuous service before retirement. For gratuity calculation, what is taken as the completed years of service?

options.A: 10 years only — the 8 months is ignored
options.B: 11 years — since 8 months exceeds 6 months, it is counted as one full year
options.C: 10.67 years — proportionate calculation is applied
options.D: 10.5 years — rounded to nearest half year

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 11 years — since 8 months exceeds 6 months, it is counted as one full year

Section 4(2): Gratuity is payable for every completed year of service or PART THEREOF IN EXCESS OF SIX MONTHS. Since 8 months > 6 months, it counts as ONE FULL ADDITIONAL YEAR. Therefore, 10 years 8 months = 11 COMPLETED YEARS for gratuity calculation. Had the service been 10 years 4 months (less than 6 months), only 10 years would be counted.
topic_text: Section 4(2) — Part Year in Excess of 6 Months

question_html: As per the notification dated 29th March 2018 under Section 4(3) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, the maximum amount of gratuity payable to an employee shall not exceed:

options.A: Rs. 10 lakhs
options.B: Rs. 15 lakhs
options.C: Rs. 20 lakhs
options.D: Rs. 25 lakhs

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Rs. 20 lakhs

Section 4(3): The amount of gratuity payable shall NOT EXCEED SUCH AMOUNT AS MAY BE NOTIFIED BY THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT. The Ministry of Labour & Employment vide Notification No. S.O. 1420(E) dated 29.03.2018 notified that the maximum gratuity amount shall not exceed RS. 20 LAKHS. The Central Government has power to revise this ceiling without amending the Act itself.

question_html: Under Section 4(5) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, if the terms of employment contract provide for a HIGHER AMOUNT of gratuity than the amount calculated under the Act, the employee is entitled to:

options.A: The statutory amount only — higher contractual gratuity is not legally recognized
options.B: The higher amount provided in the contract — the Act does not restrict better terms
options.C: An amount midway between the statutory and contractual amounts
options.D: The higher amount only after 10 years of service

answer_html:
Answer: (A) The statutory amount only — higher contractual gratuity is not legally recognized

Section 4(5): Nothing in Section 4 shall affect the RIGHT OF AN EMPLOYEE TO RECEIVE BETTER TERMS OF GRATUITY under any award, agreement, or CONTRACT WITH THE EMPLOYER. If the employment contract provides a higher gratuity than the statutory formula, the employee is entitled to the HIGHER AMOUNT. The Act provides a minimum floor — employers may offer more.

question_html: Under Section 4(4), for computing gratuity payable to an employee who is employed AFTER DISABLEMENT on reduced wages, how are wages computed for the pre-disablement period?

options.A: Average wages across entire service period
options.B: Wages actually received during the period preceding disablement — not the reduced post-disablement wages
options.C: The reduced wages applicable after disablement for the entire service period
options.D: The higher of pre-disablement and post-disablement wages

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Wages actually received during the period preceding disablement — not the reduced post-disablement wages

Section 4(4): For an employee employed AFTER DISABLEMENT ON REDUCED WAGES: (a) wages for the PERIOD PRECEDING disablement = wages received DURING THAT PERIOD (higher); (b) wages for the PERIOD SUBSEQUENT to disablement = the REDUCED wages. This bifurcated approach ensures the employee is not doubly penalized for the disablement when computing the pre-disablement portion of gratuity.

question_html: For a PIECE-RATED employee, how is the 'daily wage' calculated for purposes of computing gratuity under Section 4(2)?

options.A: Average of total wages received during 12 months before termination
options.B: The rate fixed by the appropriate Government for such category of work
options.C: Average of total wages received during 3 months immediately preceding termination of employment (excluding overtime wages)
options.D: The minimum wage applicable to that category of work

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Average of total wages received during 3 months immediately preceding termination of employment (excluding overtime wages)

Section 4(2): For a PIECE-RATED EMPLOYEE, daily wages for gratuity computation shall be the AVERAGE OF TOTAL WAGES RECEIVED BY HIM FOR A PERIOD OF THREE MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING the termination of employment. Importantly, WAGES PAID FOR OVERTIME WORK SHALL NOT BE TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT while computing this average.

question_html: In the case of an employee employed in a SEASONAL ESTABLISHMENT, the gratuity rate payable under Section 4(2) is:

options.A: Fifteen days' wages for each completed year of service
options.B: Seven days' wages for each season
options.C: Ten days' wages for each completed season
options.D: Thirty days' wages for each completed year

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Fifteen days' wages for each completed year of service

Section 4(2): For an employee employed in a SEASONAL ESTABLISHMENT, the employer shall pay gratuity at the rate of SEVEN DAYS' WAGES FOR EACH SEASON (not fifteen days). This is the only exception to the standard 15-day rule. A seasonal establishment operates for a specific season (e.g., sugarcane factories, tea gardens in harvest season). FORFEITURE OF GRATUITY — SECTION 4(6)

question_html: Under Section 4(6), in which situation can the ENTIRE gratuity be WHOLLY OR PARTIALLY forfeited?

options.A: If the employee absents himself for more than 30 days without leave
options.B: If services are terminated for riotous or disorderly conduct, other act of violence, OR any act constituting an offence involving moral turpitude committed in the course of employment
options.C: If the employee gives only 7 days' notice instead of 30 days before resignation
options.D: If the employee joins a competitor company immediately after resignation

answer_html:
Answer: (B) If services are terminated for riotous or disorderly conduct, other act of violence, OR any act constituting an offence involving moral turpitude committed in the course of employment

Section 4(6)(b): Gratuity may be WHOLLY OR PARTIALLY FORFEITED if services are terminated for: (i) RIOTOUS OR DISORDERLY CONDUCT or any other ACT OF VIOLENCE; or (ii) any act constituting an OFFENCE INVOLVING MORAL TURPITUDE committed IN THE COURSE OF EMPLOYMENT. Section 4(6)(a): Gratuity is forfeited to the extent of damage/loss if services are terminated for willful act/negligence causing damage to employer's property.

question_html: Under Section 4(6)(a), if an employee's services are terminated for any act, willful omission or negligence causing DAMAGE OR LOSS to the employer's property, the gratuity shall be forfeited:

options.A: Entirely regardless of the extent of damage
options.B: To the extent of 50% of the gratuity amount as a standard rule
options.C: To the extent of the damage or loss so caused — not necessarily the entire gratuity
options.D: Only after conviction by a court of law

answer_html:
Answer: (C) To the extent of the damage or loss so caused — not necessarily the entire gratuity

Section 4(6)(a): Gratuity of an employee whose services are terminated for any act, willful omission or negligence causing damage/loss to or DESTRUCTION OF PROPERTY belonging to the employer shall be FORFEITED TO THE EXTENT OF THE DAMAGE OR LOSS SO CAUSED — not necessarily the full gratuity. The employer must prove the extent of damage. A show-cause notice must be issued and a reasonable opportunity of hearing given before forfeiture.

question_html: The right to receive gratuity under the Payment of Gratuity Act is best described as:

options.A: A statutory right that cannot be withheld except under the specific exceptions in Section 4(6)
options.B: A contractual right depending entirely on the terms of employment
options.C: An ex gratia payment at the employer's discretion
options.D: A right that can be waived by the employee during service

answer_html:
Answer: (A) A statutory right that cannot be withheld except under the specific exceptions in Section 4(6)

The Supreme Court in D.S. Nakara v. Union of India (1982) and D.V. Kapoor v. Union of India (1990) held that the right to gratuity is a STATUTORY RIGHT. The Karnataka High Court in KSRTC v. Deputy Labour Commissioner (2014) confirmed: RIGHT TO GRATUITY IS A STATUTORY RIGHT AND CANNOT BE WITHHELD UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES EXCEPT FOR THE EXCEPTIONS IN SECTION 4(6). Withholding gratuity as punishment (without statutory authorization) is illegal.

question_html: Before forfeiting gratuity (partially or fully) under Section 4(6), the employer must:

options.A: Obtain prior approval from the Controlling Authority
options.B: Issue a show cause notice to the employee indicating grounds for forfeiture and give a reasonable opportunity of being heard
options.C: File a complaint with the appropriate Government
options.D: Only inform the employee by ordinary post

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Issue a show cause notice to the employee indicating grounds for forfeiture and give a reasonable opportunity of being heard

Before forfeiting gratuity either partially or fully, the employer shall ISSUE A SHOW CAUSE NOTICE to the employee indicating the grounds for forfeiture and shall GIVE A REASONABLE OPPORTUNITY OF BEING HEARD. The final decision is taken on the basis of the employee's reply. The Karnataka HC in KSRTC v. Deputy Labour Commissioner held that the employer was required to extend an opportunity of hearing before forfeiting the gratuity amount.

question_html: An employee commits an offence of moral turpitude OUTSIDE the workplace and unrelated to his employment. Can his gratuity be forfeited under Section 4(6)?

options.A: Yes — any offence of moral turpitude by an employee justifies forfeiture
options.B: Yes — if he is convicted by a court of law
options.C: No — the offence must be committed IN THE COURSE OF EMPLOYMENT for forfeiture to apply under Section 4(6)(b)
options.D: Yes — if the employer obtains prior court approval

answer_html:
Answer: (C) No — the offence must be committed IN THE COURSE OF EMPLOYMENT for forfeiture to apply under Section 4(6)(b)

Section 4(6)(b): Forfeiture for an offence involving moral turpitude is permissible ONLY if such offence is committed BY HIM IN THE COURSE OF HIS EMPLOYMENT. An offence committed OUTSIDE the course of employment and unrelated to the workplace does NOT attract forfeiture under Section 4(6)(b). This is a critical limitation on the forfeiture provision. NOMINATION — SECTION 6 & RULE 6

question_html: Under Section 6 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, every employee who has completed ONE YEAR of service shall make a nomination in which Form?

options.A: Form F
options.B: Form I
options.C: Form J
options.D: Form N

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Form F

Section 6 and Rule 6: Every employee who has completed ONE YEAR OF SERVICE shall make a NOMINATION in FORM F. This nomination determines who receives the gratuity after the employee's death. Rule 6(1): The nomination shall be submitted within NINETY DAYS for existing employees (from commencement of rules) and within THIRTY DAYS for new employees completing one year (from date of completion).

question_html: Under Section 6, if an employee HAS A FAMILY at the time of making a nomination, the nomination must be made in favour of:

options.A: Any person of his choice — family or non-family
options.B: One or more members of his family ONLY — nomination in favour of a non-family member shall be void
options.C: Only one member of his family — splitting nomination is not allowed
options.D: A charitable institution or trust only

answer_html:
Answer: (B) One or more members of his family ONLY — nomination in favour of a non-family member shall be void

Section 6: If an employee HAS A FAMILY at the time of making a nomination, the nomination SHALL BE MADE IN FAVOUR OF ONE OR MORE MEMBERS OF HIS FAMILY, and any nomination in favour of a PERSON WHO IS NOT A MEMBER OF HIS FAMILY SHALL BE VOID. However, if the employee has NO FAMILY at the time of nomination, he may nominate any person — but the nomination becomes INVALID if he subsequently acquires a family.

question_html: An employee makes a nomination in favour of a friend when he has no family. He later gets married. What happens to his earlier nomination?

options.A: The nomination remains valid and the friend will receive the gratuity on the employee's death
options.B: The nomination remains valid until the employee formally cancels it
options.C: The nomination automatically becomes INVALID on acquiring a family, and the employee must make a FRESH NOMINATION in favour of a family member within the prescribed time
options.D: The nomination becomes partially valid — the gratuity will be shared between the friend and the wife

answer_html:
Answer: (C) The nomination automatically becomes INVALID on acquiring a family, and the employee must make a FRESH NOMINATION in favour of a family member within the prescribed time

Section 6: If the employee has NO FAMILY at the time of nomination, he may nominate any person. But if he SUBSEQUENTLY ACQUIRES A FAMILY, such nomination shall FORTHWITH BECOME INVALID and he shall make, within the PRESCRIBED TIME, a FRESH NOMINATION in favour of one or more members of his family. Rule 6(3) requires submission of fresh nomination in Form G within NINETY DAYS of acquiring a family.

question_html: Under Section 6, if a nominee predeceases the employee, what happens to the nomination?

options.A: The interest of the predeceased nominee reverts to the employee, who must make a fresh nomination in the prescribed form
options.B: The gratuity passes to the legal heirs of the deceased nominee
options.C: The nomination is automatically transferred to the next of kin
options.D: The gratuity is deposited with the Controlling Authority permanently

answer_html:
Answer: (A) The interest of the predeceased nominee reverts to the employee, who must make a fresh nomination in the prescribed form

Section 6: If a NOMINEE PREDECEASES the employee, the INTEREST OF THE NOMINEE shall REVERT TO THE EMPLOYEE, who shall make a FRESH NOMINATION (in the prescribed form) in respect of such interest. Rule 6(4): A notice of modification of nomination (including where a nominee predeceases) shall be submitted in duplicate in FORM H to the employer.

question_html: Under Rule 6(2), within how many days of receiving a nomination in Form F must the employer verify the service particulars and return the attested duplicate to the employee?

options.A: 15 days
options.B: 30 days
options.C: 60 days
options.D: 90 days

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 30 days

Rule 6(2): Within THIRTY DAYS of receipt of nomination in Form F, the employer shall: (a) get the SERVICE PARTICULARS of the employee VERIFIED with reference to establishment records; and (b) return to the employee, after obtaining a receipt, the DUPLICATE COPY OF THE NOMINATION IN FORM F duly ATTESTED by the employer or authorised officer. The other copy is recorded by the employer.
topic_text: Rule 6 — Employer's Duty After Receiving Nomination

question_html: Under Rule 6(5), if a nomination, fresh nomination or notice of modification of nomination is made by an ILLITERATE employee, it shall bear his thumb impression. This must be done in the presence of:

options.A: Only the employer or his authorized officer
options.B: The Controlling Authority alone
options.C: Two witnesses who shall also sign a declaration to that effect in the nomination
options.D: A Magistrate or Notary Public

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Two witnesses who shall also sign a declaration to that effect in the nomination

Rule 6(5): A nomination (or fresh nomination or notice of modification) shall be signed by the employee or, if ILLITERATE, shall bear his THUMB IMPRESSION in the presence of TWO WITNESSES WHO SHALL ALSO SIGN A DECLARATION to that effect in the nomination. Rule 6(6): The nomination takes effect from the DATE OF RECEIPT THEREOF BY THE EMPLOYER. DETERMINATION, PAYMENT, INTEREST & DISPUTES — SECTIONS 7, 8

question_html: Under Section 7, when gratuity becomes payable, the employer shall determine the amount and give notice in Form L. Within how many days must the employer PAY the gratuity?

options.A: Within 30 days from the date it became payable
options.B: Within 60 days from the date it became payable
options.C: Within 15 days from the date of application
options.D: Within 45 days from the date it became payable

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Within 30 days from the date it became payable

Section 7: The employer shall DETERMINE the amount of gratuity (whether or not the employee has applied) and shall ARRANGE TO PAY within 30 DAYS from the date of its BECOMING PAYABLE. If not paid within 30 days, the employer is liable to pay INTEREST AT 10% PER ANNUM. Interest is not payable if the delay is due to the employee's fault AND the employer has obtained written permission from the Controlling Authority.
topic_text: Section 7 — Employer's Duty on Gratuity Becoming Payable

question_html: If the employer fails to pay gratuity within the stipulated 30-day period, the rate of interest payable under Section 7 is:

options.A: 6% per annum
options.B: 10% per annum
options.C: 12% per annum
options.D: 18% per annum

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 10% per annum

Section 7: If gratuity is not paid within the stipulated period (30 days from becoming payable), the employer is liable to pay INTEREST AT THE RATE OF 10% PER ANNUM from the date of expiry of the prescribed time until actual payment. Note: No interest is payable if the delay is due to the FAULT OF THE EMPLOYEE and the employer has OBTAINED WRITTEN PERMISSION from the Controlling Authority for delayed payment.

question_html: Under Rule 7(1), an employee eligible for gratuity shall ordinarily apply to the employer in Form I within how many days from the date gratuity became payable?

options.A: 15 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 90 days

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 30 days

Rule 7(1): An employee (or authorised person on his behalf) shall apply ORDINARILY WITHIN THIRTY DAYS from the date gratuity became payable, in FORM I to the employer. Where the date of superannuation/retirement is KNOWN IN ADVANCE, the employee may apply BEFORE THIRTY DAYS of that date. Rule 7(5): A belated application shall also be entertained if the applicant shows SUFFICIENT CAUSE for the delay.

question_html: Under Rule 7, within what period must a LEGAL HEIR (not a nominee) ordinarily apply for payment of gratuity in Form K?

options.A: Within one year from the date gratuity became payable
options.B: Within thirty days from the date gratuity became payable
options.C: Within sixty days from the date of death of the employee
options.D: Within three years — as per general limitation law

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Within one year from the date gratuity became payable

Rule 7: Nominee (Form J) — ordinarily within THIRTY DAYS from date gratuity became payable. LEGAL HEIR (Form K) — ordinarily within ONE YEAR from the date gratuity became payable. Employee (Form I) — within THIRTY DAYS. All these are ordinary time limits — belated applications with sufficient cause shall also be entertained.
topic_text: Rule 7 — Nominee & Legal Heir Application Period

question_html: Under Rule 8, within how many days of receiving an application for gratuity must the employer respond by issuing either Form L (admissibility notice) or Form M (non-admissibility notice)?

options.A: 7 days
options.B: 15 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 45 days

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 15 days

Rule 8(1): Within FIFTEEN DAYS of receipt of an application under Rule 7, the employer shall: (i) if admissible — issue FORM L specifying the gratuity amount and fixing a date for payment (not later than the 30th day after receipt of application); or (ii) if not admissible — issue FORM M specifying the reasons. In EITHER CASE, a copy of the notice shall be ENDORSED TO THE CONTROLLING AUTHORITY.

question_html: Under Section 8, if an employer fails to pay gratuity within the prescribed time, the controlling authority shall, on application by the aggrieved person, issue a certificate for the amount to the Collector. The Collector recovers the amount together with compound interest at what rate?

options.A: 6% per annum
options.B: 8% per annum
options.C: 9% per annum
options.D: 12% per annum

answer_html:
Answer: (C) 9% per annum

Section 8: If gratuity payable is not paid by the employer within the prescribed time, the Controlling Authority shall, on application by the aggrieved person, ISSUE A CERTIFICATE to the COLLECTOR (District Magistrate), who shall recover the same together with COMPOUND INTEREST AT 9% PER ANNUM from the date of expiry of the prescribed time, as ARREARS OF LAND REVENUE. Note the distinction: 10% simple interest under Section 7 for delayed payment; 9% compound interest under Section 8 for recovery via Collector. CONTROLLING AUTHORITY, APPEAL & NOTICES — RULES 10, 11

question_html: Under Rule 10, if an employer refuses to accept nomination, or rejects gratuity eligibility, or fails to issue notice, the aggrieved person may file an application in Form N to the Controlling Authority within:

options.A: 90 days from the date of occurrence of the cause
options.B: 30 days from the date of occurrence of the cause
options.C: 60 days from the date of occurrence of the cause
options.D: 6 months from the date of occurrence of the cause

answer_html:
Answer: (A) 90 days from the date of occurrence of the cause

Rule 10: The eligible person may file an application in FORM N within NINETY DAYS from the date of occurrence of the cause (employer's refusal to accept nomination, failure to entertain gratuity application, rejection of eligibility, indicating less amount, or failing to issue notice). If filed after 90 days, the Controlling Authority may still admit with SUFFICIENT CAUSE for the delay. Application may be submitted personally or by REGISTERED POST WITH ACKNOWLEDGEMENT DUE.

question_html: Under Section 7, any person aggrieved by an order of the Controlling Authority may prefer an appeal within how many days from the date of receipt of the order?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 90 days
options.D: 120 days

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 60 days

Section 7 (Appeal): Any person aggrieved by an order may prefer an appeal to the appropriate Government or such other authority as may be specified, within SIXTY DAYS from the date of receipt of the order. The appellate authority may condone delay if the appellant was prevented by SUFFICIENT CAUSE from filing within 60 days — and may further extend the period by a FURTHER 60 DAYS. The appellate authority may confirm, modify or reverse the Controlling Authority's decision.

question_html: For conducting an inquiry, the Controlling Authority under the Payment of Gratuity Act has the same powers as a court under the Code of Civil Procedure in respect of which of the following matters?

options.A: Sentencing persons to imprisonment
options.B: Imposing fines on parties to the dispute
options.C: Enforcing attendance and examining on oath, requiring discovery/production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavit, and issuing commissions for examination of witnesses
options.D: Attaching and selling property of the employer

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Enforcing attendance and examining on oath, requiring discovery/production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavit, and issuing commissions for examination of witnesses

For conducting an inquiry, the Controlling Authority has the SAME POWERS AS A COURT UNDER CPC in respect of: (i) ENFORCING ATTENDANCE of any person or EXAMINING HIM ON OATH; (ii) REQUIRING DISCOVERY AND PRODUCTION OF DOCUMENTS; (iii) RECEIVING EVIDENCE ON AFFIDAVIT; and (iv) ISSUING COMMISSIONS FOR EXAMINATION OF WITNESSES. These powers ensure the Authority can conduct a thorough, quasi-judicial inquiry. PENALTIES, PROTECTION & MISCELLANEOUS — SECTIONS 9, 10, 11, 13

question_html: Under Section 9(2) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, where the offence relates to NON-PAYMENT of any gratuity payable, the minimum imprisonment prescribed (unless court records reasons for a lesser term) is:

options.A: Not less than three months
options.B: Not less than six months
options.C: Not less than one year
options.D: Not less than one month

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Not less than three months

Section 9(2): An employer who contravenes any provision of the Act — imprisonment up to ONE YEAR or fine up to Rs. 1,000 or both. Specifically, WHERE THE OFFENCE RELATES TO NON-PAYMENT OF GRATUITY, the employer shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term NOT LESS THAN THREE MONTHS, UNLESS the court, FOR REASONS TO BE RECORDED IN WRITING, is of opinion that a lesser term or fine would meet the ends of justice. Section 9(1): False statement — imprisonment up to SIX MONTHS or fine up to Rs. 1,000 or both.
topic_text: Section 9 — Penalty for Non-Payment of Gratuity

question_html: Under Section 11 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, what is the minimum level of court that can try an offence under the Act?

options.A: Any Executive Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate Second Class
options.B: A Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the First Class
options.C: The High Court only
options.D: A Civil Court of first instance

answer_html:
Answer: (B) A Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the First Class

Section 11: No court shall take cognizance of any offence under the Gratuity Act SAVE ON A COMPLAINT MADE BY OR UNDER AUTHORITY OF THE APPROPRIATE GOVERNMENT. Where gratuity has not been paid or recovered within SIX MONTHS from expiry of the prescribed time, the appropriate Government shall authorize the Controlling Authority to file a complaint, which must be done within FIFTEEN DAYS of such authorization. NO COURT INFERIOR TO A PRESIDENCY MAGISTRATE OR MAGISTRATE OF THE FIRST CLASS shall try any offence under the Act.

question_html: Under Section 13 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, the gratuity payable to an employee:

options.A: Can be attached by a civil court to recover housing loan dues
options.B: Can be attached only by a revenue court for income tax arrears
options.C: Shall NOT be liable to attachment in execution of any decree or order of any civil, revenue or criminal court
options.D: Can be attached with prior permission from the Controlling Authority

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Shall NOT be liable to attachment in execution of any decree or order of any civil, revenue or criminal court

Section 13: NO GRATUITY PAYABLE UNDER THIS ACT SHALL BE LIABLE TO ATTACHMENT in execution of any DECREE OR ORDER OF ANY CIVIL, REVENUE OR CRIMINAL COURT. This absolute protection ensures the employee's (or nominee's) right to receive gratuity is not defeated by creditors attaching it through court proceedings. This is similar to Section 10 of the EPF Act which protects PF accumulations. CONSOLIDATED ANSWER KEY — ALL 50 QUESTIONS — END OF QUESTION PAPER — Prepared from ICMAI Study Module | Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 | Module 8 | Syllabus 2022 | CMA Inter June 2026
topic_text: Section 13 — Protection of Gratuity from Attachment

question_html: Under Section 23 of the Companies Act, 2013, a PUBLIC COMPANY may issue securities in which of the following ways?

options.A: Only through a public offer via prospectus — no other method is permitted
options.B: (i) To the public through a PROSPECTUS; (ii) through PRIVATE PLACEMENT; (iii) through a RIGHTS ISSUE or BONUS ISSUE (for listed companies, also as per SEBI Act and regulations)
options.C: Only through private placement and rights issue — not through a prospectus
options.D: Only through a rights issue to existing shareholders

answer_html:
Answer: (B) (i) To the public through a PROSPECTUS; (ii) through PRIVATE PLACEMENT; (iii) through a RIGHTS ISSUE or BONUS ISSUE (for listed companies, also as per SEBI Act and regulations)

Section 23(1): A PUBLIC COMPANY may issue securities: (a) to public through PROSPECTUS (Part I of Chapter III); (b) through PRIVATE PLACEMENT (Part II of Chapter III); (c) through RIGHTS ISSUE or BONUS ISSUE per the Act and, for listed companies, also per the SEBI Act. Section 23(2): A PRIVATE COMPANY may issue securities: (a) by way of RIGHTS ISSUE or BONUS ISSUE per the Act; or (b) through PRIVATE PLACEMENT. PUBLIC OFFER includes: IPO, FPO, or offer for sale by existing shareholders through a prospectus.
topic_text: Section 23 — Methods of Issue of Securities by Companies

question_html: Under Section 26 of the Companies Act, 2013, which of the following is CORRECT regarding the validity of a prospectus?

options.A: A prospectus is valid for 180 days after the date on which a copy is delivered to the Registrar
options.B: A prospectus must be delivered to the Registrar BEFORE the date of its publication, signed by every person named as director or proposed director; it is NOT VALID if issued more than 90 DAYS after delivery of copy to Registrar
options.C: A prospectus is valid for one year from the date of registration with SEBI
options.D: A prospectus is valid as long as the offer remains open

answer_html:
Answer: (C) A prospectus is valid for one year from the date of registration with SEBI

Section 26: (1) No prospectus shall be issued UNLESS on or BEFORE the date of publication, a copy thereof has been DELIVERED TO THE REGISTRAR FOR REGISTRATION, signed by every PERSON NAMED AS DIRECTOR OR PROPOSED DIRECTOR (or their duly authorised attorney); (2) No prospectus shall be VALID if issued more than 90 DAYS after the date on which a copy was delivered to the Registrar; (3) Penalty for contravention: Company — fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 50,000 up to RS. 3 LAKHS; Person — imprisonment up to 3 YEARS or fine Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 3 LAKHS or BOTH.

question_html: Under Section 27, a company shall NOT vary the terms of a contract referred to in a prospectus or the objects for which the prospectus was issued except by:

options.A: A SPECIAL RESOLUTION THROUGH POSTAL BALLOT approved by the company in general meeting — dissenting shareholders must be given an exit offer by promoters/controlling shareholders as per SEBI regulations
options.B: An ordinary resolution at a general meeting with a simple majority
options.C: Prior approval of the National Company Law Tribunal
options.D: A board resolution passed with unanimous consent of all directors

answer_html:
Answer: (A) A SPECIAL RESOLUTION THROUGH POSTAL BALLOT approved by the company in general meeting — dissenting shareholders must be given an exit offer by promoters/controlling shareholders as per SEBI regulations

Section 27: A company shall NOT vary the terms of a contract referred to in the prospectus or the OBJECTS for which the prospectus was issued — except by SPECIAL RESOLUTION THROUGH POSTAL BALLOT. Notice for the special resolution (per Rule 7(1)) must contain: original purpose, total money raised, money utilised, extent of achievement, UNUTILISED AMOUNT, proposed variation, reasons/justification, proposed time limit, risk factors, and other relevant information. The company shall NOT use prospectus funds for BUYING/TRADING/DEALING IN EQUITY SHARES OF ANY OTHER LISTED COMPANY. DISSENTING SHAREHOLDERS get an EXIT OFFER by promoters/controlling shareholders per SEBI regulations.
topic_text: Section 27 — Variation in Terms of Contract/Objects in Prospectus

question_html: Under Section 28, when certain members offer shares to the public (offer of sale), all laws applicable to a prospectus apply EXCEPT which of the following?

options.A: Provisions relating to allotment of shares and minimum subscription
options.B: Provisions relating to MINIMUM SUBSCRIPTION; provisions for MINIMUM APPLICATION VALUE; provisions requiring statement by Board of Directors regarding UTILIZATION OF MONEY; and any other provision that cannot be complied with by the offeror
options.C: Provisions requiring the prospectus to be signed by directors
options.D: Provisions relating to filing of the prospectus with SEBI

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Provisions relating to MINIMUM SUBSCRIPTION; provisions for MINIMUM APPLICATION VALUE; provisions requiring statement by Board of Directors regarding UTILIZATION OF MONEY; and any other provision that cannot be complied with by the offeror

Section 28: Members may offer whole or part of their shares to the public in consultation with the Board. Such offer of sale is DEEMED TO BE A PROSPECTUS ISSUED BY THE COMPANY — all laws applicable to a prospectus apply EXCEPT: (a) provisions relating to MINIMUM SUBSCRIPTION; (b) provisions for MINIMUM APPLICATION VALUE; (c) provisions requiring statement by Board of Directors regarding UTILIZATION OF MONEY; and (d) any other provision or information which CANNOT BE COMPILED OR GATHERED by the offeror (with justification). The prospectus shall disclose the name of the person/entity bearing the COST OF MAKING THE OFFER along with reasons.
topic_text: Section 28 — Offer for Sale: Exceptions to Normal Prospectus Rules

question_html: Under Section 29, which company is MANDATORILY required to issue securities only in dematerialised form?

options.A: Only listed companies making a rights issue
options.B: Only government companies making public offers
options.C: EVERY COMPANY MAKING A PUBLIC OFFER and such other class of public companies as prescribed — must issue securities only in DEMATERIALISED FORM per the Depositories Act, 1996; promoters' convertible securities must be in demat form before IPO; since December 2018, even unlisted shares cannot be transferred except through demat mode
options.D: Only private companies with more than 100 shareholders

answer_html:
Answer: (C) EVERY COMPANY MAKING A PUBLIC OFFER and such other class of public companies as prescribed — must issue securities only in DEMATERIALISED FORM per the Depositories Act, 1996; promoters' convertible securities must be in demat form before IPO; since December 2018, even unlisted shares cannot be transferred except through demat mode

Section 29: EVERY COMPANY MAKING A PUBLIC OFFER (and prescribed classes of public companies) shall issue securities ONLY IN DEMATERIALISED FORM per the Depositories Act, 1996. PROMOTERS of every public company making a public offer of any CONVERTIBLE SECURITIES may hold such securities only in DEMATERIALISED FORM — entire holding of convertible securities in PHYSICAL FORM must be CONVERTED INTO DEMAT FORM before the IPO. From DECEMBER 2018: MCA ordered that no TRANSFER OF SHARES — even in case of UNLISTED SHARES — can be effected other than through DEMATERIALISED MODE.
topic_text: Section 29 — Dematerialized Form for Public Offer

question_html: Under Section 30, when an advertisement of any prospectus is published in any manner, the advertisement MUST specify:

options.A: CONTENT OF ITS MEMORANDUM as regards the objects, the liability of members, the amount of share capital of the company; names of signatories to the memorandum; and number of shares subscribed for by each signatory, and its capital structure
options.B: Only the subscription price and allotment date
options.C: Only the names of directors and the promoters
options.D: Only the registered office address and CIN

answer_html:
Answer: (A) CONTENT OF ITS MEMORANDUM as regards the objects, the liability of members, the amount of share capital of the company; names of signatories to the memorandum; and number of shares subscribed for by each signatory, and its capital structure

Section 30: When an advertisement of any prospectus is published, it is necessary to specify therein: (1) CONTENT OF ITS MEMORANDUM as regards the OBJECTS, the LIABILITY OF MEMBERS and the AMOUNT OF SHARE CAPITAL of the company; (2) NAMES OF SIGNATORIES to the memorandum; (3) NUMBER OF SHARES SUBSCRIBED FOR by each signatory; and (4) its CAPITAL STRUCTURE. This ensures the advertisement gives prospective investors essential constitutional information about the company.

question_html: Under Section 31, a 'shelf prospectus' is a prospectus in respect of which securities are issued for subscription in one or more issues over a certain period without issuing a further prospectus. What is the MAXIMUM PERIOD OF VALIDITY of a shelf prospectus?

options.A: Three years from the date of opening of first offer
options.B: NOT EXCEEDING ONE YEAR from the date of opening of the first offer of securities; for a second or subsequent offer during this period, no further prospectus is required; but an information memorandum must be filed before each subsequent offer; refund of money within 15 DAYS if applicant withdraws on material change
options.C: Six months from the date of registration with the Registrar
options.D: Two years from the date of SEBI approval

answer_html:
Answer: (B) NOT EXCEEDING ONE YEAR from the date of opening of the first offer of securities; for a second or subsequent offer during this period, no further prospectus is required; but an information memorandum must be filed before each subsequent offer; refund of money within 15 DAYS if applicant withdraws on material change

Section 31: SHELF PROSPECTUS: Validity period = NOT EXCEEDING ONE YEAR from the date of OPENING OF FIRST OFFER of securities. For second or subsequent offer during this period — NO FURTHER PROSPECTUS REQUIRED. Before each subsequent offer: company must file INFORMATION MEMORANDUM containing all MATERIAL FACTS relating to new charges, changes in financial position, etc. with the Registrar. Where applicants received applications + advance subscription before a change: company must INTIMATE THE CHANGE; if they express desire to WITHDRAW, company shall REFUND ALL MONIES WITHIN 15 DAYS. Information memorandum + shelf prospectus together = DEEMED TO BE A PROSPECTUS.

question_html: Section 32 defines a 'red herring prospectus' as a prospectus which does NOT include complete particulars of the quantum or price of securities. When must a red herring prospectus be filed with the Registrar?

options.A: Within 30 days before the opening of the subscription list
options.B: At least 7 days before opening of the subscription list
options.C: AT LEAST THREE DAYS PRIOR TO THE OPENING OF THE SUBSCRIPTION LIST AND THE OFFER; variations between the red herring and final prospectus must be highlighted; at closing of offer, final prospectus stating total capital raised, closing price and other details must be filed with the Registrar AND SEBI
options.D: On the same date as the opening of the offer

answer_html:
Answer: (C) AT LEAST THREE DAYS PRIOR TO THE OPENING OF THE SUBSCRIPTION LIST AND THE OFFER; variations between the red herring and final prospectus must be highlighted; at closing of offer, final prospectus stating total capital raised, closing price and other details must be filed with the Registrar AND SEBI

Section 32: RED HERRING PROSPECTUS = a prospectus which does NOT include COMPLETE PARTICULARS OF THE QUANTUM OR PRICE of the securities. A company proposing to make an offer may issue it PRIOR TO THE ISSUE OF A PROSPECTUS. Filed with Registrar AT LEAST THREE DAYS PRIOR TO OPENING of the subscription list and offer. Carries the SAME OBLIGATIONS as a prospectus. VARIATIONS between red herring and prospectus must be HIGHLIGHTED in the prospectus. At CLOSING OF OFFER: final prospectus (stating total capital raised, closing price, other details) filed with REGISTRAR AND SEBI.

question_html: Under Section 33(1), no form of application for purchase of securities of a company shall be issued UNLESS it is accompanied by an ABRIDGED PROSPECTUS. This requirement does NOT apply in which situations?

options.A: (i) When the application form is issued in connection with a BONA FIDE INVITATION TO A PERSON TO ENTER INTO AN UNDERWRITING AGREEMENT in respect of such securities; OR (ii) when the securities were NOT OFFERED TO THE PUBLIC
options.B: Only when the company is a government company
options.C: Only when the securities are preference shares
options.D: When the offer is to institutional investors only

answer_html:
Answer: (A) (i) When the application form is issued in connection with a BONA FIDE INVITATION TO A PERSON TO ENTER INTO AN UNDERWRITING AGREEMENT in respect of such securities; OR (ii) when the securities were NOT OFFERED TO THE PUBLIC

Section 33(1): NO APPLICATION FORM for purchase of company's securities shall be issued unless accompanied by an ABRIDGED PROSPECTUS. EXCEPTIONS: (a) Application form issued in connection with a BONA FIDE INVITATION TO ENTER INTO AN UNDERWRITING AGREEMENT; or (b) Relation to securities NOT OFFERED TO THE PUBLIC. Section 33(2): Any person may request a COPY OF THE PROSPECTUS before closing of subscription list — company shall furnish it. Section 33(3): Default in compliance = company liable to penalty of RS. 50,000 FOR EACH DEFAULT.

question_html: Under Section 34, where a prospectus includes any UNTRUE STATEMENT or MISLEADING information, every person who AUTHORISED the issue of such prospectus is liable under Section 447 (Fraud). Criminal liability does NOT arise if the person proves:

options.A: That he was not a director at the time of issue of the prospectus
options.B: CRIMINAL LIABILITY DOES NOT ARISE if the person proves: (i) the statement or omission was IMMATERIAL; OR (ii) he had REASONABLE GROUNDS TO BELIEVE and DID BELIEVE UP TO THE TIME OF ISSUE that the statement was TRUE or the inclusion/omission was NECESSARY
options.C: That he had disclosed the mis-statement to SEBI before the prospectus was issued
options.D: That he was only an independent director with no executive role

answer_html:
Answer: (B) CRIMINAL LIABILITY DOES NOT ARISE if the person proves: (i) the statement or omission was IMMATERIAL; OR (ii) he had REASONABLE GROUNDS TO BELIEVE and DID BELIEVE UP TO THE TIME OF ISSUE that the statement was TRUE or the inclusion/omission was NECESSARY

Section 34: CRIMINAL LIABILITY for untrue/misleading prospectus: Every person who AUTHORISED the issue of such prospectus = liable under SECTION 447 (Fraud). DEFENCES: Criminal liability does NOT arise if: (i) the statement or omission was IMMATERIAL; OR (ii) he had REASONABLE GROUNDS TO BELIEVE AND DID BELIEVE UP TO THE TIME OF ISSUE that: (a) the statement was TRUE; or (b) the inclusion or omission was NECESSARY. Compare with Section 35 (CIVIL LIABILITY) — where a person has subscribed for securities based on mis-statement and suffered loss.
topic_text: Section 34 — Criminal Liability for Misstatement in Prospectus

question_html: Under Section 35, who is liable to pay COMPENSATION to a person who subscribed for securities based on a mis-statement in the prospectus and sustained loss or damage?

options.A: Only the company — individual directors and promoters are not personally liable
options.B: Only the promoters — directors are shielded
options.C: The COMPANY; every DIRECTOR at time of issue; every person named as DIRECTOR or who agreed to become director; every PROMOTER; every person who AUTHORISED THE ISSUE; and every EXPERT — with specific defences; if issued WITH INTENT TO DEFRAUD, personal responsibility WITHOUT ANY LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
options.D: Only the underwriters who guaranteed the issue

answer_html:
Answer: (C) The COMPANY; every DIRECTOR at time of issue; every person named as DIRECTOR or who agreed to become director; every PROMOTER; every person who AUTHORISED THE ISSUE; and every EXPERT — with specific defences; if issued WITH INTENT TO DEFRAUD, personal responsibility WITHOUT ANY LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

Section 35: CIVIL LIABILITY — PERSONS LIABLE: (1) the COMPANY; (2) every DIRECTOR at time of issue of prospectus; (3) person NAMED AS DIRECTOR or who agreed to become director (immediately or after interval); (4) every PROMOTER; (5) person who AUTHORISED THE ISSUE; and (6) every EXPERT. DEFENCES: (a) Withdrew consent BEFORE ISSUE and it was issued without his authority; (b) Prospectus issued WITHOUT HIS KNOWLEDGE and he gave REASONABLE PUBLIC NOTICE forthwith on becoming aware; (c) Expert's statement was correct and fair. Section 35(3): If issued WITH INTENT TO DEFRAUD — PERSONAL RESPONSIBILITY WITHOUT ANY LIMITATION OF LIABILITY for all losses.

question_html: Under Section 38, any person who makes or abets making of an application in a FICTITIOUS NAME to a company or makes MULTIPLE APPLICATIONS in different names for acquiring securities shall be:

options.A: Only liable for a civil penalty of Rs. 50,000
options.B: Liable for a fine equal to the application money paid
options.C: Liable for rejection of their application only
options.D: Liable for action under SECTION 447; court may order DISGORGEMENT OF GAIN; seizure and disposal of securities; amount credited to INVESTOR EDUCATION AND PROTECTION FUND

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only liable for a civil penalty of Rs. 50,000

Section 38: PERSONATION OFFENCES: (1) Application in FICTITIOUS NAME; (2) MULTIPLE APPLICATIONS in different names or name combinations; (3) Inducing company to allot or register transfer in fictitious name — all liable under SECTION 447. Additionally, court may order: (a) DISGORGEMENT OF GAIN made; (b) SEIZURE AND DISPOSAL OF SECURITIES in possession. Amount received through disgorgement/disposal credited to INVESTOR EDUCATION AND PROTECTION FUND. Section 38(3): These provisions shall be PROMINENTLY REPRODUCED in every PROSPECTUS and every FORM OF APPLICATION for securities. Section 36: Inducing persons to invest by false statements = Section 447 liability. ALLOTMENT OF SECURITIES — SECTIONS 39, 40
topic_text: Sections 36–38 — Fraudulent Acts Related to Securities

question_html: Under Section 39, allotment of securities can be made only if which condition is fulfilled?

options.A: The minimum subscription amount stated in the prospectus has been subscribed AND sums payable on application for that amount have been paid to and received by the company
options.B: Only that 50% of the shares are subscribed by institutional investors
options.C: Only that the company has received the minimum application money
options.D: Only that SEBI has approved the allotment

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Only that 50% of the shares are subscribed by institutional investors

Section 39: ALLOTMENT OF SECURITIES CONDITIONS: (1) The AMOUNT STATED IN THE PROSPECTUS AS THE MINIMUM AMOUNT HAS BEEN SUBSCRIBED; AND (2) The SUMS PAYABLE ON APPLICATION for the amount so stated have been PAID TO AND RECEIVED by the company by CHEQUE OR OTHER INSTRUMENT. Application money on every security = NOT LESS THAN 5% OF THE NOMINAL VALUE or such other percentage/amount as prescribed by SEBI. These conditions protect investors by ensuring sufficient subscription before allotment occurs.
topic_text: Section 39 — Conditions for Allotment of Securities

question_html: Under Section 39, if the minimum amount has NOT been subscribed and received within the prescribed period from the date of issue of the prospectus, the amount received must be returned. What are the TIME LIMITS and PENALTY for non-refund?

options.A: Returned within 30 days; penalty = Rs. 500 per day
options.B: Returned within 30 days; directors not personally liable
options.C: Returned within 60 days; penalty = Rs. 1,000 per day
options.D: Returned within 15 DAYS from CLOSURE OF ISSUE (if not subscribed within 30 days of issue of prospectus or SEBI-specified period); directors JOINTLY AND SEVERALLY liable to repay with INTEREST AT 15% PER ANNUM; penalty for default: Rs. 1,000 per day OR Rs. 1 LAKH (whichever is LESS); refund only to the bank account from which subscription was remitted

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Returned within 60 days; penalty = Rs. 1,000 per day

Section 39: REFUND OF APPLICATION MONEY: If minimum not subscribed and sum payable on application not received within 30 DAYS from date of issue of prospectus (or SEBI-specified period) — return within 15 DAYS from CLOSURE OF ISSUE. If NOT paid within time: DIRECTORS who are officers in default shall JOINTLY AND SEVERALLY be liable to repay with INTEREST AT 15% PER ANNUM. Application money to be refunded shall be CREDITED ONLY TO THE BANK ACCOUNT FROM WHICH SUBSCRIPTION WAS REMITTED. Default in filing refund: Rs. 1,000 per day OR Rs. 1 LAKH — whichever is LESS.

question_html: Under Section 39(4), within what period must a company file the RETURN OF ALLOTMENT with the Registrar after making any allotment of securities, and in which form?

options.A: Within 15 days in Form PAS-3
options.B: Within 60 days in Form PAS-1
options.C: Within 45 days in Form PAS-3
options.D: Within 30 DAYS in FORM PAS-3 along with the fee; list of allottees (names, address, occupation, number of securities allotted) CERTIFIED BY SIGNATORY as complete and correct shall be attached; penalty for default: Rs. 1,000 per day OR Rs. 1 LAKH (whichever is LESS)

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Within 15 days in Form PAS-3

Section 39(4): RETURN OF ALLOTMENT: Filed with Registrar WITHIN 30 DAYS in FORM PAS-3 along with fee. The attached list of allottees must contain: NAMES, ADDRESS, OCCUPATION (if any), and NUMBER OF SECURITIES allotted to each, CERTIFIED by the signatory as COMPLETE AND CORRECT per company records. Additional documents to be attached if applicable: contract for non-cash consideration (with stamp duty + valuation report); general meeting resolution for BONUS SHARES; valuation report for Sec.62(1)(c) shares. Default: Rs. 1,000 per day OR Rs. 1 LAKH — whichever is LESS.

question_html: Under Section 40, before making a public offer, a company must obtain PERMISSION for securities to be dealt with in stock exchanges. What must be done with APPLICATION MONEY received from the public?

options.A: Application money may be used for general company operations at the company's discretion
options.B: Application money should be deposited in any bank account of the company and used freely
options.C: Application money may only be used for paying underwriting commission
options.D: ALL MONIES received on application from the public must be kept in a SEPARATE BANK ACCOUNT IN A SCHEDULED BANK and shall NOT BE UTILISED for any purpose other than: (i) adjustment against allotment (where securities permitted to be dealt with in specified stock exchanges); or (ii) repayment of monies where company is unable to allot securities

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Application money should be deposited in any bank account of the company and used freely

Section 40: BEFORE PUBLIC OFFER: Every company making public offer must apply to one or more RECOGNISED STOCK EXCHANGES and obtain PERMISSION for securities to be dealt with. Prospectus must STATE THE NAME(S) OF STOCK EXCHANGE(S). ALL MONIES received on application = kept in a SEPARATE BANK ACCOUNT IN A SCHEDULED BANK. Shall NOT be utilised for any other purpose except: (a) ADJUSTMENT AGAINST ALLOTMENT where securities permitted to be dealt with in specified stock exchanges; or (b) REPAYMENT OF MONIES (within time specified by SEBI) where company unable to allot. Penalty [Sec.40(5)]: Company — fine Rs. 5 LAKHS to RS. 50 LAKHS; Officer — imprisonment up to 1 YEAR or fine Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 3 LAKHS or BOTH.
topic_text: Section 40 — Stock Exchange Permission & Application Money in Bank

question_html: Under Section 40(5), if default is made in complying with the provisions of Section 40 (relating to securities to be dealt with in stock exchanges), the penalty is:

options.A: Company: fine up to Rs. 1 lakh; Officers: fine up to Rs. 10,000
options.B: COMPANY: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 5 LAKHS but MAY EXTEND TO RS. 50 LAKHS; EVERY OFFICER IN DEFAULT: imprisonment up to 1 YEAR or fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 50,000 but MAY EXTEND TO RS. 3 LAKHS or BOTH
options.C: Company: fine up to Rs. 10 lakhs; Officers: imprisonment up to 2 years and fine up to Rs. 5 lakhs
options.D: Company: fine up to Rs. 25 lakhs only; no individual officer liability

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Company: fine up to Rs. 10 lakhs; Officers: imprisonment up to 2 years and fine up to Rs. 5 lakhs

Section 40(5): Penalty for default in complying with Section 40: COMPANY = fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 5 LAKHS but which may extend to RS. 50 LAKHS. EVERY OFFICER IN DEFAULT = punishable with IMPRISONMENT for a term which may extend to 1 YEAR or with fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 50,000 but which may extend to RS. 3 LAKHS or WITH BOTH. Section 40(4): Any CONDITION purporting to REQUIRE or BIND any applicant for securities to WAIVE COMPLIANCE with requirements of Section 40 = VOID.
topic_text: Section 40(5) — Penalty for Default in Sec. 40

question_html: Under Section 40(6) and Rule 13, what are the maximum rates of commission payable in connection with subscription to shares and debentures?

options.A: Shares: maximum 10%; Debentures: maximum 5%
options.B: SHARES: not exceed 5% OF THE PRICE AT WHICH SHARES ARE ISSUED or rate authorised by articles — whichever is LESS; DEBENTURES: not exceed 2.5% of the price at which debentures are issued or as specified in articles — whichever is LESS; commission authorised in AOA; payable from proceeds or profits or both; not to be paid on securities NOT OFFERED TO PUBLIC
options.C: Shares: maximum 7.5%; Debentures: maximum 3%
options.D: Shares and debentures: maximum 5% uniformly

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Shares: maximum 10%; Debentures: maximum 5%

Section 40(6) / Rule 13: COMMISSION FOR SUBSCRIPTION PROCUREMENT: CONDITIONS: (a) Authorised in AOA; (b) Commission paid from PROCEEDS OF ISSUE or PROFITS or BOTH; (c) Rate of commission: SHARES — not exceed 5% of issue price or articles rate, whichever LESS; DEBENTURES — not exceed 2.5% of issue price or articles rate, whichever LESS; (d) Prospectus must DISCLOSE: names of underwriters, rate and amount of commission, number of securities to be underwritten; (e) Commission shall NOT be paid to any underwriter on securities NOT OFFERED TO THE PUBLIC for subscription; (f) Copy of commission contract DELIVERED TO REGISTRAR at time of delivery of prospectus for registration. PRIVATE PLACEMENT — SECTION 42

question_html: Under Section 42(2), in a private placement, the number of persons to whom an offer or invitation may be made in a financial year shall NOT EXCEED:

options.A: 50 persons in total in any financial year
options.B: NOT EXCEED 200 IN THE AGGREGATE IN A FINANCIAL YEAR as per Rule 14(2) — Board identifies the 'identified persons'; private placement offer made only to these identified persons whose names and addresses are recorded by the company
options.C: 100 persons per offer
options.D: No limit — any number of persons can be invited for private placement

answer_html:
Answer: (B) NOT EXCEED 200 IN THE AGGREGATE IN A FINANCIAL YEAR as per Rule 14(2) — Board identifies the 'identified persons'; private placement offer made only to these identified persons whose names and addresses are recorded by the company

Section 42(2): A private placement shall be made only to a SELECT GROUP OF PERSONS identified by the Board ('IDENTIFIED PERSONS') whose number shall NOT EXCEED FIFTY or such higher number as may be prescribed. Rule 14(2): An offer or invitation to subscribe under private placement shall not be made to persons more than 200 IN THE AGGREGATE IN A FINANCIAL YEAR. The company must RECORD THE NAMES AND ADDRESSES of identified persons. Section 42(7): NO COMPANY ISSUING SECURITIES UNDER THIS SECTION shall release any PUBLIC ADVERTISEMENT or use any MEDIA, MARKETING OR DISTRIBUTION CHANNELS OR AGENTS to inform the public at large about such issue.

question_html: Under Section 42(4), when a person subscribes for securities under private placement, subscription money must be paid in which mode?

options.A: Payment may be made in any mode including cash
options.B: Payment may be made only by electronic transfer
options.C: Payment must be made only by cheque or RTGS
options.D: Payment must be by CHEQUE or DEMAND DRAFT or other BANKING CHANNEL — NOT BY CASH; and the company shall NOT UTILISE MONIES raised through private placement unless ALLOTMENT IS MADE AND RETURN OF ALLOTMENT IS FILED WITH THE REGISTRAR

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Payment must be made only by cheque or RTGS

Section 42(4): Every identified person willing to subscribe shall apply in the PRIVATE PLACEMENT AND APPLICATION with subscription money paid either by CHEQUE or DEMAND DRAFT or other BANKING CHANNEL — NOT BY CASH. KEY PROVISO: A company shall NOT UTILISE MONIES RAISED THROUGH PRIVATE PLACEMENT unless: (a) ALLOTMENT IS MADE; AND (b) RETURN OF ALLOTMENT IS FILED WITH THE REGISTRAR. This ensures traceability and protects investors. Monies received shall be kept in a SEPARATE BANK ACCOUNT in a SCHEDULED BANK.
topic_text: Section 42(4) — Payment Mode for Private Placement

question_html: Under Section 42(5), no FRESH OFFER OR INVITATION shall be made under private placement unless:

options.A: Allotments with respect to any earlier offer have been COMPLETED or that earlier offer has been WITHDRAWN OR ABANDONED BY THE COMPANY
options.B: SEBI approves the new private placement offer
options.C: The board has passed a fresh resolution authorising the new offer
options.D: Three months have elapsed since the previous private placement offer

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Allotments with respect to any earlier offer have been COMPLETED or that earlier offer has been WITHDRAWN OR ABANDONED BY THE COMPANY

Section 42(5): No FRESH OFFER OR INVITATION under private placement shall be made unless: the ALLOTMENTS with respect to any offer or invitation made EARLIER have been COMPLETED, or that offer or invitation has been WITHDRAWN OR ABANDONED by the company. This sequential requirement prevents companies from making multiple overlapping private placement offers simultaneously, which could de facto constitute a public offer.
topic_text: Section 42(5) — Fresh Offers Under Private Placement

question_html: Under Section 42(6), a company making an offer under private placement shall allot securities within how many days from receipt of application money, and what rate of interest is payable if it fails to repay within the specified period?

options.A: Allot within 30 days; interest at 10% per annum
options.B: ALLOT WITHIN 60 DAYS from date of receipt of application money; if unable to allot, REPAY WITHIN 15 DAYS from expiry of 60 days; if company fails to repay within 15 days, liable to repay with INTEREST AT 12% PER ANNUM from the EXPIRY OF THE 16TH DAY
options.C: Allot within 90 days; interest at 15% per annum
options.D: Allot within 45 days; interest at 8% per annum

answer_html:
Answer: (B) ALLOT WITHIN 60 DAYS from date of receipt of application money; if unable to allot, REPAY WITHIN 15 DAYS from expiry of 60 days; if company fails to repay within 15 days, liable to repay with INTEREST AT 12% PER ANNUM from the EXPIRY OF THE 16TH DAY

Section 42(6): ALLOTMENT PERIOD: Company shall allot securities within 60 DAYS from date of receipt of application money. If unable to allot within 60 days: REPAY APPLICATION MONEY to subscribers within 15 DAYS from expiry of 60 days. If company FAILS TO REPAY within 15 days: liable to repay with INTEREST AT 12% PER ANNUM from the EXPIRY OF THE 16TH DAY. Monies received shall be kept in a SEPARATE BANK ACCOUNT in a SCHEDULED BANK and shall NOT BE UTILISED except for: (a) ADJUSTMENT AGAINST ALLOTMENT; or (b) REPAYMENT where company unable to allot.
topic_text: Section 42(6) — Allotment Period & Interest for Non-Allotment

question_html: Under Section 42(8), a company making allotment under private placement shall file with the Registrar a return of allotment within how many days, and what is the PENALTY under Section 42(9) for default in filing?

options.A: Within 30 days; penalty Rs. 1,000 per day up to Rs. 1 lakh
options.B: Within 30 days; penalty Rs. 500 per day
options.C: WITHIN 15 DAYS from date of allotment in Form PAS-3 (with fee and complete list of allottees); PENALTY under Sec.42(9): company, its PROMOTERS AND DIRECTORS liable for EACH DEFAULT at RS. 1,000 FOR EACH DAY continuing but NOT EXCEEDING RS. 25 LAKHS
options.D: Within 7 days; penalty Rs. 2,000 per day up to Rs. 50 lakhs

answer_html:
Answer: (C) WITHIN 15 DAYS from date of allotment in Form PAS-3 (with fee and complete list of allottees); PENALTY under Sec.42(9): company, its PROMOTERS AND DIRECTORS liable for EACH DEFAULT at RS. 1,000 FOR EACH DAY continuing but NOT EXCEEDING RS. 25 LAKHS

Section 42(8): RETURN OF ALLOTMENT for private placement: Filed with Registrar WITHIN 15 DAYS from date of allotment — in the prescribed form (Form PAS-3 per Rule 14(6)) with fee and COMPLETE LIST OF ALL ALLOTTEES (full names, addresses, number of securities allotted, and other relevant information). Section 42(9): Penalty for default in filing = COMPANY, ITS PROMOTERS AND DIRECTORS liable for each default of RS. 1,000 FOR EACH DAY during which default continues but NOT EXCEEDING RS. 25 LAKHS. Section 42(10): Contravention of Section 42 = penalty up to amount raised or RS. 2 CRORES — whichever is LOWER.
topic_text: Section 42(8) & (9) — Return of Allotment and Penalty

question_html: Under Rule 14(1), before making any offer under private placement, which approval is required and in which form must the private placement offer cum application be issued?

options.A: Prior SPECIAL RESOLUTION APPROVAL BY SHAREHOLDERS for each offer or invitation; offer cum application letter in FORM PAS-4, serially numbered, addressed specifically to each person, sent within 30 DAYS of recording the person's name
options.B: Only board resolution required; application form may be general
options.C: Prior approval by SEBI and application in Form PAS-1
options.D: Only ordinary resolution at AGM; no specific form required

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Prior SPECIAL RESOLUTION APPROVAL BY SHAREHOLDERS for each offer or invitation; offer cum application letter in FORM PAS-4, serially numbered, addressed specifically to each person, sent within 30 DAYS of recording the person's name

Rule 14(1): A company shall NOT make an offer/invitation to subscribe to securities through private placement UNLESS the proposal has been previously approved by SHAREHOLDERS OF THE COMPANY BY SPECIAL RESOLUTION for EACH of the offers or invitations. Rule 14(3): Private placement offer cum application letter shall be in FORM PAS-4 — SERIALLY NUMBERED, addressed SPECIFICALLY TO THE PERSON to whom the offer is made; sent within 30 DAYS of recording the name of such person — in writing or electronic mode. Rule 14(4): Company shall maintain a complete record of private placement offers in FORM PAS-5.
topic_text: Rule 14 — Private Placement: Prior Shareholder Approval

question_html: Under Section 42(10), if a company makes an offer or accepts monies in CONTRAVENTION of the private placement provisions, the penalty is:

options.A: Penalty equal to the full amount raised plus 50% additional
options.B: PENALTY WHICH MAY EXTEND TO THE AMOUNT RAISED THROUGH PRIVATE PLACEMENT OR RS. 2 CRORES — WHICHEVER IS LOWER; company shall also REFUND ALL MONIES WITH INTEREST as specified in Sec.42(6) to subscribers within 30 DAYS of the order imposing the penalty
options.C: Fixed penalty of Rs. 50 lakhs regardless of amount raised
options.D: Penalty equal to 10 times the amount raised

answer_html:
Answer: (B) PENALTY WHICH MAY EXTEND TO THE AMOUNT RAISED THROUGH PRIVATE PLACEMENT OR RS. 2 CRORES — WHICHEVER IS LOWER; company shall also REFUND ALL MONIES WITH INTEREST as specified in Sec.42(6) to subscribers within 30 DAYS of the order imposing the penalty

Section 42(10): CONTRAVENTION OF PRIVATE PLACEMENT: Company, its PROMOTERS AND DIRECTORS = liable for penalty which may extend to the AMOUNT RAISED THROUGH PRIVATE PLACEMENT OR RS. 2 CRORES — WHICHEVER IS LOWER. Additionally: company shall also REFUND ALL MONIES WITH INTEREST as specified in Section 42(6) to subscribers WITHIN A PERIOD OF 30 DAYS of the ORDER IMPOSING THE PENALTY. Compare with Section 42(9): default only in filing return of allotment = Rs. 1,000 per day max Rs. 25 lakhs; Section 42(10): for actual contravention = Rs. 2 crores ceiling. SHARE CAPITAL & KINDS OF SHARES — SECTIONS 43–48
topic_text: Section 42(10) — Penalty for Contravention of Private Placement

question_html: Under Section 43, the share capital of a company limited by shares shall be of which two kinds?

options.A: Ordinary shares and preference shares only with no further classification
options.B: Equity shares and debentures
options.C: EQUITY SHARE CAPITAL (including equity with differential rights as to dividend/voting) and PREFERENCE SHARE CAPITAL; equity share capital = all share capital which is NOT preference share capital
options.D: Redeemable shares and irredeemable shares

answer_html:
Answer: (C) EQUITY SHARE CAPITAL (including equity with differential rights as to dividend/voting) and PREFERENCE SHARE CAPITAL; equity share capital = all share capital which is NOT preference share capital

Section 43: SHARE CAPITAL of a company limited by shares shall be of two kinds: (i) EQUITY SHARE CAPITAL; and (ii) PREFERENCE SHARE CAPITAL. Section 43 Explanation I: EQUITY SHARE CAPITAL = all share capital which is NOT PREFERENCE SHARE CAPITAL. Equity share capital is of two types: (a) WITH VOTING RIGHTS; or (b) WITH DIFFERENTIAL RIGHTS as to DIVIDEND, VOTING. Section 43 Explanation II: PREFERENCE SHARE CAPITAL = that part which carries a preferential right regarding dividend and in distribution of assets on winding up.
topic_text: Section 43 — Two Kinds of Share Capital

question_html: Under Rule 4, which of the following is a condition for issuing EQUITY SHARES WITH DIFFERENTIAL RIGHTS as to dividend, voting?

options.A: Shares with differential rights shall NOT exceed 26% of the TOTAL POST-ISSUE PAID UP SHARE CAPITAL including DVR shares issued at any point; company must have consistent distributable profits for last 3 years and no subsisting defaults
options.B: Differential rights shares can be up to 50% of total post-issue paid-up capital
options.C: These shares can only be issued if all existing shareholders consent in writing
options.D: These shares can be issued only by unlisted companies

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Shares with differential rights shall NOT exceed 26% of the TOTAL POST-ISSUE PAID UP SHARE CAPITAL including DVR shares issued at any point; company must have consistent distributable profits for last 3 years and no subsisting defaults

Rule 4 — EQUITY SHARES WITH DIFFERENTIAL RIGHTS CONDITIONS: (1) AOA authorises issue; (2) Authorised by ORDINARY RESOLUTION at general meeting (for listed companies — through POSTAL BALLOT); (3) Shares with differential rights shall NOT EXCEED 26% OF TOTAL POST-ISSUE PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL (including DVR issued at any point); (4) Company has CONSISTENT TRACK RECORD OF DISTRIBUTABLE PROFITS for last 3 YEARS; (5) No default in filing financial statements/annual returns for 3 years; (6) No subsisting default in payment of declared dividend, matured deposits, debentures, preference shares, or statutory employee payments; (7) Company not penalised by Court or Tribunal in last 3 years under RBI Act, SEBI Act, SCRA, FEMA or any special act.
topic_text: Rule 4 — Equity Shares with Differential Rights (DVR)

question_html: Under Section 46(1), a share certificate issued by a company is what type of evidence of title?

options.A: Conclusive evidence of the title of the person to such shares
options.B: PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE of the TITLE of the person of such shares; issued under COMMON SEAL (if any) or SIGNED BY TWO DIRECTORS or ONE DIRECTOR AND COMPANY SECRETARY; every share must have a DISTINCTIVE NUMBER (unless in demat form); certificate in FORM SH-1
options.C: Merely an internal document with no evidentiary value
options.D: Secondary evidence requiring corroboration from other documents

answer_html:
Answer: (B) PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE of the TITLE of the person of such shares; issued under COMMON SEAL (if any) or SIGNED BY TWO DIRECTORS or ONE DIRECTOR AND COMPANY SECRETARY; every share must have a DISTINCTIVE NUMBER (unless in demat form); certificate in FORM SH-1

Section 45: Every share shall be DISTINGUISHED BY ITS DISTINCTIVE NUMBER (not applicable to dematerialised form). Section 46(1): A certificate issued under the COMMON SEAL (if any) or SIGNED BY TWO DIRECTORS or ONE DIRECTOR AND COMPANY SECRETARY = PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE OF TITLE of the person to such shares. If no common seal: signed by TWO DIRECTORS or ONE DIRECTOR AND COMPANY SECRETARY. A director's SIGNATURE printed as FACSIMILE (engraving, lithography, digital signing) = deemed to have signed, but the director is personally responsible. Certificate issued in FORM SH-1. Section 46(4): Where share held in DEPOSITORY form — RECORD OF THE DEPOSITORY = prima facie evidence of BENEFICIAL OWNER'S INTEREST.
