topic_text: Section 45 & 46 — Share Certificate as Prima Facie Evidence

question_html: Under Section 46, the conditions for issuing a DUPLICATE SHARE CERTIFICATE and the penalty for fraudulent issue of a duplicate certificate are:

options.A: Duplicate can be issued without any conditions; penalty is Rs. 1,000 per share
options.B: Duplicate issued if certificate PROVED LOST/DESTROYED or DEFACED/MUTILATED/TORN AND SURRENDERED; prior CONSENT OF BOARD required; fee not exceeding RS. 50 per certificate; UNLISTED: within 3 MONTHS; LISTED: within 45 DAYS; FRAUDULENT ISSUE: fine NOT LESS THAN 5 TIMES FACE VALUE but may extend to 10 TIMES FACE VALUE OR RS. 10 CRORES (whichever is HIGHER); officers: Section 447
options.C: Duplicate requires shareholder AGM approval; penalty is Rs. 10,000 per certificate
options.D: Duplicate can be issued only by court order

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Duplicate requires shareholder AGM approval; penalty is Rs. 10,000 per certificate

Section 46(2): DUPLICATE SHARE CERTIFICATE: Issued if: (a) certificate PROVED TO HAVE BEEN LOST OR DESTROYED; or (b) DEFACED, MUTILATED OR TORN and SURRENDERED to the company. Requires: PRIOR CONSENT OF THE BOARD; fee NOT EXCEEDING RS. 50 PER CERTIFICATE; supporting evidence and indemnity; word 'DUPLICATE' must be STAMPED OR PRINTED PROMINENTLY on face; recorded in SH-2 register. TIME LIMITS: UNLISTED COMPANIES = within 3 MONTHS; LISTED COMPANIES = within 45 DAYS of submission of complete documents. Section 46(5) FRAUDULENT ISSUE: Company fine NOT LESS THAN 5 TIMES FACE VALUE of shares involved but may extend to 10 TIMES FACE VALUE OR RS. 10 CRORES — whichever is HIGHER. Officers: liable under Section 447.

question_html: Under Section 56(4), within what periods must a company deliver share certificates in various situations?

options.A: Always within 30 days in all cases
options.B: SUBSCRIBERS TO MOA: 2 MONTHS from date of incorporation; ALLOTMENT OF SHARES: 2 MONTHS from date of allotment; TRANSFER OR TRANSMISSION: 1 MONTH from receipt of instrument of transfer/intimation of transmission; ALLOTMENT OF DEBENTURES: 6 MONTHS from date of allotment
options.C: Subscribers to MOA: 3 months; Allotment: 3 months; Transfer: 2 months; Debentures: 3 months
options.D: All certificates must be delivered within 15 days

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Always within 30 days in all cases

Section 56(4): DELIVERY OF CERTIFICATES: (a) SUBSCRIBERS TO MOA = within 2 MONTHS from date of INCORPORATION; (b) ALLOTMENT OF SHARES = within 2 MONTHS from date of ALLOTMENT; (c) TRANSFER OR TRANSMISSION = within 1 MONTH from date of receipt of INSTRUMENT OF TRANSFER or INTIMATION OF TRANSMISSION; (d) ALLOTMENT OF DEBENTURES = within 6 MONTHS from date of ALLOTMENT. These are time-bound obligations and failure to deliver certificates within prescribed periods is a default. Certificate renewal/replacement: fee not exceeding RS. 50 per certificate on splitting, consolidation, or replacement of defaced/mutilated/torn/worn out certificates.

question_html: Under Section 47(2), a PREFERENCE SHAREHOLDER has the right to vote only on resolutions DIRECTLY AFFECTING his preference shares. In which ADDITIONAL SITUATION do preference shareholders acquire the right to vote on ALL resolutions?

options.A: When the company makes a public offer of new shares
options.B: When the company's paid-up equity share capital falls below 10% of total share capital
options.C: Only when the company is under SEBI investigation
options.D: Where DIVIDEND HAS NOT BEEN PAID to preference shareholders for a period of 2 YEARS OR MORE — they shall have a right to VOTE ON ALL THE RESOLUTIONS placed before the company

answer_html:
Answer: (B) When the company's paid-up equity share capital falls below 10% of total share capital

Section 47(2): PREFERENCE SHAREHOLDER has a right to vote ONLY on resolutions: (a) which DIRECTLY AFFECT THE RIGHTS ATTACHED to his preference shares; (b) for WINDING UP of the company; or (c) for REPAYMENT OR REDUCTION OF EQUITY OR PREFERENCE SHARE CAPITAL. His voting right on poll = in proportion to share in PAID-UP PREFERENCE SHARE CAPITAL. ADDITIONAL VOTING RIGHT: Where DIVIDEND IS NOT PAID to preference shareholders for a PERIOD OF 2 YEARS OR MORE — such preference shareholders shall have a right to VOTE ON ALL RESOLUTIONS placed before the company. Section 47(1): EQUITY SHAREHOLDERS vote on EVERY resolution — voting right on poll in proportion to share in PAID-UP EQUITY SHARE CAPITAL.
topic_text: Section 47 — Voting Rights of Preference Shareholders

question_html: Under Section 48, the rights attached to the shares of any class may be varied. How, and under what circumstances, can DISSENTING SHAREHOLDERS challenge a variation of rights?

options.A: Dissenting shareholders may file a complaint with SEBI within 30 days
options.B: Variation requires: CONSENT IN WRITING of holders of NOT LESS THAN 3/4TH of issued shares of that class OR SPECIAL RESOLUTION at SEPARATE MEETING of that class; DISSENTING SHAREHOLDERS: holders of NOT LESS THAN 10% of issued shares who did NOT CONSENT may apply to Tribunal within 21 DAYS from when consent given or resolution passed; company files copy of Tribunal order with Registrar within 30 DAYS
options.C: Variation of rights requires simple majority at AGM; no challenge rights
options.D: Variation requires unanimous consent; no dissenting shareholder rights

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Variation of rights requires simple majority at AGM; no challenge rights

Section 48: VARIATION OF SHAREHOLDERS' RIGHTS: Rights may be varied: (a) with CONSENT IN WRITING of holders of NOT LESS THAN THREE-FOURTHS of issued shares of that class; OR (b) by SPECIAL RESOLUTION at a SEPARATE MEETING of the holders of the issued shares of that class. Must be provided for in articles or memorandum. Section 48(2): DISSENTING SHAREHOLDERS: Holders of NOT LESS THAN 10% of issued shares of that class who did NOT CONSENT or vote in favour may apply to the TRIBUNAL to have the variation CANCELLED — within 21 DAYS from date of consent/resolution. Decision of TRIBUNAL = BINDING. Company files copy of Tribunal order with Registrar within 30 DAYS. SWEAT EQUITY, BONUS SHARES, ESOP — SECTIONS 54, 63, RULE 12

question_html: Under Section 2(88) and Section 54, 'sweat equity shares' are issued by a company to its directors or employees. Which condition is MANDATORY for issuing sweat equity shares?

options.A: SPECIAL RESOLUTION passed by the company; resolution specifies number of shares, current market price, consideration, and class of directors/employees to whom issued; if listed — per SEBI regulations; max 15% of existing paid-up share capital or Rs. 5 crores (whichever is HIGHER) per year; max 25% of paid-up equity capital at any time; LOCKED IN for 3 years from allotment
options.B: Board resolution sufficient — no shareholder approval required
options.C: Only ordinary resolution required; no lock-in period
options.D: Sweat equity can be issued only if the company is in losses

answer_html:
Answer: (A) SPECIAL RESOLUTION passed by the company; resolution specifies number of shares, current market price, consideration, and class of directors/employees to whom issued; if listed — per SEBI regulations; max 15% of existing paid-up share capital or Rs. 5 crores (whichever is HIGHER) per year; max 25% of paid-up equity capital at any time; LOCKED IN for 3 years from allotment

Section 54: SWEAT EQUITY SHARES CONDITIONS: (1) SPECIAL RESOLUTION passed by the company; (2) Resolution specifies: NUMBER OF SHARES, CURRENT MARKET PRICE, CONSIDERATION (if any), CLASS OF DIRECTORS/EMPLOYEES to whom issued; (3) If LISTED — per SEBI regulations; if UNLISTED — per prescribed rules. LIMITS: (a) In a year: not more than 15% OF EXISTING PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL or SHARES OF ISSUE VALUE OF RS. 5 CRORES — WHICHEVER IS HIGHER; (b) At any time: NOT EXCEED 25% OF PAID-UP EQUITY CAPITAL. LOCK-IN: 3 YEARS from date of allotment. Start-up company: up to 50% of paid-up capital for up to 5 years from incorporation. Section 54(2): PARI PASSU with other equity shareholders.

question_html: Under Section 63(1), a company may issue FULLY PAID-UP BONUS SHARES to its members out of which sources?

options.A: Out of any available funds including revaluation of assets reserve
options.B: Out of FREE RESERVES; the SECURITIES PREMIUM ACCOUNT; or the CAPITAL REDEMPTION RESERVE ACCOUNT — bonus shares shall NOT be made by capitalising reserves created by REVALUATION OF ASSETS; and shall NOT be issued IN LIEU OF DIVIDEND
options.C: Only from current year profits
options.D: From any reserve or surplus fund available with the company

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Out of FREE RESERVES; the SECURITIES PREMIUM ACCOUNT; or the CAPITAL REDEMPTION RESERVE ACCOUNT — bonus shares shall NOT be made by capitalising reserves created by REVALUATION OF ASSETS; and shall NOT be issued IN LIEU OF DIVIDEND

Section 63(1): Bonus shares sources: (a) FREE RESERVES; (b) SECURITIES PREMIUM ACCOUNT; or (c) CAPITAL REDEMPTION RESERVE ACCOUNT. RESTRICTIONS: (1) NO BONUS SHARES by capitalising reserves created by REVALUATION OF ASSETS; (2) Bonus shares shall NOT be issued IN LIEU OF DIVIDEND [Section 63(3)]. Section 63(2): Pre-conditions: (a) AUTHORISED BY ARTICLES; (b) Authorised in GENERAL MEETING on recommendation of Board; (c) No default in payment of INTEREST/PRINCIPAL on fixed deposits or DEBT SECURITIES; (d) No default in STATUTORY DUES of employees (PF, gratuity, bonus); (e) PARTLY PAID UP SHARES, if any, must be made FULLY PAID UP first. Rule 14: Once Board decision announced for bonus issue, CANNOT BE SUBSEQUENTLY WITHDRAWN.

question_html: Under Rule 12(6)(a) of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, what is the MINIMUM PERIOD required between the grant of options and the VESTING of the option in an ESOP?

options.A: 6 months minimum between grant and vesting
options.B: MINIMUM PERIOD OF ONE YEAR between grant of options and vesting; options are NOT TRANSFERABLE; cannot be pledged/hypothecated/mortgaged or alienated; on DEATH of employee — options vest in LEGAL HEIRS OR NOMINEES; on PERMANENT INCAPACITY — all options vest on that day; on RESIGNATION OR TERMINATION — unvested options expire
options.C: Minimum period of 3 years between grant and vesting
options.D: No minimum vesting period is prescribed

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Minimum period of 3 years between grant and vesting

Rule 12(6)(a): MINIMUM PERIOD OF ONE YEAR between GRANT OF OPTIONS AND VESTING. Special rule: if options granted in lieu of options held in a MERGING/AMALGAMATING COMPANY — the period during which earlier options were held is ADJUSTED against the minimum vesting period. ESOP restrictions: (1) OPTIONS NOT TRANSFERABLE; (2) Cannot be PLEDGED, HYPOTHECATED, MORTGAGED or ALIENATED; (3) Only the EMPLOYEE can exercise the option. On DEATH while in employment: ALL OPTIONS GRANTED vest in LEGAL HEIRS OR NOMINEES. On PERMANENT INCAPACITY: ALL OPTIONS vest on THAT DAY. On RESIGNATION OR TERMINATION: all OPTIONS NOT VESTED shall EXPIRE; vested options exercisable within specified period per scheme.

question_html: Under Rule 12 for Employee Stock Option Schemes, which persons are EXCLUDED from the definition of 'employee' who can be granted ESOPs?

options.A: Only non-executive directors are excluded
options.B: EXCLUDED: (i) employee who IS A PROMOTER or belongs to PROMOTER GROUP; (ii) DIRECTOR who — directly or indirectly through relative/body corporate — holds MORE THAN 10% OF OUTSTANDING EQUITY SHARES; INCLUDED: permanent employees (India/outside India), whole-time AND non-whole-time directors (excluding independent directors), employees of holding or subsidiary companies
options.C: All directors are excluded — only permanent employees can receive ESOPs
options.D: Only part-time employees are excluded

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only non-executive directors are excluded

Rule 12 — ESOP EMPLOYEE DEFINITION: INCLUDED: (a) PERMANENT EMPLOYEE working in India or OUTSIDE INDIA; (b) A DIRECTOR — whether WHOLE-TIME or not — but EXCLUDING AN INDEPENDENT DIRECTOR; (c) Employee or DIRECTOR of a SUBSIDIARY (India/outside India) or HOLDING COMPANY. EXCLUDED: (a) Employee who IS A PROMOTER or belongs to the PROMOTER GROUP; (b) A director who (himself or through RELATIVE or BODY CORPORATE) directly or indirectly holds MORE THAN 10% OF OUTSTANDING EQUITY SHARES. Rule 12(4): Separate resolution required for: grant to employees of SUBSIDIARY/HOLDING COMPANY; or grant to identified employees during any one year equal to or exceeding 1% OF ISSUED CAPITAL. RIGHTS ISSUE, PREFERENTIAL ALLOTMENT & SHARE CAPITAL PUBLICATION — SECTIONS 60, 62
topic_text: Rule 12 — ESOP: Who is Excluded from Employee Definition

question_html: Under Section 60(1), whenever a company's notice, advertisement, business letter, billhead, or letter paper contains a statement of the AUTHORIZED CAPITAL, it must also contain a statement of:

options.A: Only the authorized capital — no other information is required
options.B: In an EQUALLY PROMINENT POSITION and EQUALLY CONSPICUOUS CHARACTERS: the amount of capital SUBSCRIBED and amount PAID UP; penalty: COMPANY = RS. 10,000; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER = RS. 1,000 for each default
options.C: Only the names of the directors and promoters
options.D: Only the registered office address

answer_html:
Answer: (B) In an EQUALLY PROMINENT POSITION and EQUALLY CONSPICUOUS CHARACTERS: the amount of capital SUBSCRIBED and amount PAID UP; penalty: COMPANY = RS. 10,000; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER = RS. 1,000 for each default

Section 60(1): Where any notice, advertisement, official publication, business letter, billhead or letter paper of a company contains a statement of AUTHORIZED CAPITAL — it shall ALSO contain a statement in an EQUALLY PROMINENT POSITION and in EQUALLY CONSPICUOUS CHARACTERS of: (a) AMOUNT OF CAPITAL SUBSCRIBED; and (b) AMOUNT PAID UP. Section 60(2): Penalty for default: COMPANY = RS. 10,000; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER = RS. 1,000 for each such default. The purpose is to prevent investors and public from being misled by only seeing the authorized capital figure.

question_html: Under Section 62(1)(a), when a company proposes to increase its subscribed capital by issue of further shares, these shall first be offered to EXISTING EQUITY SHAREHOLDERS. What is the NOTICE PERIOD for a rights issue offer and when does the offer lapse?

options.A: Offer open for 30 days; lapses after 30 days without acceptance
options.B: Offer by NOTICE SPECIFYING NUMBER OF SHARES OFFERED AND TIME within which offer must be accepted; offer open for NOT LESS THAN 15 DAYS AND NOT MORE THAN 30 DAYS; if not accepted within time, BOARD MAY DISPOSE OF THEM in a manner NOT DISADVANTAGEOUS TO SHAREHOLDERS AND COMPANY
options.C: Offer open for 60 days; board has absolute discretion in disposal
options.D: Offer open for 21 days; lapses automatically after 21 days

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Offer open for 60 days; board has absolute discretion in disposal

Section 62(1)(a): RIGHTS ISSUE: Further shares must first be offered to EXISTING EQUITY SHAREHOLDERS pro-rata to existing paid-up capital. Offer by NOTICE SPECIFYING: (1) Number of shares offered; (2) Time limit within which offer must be accepted. NOTICE PERIOD: Not less than 15 DAYS AND not more than 30 DAYS from date of offer. If offer not accepted within time: Board may DISPOSE OF THEM in such manner as NOT DISADVANTAGEOUS TO SHAREHOLDERS AND COMPANY. Section 62(1)(b): Employees under scheme of EMPLOYEES' STOCK OPTION may also be offered shares. Section 62(1)(c): Any OTHER PERSONS — by SPECIAL RESOLUTION if company is a LISTED COMPANY (as per SEBI) or if UNLISTED (by special resolution). Section 62(3): Existing shareholders may decline rights issue by WRITTEN RENUNCIATION.

question_html: Under Section 62(3), an existing shareholder who receives an offer for rights shares may decline the offer. How must this renunciation be done?

options.A: Written renunciation sent to the company within the period specified in the offer notice
options.B: Verbal instruction to the company's registrar
options.C: Electronic mail to SEBI
options.D: Filing a notice with the Registrar of Companies

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Written renunciation sent to the company within the period specified in the offer notice

Section 62(3): Nothing in Section 62 shall apply to the INCREASE OF THE SUBSCRIBED CAPITAL caused by the exercise of an option contained in: (a) DEBENTURES ISSUED or LOAN RAISED by the company to convert such debentures or loans, or any part thereof, into shares in the company; or (b) in the terms of issue of certain type of preference shares or such shares. A shareholder who does not wish to exercise his rights issue entitlement may send a WRITTEN RENUNCIATION to the company within the period specified in the rights issue offer notice — thereby allowing the Board to dispose of those shares in a manner not disadvantageous to shareholders and the company.

question_html: Under Section 2(84) and Section 44 of the Companies Act, 2013, a 'share' means a share in the share capital of a company and includes stock. How are shares legally classified?

options.A: Shares are immoveable property and can only be transferred by a registered instrument
options.B: SHARES ARE MOVEABLE PROPERTY, TRANSFERABLE IN THE MANNER PRESCRIBED BY THE ARTICLES of the company; every share shall be DISTINGUISHED BY ITS DISTINCTIVE NUMBER (not applicable to demat shares); no certificate shall be issued except pursuant to a Board RESOLUTION
options.C: Shares are a form of actionable claim and can only be transferred by assignment
options.D: Shares are considered fixed assets on the company's balance sheet

answer_html:
Answer: (B) SHARES ARE MOVEABLE PROPERTY, TRANSFERABLE IN THE MANNER PRESCRIBED BY THE ARTICLES of the company; every share shall be DISTINGUISHED BY ITS DISTINCTIVE NUMBER (not applicable to demat shares); no certificate shall be issued except pursuant to a Board RESOLUTION

Section 2(84): SHARE = a share in the SHARE CAPITAL of a company and INCLUDES STOCK. Section 44: SHARES ARE MOVEABLE PROPERTY, TRANSFERABLE IN THE MANNER PROVIDED BY THE ARTICLES of the company. Section 45: Every share in a company having a share capital shall be DISTINGUISHED BY ITS DISTINCTIVE NUMBER (not applicable to DEMATERIALISED FORM). Rule 5(1): No share certificate shall be issued EXCEPT: (a) in pursuance of a RESOLUTION BY THE BOARD; and (b) on surrender of the letter of allotment or fractional coupons. Section 2(84) read with Section 44 ensures that shares, unlike land/buildings, can be freely transferred in the manner prescribed in the Articles.
topic_text: Section 2(84) & Section 44 — Shares as Moveable Property

question_html: Under Section 62(1)(c), if a company wishes to allot shares to persons OTHER THAN existing equity shareholders or employees under ESOP, the approval required is:

options.A: Only board approval by special majority
options.B: Only ordinary resolution at AGM
options.C: SEBI approval only, no shareholder vote required
options.D: SPECIAL RESOLUTION at a general meeting; for LISTED COMPANY — special resolution through POSTAL BALLOT and SEBI compliance; for UNLISTED COMPANY — special resolution; price not less than price determined by VALUATION REPORT of a registered valuer

answer_html:
Answer: (C) SEBI approval only, no shareholder vote required

Section 62(1)(c): PREFERENTIAL ALLOTMENT to any PERSON OTHER THAN EXISTING EQUITY SHAREHOLDERS or ESOP employees: (a) SPECIAL RESOLUTION at a general meeting; (b) For LISTED COMPANIES — by SPECIAL RESOLUTION THROUGH POSTAL BALLOT and compliance with SEBI Act regulations; (c) For UNLISTED COMPANIES other than listed companies — by SPECIAL RESOLUTION and price of shares shall NOT BE LESS THAN THE PRICE determined by the VALUATION REPORT of a REGISTERED VALUER. Section 62(1)(b): Shares to EMPLOYEES under ESOP scheme — by SPECIAL RESOLUTION. Section 62 ensures that existing shareholders' rights are not diluted without proper authorization.

question_html: Under Rule 4(6) for DVR shares, Rule 6(3) for renewed/duplicate certificates, and Rule 12(10) for ESOP, which registers must a company maintain and where are they preserved?

options.A: All registers can be maintained at any convenient location outside India
options.B: Only the Register of Members needs to be maintained — other registers are optional
options.C: Only digital registers are required — no physical registers needed
options.D: REGISTER OF MEMBERS (Sec.88) for DVR particulars; REGISTER OF RENEWED AND DUPLICATE SHARE CERTIFICATES in FORM SH-2 (at registered office/where Register of Members kept, preserved PERMANENTLY, authenticated by CS or authorised person); REGISTER OF SWEAT EQUITY SHARES in FORM SH-3; REGISTER OF EMPLOYEE STOCK OPTIONS in FORM SH-6 — all at registered office or Board-decided place; authenticated by CS or authorised person

answer_html:
Answer: (A) All registers can be maintained at any convenient location outside India

Mandatory REGISTERS: (1) REGISTER OF MEMBERS [Sec.88]: includes particulars of DVR shares; (2) REGISTER OF RENEWED AND DUPLICATE SHARE CERTIFICATES [Form SH-2, Rule 6(3)]: kept at registered office or where Register of Members is kept; PRESERVED PERMANENTLY; authenticated by CS or authorised person; (3) REGISTER OF SWEAT EQUITY SHARES [Form SH-3]: at registered office or Board-decided place; (4) REGISTER OF EMPLOYEE STOCK OPTIONS [Form SH-6, Rule 12(10)]: at registered office or Board-decided place; entries authenticated by CS or authorised person. ALL REGISTERS must have entries AUTHENTICATED by CS or authorised person. MISCELLANEOUS PENALTIES & KEY PROVISIONS

question_html: Which of the following CORRECTLY matches the PENALTY for violation of Section 26 (prospectus provisions) and Section 33 (application form without abridged prospectus)?

options.A: Both sections: only fine — no imprisonment
options.B: Section 26: COMPANY — fine Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 3 LAKHS; PERSON — imprisonment up to 3 YEARS or fine Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 3 LAKHS or BOTH; Section 33(3): COMPANY = RS. 50,000 FOR EACH DEFAULT (no imprisonment for company for Section 33 violation)
options.C: Both sections: imprisonment only — no fine
options.D: Section 26: fine Rs. 5,000; Section 33: fine Rs. 10,000

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Section 26: COMPANY — fine Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 3 LAKHS; PERSON — imprisonment up to 3 YEARS or fine Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 3 LAKHS or BOTH; Section 33(3): COMPANY = RS. 50,000 FOR EACH DEFAULT (no imprisonment for company for Section 33 violation)

PENALTY COMPARISON: Section 26 (PROSPECTUS PROVISIONS): COMPANY = fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 50,000 but may extend to RS. 3 LAKHS; PERSON KNOWINGLY A PARTY = imprisonment up to 3 YEARS or fine Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 3 LAKHS or BOTH. Section 33(3) (APPLICATION FORM WITHOUT ABRIDGED PROSPECTUS): Company = liable to penalty of RS. 50,000 FOR EACH DEFAULT. Note: Section 40(5): Rs. 5 LAKHS to Rs. 50 LAKHS (company); Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 3 LAKHS or imprisonment 1 year (officer). Penalty comparison questions are very frequently tested.

question_html: Under Section 35(3), if a prospectus is issued WITH INTENT TO DEFRAUD applicants, what is the extent of liability of the persons responsible?

options.A: Limited to the face value of shares subscribed by the defrauded applicant
options.B: Limited to the amount of commission earned by each person
options.C: Limited to the premium amount charged on the shares
options.D: PERSONALLY RESPONSIBLE WITHOUT ANY LIMITATION OF LIABILITY for all or any of the losses or damages incurred by any person who subscribed to the securities on the basis of such prospectus

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Limited to the premium amount charged on the shares

Section 35(3): Where a prospectus was issued WITH INTENT TO DEFRAUD the applicants for securities or any other person or FOR ANY FRAUDULENT PURPOSE — every person who AUTHORISED THE ISSUE of such a prospectus shall be PERSONALLY RESPONSIBLE, WITHOUT ANY LIMITATION OF LIABILITY, for ALL OR ANY OF THE LOSSES OR DAMAGES that may have been incurred by any person who subscribed to the securities on the basis of such prospectus. This absolute unlimited liability provision provides the strongest protection against fraudulent prospectuses.

question_html: Under Section 42(7), a company issuing securities under private placement shall NOT:

options.A: Issue any form of securities without public advertisement
options.B: RELEASE ANY PUBLIC ADVERTISEMENT OR UTILISE ANY MEDIA, MARKETING OR DISTRIBUTION CHANNELS OR AGENTS TO INFORM THE PUBLIC AT LARGE about such an issue
options.C: File any return of allotment — private placement is exempt from this
options.D: Pay any commission to agents or intermediaries

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Issue any form of securities without public advertisement

Section 42(7): NO COMPANY ISSUING SECURITIES UNDER PRIVATE PLACEMENT shall RELEASE ANY PUBLIC ADVERTISEMENT or utilise any MEDIA, MARKETING OR DISTRIBUTION CHANNELS OR AGENTS to INFORM THE PUBLIC AT LARGE about such an issue. This is the fundamental distinction between PRIVATE PLACEMENT (restricted to identified persons) and PUBLIC OFFER (open to the public at large). Violation of this distinction could render the private placement an illegal public offer with serious penalties.
topic_text: Section 42(7) — No Public Advertisement for Private Placement

question_html: Under Section 43 Explanation II, 'preference share capital' is defined as that part of share capital which carries PREFERENTIAL RIGHTS regarding which of the following?

options.A: Right to attend and vote at all general meetings regardless of circumstances
options.B: A PREFERENTIAL RIGHT AS TO PAYMENT OF DIVIDEND (fixed rate or fixed amount) AND a PREFERENTIAL RIGHT AS TO REPAYMENT OF CAPITAL in winding up or repayment of capital; preference shareholders vote only on matters directly affecting their rights (unless dividend unpaid for 2+ years)
options.C: Preferential right to appoint directors on the Board
options.D: Preferential right in all matters above equity shareholders

answer_html:
Answer: (B) A PREFERENTIAL RIGHT AS TO PAYMENT OF DIVIDEND (fixed rate or fixed amount) AND a PREFERENTIAL RIGHT AS TO REPAYMENT OF CAPITAL in winding up or repayment of capital; preference shareholders vote only on matters directly affecting their rights (unless dividend unpaid for 2+ years)

Section 43 Explanation II: PREFERENCE SHARE CAPITAL = that part of share capital which carries: (i) PREFERENTIAL RIGHT AS TO PAYMENT OF DIVIDEND at a FIXED RATE OR FIXED AMOUNT; AND (ii) PREFERENTIAL RIGHT AS TO REPAYMENT OF CAPITAL in the case of a WINDING UP or REPAYMENT OF CAPITAL. VOTING RIGHTS: Preference shareholders [Sec.47(2)] vote only on: (1) resolutions DIRECTLY AFFECTING THEIR RIGHTS; (2) WINDING UP; (3) REPAYMENT OR REDUCTION OF SHARE CAPITAL. If dividend UNPAID FOR 2 YEARS OR MORE: preference shareholders get RIGHT TO VOTE ON ALL RESOLUTIONS.

question_html: Which of the following CORRECTLY compares the KEY TIME LIMITS under Section 39 (Public Offer Allotment) and Section 42 (Private Placement Allotment)?

options.A: Both require allotment within 30 days and return filing within 15 days
options.B: SEC.39: min. subscription period = 30 DAYS; refund = within 15 DAYS of closure; directors' interest = 15% p.a.; return of allotment = 30 DAYS (Form PAS-3); SEC.42: allotment = within 60 DAYS; repayment = within 15 DAYS of expiry of 60 days; interest from 16th day = 12% p.a.; return of allotment = 15 DAYS (Form PAS-3)
options.C: Section 39: allotment within 60 days; Section 42: allotment within 30 days
options.D: Both are identical — same time limits apply to both

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Section 39: allotment within 60 days; Section 42: allotment within 30 days

COMPARISON — SEC.39 vs SEC.42: SECTION 39 (PUBLIC OFFER): Minimum subscription not received within 30 DAYS → refund within 15 DAYS from closure → directors jointly & severally liable at 15% p.a.; Return of allotment = 30 DAYS in Form PAS-3; Default penalty = Rs. 1,000/day max Rs. 1 LAKH. SECTION 42 (PRIVATE PLACEMENT): Allotment within 60 DAYS of receipt of application money; if unable to allot → repay within 15 DAYS of expiry of 60 days; if fails → 12% p.a. from 16th day; Return of allotment = 15 DAYS in Form PAS-3; Default penalty = Rs. 1,000/day max Rs. 25 LAKHS. Contravention of Sec.42 = amount raised or Rs. 2 Crores (lower).

question_html: Under the Companies Act, 2013, which of the following is PROHIBITED regarding allotment of shares by a company to its SUBSIDIARY?

options.A: Allotment of preference shares to subsidiary is prohibited but equity shares are allowed
options.B: Only listed companies are prohibited from allotting shares to subsidiaries
options.C: No restrictions exist on allotment to subsidiaries
options.D: ANY SUCH ALLOTMENT OR TRANSFER OF SHARES OF A COMPANY TO ITS SUBSIDIARY COMPANY SHALL BE VOID — this prevents circular shareholding between holding and subsidiary companies

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Allotment of preference shares to subsidiary is prohibited but equity shares are allowed

Under the Companies Act, 2013: ANY SUCH ALLOTMENT OR TRANSFER OF SHARES OF A COMPANY TO ITS SUBSIDIARY COMPANY SHALL BE VOID. This prohibition prevents CIRCULAR SHAREHOLDING — where the subsidiary holds shares in the holding company, creating a circular ownership structure. However, this provision SHALL NOT APPLY in certain cases as provided under the Act (e.g., where a company is acting as a trustee). This rule prevents distortion of the corporate governance and accountability structure.

question_html: Under Section 63(3), which of the following restrictions applies to the issue of BONUS SHARES?

options.A: Bonus shares can be issued instead of paying cash dividend to save cash
options.B: BONUS SHARES SHALL NOT BE ISSUED IN LIEU OF DIVIDEND; once the Board has ANNOUNCED THE DECISION RECOMMENDING A BONUS ISSUE, it shall NOT SUBSEQUENTLY WITHDRAW the same (Rule 14)
options.C: Bonus shares may be issued in lieu of dividend with all shareholders' consent
options.D: Bonus shares can be issued in lieu of interim dividend but not final dividend

answer_html:
Answer: (B) BONUS SHARES SHALL NOT BE ISSUED IN LIEU OF DIVIDEND; once the Board has ANNOUNCED THE DECISION RECOMMENDING A BONUS ISSUE, it shall NOT SUBSEQUENTLY WITHDRAW the same (Rule 14)

Section 63(3): BONUS SHARES SHALL NOT BE ISSUED IN LIEU OF DIVIDEND. Rule 14: A company which has ONCE ANNOUNCED THE DECISION OF THE BOARD RECOMMENDING A BONUS ISSUE shall NOT subsequently WITHDRAW THE SAME. Sources for bonus shares [Sec.63(1)]: FREE RESERVES, SECURITIES PREMIUM ACCOUNT, CAPITAL REDEMPTION RESERVE ACCOUNT. PROHIBITED SOURCE: Reserves created by REVALUATION OF ASSETS — cannot be capitalised for bonus shares. Pre-conditions [Sec.63(2)]: No default in interest/principal on fixed deposits or debt securities; no default in statutory dues of employees; partly paid shares must be fully paid up first.
topic_text: Section 63(3) — Bonus Shares Not in Lieu of Dividend

question_html: Under Section 54 and its rules, what is the LOCK-IN PERIOD for sweat equity shares, and what is the SPECIAL RELAXATION available to START-UP companies?

options.A: Lock-in: 1 year; Start-ups: no relaxation
options.B: Lock-in: 5 years; Start-ups: 75% of paid-up capital allowed
options.C: Lock-in: 2 years; Start-ups: issue up to 30% for 3 years
options.D: LOCK-IN: 3 YEARS FROM DATE OF ALLOTMENT; REGULAR COMPANIES: max 15% of existing paid-up share capital or shares of issue value RS. 5 CRORES (whichever is HIGHER) per year; max 25% of paid-up equity capital at any time; START-UP COMPANY: may issue NOT EXCEEDING 50% OF ITS PAID-UP CAPITAL up to 5 YEARS from date of incorporation or registration

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Lock-in: 2 years; Start-ups: issue up to 30% for 3 years

SWEAT EQUITY LOCK-IN: LOCK-IN PERIOD = 3 YEARS FROM DATE OF ALLOTMENT. ANNUAL LIMIT (regular companies): Not more than 15% OF EXISTING PAID-UP SHARE CAPITAL or SHARES OF ISSUE VALUE OF RS. 5 CRORES — WHICHEVER IS HIGHER. OVERALL LIMIT: Issuance shall NOT EXCEED 25% OF PAID-UP EQUITY CAPITAL at any time. SPECIAL RULE FOR START-UP COMPANIES: May issue sweat equity shares NOT EXCEEDING 50% OF ITS PAID-UP CAPITAL UP TO 5 YEARS from the date of its incorporation or registration. Board of Directors shall DISCLOSE IN THE DIRECTORS' REPORT for the year in which shares are issued. Register maintained in FORM SH-3. CONSOLIDATED ANSWER KEY — ALL 50 QUESTIONS — END OF QUESTION PAPER — Prepared from ICMAI Study Module | Prospectus & Allotment of Securities | Companies Act, 2013 — Chapter III | Module 12.1 | Syllabus 2022 | CMA Inter June 2026
topic_text: Section 2(88) — Sweat Equity Lock-in & Start-up Exception

question_html: Under Section 2(16) of the Companies Act, 2013, a 'charge' is defined as:

options.A: Only a fixed charge created on immovable property of a company by way of mortgage
options.B: An INTEREST OR LIEN CREATED ON THE PROPERTY OR ASSETS OF A COMPANY OR ANY OF ITS UNDERTAKINGS OR BOTH AS SECURITY AND INCLUDING A MORTGAGE — whether the property is tangible or intangible, within or outside India
options.C: Only a floating charge created on the current assets of a company
options.D: Only a pledge of moveable property created in favour of a bank or financial institution

answer_html:
Answer: (B) An INTEREST OR LIEN CREATED ON THE PROPERTY OR ASSETS OF A COMPANY OR ANY OF ITS UNDERTAKINGS OR BOTH AS SECURITY AND INCLUDING A MORTGAGE — whether the property is tangible or intangible, within or outside India

Section 2(16): CHARGE = an INTEREST OR LIEN CREATED ON THE PROPERTY OR ASSETS OF A COMPANY OR ANY OF ITS UNDERTAKINGS OR BOTH AS SECURITY AND INCLUDING A MORTGAGE. Key features: (1) May be a FIXED CHARGE (specific property) or FLOATING CHARGE (circulating assets); (2) Property may be TANGIBLE or INTANGIBLE; (3) Property may be situated WITHIN OR OUTSIDE INDIA; (4) May be on any assets or undertakings of the company; (5) INCLUDES A MORTGAGE. A charge is security for a debt — without the charge, the lender is an unsecured creditor.

question_html: Under Section 77(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, once a charge is created by the company, what is the company's obligation?

options.A: The company may register the charge within 90 days of creation at its option
options.B: Company secretaries must register charges — the company itself has no obligation
options.C: IT SHALL BE THE DUTY OF THE COMPANY to register particulars of the charge SIGNED BY BOTH THE COMPANY AND THE CHARGE HOLDER, together with instruments creating the charge, with the Registrar WITHIN 30 DAYS from the date of creation of the charge — regardless of where the property is situated
options.D: The charge holder must register the charge; the company has no obligation

answer_html:
Answer: (C) IT SHALL BE THE DUTY OF THE COMPANY to register particulars of the charge SIGNED BY BOTH THE COMPANY AND THE CHARGE HOLDER, together with instruments creating the charge, with the Registrar WITHIN 30 DAYS from the date of creation of the charge — regardless of where the property is situated

Section 77(1): IT SHALL BE THE DUTY OF THE COMPANY to register the charge with the Registrar. PARTICULARS: signed by BOTH THE COMPANY AND THE CHARGE HOLDER, together with INSTRUMENTS (if any) creating such charge. TIME LIMIT: 30 DAYS from date of creation of charge. SCOPE: The charge may be within India OR outside India on properties of the company or assets or any of its undertakings, situated in OR outside India. PROPERTY: may be TANGIBLE or INTANGIBLE. EXCEPTION: Section shall NOT APPLY TO SUCH CHARGES AS MAY BE PRESCRIBED in consultation with the RBI.

question_html: Under Section 77 and the Companies (Registration of Charges) Rules, 2014, which of the following types of charges are required to be registered?

options.A: ALL types of charges on any property or assets of the company — including charges on movable property (tangible and intangible), immovable property, floating charges, charges securing any issue of debentures, and charges on book debts
options.B: Only charges on immovable property require registration
options.C: Only charges created in favour of banks require registration
options.D: Only charges exceeding Rs. 50 lakhs in value require registration

answer_html:
Answer: (A) ALL types of charges on any property or assets of the company — including charges on movable property (tangible and intangible), immovable property, floating charges, charges securing any issue of debentures, and charges on book debts

Section 77: ALL CHARGES created by a company shall be registered — including: (1) Charges on MOVABLE PROPERTY (tangible and intangible); (2) Charges on IMMOVABLE PROPERTY; (3) FLOATING CHARGES on all or any of the undertaking's assets; (4) Charges securing any issue of DEBENTURES; (5) Charges on BOOK DEBTS; (6) Charges on UNPAID SHARE CAPITAL; (7) Charges on any GOODWILL, PATENT or TRADE MARK; (8) Charges on any SHIP or SHARE IN A SHIP. There is NO minimum amount threshold — all charges must be registered. EXCEPTION: Charges as prescribed in CONSULTATION WITH RBI are exempt.
topic_text: Section 77 — Types of Charges Subject to Registration

question_html: Under Section 77(1), which of the following CORRECTLY describes the territorial scope of charge registration?

options.A: Only charges on property situated within India need to be registered
options.B: CHARGES MAY BE WITHIN INDIA OR OUTSIDE INDIA on properties of the company or assets or any of its undertakings, SITUATED IN OR OUTSIDE INDIA — all such charges must be registered with the Registrar of Companies; this extraterritorial scope ensures foreign asset-backed borrowings are also disclosed
options.C: Only charges on Indian property registered with Indian banks require registration
options.D: Charges outside India need to be registered only with the foreign country's authority

answer_html:
Answer: (B) CHARGES MAY BE WITHIN INDIA OR OUTSIDE INDIA on properties of the company or assets or any of its undertakings, SITUATED IN OR OUTSIDE INDIA — all such charges must be registered with the Registrar of Companies; this extraterritorial scope ensures foreign asset-backed borrowings are also disclosed

Section 77(1): The charge registration obligation has EXTRATERRITORIAL SCOPE: The charge may be WITHIN INDIA OR OUTSIDE INDIA on the PROPERTIES OF THE COMPANY OR ASSETS or any of its undertakings, SITUATED IN OR OUTSIDE INDIA. This means: (1) A charge on company's property in the USA must also be registered with the Indian Registrar; (2) A charge by an Indian company on its foreign assets for a foreign loan must be registered. This global disclosure ensures creditors, investors and regulators in India have complete information about all the company's security obligations worldwide.
topic_text: Section 77 — Scope: Within and Outside India

question_html: Under Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Registration of Charges) Rules, 2014, in which forms must the particulars of charges be registered?

options.A: All charges in Form CHG-1 regardless of the type
options.B: All charges in Form CHG-9 regardless of the type
options.C: FORM CHG-1 for charges OTHER THAN DEBENTURES; and FORM CHG-9 for charges SECURING ISSUE OF DEBENTURES or charge created on debentures
options.D: All charges in Form CHG-2 — which is the only form for charge registration

answer_html:
Answer: (C) FORM CHG-1 for charges OTHER THAN DEBENTURES; and FORM CHG-9 for charges SECURING ISSUE OF DEBENTURES or charge created on debentures

Rule 3(1): FORMS FOR REGISTRATION OF CHARGES: (1) FORM CHG-1: for charges OTHER THAN DEBENTURES (including all types of charges on movable/immovable property, floating charges, charges on book debts etc.); (2) FORM CHG-9: for charges SECURING ISSUE OF DEBENTURES or charge created by a company through ISSUE OF DEBENTURES. After registration, the Registrar issues: FORM CHG-2 (certificate of registration of charge creation); FORM CHG-3 (certificate of registration of modification of charge); FORM CHG-5 (memorandum of satisfaction of charge).
topic_text: Rule 3 — Forms for Registration of Charges

question_html: Under Section 77(1), the particulars of the charge submitted to the Registrar for registration must be signed by:

options.A: Only the company's Board of Directors
options.B: Only the charge holder (lender) — not the company
options.C: Only the Company Secretary of the company
options.D: Both the COMPANY AND THE CHARGE HOLDER — the particulars shall be signed by both the company and the charge holder together with instruments creating such charge

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only the company's Board of Directors

Section 77(1): The PARTICULARS OF THE CHARGE must be signed by BOTH: (1) THE COMPANY; and (2) THE CHARGE HOLDER. This dual signature requirement ensures that: (a) The company acknowledges the security interest created; (b) The charge holder confirms the creation of the charge. Both parties must sign along with the INSTRUMENTS (if any) creating such charge. This bilateral authentication is fundamental to the charge registration process and prevents unilateral or fraudulent registration of fictitious charges. TIME LIMITS & CONDONATION OF DELAY — RULES 4, 5, SECTION 77
topic_text: Section 77 — Who Signs the Registration Particulars

question_html: Under Section 77(1), within what period from the date of CREATION OF A CHARGE must the company register it with the Registrar?

options.A: Within 60 days from date of creation
options.B: Within 30 DAYS from the date of creation of the charge — this is the PRIMARY TIME LIMIT; failure to register within 30 days requires application for condonation of delay or extension of time
options.C: Within 45 days from date of creation
options.D: Within 90 days from date of creation

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Within 30 DAYS from the date of creation of the charge — this is the PRIMARY TIME LIMIT; failure to register within 30 days requires application for condonation of delay or extension of time

Section 77(1): The TIME LIMIT for registration is 30 DAYS FROM THE DATE OF CREATION OF CHARGE. This is the primary filing deadline. After 30 days: FIRST EXTENSION via Registrar's condonation (up to total 120 days from creation) [Rule 4(1)]; SECOND EXTENSION via Registrar (within 300 days from creation) on payment of additional fees; BEYOND 300 DAYS: Application to CENTRAL GOVERNMENT for extension (Form CHG-8). Any subsequent registration shall NOT PREJUDICE rights acquired in respect of any property BEFORE the charge is actually registered.
topic_text: Section 77 — Primary Time Limit for Registration

question_html: Under Rule 4(1), if a company fails to register a charge within 30 days of its creation, the Registrar may condone the delay and allow registration within what maximum period?

options.A: Up to 60 days from date of creation
options.B: Up to 90 days from date of creation
options.C: Within 120 DAYS of creation of the charge or modification (i.e., another 30 days beyond the initial 30-day period) on payment of additional fee, if satisfied that company had SUFFICIENT CAUSE for not filing within 30 days
options.D: Up to 180 days from date of creation

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Within 120 DAYS of creation of the charge or modification (i.e., another 30 days beyond the initial 30-day period) on payment of additional fee, if satisfied that company had SUFFICIENT CAUSE for not filing within 30 days

Rule 4(1): FIRST CONDONATION: The Registrar may, if satisfied that the company had SUFFICIENT CAUSE for not filing within 30 days, allow registration for ANOTHER 30 DAYS but WITHIN A PERIOD OF 120 DAYS of the creation or modification of charge — on PAYMENT OF ADDITIONAL FEE. APPLICATION: Shall be made in FORM CHG-1 supported by a DECLARATION from the company signed by its SECRETARY OR DIRECTOR that such belated filing shall NOT ADVERSELY AFFECT THE RIGHTS OF ANY OTHER INTERVENING CREDITORS of the company. SUMMARY: 30 days (normal) + 30 days more (condonation) = within 120 days total from creation.

question_html: Under Section 77 and Rule 4, if a company fails to file within 120 days, the Registrar may allow further extension. What is the maximum total period allowed by the Registrar?

options.A: Up to 200 days from date of creation
options.B: Up to 400 days from date of creation
options.C: Up to 600 days from date of creation
options.D: Up to 300 DAYS from date of creation — Registrar may allow registration within 300 DAYS on payment of additional fees; if not registered within 300 days — company shall seek EXTENSION from Central Government

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Up to 200 days from date of creation

Section 77 / SECOND EXTENSION: The Registrar may, on APPLICATION BY THE COMPANY, allow registration to be made WITHIN A PERIOD OF 300 DAYS of such creation on payment of ADDITIONAL FEES. BEYOND 300 DAYS: If registration is NOT made within 300 days — the company shall SEEK EXTENSION OF TIME from the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT (Rule 12 — application in Form CHG-8). TIME SUMMARY: 0–30 days: Normal period; 31–120 days: First condonation (Rule 4(1)); 121–300 days: Second extension by Registrar; Beyond 300 days: Application to CG in Form CHG-8. ANY SUBSEQUENT REGISTRATION shall NOT PREJUDICE rights acquired BEFORE the charge is actually registered.
topic_text: Section 77 — Second Extension by Registrar (300 Days)

question_html: Under Rule 4(1), what must accompany the application for CONDONATION OF DELAY in registration of a charge?

options.A: Only an auditor's report confirming the creation of the charge
options.B: A DECLARATION from the company signed by its SECRETARY OR DIRECTOR (whoever is available) that such BELATED FILING SHALL NOT ADVERSELY AFFECT THE RIGHTS OF ANY OTHER INTERVENING CREDITORS of the company; the application is made in Form CHG-1
options.C: A court order directing the Registrar to accept the late filing
options.D: A certificate from the charge holder confirming the delay was justified

answer_html:
Answer: (B) A DECLARATION from the company signed by its SECRETARY OR DIRECTOR (whoever is available) that such BELATED FILING SHALL NOT ADVERSELY AFFECT THE RIGHTS OF ANY OTHER INTERVENING CREDITORS of the company; the application is made in Form CHG-1

Rule 4(1): The APPLICATION FOR CONDONATION OF DELAY must be made in FORM CHG-1 supported by a DECLARATION FROM THE COMPANY signed by its SECRETARY OR DIRECTOR (not necessarily managing director) that such BELATED FILING SHALL NOT ADVERSELY AFFECT THE RIGHTS OF ANY OTHER INTERVENING CREDITORS of the company. This declaration is crucial — it protects creditors who may have advanced credit relying on the absence of prior charges. The Registrar must be satisfied: (a) sufficient cause for not filing within 30 days; AND (b) the declaration confirms no adverse effect on intervening creditors.
topic_text: Rule 4 — Declaration for Condonation of Delay

question_html: Under Section 77, when a charge is registered BEYOND the normal 30-day period (whether within 120 days, 300 days, or later with CG extension), what is the effect on rights acquired BEFORE the actual registration?

options.A: All prior rights are extinguished — only rights arising after registration are protected
options.B: Any subsequent registration of a charge shall NOT PREJUDICE ANY RIGHT ACQUIRED IN RESPECT OF ANY PROPERTY BEFORE THE CHARGE IS ACTUALLY REGISTERED — registration has prospective protective effect only
options.C: Prior creditors get priority only if they had actual knowledge of the charge
options.D: Prior rights are protected only if the prior creditor files an objection

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Prior creditors get priority only if they had actual knowledge of the charge

Section 77: ANY SUBSEQUENT REGISTRATION OF A CHARGE shall NOT PREJUDICE ANY RIGHT ACQUIRED IN RESPECT OF ANY PROPERTY BEFORE THE CHARGE IS ACTUALLY REGISTERED. This critical provision protects: (1) Persons who acquired rights over the property (e.g., mortgagees, purchasers) AFTER the creation of the charge but BEFORE its actual registration; (2) Creditors who extended credit relying on the clean title of the property. The charge only binds persons who acquire rights AFTER the date of actual registration — not those who acquired rights in the gap between creation and registration.
topic_text: Section 77 — Subsequent Registration Not to Prejudice Earlier Rights

question_html: Under Rule 12(1), when must a company apply to the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT for extension of time to register a charge?

options.A: If the charge is not filed within 30 days of creation
options.B: If the charge is not filed within 120 days of creation
options.C: Where instrument creating/modifying charge NOT FILED WITHIN 300 DAYS; or SATISFACTION OF CHARGES not filed within 30 DAYS — Registrar shall NOT REGISTER unless delay condoned by Government; application in FORM CHG-8
options.D: If the charge is not filed within 60 days of creation

answer_html:
Answer: (A) If the charge is not filed within 30 days of creation

Rule 12(1): Two situations requiring CENTRAL GOVERNMENT condonation: (1) CREATION/MODIFICATION OF CHARGE: If instrument is NOT filed WITHIN 300 DAYS from creation or modification — Registrar shall NOT REGISTER unless delay condoned by CG; (2) SATISFACTION OF CHARGE: If not filed WITHIN 30 DAYS from date of payment/satisfaction (Note: Rule 8 says 300 days for satisfaction — there appears to be an inconsistency in rules; examination material treats this as requiring CG condonation if filed beyond 300 days). APPLICATION: in FORM CHG-8 along with fee. COMPLIANCE: CG's order must be filed with Registrar in FORM INC-28 [Rule 12(3)].
topic_text: Rule 12 — Central Government Extension of Time

question_html: Under Section 87(1), on what grounds may the Central Government extend time or rectify the register of charges?

options.A: Only if the company is a government company
options.B: Only on financial hardship grounds
options.C: Only if the charge holder consents to extension
options.D: CG may act if OMISSION was: (a) ACCIDENTAL or due to INADVERTENCE or SUFFICIENT CAUSE; (b) NOT OF A NATURE TO PREJUDICE position of CREDITORS OR SHAREHOLDERS; or (c) on any other grounds JUST AND EQUITABLE — CG may direct extension of time or rectification of omission or mis-statement

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Only on financial hardship grounds

Section 87(1): The CENTRAL GOVERNMENT, on being satisfied that: (a) omission to file particulars of charge/modification; (b) omission to register within required time or give intimation of satisfaction within stipulated time; (c) OMISSION OR MIS-STATEMENT of any particular was ACCIDENTAL OR DUE TO INADVERTENCE OR SOME OTHER SUFFICIENT CAUSE or is NOT OF A NATURE TO PREJUDICE THE POSITION OF CREDITORS OR SHAREHOLDERS; or (d) on any other ground IT IS JUST AND EQUITABLE TO GRANT RELIEF — may on application of the company or any PERSON INTERESTED, DIRECT that: time for filing/registration/intimation be EXTENDED, or OMISSION OR MIS-STATEMENT BE RECTIFIED. Section 87(2): Where CG extends time, the ORDER SHALL NOT PREJUDICE rights acquired BEFORE the charge is actually registered.
topic_text: Section 87 — Central Government Power to Rectify

question_html: Under Rule 12(3), when the Central Government passes an order for extension of time or rectification of the register of charges, where must this order be filed?

options.A: Only with SEBI for listed companies
options.B: With the company's internal compliance officer for record-keeping
options.C: The order shall be sent to both the charge holder and the depositor
options.D: The order passed by the Central Government shall be FILED WITH THE REGISTRAR in FORM INC-28 along with fees AS PER THE CONDITIONS STIPULATED IN THE ORDER

answer_html:
Answer: (C) The order shall be sent to both the charge holder and the depositor

Rule 12(3): The ORDER PASSED BY THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT (for extension of time or rectification) shall be REQUIRED TO BE FILED WITH THE REGISTRAR in FORM INC-28 along with FEES as per the conditions stipulated in the order. This ensures the CG's relief order is recorded in the public register maintained by the Registrar, maintaining transparency of the charge registration system. The filing in Form INC-28 brings the CG's order into the public domain and updates the official record accordingly.

question_html: Which of the following CORRECTLY states the complete time framework for registration of a charge under the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: 0–30 days: normal; 31–60 days: condonation by Registrar; 61–90 days: further extension; beyond 90 days: CG extension
options.B: 0–30 days: NORMAL PERIOD (Section 77); 31–120 days: FIRST CONDONATION by Registrar with sufficient cause + declaration (Rule 4(1)); 121–300 days: FURTHER EXTENSION by Registrar on payment of additional fees (Section 77); beyond 300 days: APPLICATION TO CENTRAL GOVERNMENT in Form CHG-8 (Rule 12); CG order filed with Registrar in Form INC-28
options.C: 0–60 days: normal; 61–180 days: extension by Registrar; beyond 180 days: CG extension
options.D: 0–15 days: normal; 16–90 days: Registrar extension; beyond 90 days: CG extension

answer_html:
Answer: (A) 0–30 days: normal; 31–60 days: condonation by Registrar; 61–90 days: further extension; beyond 90 days: CG extension

COMPLETE TIMELINE for charge registration: (1) 0–30 DAYS: NORMAL PERIOD under Section 77(1) — file in Form CHG-1 (or CHG-9 for debentures); (2) 31–120 DAYS: FIRST CONDONATION by Registrar [Rule 4(1)] — if satisfied of sufficient cause + declaration by CS/Director that belated filing won't harm intervening creditors; payment of additional fee; application in Form CHG-1; (3) 121–300 DAYS: SECOND EXTENSION by Registrar on application by company with additional fee [Section 77]; (4) BEYOND 300 DAYS: APPLICATION TO CENTRAL GOVERNMENT [Rule 12] in Form CHG-8; CG order filed with Registrar in Form INC-28. Throughout: subsequent registration shall NOT PREJUDICE rights acquired BEFORE actual registration. CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION — SECTIONS 77(2), RULE 6
topic_text: Time Limit Summary — Charge Registration Timeline

question_html: Under Section 77(2) and Rule 6, which of the following correctly describes the CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION of a charge?

options.A: Issued by the company to the charge holder — prima facie evidence of charge creation
options.B: ISSUED BY THE REGISTRAR in FORM CHG-2 to the company or the person in whose favour the charge is created; Rule 6(3): the certificate is CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE that the requirements of Chapter VI and the rules as to registration of creation or modification of the charge have been complied with
options.C: Issued by the company's auditors as part of annual audit certificate
options.D: Issued by SEBI for listed companies only

answer_html:
Answer: (B) ISSUED BY THE REGISTRAR in FORM CHG-2 to the company or the person in whose favour the charge is created; Rule 6(3): the certificate is CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE that the requirements of Chapter VI and the rules as to registration of creation or modification of the charge have been complied with

Section 77(2): Where a charge is REGISTERED WITH THE REGISTRAR, he shall ISSUE A CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION in such form and manner as may be prescribed to the COMPANY or to the PERSON IN WHOSE FAVOUR THE CHARGE IS CREATED. FORM: FORM CHG-2 [Rule 6(1)]. Rule 6(3): The CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION shall be CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE that the requirements of CHAPTER VI of the Act and the rules as to REGISTRATION OF CREATION OR MODIFICATION OF THE CHARGE have been complied with. CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE (not merely prima facie) — cannot be challenged or rebutted once issued. Compare: Registers = PRIMA FACIE evidence [Section 95].
topic_text: Section 77(2) — Certificate of Registration: Form & Evidentiary Value

question_html: Under Rule 6(2), when modification of a charge is registered under Section 79, the Registrar issues a certificate of modification. In which form is this certificate issued?

options.A: Form CHG-1 — same as the original registration form
options.B: FORM CHG-3 — the Registrar shall issue a CERTIFICATE OF MODIFICATION OF CHARGE in Form CHG-3 where particulars of modification are registered under Section 79
options.C: Form CHG-5 — the same form used for satisfaction of charges
options.D: Form CHG-2 — the same form used for original charge registration

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Form CHG-5 — the same form used for satisfaction of charges

Rule 6(2): Where the PARTICULARS OF MODIFICATION OF CHARGE are registered under Section 79, the Registrar shall issue a CERTIFICATE OF MODIFICATION OF CHARGE in FORM CHG-3. SUMMARY OF CERTIFICATES ISSUED BY REGISTRAR: (1) FORM CHG-2: Certificate of REGISTRATION OF CHARGE (original creation); (2) FORM CHG-3: Certificate of MODIFICATION of registered charge; (3) FORM CHG-5: MEMORANDUM OF SATISFACTION of charge. All three certificates represent conclusive evidence that the respective Chapter VI requirements have been complied with.
topic_text: Certificate of Modification of Charge — Form CHG-3

question_html: The Certificate of Registration of Charge (Form CHG-2) is CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE. What does this mean compared to 'PRIMA FACIE' evidence?

options.A: Conclusive evidence means the same evidentiary weight as prima facie evidence
options.B: Conclusive evidence means it can only be used in criminal proceedings
options.C: CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE = IRREBUTTABLE — CANNOT be contradicted by any other evidence; PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE (Sec.95: registers) = REBUTTABLE — presumed true unless contrary is proved; the distinction is critical in legal proceedings
options.D: Conclusive evidence means only admissible in civil courts

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Conclusive evidence means the same evidentiary weight as prima facie evidence

DISTINCTION in EVIDENTIARY VALUE: CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE [Rule 6(3) — Certificate of Registration CHG-2]: CANNOT BE REBUTTED or contradicted by any other evidence — it is FINAL AND IRREBUTTABLE proof that Chapter VI requirements for charge registration have been complied with. Once issued, no party can argue that the charge was not properly registered. PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE [Section 95 — Registers of members/debentures etc.]: Presumed to be true and accepted as proof UNLESS THE CONTRARY IS PROVED by other evidence — it is REBUTTABLE. Examination questions frequently test this crucial distinction.
topic_text: Conclusive Evidence vs Prima Facie Evidence

question_html: Under Section 77(3), what happens to a charge created by a company that is NOT DULY REGISTERED with the Registrar?

options.A: The charge becomes voidable at the option of the company but remains valid against the charge holder
options.B: NO CHARGE created by a company shall be TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT BY THE LIQUIDATOR OR ANY OTHER CREDITOR unless it is DULY REGISTERED AND A CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION HAS BEEN GIVEN by the Registrar — unregistered charge is VOID against liquidator and other creditors
options.C: The charge remains valid but the company is liable to a penalty only
options.D: The unregistered charge becomes void only after 60 days from creation

answer_html:
Answer: (B) NO CHARGE created by a company shall be TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT BY THE LIQUIDATOR OR ANY OTHER CREDITOR unless it is DULY REGISTERED AND A CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION HAS BEEN GIVEN by the Registrar — unregistered charge is VOID against liquidator and other creditors

Section 77(3): NO CHARGE CREATED BY A COMPANY shall be TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT by: (1) THE LIQUIDATOR (on winding up); or (2) ANY OTHER CREDITOR — unless it is DULY REGISTERED AND A CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION HAS BEEN GIVEN by the Registrar. EFFECT OF NON-REGISTRATION: The charge becomes VOID against the liquidator and other creditors — meaning in a winding up, the charge holder is treated as an UNSECURED CREDITOR. IMPORTANT SAVING [Section 77(4)]: This does NOT PREJUDICE any CONTRACT OR OBLIGATION for the REPAYMENT OF THE MONEY SECURED by the charge — the DEBT ITSELF REMAINS ENFORCEABLE even though the SECURITY (charge) is void.

question_html: Under Section 77(4), if a charge is not registered and becomes void against the liquidator/creditors, what happens to the UNDERLYING DEBT?

options.A: The debt also becomes unenforceable — the entire transaction is void
options.B: The debt is enforceable but only to the extent of 50% of the original amount
options.C: Section 77(3) shall NOT PREJUDICE any CONTRACT OR OBLIGATION for the REPAYMENT OF THE MONEY SECURED by the charge — the DEBT REMAINS FULLY ENFORCEABLE even though the SECURITY (charge) is void
options.D: The debt is only enforceable against the company's directors personally

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Section 77(3) shall NOT PREJUDICE any CONTRACT OR OBLIGATION for the REPAYMENT OF THE MONEY SECURED by the charge — the DEBT REMAINS FULLY ENFORCEABLE even though the SECURITY (charge) is void

Section 77(4): SAVINGS CLAUSE — Section 77(3) shall NOT PREJUDICE any CONTRACT OR OBLIGATION FOR THE REPAYMENT OF THE MONEY SECURED BY A CHARGE. PRACTICAL SIGNIFICANCE: (1) The SECURITY (CHARGE) is void against the liquidator and other creditors — the charge holder cannot enforce the charge; (2) BUT the DEBT ITSELF remains valid and enforceable; (3) The charge holder is TREATED AS AN UNSECURED CREDITOR and can still claim repayment from the company; (4) The company cannot argue that it need not repay the loan because the charge was not registered. The void charge only affects priority, not the underlying contractual obligation. MODIFICATION OF CHARGES — SECTION 79
topic_text: Section 77(4) — Debt Remains Enforceable Despite Void Charge

question_html: Under Section 79, the charge registration provisions of Section 77 apply mutatis mutandis to which of the following?

options.A: Only when a new charge is created on the same property
options.B: When company ACQUIRES ANY PROPERTY SUBJECT TO A CHARGE; or ANY MODIFICATION IN TERMS AND CONDITIONS OR EXTENT OR OPERATION OF ANY REGISTERED CHARGE — same registration procedure as original charge creation applies
options.C: Only when the charge holder changes due to assignment of the loan
options.D: Only when the company changes its name or registered office

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only when a new charge is created on the same property

Section 79: The provisions of Section 77 relating to REGISTRATION OF CHARGES shall, SO FAR AS MAY BE, apply to: (a) A company ACQUIRING ANY PROPERTY SUBJECT TO A CHARGE WITHIN THE MEANING OF SECTION 77 — when the company buys property that already has a charge on it; or (b) ANY MODIFICATION IN THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS OR THE EXTENT OR OPERATION OF ANY CHARGE REGISTERED under Section 77. MODIFICATION examples: change in interest rate; change in amount secured; substitution of property; extension of time for repayment; change of guarantee terms. After registration: Registrar issues certificate in FORM CHG-3 [Rule 6(2)].

question_html: Under Section 79, if a company ACQUIRES PROPERTY that already has a CHARGE on it, what obligation does the acquiring company have?

options.A: No obligation — the pre-existing charge dies automatically on acquisition
options.B: The company must REGISTER THE PARTICULARS OF SUCH CHARGE with the Registrar within 30 days of acquisition — applying Section 77 mutatis mutandis; must file particulars along with instruments evidencing the charge
options.C: The company must obtain charge holder's permission before acquiring property
options.D: The charge automatically gets discharged on transfer

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The company must REGISTER THE PARTICULARS OF SUCH CHARGE with the Registrar within 30 days of acquisition — applying Section 77 mutatis mutandis; must file particulars along with instruments evidencing the charge

Section 79: When a company ACQUIRES PROPERTY SUBJECT TO A CHARGE — the PROVISIONS OF SECTION 77 apply MUTATIS MUTANDIS (with appropriate modifications). This means: (1) The ACQUIRING COMPANY must REGISTER the particulars of the charge with the Registrar WITHIN 30 DAYS of acquisition; (2) The registration must be signed by both the acquiring company and the charge holder; (3) The Registrar will issue a certificate in Form CHG-2 or CHG-3 as appropriate; (4) All the time extension provisions (Rule 4, 300 days, CG condonation) apply equally. The rationale: the charge 'runs with the property' — the new owner must be known to have acquired encumbered property.
topic_text: Section 79 — Acquired Property with Existing Charge

question_html: Under Rule 6(2), when particulars of a MODIFICATION OF CHARGE are registered under Section 79, the Registrar issues:

options.A: Form CHG-1 — a new charge registration form
options.B: Form CHG-4 — the same form used for satisfaction
options.C: FORM CHG-3 — a CERTIFICATE OF MODIFICATION OF CHARGE showing modified particulars have been registered
options.D: Form CHG-9 — irrespective of type

answer_html:
Answer: (C) FORM CHG-3 — a CERTIFICATE OF MODIFICATION OF CHARGE showing modified particulars have been registered

Rule 6(2): Where the PARTICULARS OF MODIFICATION OF CHARGE are registered under Section 79, the Registrar shall issue a CERTIFICATE OF MODIFICATION OF CHARGE in FORM CHG-3. COMPLETE FORMS CHART: CHG-1: Application for registration (non-debenture); CHG-2: Certificate of CREATION of charge; CHG-3: Certificate of MODIFICATION of charge; CHG-4: Intimation of SATISFACTION of charge by company/charge holder; CHG-5: MEMORANDUM OF SATISFACTION issued by Registrar; CHG-6: Notice of APPOINTMENT/CESSATION of receiver or manager; CHG-7: Company's own REGISTER OF CHARGES; CHG-8: Application for CONDONATION of delay (Central Government); CHG-9: Application for registration of charge for DEBENTURES.

question_html: What is the KEY DISTINCTION between registering a MODIFICATION OF AN EXISTING CHARGE (Section 79) and creating a NEW CHARGE (Section 77)?

options.A: There is no practical distinction — both use the same form and procedure
options.B: Modification of charge does not require registration — only new charges need registration
options.C: Modification uses SAME SECTION 77 PROCEDURE mutatis mutandis — same 30-day limit, Forms CHG-1/CHG-9 for filing; DISTINCTION: New charge = Certificate CHG-2; Modification = Certificate CHG-3; modification does NOT create fresh security — it alters existing registered security
options.D: Modification requires CG approval but new charge requires only Registrar approval

answer_html:
Answer: (A) There is no practical distinction — both use the same form and procedure

MODIFICATION vs NEW CHARGE: SIMILARITIES (both under Section 77 procedure): (1) Same 30-day registration time limit; (2) Same Form CHG-1 (non-debenture) or CHG-9 (debentures) for filing; (3) Same condonation provisions (Rule 4, 300 days, CG extension); (4) Same requirement for signatures of company and charge holder; (5) Same registration fee structure. DIFFERENCES: (1) New charge: Certificate = FORM CHG-2; Modification: Certificate = FORM CHG-3; (2) New charge creates a fresh security interest; modification changes terms of existing security; (3) New charge triggers constructive notice from the date of its registration; modification updates the notice from the date of registration of the modification. REGISTRATION BY CHARGE HOLDER — SECTION 78
topic_text: Modification vs New Charge: Key Distinction

question_html: Under Section 78, when may the PERSON IN WHOSE FAVOUR A CHARGE IS CREATED apply to the Registrar for registration?

options.A: At any time — the charge holder has an independent right to register at any time
options.B: If the COMPANY FAILS TO REGISTER WITHIN PRESCRIBED PERIOD — the CHARGE HOLDER may apply to Registrar for registration along with INSTRUMENT CREATED FOR THE CHARGE; Registrar shall ISSUE NOTICE TO COMPANY giving 14 DAYS TIME to register or show sufficient cause
options.C: Only before the company becomes insolvent
options.D: Only with prior permission of NCLT

answer_html:
Answer: (B) If the COMPANY FAILS TO REGISTER WITHIN PRESCRIBED PERIOD — the CHARGE HOLDER may apply to Registrar for registration along with INSTRUMENT CREATED FOR THE CHARGE; Registrar shall ISSUE NOTICE TO COMPANY giving 14 DAYS TIME to register or show sufficient cause

Section 78: CHARGE HOLDER'S RIGHT: If a company FAILS TO REGISTER THE CHARGE WITHIN THE PRESCRIBED PERIOD (30 days + applicable extensions) — the PERSON IN WHOSE FAVOUR THE CHARGE IS CREATED (charge holder) may apply to the Registrar for registration of the charge along with the INSTRUMENT CREATED FOR THE CHARGE. REGISTRAR'S PROCEDURE: Issue NOTICE TO THE COMPANY giving 14 DAYS TIME — stating that unless the company itself registers the charge or SHOWS SUFFICIENT CAUSE why the charge should not be registered, the Registrar may allow such registration on PAYMENT OF PRESCRIBED FEES. RECOVERY: The charge holder who registered the charge is entitled to RECOVER THE AMOUNT OF ANY FEES OR ADDITIONAL FEES PAID from the COMPANY.
topic_text: Section 78 — Right of Charge Holder to Register

question_html: Under Section 78, when the Registrar receives an application from the CHARGE HOLDER for registration of a charge, what is the content and purpose of the 14-day notice issued to the company?

options.A: A show cause notice requiring the company to explain why it should not be penalised
options.B: The notice states: unless the COMPANY ITSELF REGISTERS THE CHARGE or SHOWS SUFFICIENT CAUSE WHY THE CHARGE SHOULD NOT BE REGISTERED — the Registrar may allow registration on payment of prescribed fees; giving company a final opportunity to register voluntarily or object
options.C: A notice requiring the company to pay all outstanding dues to the charge holder
options.D: A notice requiring the company to file a formal objection

answer_html:
Answer: (C) A notice requiring the company to pay all outstanding dues to the charge holder

Section 78: The REGISTRAR'S NOTICE to the company (on charge holder's application) shall state that: UNLESS the company: (a) ITSELF REGISTERS THE CHARGE (i.e., takes voluntary action to comply); or (b) SHOWS SUFFICIENT CAUSE WHY THE CHARGE SHOULD NOT BE REGISTERED — the Registrar may allow such registration on PAYMENT OF PRESCRIBED FEES. The notice provides: (1) A final opportunity for the company to comply voluntarily; (2) An opportunity for the company to challenge registration if there is a genuine dispute; (3) A 14-day deadline to respond. This balanced approach protects both the company (which may have a valid reason to object) and the charge holder (who needs the charge registered for security purposes).

question_html: Under Section 78, if the CHARGE HOLDER registers the charge on behalf of the company, who bears the cost of registration fees?

options.A: The charge holder bears the fees permanently — no recovery from company
options.B: Fees are shared equally between company and charge holder
options.C: The CHARGE HOLDER IS ENTITLED TO RECOVER THE AMOUNT OF FEES OR ADDITIONAL FEES PAID BY HIM for registration FROM THE COMPANY — company is ultimately responsible for all registration costs
options.D: The Registrar waives fees when registration is by the charge holder

answer_html:
Answer: (A) The charge holder bears the fees permanently — no recovery from company

Section 78: RECOVERY OF FEES: The CHARGE HOLDER WHO REGISTERED THE CHARGE is entitled to RECOVER THE AMOUNT OF ANY FEES OR ADDITIONAL FEES PAID BY HIM for the purpose of registration FROM THE COMPANY. This recovery right ensures: (1) The COMPANY is ultimately responsible for charge registration costs even when the charge holder had to initiate the registration process; (2) The charge holder is not financially penalised for the company's failure to register; (3) The company cannot escape its obligation by simply not registering and allowing the charge holder to pay. This right to recover fees is a DIRECT CONSEQUENCE of the company's breach of its duty under Section 77(1).
topic_text: Section 78 — Recovery of Registration Fees by Charge Holder

question_html: After the CHARGE HOLDER registers the charge under Section 78, what is the effect of such registration compared to registration by the company under Section 77?

options.A: Registration by charge holder has lesser evidentiary value than by the company
options.B: After charge holder registration, the company cannot subsequently modify or satisfy the charge
options.C: Registration by charge holder has THE SAME LEGAL EFFECT as by the company — Registrar issues same Form CHG-2 certificate; charge becomes effective against liquidator and other creditors from date of registration; charge holder recovers fees from company
options.D: Registration by charge holder is only valid for 6 months

answer_html:
Answer: (B) After charge holder registration, the company cannot subsequently modify or satisfy the charge

Section 78: Registration by the charge holder has THE SAME LEGAL EFFECT as registration by the company. After such registration: (1) The Registrar issues a CERTIFICATE IN FORM CHG-2 — CONCLUSIVE EVIDENCE of compliance; (2) The charge becomes PROTECTED AGAINST THE LIQUIDATOR AND OTHER CREDITORS from the date of actual registration; (3) CONSTRUCTIVE NOTICE under Section 80 operates from the date of registration; (4) The company's duty to register (Section 77) is deemed fulfilled; (5) The charge holder is entitled to recover fees from the company. The process gives the charge holder a practical remedy when the company defaults on its registration obligation. SATISFACTION OF CHARGES — SECTIONS 82, 83, RULE 8

question_html: Under Rule 8(1), within what period must a COMPANY OR CHARGE HOLDER give intimation of SATISFACTION OF A CHARGE to the Registrar?

options.A: Within 30 days from date of payment or satisfaction
options.B: Within 90 days from date of payment or satisfaction
options.C: Within 300 DAYS from date of PAYMENT OR SATISFACTION IN FULL — in FORM CHG-4 along with fee; can be given by either COMPANY or CHARGE HOLDER
options.D: Within 60 days from date of payment or satisfaction

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Within 300 DAYS from date of PAYMENT OR SATISFACTION IN FULL — in FORM CHG-4 along with fee; can be given by either COMPANY or CHARGE HOLDER

Rule 8(1): A COMPANY OR CHARGE HOLDER shall WITHIN A PERIOD OF 300 DAYS from the date of the PAYMENT OR SATISFACTION IN FULL of any charge registered under Chapter VI, give intimation of the same to the Registrar in FORM CHG-4 along with the fee. IMPORTANT ASPECTS: (1) BOTH the company AND the charge holder can give this intimation — unlike creation (where company has primary duty); (2) The 300-day period is much longer than the 30-day period for initial registration, recognising that satisfaction typically involves documentation and legal processes; (3) After intimation: Registrar gives 14-day notice to charge holder (unless charge holder signed the intimation).
topic_text: Rule 8(1) — Intimation of Satisfaction: Filing Period

question_html: Under Section 82(2), after receiving intimation of satisfaction of a charge from the company, what procedure does the Registrar follow?

options.A: Immediately records the satisfaction without further process
options.B: Registers satisfaction only after receiving confirmation from charge holder
options.C: REGISTRAR GIVES NOTICE TO CHARGE HOLDER to SHOW CAUSE within time NOT EXCEEDING 14 DAYS why satisfaction should not be recorded; if NO CAUSE SHOWN — Registrar orders MEMORANDUM OF SATISFACTION in Register and informs company in FORM CHG-5; if cause shown — Registrar records a NOTE and informs company
options.D: Cancels the charge automatically upon receipt of intimation

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Immediately records the satisfaction without further process

Section 82(2): On receiving intimation of satisfaction — REGISTRAR'S PROCEDURE: (1) GIVE NOTICE TO THE HOLDER OF THE CHARGE to SHOW CAUSE within such time NOT EXCEEDING 14 DAYS (as specified in the notice) as to WHY PAYMENT OR SATISFACTION IN FULL SHOULD NOT BE RECORDED; (2) If NO CAUSE IS SHOWN: Registrar shall ORDER that a MEMORANDUM OF SATISFACTION be entered in the Register of Charges and INFORM THE COMPANY in FORM CHG-5; (3) If CAUSE IS SHOWN: Registrar shall RECORD A NOTE TO THAT EFFECT in the Register and INFORM THE COMPANY. EXCEPTION: Notice NOT required to charge holder IF THE HOLDER OF CHARGE HAS SIGNED THE INTIMATION to the Registrar (self-verification).
topic_text: Section 82(2) — Registrar's Procedure After Satisfaction Notice

question_html: Under Section 82(2), in which specific situation is it NOT NECESSARY to send a notice to the CHARGE HOLDER before recording the satisfaction of a charge?

options.A: When the charge was created more than 10 years ago
options.B: When the company's auditors certify that the charge has been fully repaid
options.C: When the intimation to the Registrar has already been SIGNED BY THE HOLDER OF THE CHARGE HIMSELF — the charge holder has already acknowledged satisfaction, making the separate notice redundant
options.D: When the company's Board passes a resolution confirming satisfaction

answer_html:
Answer: (B) When the company's auditors certify that the charge has been fully repaid

Section 82(2): The notice (14-day show cause notice to charge holder) shall NOT BE REQUIRED to be sent to the holder of the charge, IF THE HOLDER OF CHARGE SIGNED IN THE INTIMATION TO THE REGISTRAR. RATIONALE: If the charge holder himself has signed the intimation of satisfaction, it indicates that the charge holder has already acknowledged that the debt has been paid and the charge satisfied. Sending a further notice to ask him to 'show cause why satisfaction should not be recorded' would be redundant — he has already confirmed it. This is a PRACTICAL EXCEPTION that simplifies the process when both parties agree on the satisfaction.
topic_text: Section 82 — When Notice to Charge Holder is NOT Required

question_html: Under Section 83(1), the Registrar may enter a MEMORANDUM OF SATISFACTION in the register of charges on his OWN MOTION. On what evidence may he do so?

options.A: Only on receipt of a court order directing such entry
options.B: Only when both the company and the charge holder agree and file joint application
options.C: On evidence to his satisfaction that: (a) DEBT HAS BEEN PAID OR SATISFIED in whole or in part; OR (b) PART OF PROPERTY released from charge or CEASED TO FORM PART OF COMPANY'S PROPERTY — he may enter memorandum of satisfaction NOTWITHSTANDING NO INTIMATION from company
options.D: Only when company has been wound up

answer_html:
Answer: (C) On evidence to his satisfaction that: (a) DEBT HAS BEEN PAID OR SATISFIED in whole or in part; OR (b) PART OF PROPERTY released from charge or CEASED TO FORM PART OF COMPANY'S PROPERTY — he may enter memorandum of satisfaction NOTWITHSTANDING NO INTIMATION from company

Section 83(1): The REGISTRAR MAY, on EVIDENCE GIVEN TO HIS SATISFACTION with respect to any REGISTERED CHARGE — that: (a) The DEBT for which the charge was given HAS BEEN PAID OR SATISFIED in whole or in part; or (b) PART OF THE PROPERTY or undertaking CHARGED HAS BEEN RELEASED from the charge or HAS CEASED TO FORM PART OF THE COMPANY'S PROPERTY OR UNDERTAKING — enter in the register of charges a MEMORANDUM OF SATISFACTION in whole or in part, NOTWITHSTANDING THAT NO INTIMATION HAS BEEN RECEIVED BY HIM FROM THE COMPANY. This suo motu power ensures the register remains accurate even when companies fail to report satisfaction. Section 83(2): Registrar shall INFORM AFFECTED PARTIES WITHIN 30 DAYS of making the entry.

question_html: Under Section 83(2), after the Registrar enters a memorandum of satisfaction on his OWN MOTION (without intimation from company), what must he do?

options.A: No further action required — the entry is final and binding
