Transit ENDS when: (a) BUYER OBTAINS DELIVERY BEFORE ARRIVAL at destination; (b) after ARRIVAL AT DESTINATION, the carrier ACKNOWLEDGES TO THE BUYER that he holds goods ON HIS BEHALF (even if further destination indicated); (c) if the carrier WRONGFULLY REFUSES TO DELIVER to the buyer. SPECIAL RULE: If goods are REJECTED BY THE BUYER and the carrier holds them, TRANSIT CONTINUES EVEN IF THE SELLER HAS REFUSED TO RECEIVE THEM BACK.

question_html: Under Section 54, an unpaid seller may RESELL the goods in which of the following situations?

options.A: At any time after the buyer fails to pay on the due date
options.B: Only after obtaining a court order for resale
options.C: (a) Where goods are PERISHABLE; (b) where the RIGHT IS EXPRESSLY RESERVED in the contract; (c) where after exercising lien/stoppage in transit the seller gives NOTICE OF INTENTION TO RESELL and the buyer does not pay within a REASONABLE TIME
options.D: Only where the goods are seasonal in nature

answer_html:
Answer: (C) (a) Where goods are PERISHABLE; (b) where the RIGHT IS EXPRESSLY RESERVED in the contract; (c) where after exercising lien/stoppage in transit the seller gives NOTICE OF INTENTION TO RESELL and the buyer does not pay within a REASONABLE TIME

Section 54 RIGHT OF RESALE: The unpaid seller may resell: (a) where goods are PERISHABLE; (b) where the RIGHT IS EXPRESSLY RESERVED IN THE CONTRACT; (c) where in exercise of RIGHT OF LIEN OR STOPPAGE IN TRANSIT, the seller gives NOTICE TO THE BUYER OF HIS INTENTION TO RESELL, and buyer DOES NOT PAY OR TENDER PRICE WITHIN A REASONABLE TIME. On resale: if there is a DEFICIENCY between price due and amount realized — seller can RECOVER from buyer; if SURPLUS — seller can KEEP IT (but must give surplus to buyer if no notice was given). REMEDIES & AUCTION SALES — SECTIONS 55–64

question_html: Under Section 58, a buyer may sue the seller for SPECIFIC PERFORMANCE in which situations?

options.A: When the goods are SPECIFIC OR ASCERTAINED and a court order for damages would NOT be an adequate remedy — generally for goods of special significance or unique value
options.B: Only when the goods are worth more than Rs. 1 lakh
options.C: In all cases of breach of contract by the seller
options.D: Only when the buyer has already paid the full price

answer_html:
Answer: (A) When the goods are SPECIFIC OR ASCERTAINED and a court order for damages would NOT be an adequate remedy — generally for goods of special significance or unique value

Section 58: When goods are SPECIFIC OR ASCERTAINED, a buyer may sue for SPECIFIC PERFORMANCE compelling the seller to deliver THOSE SPECIFIC GOODS. A court orders specific performance ONLY when: (a) goods are SPECIFIC OR ASCERTAINED; and (b) an order for DAMAGES WOULD NOT BE AN ADEQUATE REMEDY. Specific performance is generally allowed where goods are of SPECIAL SIGNIFICANCE OR VALUE — e.g., a RARE PAINTING, a UNIQUE PIECE OF JEWELLERY, an antique, etc. Section 57: Buyer may also sue for DAMAGES FOR NON-DELIVERY when seller wrongfully refuses to deliver.

question_html: An unpaid seller's RIGHTS AGAINST THE BUYER PERSONALLY (not against goods) under Sections 55, 56 and 61 include which of the following?

options.A: Only the right to sue for price — no other personal remedy
options.B: (i) Suit for PRICE when property has passed and buyer wrongfully refuses to pay; (ii) Suit for DAMAGES FOR NON-ACCEPTANCE when buyer wrongfully refuses to accept/pay; (iii) Suit for REPUDIATION (treating contract as cancelled and suing for damages); (iv) Suit for INTEREST
options.C: Only the right to sue for damages — not for price
options.D: Only the right of stoppage in transit

answer_html:
Answer: (B) (i) Suit for PRICE when property has passed and buyer wrongfully refuses to pay; (ii) Suit for DAMAGES FOR NON-ACCEPTANCE when buyer wrongfully refuses to accept/pay; (iii) Suit for REPUDIATION (treating contract as cancelled and suing for damages); (iv) Suit for INTEREST

Unpaid seller's RIGHTS AGAINST THE BUYER PERSONALLY: (1) SUIT FOR PRICE [Section 55]: Where PROPERTY HAS PASSED and buyer wrongfully refuses to pay — seller can sue for PRICE; (2) SUIT FOR DAMAGES FOR NON-ACCEPTANCE [Section 56]: Where buyer wrongfully refuses to accept and pay — seller sues for DAMAGES; (3) SUIT FOR REPUDIATION: If buyer repudiates BEFORE delivery date — seller may wait, or treat as cancelled and sue; (4) SUIT FOR INTEREST [Section 61]: Under specific agreement or from date notified by seller.

question_html: Under Section 64, when is an auction sale COMPLETE and binding, and what rights does the SELLER have regarding bidding?

options.A: Sale is complete when the auctioneer accepts the bid verbally — seller can freely bid through agents even without disclosure
options.B: Sale is complete when the reserve price is crossed — seller can always bid
options.C: Sale is COMPLETE when the auctioneer ANNOUNCES COMPLETION BY THE FALL OF THE HAMMER or other customary manner; a bidder may RETRACT HIS BID before such announcement; seller can bid ONLY if the right is EXPRESSLY RESERVED; if seller uses PRETENDED BIDDING to raise price, sale is VOIDABLE AT BUYER'S OPTION
options.D: Sale is complete when the highest bidder signs a written agreement — the seller can never bid

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Sale is COMPLETE when the auctioneer ANNOUNCES COMPLETION BY THE FALL OF THE HAMMER or other customary manner; a bidder may RETRACT HIS BID before such announcement; seller can bid ONLY if the right is EXPRESSLY RESERVED; if seller uses PRETENDED BIDDING to raise price, sale is VOIDABLE AT BUYER'S OPTION

Section 64 AUCTION SALES: (a) Each LOT is prima facie a SEPARATE CONTRACT; (b) Sale COMPLETE on FALL OF HAMMER or other customary announcement — any BIDDER MAY RETRACT HIS BID before such announcement; (c) SELLER MAY BID only if the RIGHT IS EXPRESSLY RESERVED — where not notified, it is NOT LAWFUL for the seller or auctioneer (knowingly) to take seller's bids; any such sale may be treated as FRAUDULENT by buyer; (d) Sale may have a RESERVE/SET-UP PRICE; (e) If seller uses PRETENDED BIDDING (shill bidding) to raise price — VOIDABLE AT BUYER'S OPTION. Section 64A: Tax changes after contract — seller may add/buyer may deduct the tax change amount. CONSOLIDATED ANSWER KEY — ALL 50 QUESTIONS — END OF QUESTION PAPER — Prepared from ICMAI Study Module | Sale of Goods Act, 1930 | Module 3 | Syllabus 2022 | CMA Inter June 2026

question_html: Under Section 61 of the Companies Act, 2013, a limited company having a share capital may, if authorized by its articles, alter its share capital in a general meeting in which of the following ways?

options.A: Only by increasing authorized capital — no other alterations are permitted without court approval
options.B: By increasing authorized capital; consolidating and dividing shares into larger amounts; converting fully paid shares into stock; sub-dividing shares into smaller amounts; or cancelling shares not taken — cancellation of shares shall NOT be deemed reduction of share capital
options.C: By reducing share capital — which can be done without Tribunal confirmation
options.D: By issuing bonus shares from revaluation reserves

answer_html:
Answer: (B) By increasing authorized capital; consolidating and dividing shares into larger amounts; converting fully paid shares into stock; sub-dividing shares into smaller amounts; or cancelling shares not taken — cancellation of shares shall NOT be deemed reduction of share capital

Section 61: A limited company may, if AUTHORIZED BY ITS ARTICLES, alter its memorandum in a general meeting to: (1) INCREASE authorized share capital; (2) CONSOLIDATE AND DIVIDE shares into larger amounts (no consolidation that changes voting % without Tribunal approval); (3) CONVERT fully paid-up shares into STOCK and reconvert; (4) SUB-DIVIDE shares into smaller amounts (paid/unpaid proportion must be maintained); (5) CANCEL shares not taken (deemed to DIMINISH, NOT REDUCE, share capital). Section 64: Notice to Registrar in Form SH-7 within 30 DAYS.
topic_text: Section 61 — Modes of Alteration of Share Capital

question_html: Under Section 64(1), within what period must a company file notice with the Registrar of Companies when it alters its share capital, or redeems any redeemable preference shares?

options.A: Within 15 days of such alteration or redemption
options.B: Within 7 days of such alteration or redemption
options.C: Within 30 DAYS of such alteration or increase or redemption — in Form No. SH-7 along with fee and altered memorandum; penalty for default: Rs. 1,000 for each day of default OR Rs. 5 LAKHS — whichever is LESS
options.D: Within 60 days of such alteration

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Within 30 DAYS of such alteration or increase or redemption — in Form No. SH-7 along with fee and altered memorandum; penalty for default: Rs. 1,000 for each day of default OR Rs. 5 LAKHS — whichever is LESS

Section 64(1): When a company ALTERS ITS SHARE CAPITAL, or an ORDER by the Government INCREASES authorized capital, or a company REDEEMS any REDEEMABLE PREFERENCE SHARES — the company shall file notice in FORM SH-7 with the Registrar WITHIN 30 DAYS of such alteration/increase/redemption, along with an ALTERED MEMORANDUM. PENALTY for default: Fine which may extend to RS. 1,000 FOR EACH DAY during which such default continues OR RS. 5 LAKHS — WHICHEVER IS LESS, for both company and defaulting officer.
topic_text: Section 64 — Notice of Alteration/Redemption to Registrar

question_html: Under Section 52 of the Companies Act, 2013, the Securities Premium Account may be applied by a company for which of the following purposes?

options.A: Issue of unissued shares as fully paid BONUS SHARES; writing off PRELIMINARY EXPENSES; writing off ISSUE EXPENSES or commission/discount on shares or debentures; providing for PREMIUM ON REDEMPTION of redeemable preference shares or debentures; and PURCHASE OF OWN SHARES (buy-back)
options.B: Only for issue of bonus shares and paying dividend to shareholders
options.C: Only for writing off preliminary expenses and providing for redemption premium
options.D: The securities premium account cannot be used for any purpose — it must remain as a reserve

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Issue of unissued shares as fully paid BONUS SHARES; writing off PRELIMINARY EXPENSES; writing off ISSUE EXPENSES or commission/discount on shares or debentures; providing for PREMIUM ON REDEMPTION of redeemable preference shares or debentures; and PURCHASE OF OWN SHARES (buy-back)

Section 52: SECURITIES PREMIUM ACCOUNT may be applied for: (1) ISSUE OF UNISSUED SHARES as fully paid BONUS SHARES to members; (2) WRITING OFF PRELIMINARY EXPENSES of the company; (3) WRITING OFF EXPENSES OF, or COMMISSION PAID OR DISCOUNT ALLOWED on any issue of SHARES OR DEBENTURES; (4) Providing for PREMIUM PAYABLE ON REDEMPTION of redeemable preference shares or debentures; and (5) PURCHASE OF OWN SHARES (buy-back) or other securities under Section 68. Section 52 provisions of reducing share capital apply to Securities Premium Account.

question_html: Under Section 53 of the Companies Act, 2013, shares issued at a discount are void. What is the EXCEPTION to this rule and what is the penalty?

options.A: Exception: Rights issue to existing shareholders; Penalty: fine up to Rs. 1 lakh
options.B: Exception: issue of SWEAT EQUITY SHARES and issue to creditors when DEBT IS CONVERTED INTO SHARES per RBI directions under statutory resolution plan/debt restructuring; Penalty: Company — fine Rs. 1 LAKH to Rs. 5 LAKHS; Officer — imprisonment up to 6 MONTHS or fine Rs. 1 LAKH to Rs. 5 LAKHS or BOTH
options.C: Exception: ESOP shares; Penalty: fine up to Rs. 5 lakhs only
options.D: Exception: bonus shares; no penalty prescribed

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Exception: issue of SWEAT EQUITY SHARES and issue to creditors when DEBT IS CONVERTED INTO SHARES per RBI directions under statutory resolution plan/debt restructuring; Penalty: Company — fine Rs. 1 LAKH to Rs. 5 LAKHS; Officer — imprisonment up to 6 MONTHS or fine Rs. 1 LAKH to Rs. 5 LAKHS or BOTH

Section 53: NO COMPANY shall issue shares AT A DISCOUNT — any share issued at a discounted price shall be VOID. EXCEPTIONS: (1) SWEAT EQUITY SHARES (Section 54); (2) A company may issue shares at a discount to its CREDITORS when DEBT IS CONVERTED INTO SHARES in pursuance of any STATUTORY RESOLUTION PLAN OR DEBT RESTRUCTURING SCHEME per RBI directions under RBI Act, 1934 or Banking (Regulation) Act, 1949. PENALTY [Section 53(3)]: COMPANY — fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 1 LAKH but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER — imprisonment up to 6 MONTHS or fine RS. 1 LAKH to RS. 5 LAKHS or BOTH.
topic_text: Section 53 — Prohibition on Issue of Shares at Discount

question_html: Under Section 66, a company limited by shares may reduce its share capital by special resolution. Which of the following requirements is CORRECT?

options.A: Only board approval required — no Tribunal confirmation needed for reduction of share capital
options.B: Reduction is valid only for listed companies with SEBI permission
options.C: SPECIAL RESOLUTION is required; TRIBUNAL CONFIRMATION is necessary; Tribunal gives notice to CG, Registrar, SEBI (listed), and creditors; creditors have 3 months to respond; accounting treatment must conform with accounting standards and AUDITOR'S CERTIFICATE must be filed with Tribunal; company delivers certified copy of order to Registrar within 30 DAYS
options.D: Simple majority resolution is required with NCLT approval; no auditor certificate needed

answer_html:
Answer: (C) SPECIAL RESOLUTION is required; TRIBUNAL CONFIRMATION is necessary; Tribunal gives notice to CG, Registrar, SEBI (listed), and creditors; creditors have 3 months to respond; accounting treatment must conform with accounting standards and AUDITOR'S CERTIFICATE must be filed with Tribunal; company delivers certified copy of order to Registrar within 30 DAYS

Section 66(1): REDUCTION OF SHARE CAPITAL by SPECIAL RESOLUTION; subject to CONFIRMATION BY TRIBUNAL. Forms of reduction: (a) EXTINGUISH/REDUCE LIABILITY on unpaid shares; (b) CANCEL PAID-UP CAPITAL lost or unrepresented by available assets; (c) PAY OFF PAID-UP CAPITAL in excess. TRIBUNAL PROCEDURE: Gives notice to CG, Registrar, SEBI (listed), and CREDITORS; creditors have 3 MONTHS to respond; if no response — presumed no objection. AUDITOR'S CERTIFICATE (accounting treatment conforming with standards) MUST BE FILED. FILING: Certified copy of order + minute to Registrar within 30 DAYS — Registrar registers and issues CERTIFICATE. PROHIBITION: No reduction if company in arrears in REPAYMENT OF DEPOSITS or INTEREST thereon.
topic_text: Section 66 — Reduction of Share Capital: Tribunal Confirmation

question_html: Under Section 66(10), if any officer of the company knowingly conceals the name of any creditor entitled to object to reduction, or misrepresents the debt/claim of any creditor, the penalty is:

options.A: Fine up to Rs. 1 lakh
options.B: Fine up to Rs. 5 lakhs; company and officer equally liable
options.C: Liable under SECTION 447 (Fraud); additionally, failure to comply with Tribunal's directions to publish order: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 5 LAKHS but may extend to RS. 25 LAKHS
options.D: Imprisonment up to 3 years only

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Fine up to Rs. 1 lakh

Section 66(10): PENALTY for officer who KNOWINGLY CONCEALS name of creditor entitled to object, KNOWINGLY MISREPRESENTS nature/amount of debt/claim, or ABETS/IS PRIVY TO such concealment/misrepresentation: LIABILITY UNDER SECTION 447 (FRAUD). SEPARATELY: If company FAILS TO COMPLY WITH TRIBUNAL'S DIRECTIONS to publish its order — company punishable with fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 5 LAKHS but may extend to RS. 25 LAKHS. These provisions are to protect creditors whose claims may be adversely affected by a reduction. TRANSFER & TRANSMISSION OF SHARES — SECTIONS 56, 57, 58, 59
topic_text: Section 66(10) — Penalty for Reduction of Share Capital Violations

question_html: Under Section 56 and Rule 11(1), an instrument of transfer of securities in physical form must be delivered to the company within what period from the date of execution?

options.A: Within 30 days from date of execution
options.B: Within 60 DAYS from the date of execution; filed in FORM SH-4; duly stamped, dated and executed by/on behalf of transferor AND transferee; share certificate to be attached (or letter of allotment if no certificate); transfer of partly paid shares — company gives notice in Form SH-5 to transferee; transferee must NOT OBJECT within 2 weeks
options.C: Within 90 days from date of execution
options.D: Within 15 days from date of execution

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Within 60 DAYS from the date of execution; filed in FORM SH-4; duly stamped, dated and executed by/on behalf of transferor AND transferee; share certificate to be attached (or letter of allotment if no certificate); transfer of partly paid shares — company gives notice in Form SH-5 to transferee; transferee must NOT OBJECT within 2 weeks

Section 56 / Rule 11(1): Instrument of transfer in PHYSICAL FORM shall be filed in FORM SH-4; every instrument of transfer shall be DELIVERED TO THE COMPANY WITHIN 60 DAYS from date of EXECUTION. Must be: duly STAMPED, DATED, and EXECUTED by or on behalf of the TRANSFEROR AND TRANSFEREE; CERTIFICATE relating to securities also to be sent (or LETTER OF ALLOTMENT if no certificate). PARTLY PAID SHARES: Company gives notice in FORM SH-5 to transferee; transfer shall NOT BE REGISTERED unless transferee gives NO OBJECTION within 2 WEEKS of receipt of notice. LOST INSTRUMENT: Company may register transfer on terms of INDEMNITY as Board thinks fit.

question_html: Under Section 56(6), what is the penalty if a company fails to comply with the provisions relating to transfer of securities?

options.A: Company: fine up to Rs. 5,000; officers: fine up to Rs. 1,000
options.B: Company and officers: imprisonment only
options.C: COMPANY: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25,000 but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 10,000 but may extend to RS. 1 LAKH; additionally, depository or depository participant who with INTENT TO DEFRAUD transfers shares: liable under SECTION 447
options.D: Company: fine up to Rs. 10,000; officers: fine up to Rs. 5,000

answer_html:
Answer: (C) COMPANY: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25,000 but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 10,000 but may extend to RS. 1 LAKH; additionally, depository or depository participant who with INTENT TO DEFRAUD transfers shares: liable under SECTION 447

Section 56(6): PENALTY for default in complying with Section 56: COMPANY = fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25,000 but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER = fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 10,000 but may extend to RS. 1 LAKH. SPECIAL PROVISION: Where any DEPOSITORY OR DEPOSITORY PARTICIPANT, WITHOUT PREJUDICE to any liability under the Depositories Act, 1996, WITH AN INTENTION TO DEFRAUD A PERSON, has transferred shares — it shall be liable under SECTION 447.
topic_text: Section 56(6) — Penalty for Default in Transfer

question_html: Under Section 57, any person who DECEITFULLY PERSONATES as an owner of any security or interest in a company is punishable with:

options.A: Imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 1 lakh
options.B: Fine only up to Rs. 5 lakhs without imprisonment
options.C: Only civil penalty payable to the genuine owner
options.D: Imprisonment NOT LESS THAN 1 YEAR but may extend to 3 YEARS AND fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 1 LAKH but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 1 lakh

Section 57: PERSONATION OF SHAREHOLDER: Any person who DECEITFULLY PERSONATES as an OWNER OF ANY SECURITY or INTEREST IN A COMPANY, or of any share warrant or coupon, and thereby OBTAINS OR ATTEMPTS TO OBTAIN any security/interest/warrant/coupon or RECEIVES OR ATTEMPTS TO RECEIVE any money due to such owner: Punishable with IMPRISONMENT for a term NOT LESS THAN 1 YEAR but may extend to 3 YEARS AND fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 1 LAKH but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS. This mandatory minimum imprisonment reflects the seriousness of impersonation of shareholders.

question_html: Under Section 58, a PRIVATE COMPANY that refuses to register a transfer of shares must send notice of refusal within 30 days. Within what period may the TRANSFEREE appeal to the Tribunal?

options.A: Within 15 days from receipt of refusal notice
options.B: Within 30 DAYS from receipt of refusal notice; OR within 60 DAYS from date of delivery of instrument if NO NOTICE was sent; for PUBLIC COMPANY refusal: appeal within 60 DAYS of refusal or 90 DAYS if no intimation received; Tribunal may direct transfer within 10 DAYS of its order and may award damages
options.C: Within 90 days from receipt of refusal notice
options.D: Within 45 days from receipt of refusal notice

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Within 30 DAYS from receipt of refusal notice; OR within 60 DAYS from date of delivery of instrument if NO NOTICE was sent; for PUBLIC COMPANY refusal: appeal within 60 DAYS of refusal or 90 DAYS if no intimation received; Tribunal may direct transfer within 10 DAYS of its order and may award damages

Section 58: PRIVATE COMPANY: Must send notice of refusal within 30 DAYS of receipt of instrument/intimation; TRANSFEREE may appeal to Tribunal within 30 DAYS of receipt of notice OR within 60 DAYS of delivery of instrument/intimation if NO NOTICE was sent. PUBLIC COMPANY: If refuses without sufficient cause within 30 DAYS of receipt — TRANSFEREE may appeal within 60 DAYS of refusal OR within 90 DAYS of delivery if no intimation received. TRIBUNAL ORDER: Dismiss appeal or direct TRANSFER/TRANSMISSION to be registered within 10 DAYS; direct RECTIFICATION of register; award DAMAGES. PENALTY for contravening Tribunal order: Imprisonment up to 3 YEARS and fine RS. 1 LAKH to RS. 5 LAKHS.
topic_text: Section 58 — Refusal to Register Transfer: Appeal Periods

question_html: Under Section 59, the Tribunal may pass an order for rectification of the register of members. Within what period must the company comply with such order, and what is the penalty for non-compliance?

options.A: Comply within 30 days; penalty Rs. 5,000
options.B: Comply within 15 days; penalty Rs. 10,000
options.C: The Tribunal directs transfer/transmission to be registered within 10 DAYS of receipt of order; PENALTY for default in complying with Tribunal order: COMPANY — fine RS. 1 LAKH to RS. 5 LAKHS; OFFICER — imprisonment up to 1 YEAR or fine RS. 1 LAKH to RS. 3 LAKHS or BOTH
options.D: Comply within 60 days; penalty Rs. 50,000

answer_html:
Answer: (C) The Tribunal directs transfer/transmission to be registered within 10 DAYS of receipt of order; PENALTY for default in complying with Tribunal order: COMPANY — fine RS. 1 LAKH to RS. 5 LAKHS; OFFICER — imprisonment up to 1 YEAR or fine RS. 1 LAKH to RS. 3 LAKHS or BOTH

Section 59(2): Tribunal may direct the transfer/transmission to be registered by the company WITHIN 10 DAYS of receipt of order, or direct rectification of records of depository or register, or direct payment of DAMAGES. Section 59(3): Right of HOLDER OF SECURITIES to transfer such securities shall not be restricted by Section 59; person acquiring such securities shall be ENTITLED TO VOTING RIGHTS unless suspended by Tribunal. Section 59(5) PENALTY for default in complying with Tribunal order: COMPANY — fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 1 LAKH but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER — imprisonment up to 1 YEAR or fine RS. 1 LAKH to RS. 3 LAKHS or BOTH.
topic_text: Section 59 — Rectification of Register of Members

question_html: Under Section 56, how is transmission of shares (as opposed to transfer) treated under the Companies Act?

options.A: Transmission is treated exactly like a transfer and the legal representative must be on register first
options.B: Transmission is only possible for listed company shares
options.C: Transmission by operation of law requires a court decree
options.D: Transmission by OPERATION OF LAW is registered on receipt of INTIMATION; transfer of deceased person's securities by LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE is VALID EVEN IF THE LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE IS NOT A HOLDER THEREOF at time of execution

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Transmission is treated exactly like a transfer and the legal representative must be on register first

Section 56: TRANSMISSION BY OPERATION OF LAW: Nothing in Section 56 prejudices the power of the company to REGISTER, ON RECEIPT OF AN INTIMATION OF TRANSMISSION OF ANY RIGHT TO SECURITIES BY OPERATION OF LAW from any person to whom such right has been transmitted. DECEASED PERSON'S SHARES: The transfer of any security or other interest of a DECEASED PERSON in a company made by his LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE shall, even if the legal representative is NOT A HOLDER THEREOF at the time of execution, be VALID AS IF HE HAD BEEN THE HOLDER at that time. Transmission is distinct from transfer — transmission occurs by operation of law (on death, insolvency, etc.) whereas transfer is by voluntary act. PREFERENCE SHARES — SECTIONS 43, 55, RULE 9, 10
topic_text: Section 56 — Transmission by Operation of Law

question_html: Under Section 43 Explanation (ii), preference share capital carries which of the following preferential rights?

options.A: Only preferential right to dividend — no right on capital repayment
options.B: Preferential right as to PAYMENT OF DIVIDEND (fixed amount or fixed rate) AND preferential right as to REPAYMENT OF CAPITAL in the case of WINDING UP or REPAYMENT OF CAPITAL; capital deemed preference capital even if it also has participatory rights in surplus dividend or surplus capital
options.C: Only preferential right to vote on all company matters
options.D: Preferential right to asset ownership in all resolutions

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Preferential right as to PAYMENT OF DIVIDEND (fixed amount or fixed rate) AND preferential right as to REPAYMENT OF CAPITAL in the case of WINDING UP or REPAYMENT OF CAPITAL; capital deemed preference capital even if it also has participatory rights in surplus dividend or surplus capital

Section 43 Explanation (ii): PREFERENCE SHARE CAPITAL = part of issued share capital carrying PREFERENTIAL RIGHTS: (a) PAYMENT OF DIVIDEND at FIXED AMOUNT or FIXED RATE (free of/subject to income tax); AND (b) REPAYMENT OF CAPITAL in case of WINDING UP or REPAYMENT (whether or not there is a right to payment of fixed premium). Explanation (iii): Capital is STILL PREFERENCE CAPITAL even if it has rights to PARTICIPATE in surplus dividend or SURPLUS CAPITAL on winding up — in addition to the preferential rights. Types: CUMULATIVE vs NON-CUMULATIVE; PARTICIPATING vs NON-PARTICIPATING; CONVERTIBLE vs NON-CONVERTIBLE; REDEEMABLE vs IRREDEEMABLE.
topic_text: Section 43 Explanation II — Preference Share Capital Definition

question_html: Under Section 55(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, which statement about IRREDEEMABLE PREFERENCE SHARES is correct?

options.A: Irredeemable preference shares may be issued with SEBI approval for infrastructure projects
options.B: Irredeemable preference shares may be issued for a period not exceeding 30 years for infrastructure companies
options.C: No company limited by shares shall, AFTER COMMENCEMENT OF THIS ACT, ISSUE ANY PREFERENCE SHARES WHICH ARE IRREDEEMABLE — all preference shares must be redeemable within 20 years (infrastructure companies: up to 30 years with minimum 10% redemption per year from 21st year onwards)
options.D: Irredeemable preference shares may be issued with consent of 3/4th of shareholders

answer_html:
Answer: (C) No company limited by shares shall, AFTER COMMENCEMENT OF THIS ACT, ISSUE ANY PREFERENCE SHARES WHICH ARE IRREDEEMABLE — all preference shares must be redeemable within 20 years (infrastructure companies: up to 30 years with minimum 10% redemption per year from 21st year onwards)

Section 55(1): NO COMPANY LIMITED BY SHARES shall, after commencement of the Act, ISSUE ANY PREFERENCE SHARES WHICH ARE IRREDEEMABLE. Section 55(2): A company may, if authorized by articles, issue preference shares REDEEMABLE WITHIN A PERIOD NOT EXCEEDING 20 YEARS from date of issue. EXCEPTION — Rule 10: A company engaged in SETTING UP AND DEALING WITH INFRASTRUCTURAL PROJECTS may issue preference shares for a period EXCEEDING 20 YEARS BUT NOT EXCEEDING 30 YEARS, subject to MINIMUM REDEMPTION OF 10% PER YEAR from the 21ST YEAR ONWARDS (or earlier on proportionate basis at shareholder's option).

question_html: Under Section 55(2) proviso, which of the following conditions must be satisfied for REDEMPTION OF PREFERENCE SHARES?

options.A: Preference shares may be redeemed out of any reserve from any source; partly paid shares can be redeemed
options.B: ONLY FULLY PAID preference shares shall be redeemed; redemption only out of PROFITS AVAILABLE FOR DIVIDEND OR PROCEEDS OF FRESH ISSUE OF SHARES for redemption; where redeemed out of profits — CAPITAL REDEMPTION RESERVE (CRR) created equal to NOMINAL AMOUNT of shares redeemed; PREMIUM ON REDEMPTION — from PROFITS or SECURITIES PREMIUM ACCOUNT
options.C: Any preference shares (fully or partly paid) may be redeemed; no CRR creation required
options.D: Preference shares may be redeemed from general reserve without CRR requirement

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Preference shares may be redeemed out of any reserve from any source; partly paid shares can be redeemed

Section 55(2) PROVISO — CONDITIONS FOR REDEMPTION: (a) ONLY FULLY PAID shares shall be redeemed; (b) Redeemed only out of: (i) PROFITS AVAILABLE FOR DIVIDEND; or (ii) PROCEEDS OF A FRESH ISSUE OF SHARES made for the purposes of redemption; (c) Where redeemed out of PROFITS — TRANSFER TO CAPITAL REDEMPTION RESERVE ACCOUNT (CRR) of a sum equal to NOMINAL AMOUNT of shares redeemed (CRR provisions as if paid-up share capital); (d) PREMIUM PAYABLE ON REDEMPTION: for prescribed class of companies — from PROFITS before redemption; for others — from PROFITS or SECURITIES PREMIUM ACCOUNT before redemption.
topic_text: Section 55(2) — Conditions for Redemption of Preference Shares

question_html: Under Section 55(3), where a company is UNABLE TO REDEEM preference shares or PAY DIVIDEND on them, the company may issue further redeemable preference shares with:

options.A: Board of Directors approval only
options.B: Consent of holders of THREE-FOURTHS IN VALUE of such preference shares AND APPROVAL OF THE TRIBUNAL; on issue of further shares, unredeemed shares deemed REDEEMED; Tribunal shall order IMMEDIATE REDEMPTION for those who did NOT CONSENT
options.C: Only SEBI approval for listed companies
options.D: Consent of majority holders and ROC approval

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Consent of holders of THREE-FOURTHS IN VALUE of such preference shares AND APPROVAL OF THE TRIBUNAL; on issue of further shares, unredeemed shares deemed REDEEMED; Tribunal shall order IMMEDIATE REDEMPTION for those who did NOT CONSENT

Section 55(3): Where a company is NOT IN A POSITION TO REDEEM any preference shares or PAY DIVIDEND — it may, WITH THE CONSENT OF SHAREHOLDERS OF THREE-FOURTHS IN VALUE OF SUCH PREFERENCE SHARES AND WITH THE APPROVAL OF THE TRIBUNAL on a petition, issue FURTHER REDEEMABLE PREFERENCE SHARES equal to the amount due (including dividend) in respect of unredeemed preference shares. On issue of such further shares: UNREDEEMED PREFERENCE SHARES DEEMED TO HAVE BEEN REDEEMED. TRIBUNAL ORDER: Order REDEMPTION FORTHWITH of preference shares held by persons who DID NOT CONSENT to the issue of further redeemable preference shares. Issue/redemption of such shares is NOT deemed INCREASE OR REDUCTION of share capital.
topic_text: Section 55(3) — Further Issue of Redeemable Preference Shares

question_html: Under Rule 9 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, what conditions must be fulfilled before issuing preference shares?

options.A: Only board approval is required for issuing preference shares
options.B: Only ordinary resolution at AGM required; no restriction on existing defaults
options.C: SPECIAL RESOLUTION at general meeting AUTHORISING THE ISSUE; NO SUBSISTING DEFAULT in redemption of EARLIER PREFERENCE SHARES or payment of DIVIDEND DUE on any preference shares; resolution must set out: priority for dividend/capital, participation in surplus, cumulative/non-cumulative, conversion terms, voting rights, redemption terms
options.D: SEBI approval is the only mandatory requirement

answer_html:
Answer: (C) SPECIAL RESOLUTION at general meeting AUTHORISING THE ISSUE; NO SUBSISTING DEFAULT in redemption of EARLIER PREFERENCE SHARES or payment of DIVIDEND DUE on any preference shares; resolution must set out: priority for dividend/capital, participation in surplus, cumulative/non-cumulative, conversion terms, voting rights, redemption terms

Rule 9 CONDITIONS for issue of preference shares: (1) SPECIAL RESOLUTION at general meeting authorising the issue; (2) Company has NO SUBSISTING DEFAULT in: (a) REDEMPTION OF PREFERENCE SHARES ISSUED EARLIER (before or after commencement of Act); or (b) PAYMENT OF DIVIDEND DUE on any preference shares. The RESOLUTION must set out: PRIORITY w.r.t. dividend/capital repayment vs equity shares; PARTICIPATION in surplus fund and surplus assets; CUMULATIVE or NON-CUMULATIVE dividend; CONVERSION terms; VOTING RIGHTS; REDEMPTION TERMS. Must be listed on stock exchange per SEBI regulations if company intends to list preference shares.
topic_text: Rule 9 — Issue of Preference Shares: Conditions

question_html: Under Rule 9(6), what are the permitted MODES OF REDEMPTION of preference shares?

options.A: Redemption only at a fixed date specified at time of issue
options.B: Redemption only at company's option after Tribunal approval
options.C: Redemption only on shareholder demand with board approval
options.D: Redemption: (a) at FIXED TIME or on HAPPENING OF PARTICULAR EVENT; (b) any time at COMPANY'S OPTION; or (c) any time at SHAREHOLDER'S OPTION — only on terms on which they were issued or as VARIED WITH APPROVAL OF PREFERENCE SHAREHOLDERS UNDER SECTION 48

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Redemption only at a fixed date specified at time of issue

Rule 9(6): MODES OF REDEMPTION of preference shares: (a) At a FIXED TIME or on the HAPPENING OF A PARTICULAR EVENT; (b) At any time at the COMPANY'S OPTION; or (c) At any time at the SHAREHOLDER'S OPTION. CONDITION: Preference shares may be redeemed ONLY ON THE TERMS ON WHICH THEY WERE ISSUED or as VARIED AFTER DUE APPROVAL OF PREFERENCE SHAREHOLDERS under Section 48 (variation of shareholders' rights). This flexibility in redemption modes allows companies to structure preference shares suited to their financing needs.

question_html: Which of the following CORRECTLY matches a type of preference share with its correct definition?

options.A: Cumulative preference share: Dividends lapse if not paid in any year; they do not carry forward
options.B: PARTICIPATING PREFERENCE SHARES: Fixed dividend PLUS right to PARTICIPATE IN SURPLUS PROFITS after equity dividend; CUMULATIVE PREFERENCE SHARES: Arrears of dividend ACCUMULATE and must be paid before equity shareholders receive any dividend
options.C: Non-participating preference shares: carry full right to participate in surplus profits
options.D: Convertible preference shares: automatically convert to debentures on non-payment

answer_html:
Answer: (B) PARTICIPATING PREFERENCE SHARES: Fixed dividend PLUS right to PARTICIPATE IN SURPLUS PROFITS after equity dividend; CUMULATIVE PREFERENCE SHARES: Arrears of dividend ACCUMULATE and must be paid before equity shareholders receive any dividend

TYPES OF PREFERENCE SHARES: (1) CUMULATIVE: Dividend arrears ACCUMULATE; must be cleared before equity dividend; unpaid for 2+ years → right to vote on ALL resolutions [Sec.47(2)]; (2) NON-CUMULATIVE: If dividend not paid in a year, it LAPSES — does not accumulate; (3) PARTICIPATING: Fixed preferential dividend + RIGHT TO PARTICIPATE IN SURPLUS PROFITS after equity gets their dividend; (4) NON-PARTICIPATING: Only fixed preferential dividend; (5) CONVERTIBLE: Can be CONVERTED INTO EQUITY SHARES on specified terms [Sec.71(1) for debenture conversion]; (6) NON-CONVERTIBLE: Cannot be converted; (7) REDEEMABLE: Must be redeemed within 20 years (or 30 for infra); (8) IRREDEEMABLE: PROHIBITED [Sec.55(1)].

question_html: Under Section 48(5), what is the PENALTY for default in complying with the provisions of Section 48 (variation of shareholders' rights)?

options.A: Company: fine up to Rs. 1 lakh; officers: fine up to Rs. 10,000
options.B: COMPANY: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25,000 but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER: imprisonment up to 6 MONTHS or fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25,000 but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS or BOTH
options.C: Company: fine up to Rs. 10 lakhs; officers: imprisonment up to 1 year
options.D: Only NCLT can impose penalty for violation of Section 48

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Company: fine up to Rs. 10 lakhs; officers: imprisonment up to 1 year

Section 48(5): Penalty for DEFAULT in complying with Section 48 (VARIATION OF SHAREHOLDERS' RIGHTS): COMPANY = fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25,000 but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS. EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER = punishable with IMPRISONMENT for a term which may extend to 6 MONTHS or with fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25,000 but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS or WITH BOTH. BUY-BACK OF SHARES — SECTIONS 68, 70

question_html: Under Section 68(2), which of the following conditions must be satisfied for a company to purchase its own shares (buy-back)?

options.A: Only board approval and AOA authorization required; no limit on quantum or debt ratio
options.B: Buy-back authorized by ARTICLES; SPECIAL RESOLUTION at general meeting (except if 10% or less of total paid-up equity capital and free reserves — BOARD RESOLUTION suffices); buy-back ≤ 25% of aggregate paid-up capital and free reserves; DEBT:EQUITY ≤ 2:1 after buy-back; shares must be FULLY PAID UP; no offer within 1 YEAR of preceding buy-back closure
options.C: Any proportion of shares can be bought back with board approval; no time gap requirement
options.D: Buy-back requires court order and ROC approval

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only board approval and AOA authorization required; no limit on quantum or debt ratio

Section 68(2) CONDITIONS for buy-back: (1) AUTHORIZED BY ARTICLES; (2) SPECIAL RESOLUTION at general meeting EXCEPT where buy-back is 10% OR LESS of total paid-up EQUITY CAPITAL AND FREE RESERVES (then BOARD RESOLUTION); (3) Buy-back ≤ 25% of AGGREGATE PAID-UP CAPITAL AND FREE RESERVES (for equity shares in any financial year — 25% of total PAID-UP EQUITY CAPITAL); (4) DEBT:EQUITY RATIO after buy-back ≤ 2:1 (CG may notify higher ratio for class/classes); (5) All securities for buy-back FULLY PAID UP; (6) For LISTED company — per SEBI regulations; for UNLISTED — per prescribed rules. TIME GAP: NO OFFER OF BUY-BACK WITHIN 1 YEAR from date of closure of PRECEDING BUY-BACK.

question_html: Under Section 68(4), every buy-back must be completed within what period from passing of the special resolution or board resolution?

options.A: Within 6 months from passing of resolution
options.B: Within 1 YEAR from passing of the special resolution or the resolution passed by the Board
options.C: Within 2 years from passing of resolution
options.D: Within 3 months from passing of resolution

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Within 1 YEAR from passing of the special resolution or the resolution passed by the Board

Section 68(4): Every BUY-BACK shall be COMPLETED WITHIN A PERIOD OF 1 YEAR from the date of passing of the SPECIAL RESOLUTION or the RESOLUTION PASSED BY THE BOARD. The letter of offer (Form SH-8) must be filed with Registrar (and SEBI for listed companies) BEFORE buy-back. Letter of offer dispatched to shareholders NOT LATER THAN 20 DAYS from filing with Registrar. Offer must remain open for NOT LESS THAN 15 DAYS and NOT MORE THAN 30 DAYS (less than 15 days if all members agree).

question_html: Under Section 68(5), buy-back may be made from which of the following sources?

options.A: Only from shareholders — market buy-back is not permitted
options.B: Only from the open market — not from shareholders directly
options.C: (a) From EXISTING SHAREHOLDERS OR SECURITY HOLDERS on a proportionate basis; (b) from the OPEN MARKET; or (c) by purchasing securities issued to EMPLOYEES under a scheme of STOCK OPTION or SWEAT EQUITY
options.D: Only from institutional investors and promoters

answer_html:
Answer: (C) (a) From EXISTING SHAREHOLDERS OR SECURITY HOLDERS on a proportionate basis; (b) from the OPEN MARKET; or (c) by purchasing securities issued to EMPLOYEES under a scheme of STOCK OPTION or SWEAT EQUITY

Section 68(5): BUY-BACK may be from: (a) EXISTING SHAREHOLDERS OR SECURITY HOLDERS on a PROPORTIONATE BASIS; (b) from the OPEN MARKET; or (c) by purchasing securities issued to employees under a SCHEME OF STOCK OPTION OR SWEAT EQUITY. IMPORTANT OBLIGATIONS (Rule 17(10)): (1) Company shall not ISSUE ANY NEW SHARES including bonus shares from date of passing of SR authorising buy-back till date of closure of offer (except convertible instruments); (2) Company shall not WITHDRAW the offer once announced; (3) Company shall not utilise BORROWED MONEY from banks/financial institutions for buy-back.

question_html: Under Section 68(6) and (7), which of the following statements about a company's obligations in a buy-back is CORRECT?

options.A: LISTED COMPANY must file a DECLARATION OF SOLVENCY in Form SH-9 with Registrar AND SEBI before buy-back (signed by at least 2 directors including MD; UNLISTED company need NOT file with SEBI); shares bought back must be EXTINGUISHED AND PHYSICALLY DESTROYED within 7 DAYS of last date of completion of buy-back
options.B: Unlisted company must file solvency declaration with both Registrar and SEBI
options.C: Shares bought back may be kept in treasury for re-issue within 6 months
options.D: Destruction of share certificates is optional at the company's discretion

answer_html:
Answer: (A) LISTED COMPANY must file a DECLARATION OF SOLVENCY in Form SH-9 with Registrar AND SEBI before buy-back (signed by at least 2 directors including MD; UNLISTED company need NOT file with SEBI); shares bought back must be EXTINGUISHED AND PHYSICALLY DESTROYED within 7 DAYS of last date of completion of buy-back

Section 68(6): LISTED COMPANY must before buy-back FILE WITH REGISTRAR AND SEBI a DECLARATION OF SOLVENCY in FORM SH-9; signed by AT LEAST 2 DIRECTORS including the MANAGING DIRECTOR (if any); VERIFIED BY AFFIDAVIT that Board has made full inquiry and formed opinion that company is CAPABLE OF MEETING ITS LIABILITIES and will NOT BE RENDERED INSOLVENT within 1 YEAR. UNLISTED COMPANY: NOT required to file with SEBI. Section 68(7): Company shall EXTINGUISH AND PHYSICALLY DESTROY the shares/securities bought back WITHIN 7 DAYS OF THE LAST DATE OF COMPLETION OF BUY-BACK. Register of buy-back shares: FORM SH-10.
topic_text: Section 68(6)(7) — Solvency Certificate & Destruction of Certificates

question_html: Under Section 68(8), after completing a buy-back, a company is PROHIBITED from making a further issue of the SAME KIND of shares or securities within what period?

options.A: Within 1 year — no exceptions
options.B: Within 6 MONTHS — EXCEPT by way of: BONUS SHARES; discharge of subsisting obligations such as CONVERSION OF WARRANTS, STOCK OPTION SCHEMES, SWEAT EQUITY, or CONVERSION OF PREFERENCE SHARES OR DEBENTURES into equity shares
options.C: Within 3 months — no exceptions
options.D: Within 2 years — except for rights issue

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Within 6 MONTHS — EXCEPT by way of: BONUS SHARES; discharge of subsisting obligations such as CONVERSION OF WARRANTS, STOCK OPTION SCHEMES, SWEAT EQUITY, or CONVERSION OF PREFERENCE SHARES OR DEBENTURES into equity shares

Section 68(8): After completing buy-back of shares/securities, company shall NOT make a FURTHER ISSUE OF THE SAME KIND OF SHARES OR OTHER SECURITIES (including allotment of new shares) within a period of 6 MONTHS — EXCEPT: (a) by way of BONUS SHARES; or (b) in discharge of SUBSISTING OBLIGATIONS such as CONVERSION OF WARRANTS, STOCK OPTION SCHEMES, SWEAT EQUITY, or CONVERSION OF PREFERENCE SHARES OR DEBENTURES INTO EQUITY SHARES. This prevents companies from conducting frequent buy-backs and fresh issues as a pattern.
topic_text: Section 68(8) — Prohibition on Fresh Issue After Buy-Back

question_html: Under Section 68(10), within what period must a LISTED company file the return after completion of buy-back, and in which forms?

options.A: Within 15 days of completion; in Form SH-9
options.B: Within 60 days of completion; in Form SH-11
options.C: Within 30 DAYS of completion: in FORM SH-11 (with fee); CERTIFICATE in FORM SH-15 signed by 2 directors including MD certifying compliance; UNLISTED need not file with SEBI; penalty: Company — fine RS. 1 LAKH to RS. 3 LAKHS; Officer — imprisonment up to 3 YEARS or fine RS. 1 LAKH to RS. 3 LAKHS or BOTH
options.D: Within 45 days of completion; in Form SH-8

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Within 30 DAYS of completion: in FORM SH-11 (with fee); CERTIFICATE in FORM SH-15 signed by 2 directors including MD certifying compliance; UNLISTED need not file with SEBI; penalty: Company — fine RS. 1 LAKH to RS. 3 LAKHS; Officer — imprisonment up to 3 YEARS or fine RS. 1 LAKH to RS. 3 LAKHS or BOTH

Section 68(10): LISTED COMPANY: After completion of buy-back, file with REGISTRAR AND SEBI a RETURN in FORM SH-11 with fee, containing prescribed particulars, WITHIN 30 DAYS of completion. Annexe: CERTIFICATE IN FORM SH-15 signed by 2 DIRECTORS including MD (if any) certifying buy-back compliance. UNLISTED COMPANY: No return required to be filed with SEBI. Section 68(11) PENALTY: COMPANY — fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 1 LAKH but may extend to RS. 3 LAKHS; EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER — imprisonment up to 3 YEARS or fine RS. 1 LAKH to RS. 3 LAKHS or BOTH.

question_html: Under Section 70, a company is PROHIBITED from directly or indirectly purchasing its own shares through which of the following?

options.A: Only through third-party brokers
options.B: Only through its holding company
options.C: Through any SUBSIDIARY COMPANY (including own subsidiaries); through any INVESTMENT COMPANY or group of investment companies; OR if there is a DEFAULT in: repayment of deposits/interest, redemption of debentures or preference shares, payment of dividend, or repayment of term loan/interest to financial institution/banking company — UNLESS default remedied AND 3 YEARS HAVE LAPSED after default ceased
options.D: Only through its associate companies; subsidiaries excluded

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only through third-party brokers

Section 70: NO COMPANY shall directly or indirectly purchase its own shares through: (1) Any SUBSIDIARY COMPANY including its own subsidiary companies; (2) Any INVESTMENT COMPANY or GROUP OF INVESTMENT COMPANIES; (3) Where there is a DEFAULT in: REPAYMENT OF DEPOSITS (before or after Act), INTEREST PAYMENT, REDEMPTION OF DEBENTURES OR PREFERENCE SHARES, PAYMENT OF DIVIDEND to any shareholder, REPAYMENT OF ANY TERM LOAN OR INTEREST to any FINANCIAL INSTITUTION OR BANKING COMPANY. EXCEPTION: Buy-back NOT PROHIBITED if the default is REMEDIED and a period of 3 YEARS has LAPSED after such default ceased to subsist.
topic_text: Section 70 — Prohibition on Buy-Back in Certain Circumstances

question_html: Under Section 68(3), the notice of the meeting at which the special resolution is proposed to be passed for buy-back shall be accompanied by an EXPLANATORY STATEMENT stating which information?

options.A: Only the buy-back price and total number of shares
options.B: FULL AND COMPLETE DISCLOSURE OF ALL MATERIAL FACTS; NECESSITY for buy-back; CLASS OF SHARES OR SECURITIES intended to be purchased; AMOUNT TO BE INVESTED under buy-back; and TIME LIMIT FOR COMPLETION of buy-back
options.C: Only the names of shareholders from whom shares will be purchased
options.D: Only the buy-back price and source of funds

answer_html:
Answer: (B) FULL AND COMPLETE DISCLOSURE OF ALL MATERIAL FACTS; NECESSITY for buy-back; CLASS OF SHARES OR SECURITIES intended to be purchased; AMOUNT TO BE INVESTED under buy-back; and TIME LIMIT FOR COMPLETION of buy-back

Section 68(3): The notice of the meeting (at which special resolution for buy-back is proposed) shall be accompanied by an EXPLANATORY STATEMENT stating: (a) FULL AND COMPLETE DISCLOSURE OF ALL MATERIAL FACTS; (b) NECESSITY FOR BUY-BACK; (c) CLASS OF SHARES OR SECURITIES intended to be purchased; (d) AMOUNT TO BE INVESTED under the buy-back; and (e) TIME LIMIT FOR COMPLETION of the buy-back. The explanatory statement must also contain (per Rule 17 for private/unlisted companies): board meeting date approving proposal; objective; buy-back method; price and basis; source of funds; promoters' shareholding; solvency confirmation; and auditors' report.
topic_text: Section 68(3) — Special Resolution for Buy-Back: Contents

question_html: Under Rule 17(2), (5) and (7), which of the following correctly states the key timelines for the buy-back letter of offer process?

options.A: Filed with Registrar 30 days before dispatch; offer open for 60 days; verification within 30 days
options.B: LETTER OF OFFER (Form SH-8) filed with Registrar; dispatched to shareholders NOT LATER THAN 20 DAYS of filing; OFFER OPEN: NOT LESS THAN 15 DAYS AND NOT MORE THAN 30 DAYS from dispatch (less than 15 if all members agree); VERIFICATION: within 15 DAYS from closure; shares deemed ACCEPTED unless REJECTION communicated within 21 DAYS from closure; separate bank account opened IMMEDIATELY after closure
options.C: Filed 10 days before dispatch; offer open for 7 days; verification within 7 days
options.D: Filed 60 days before dispatch; offer open for 45 days; verification within 30 days

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Filed 10 days before dispatch; offer open for 7 days; verification within 7 days

Rule 17 TIMELINES: (2) LETTER OF OFFER (Form SH-8): filed with Registrar; dispatched to shareholders IMMEDIATELY after filing but NOT LATER THAN 20 DAYS from filing; (5) OFFER OPEN: NOT LESS THAN 15 DAYS AND NOT MORE THAN 30 DAYS from date of dispatch (less than 15 days if ALL MEMBERS AGREE); (6) If oversubscribed: acceptance on PROPORTIONATE BASIS; (7) VERIFICATION: Company completes verification WITHIN 15 DAYS from closure; shares lodged DEEMED ACCEPTED unless COMMUNICATION OF REJECTION made within 21 DAYS from closure; (8) Separate bank account opened IMMEDIATELY after closure; (9) Within 7 DAYS of the 21-day period — make CASH PAYMENT to accepted shareholders OR return certificates to those not accepted.
topic_text: Buy-Back Letter of Offer: Rule 17 Key Requirements

question_html: Under Rule 17(10), what is a company PROHIBITED from doing from the date of passing the special resolution authorising buy-back till the date of closure of offer?

options.A: The company is only prohibited from reducing its authorized share capital
options.B: PROHIBITED: ISSUING ANY NEW SHARES including BONUS SHARES (except from outstanding convertible instruments); WITHDRAWING the offer once announced; UTILISING BORROWED MONEY from banks/FIs for buy-back; using PROCEEDS OF EARLIER ISSUE OF SAME KIND of securities for buy-back
options.C: The company is prohibited only from issuing debentures or preference shares
options.D: The company is prohibited from paying dividends during the buy-back period

answer_html:
Answer: (A) The company is only prohibited from reducing its authorized share capital

Rule 17(10) OBLIGATIONS DURING BUY-BACK: (1) NOT ISSUE ANY NEW SHARES including bonus shares from date of SR till date of closure (EXCEPT arising from outstanding convertible instruments); (2) NOT WITHDRAW the offer once announced; (3) Confirm opening of SEPARATE BANK ACCOUNT and payment by CASH; (4) NOT UTILISE BORROWED MONEY FROM BANKS OR FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS for buy-back purposes; (5) NOT UTILISE PROCEEDS OF AN EARLIER ISSUE OF THE SAME KIND OF SHARES OR SAME KIND OF OTHER SPECIFIED SECURITIES for buy-back. DEBENTURES — SECTIONS 2(30), 71, RULE 18

question_html: Under Section 2(30) and Section 71, which of the following correctly describes debentures under the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Debentures must always be secured by a charge on company's assets
options.B: DEBENTURES include DEBENTURE STOCK, BONDS or any INSTRUMENT OF A COMPANY EVIDENCING A DEBT — whether or not constituting a charge on assets; convertible debentures require SPECIAL RESOLUTION; debentures shall NOT CARRY VOTING RIGHTS; MOVEABLE PROPERTY transferable per articles
options.C: Debentures carry voting rights equal to number of shares they can be converted into
options.D: Debentures can only be issued for a period not exceeding 5 years

answer_html:
Answer: (B) DEBENTURES include DEBENTURE STOCK, BONDS or any INSTRUMENT OF A COMPANY EVIDENCING A DEBT — whether or not constituting a charge on assets; convertible debentures require SPECIAL RESOLUTION; debentures shall NOT CARRY VOTING RIGHTS; MOVEABLE PROPERTY transferable per articles

Section 2(30): DEBENTURE includes DEBENTURE STOCK, BONDS or ANY OTHER INSTRUMENT of a company EVIDENCING A DEBT — whether CONSTITUTING A CHARGE ON THE ASSETS OF A COMPANY OR NOT. Section 44: Debentures are MOVEABLE PROPERTY transferable in the manner provided in articles. Section 71(1): Convertible debentures (option to convert into shares wholly or partly) require SPECIAL RESOLUTION. Section 71(2): NO COMPANY shall issue any DEBENTURES CARRYING VOTING RIGHTS. Key comparison: unlike equity shares, debentures confer NO VOTING RIGHTS but have priority in repayment over shareholders.
topic_text: Section 2(30) & 71 — Definition and Key Features of Debentures

question_html: Under Rule 18(1) of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, what is the maximum period for redemption of SECURED DEBENTURES, and which types of companies can exceed this?

options.A: Maximum 5 years; no exceptions for any company
options.B: Maximum 10 YEARS from date of issue (general rule); EXCEPTIONS (may exceed 10 YEARS BUT NOT 30 YEARS): companies engaged in INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS; INFRASTRUCTURE FINANCE COMPANIES; INFRASTRUCTURE DEBT FUND NBFCs; debenture trustee must be appointed BEFORE ISSUE OF PROSPECTUS or NOT LATER THAN 60 DAYS AFTER ALLOTMENT
options.C: Maximum 20 years; only government companies can exceed this
options.D: No maximum period; debentures can be issued for any period

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Maximum 20 years; only government companies can exceed this

Rule 18(1) SECURED DEBENTURES: Date of redemption shall NOT EXCEED 10 YEARS from date of issue. EXCEPTIONS (MAY EXCEED 10 YEARS BUT NOT EXCEED 30 YEARS): (a) Companies engaged in INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS; (b) INFRASTRUCTURE FINANCE COMPANIES; (c) INFRASTRUCTURE DEBT FUND NON BANKING FINANCIAL COMPANIES. Security: CHARGE ON PROPERTIES/ASSETS sufficient for repayment of principal and interest; DEBENTURE TRUSTEE must be appointed BEFORE ISSUE OF PROSPECTUS or offer or NOT LATER THAN 60 DAYS AFTER ALLOTMENT; DEBENTURE DEED executed to protect debenture holders; CHARGE or MORTGAGE in favour of debenture trustee on specific movable or immovable property.

question_html: Under Rule 18(2)(c), which of the following persons CANNOT be appointed as a DEBENTURE TRUSTEE?

options.A: A person who BENEFICIALLY HOLDS SHARES in the company; who IS A PROMOTER, DIRECTOR or KMP or employee of the company or its holding/subsidiary/associate; who is BENEFICIALLY ENTITLED TO MONEYS payable by the company; who is INDEBTED to the company; who has a PECUNIARY RELATIONSHIP amounting to 2% of gross turnover/total income or Rs. 50 LAKHS (lower) in 2 preceding/current financial years; who is a RELATIVE OF PROMOTER or director/KMP
options.B: A professional like a chartered accountant or company secretary
options.C: A person who is employed by a public financial institution
options.D: Any person who is not a resident of India

answer_html:
Answer: (A) A person who BENEFICIALLY HOLDS SHARES in the company; who IS A PROMOTER, DIRECTOR or KMP or employee of the company or its holding/subsidiary/associate; who is BENEFICIALLY ENTITLED TO MONEYS payable by the company; who is INDEBTED to the company; who has a PECUNIARY RELATIONSHIP amounting to 2% of gross turnover/total income or Rs. 50 LAKHS (lower) in 2 preceding/current financial years; who is a RELATIVE OF PROMOTER or director/KMP

Rule 18(2)(c): CANNOT BE DEBENTURE TRUSTEE: (1) Beneficially holds SHARES IN THE COMPANY; (2) Is a PROMOTER, DIRECTOR, KMP, OTHER OFFICER OR EMPLOYEE of the company or its HOLDING, SUBSIDIARY OR ASSOCIATE; (3) Beneficially entitled to MONEYS payable by the company (other than trustee remuneration); (4) INDEBTED to the company, its subsidiary, holding, associate, or subsidiary of holding; (5) Has PECUNIARY RELATIONSHIP with the company amounting to 2% of gross turnover or total income or RS. 50 LAKHS (whichever is LOWER) during 2 preceding or current financial years; (6) Is a RELATIVE of any PROMOTER or any person in the employment of company as DIRECTOR or KMP.
topic_text: Rule 18(2) — Who CANNOT be Debenture Trustee

question_html: Under Rule 18, any DEBENTURE TRUSTEE may be REMOVED from office before the expiry of his term only with the approval of:

options.A: Simple majority of the Board of Directors
options.B: Approval of NCLT on application by any debenture holder
options.C: Approval of CG and ROC jointly
options.D: Holders of NOT LESS THAN THREE-FOURTHS IN VALUE OF DEBENTURES OUTSTANDING at their meeting; VACANCY BY RESIGNATION: filled only with WRITTEN CONSENT OF MAJORITY OF DEBENTURE HOLDERS; Board may fill CASUAL VACANCY; remaining trustee(s) may act while vacancy continues

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Approval of NCLT on application by any debenture holder

Rule 18(2): REMOVAL OF DEBENTURE TRUSTEE: Any debenture trustee may be removed from office BEFORE EXPIRY OF HIS TERM only if approved by holders of NOT LESS THAN THREE-FOURTHS IN VALUE OF THE DEBENTURES OUTSTANDING at their meeting. VACANCY: Board may fill any CASUAL VACANCY; while any vacancy continues, REMAINING TRUSTEE(S), IF ANY, MAY ACT. VACANCY BY RESIGNATION: shall only be filled with the WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE MAJORITY OF THE DEBENTURE HOLDERS. MEETING OF DEBENTURE HOLDERS [Rule 18(4)]: Convened by debenture trustees on: requisition in writing signed by debenture holders holding AT LEAST ONE-TENTH IN VALUE of debentures outstanding; OR happening of any breach, default or event affecting interests of debenture holders.

question_html: Under Rule 18(3), which of the following is a DUTY of the debenture trustee?

options.A: To maximise returns for the company and approve all board decisions
options.B: To audit the company's financial statements annually
options.C: APPOINTMENT OF NOMINEE DIRECTOR on Board in event of: (i) TWO CONSECUTIVE DEFAULTS in payment of INTEREST; (ii) DEFAULT IN CREATION OF SECURITY for debentures; or (iii) DEFAULT IN REDEMPTION OF DEBENTURES; and ensure debenture redemption reserve creation and adequate assets for discharge of interest and principal
options.D: To approve annual report and dividend declaration

answer_html:
Answer: (C) APPOINTMENT OF NOMINEE DIRECTOR on Board in event of: (i) TWO CONSECUTIVE DEFAULTS in payment of INTEREST; (ii) DEFAULT IN CREATION OF SECURITY for debentures; or (iii) DEFAULT IN REDEMPTION OF DEBENTURES; and ensure debenture redemption reserve creation and adequate assets for discharge of interest and principal

Rule 18(3) DUTIES OF DEBENTURE TRUSTEE include: (1) Satisfy that LETTER OF OFFER does not contain matters inconsistent with terms of debenture issue or trust deed; (2) Satisfy that COVENANTS IN TRUST DEED are not PREJUDICIAL to debenture holders' interests; (3) COMMUNICATE PROMPTLY TO DEBENTURE HOLDERS any defaults in payment of interest/redemption; (4) APPOINT NOMINEE DIRECTOR on Board in event of: (a) TWO CONSECUTIVE DEFAULTS in interest payment; (b) DEFAULT IN CREATION OF SECURITY; or (c) DEFAULT IN REDEMPTION; (5) Ensure implementation of conditions regarding SECURITY CREATION and DEBENTURE REDEMPTION RESERVE; (6) Ensure ADEQUATE ASSETS to discharge interest and principal; (7) Report on UTILIZATION OF FUNDS raised by debenture issue.

question_html: Under Section 71(4) and Rule 18(7), which of the following is CORRECT about the Debenture Redemption Reserve (DRR)?

options.A: DRR must be created from any reserve available with the company
options.B: DRR created from PROFITS AVAILABLE FOR DIVIDEND; by 30th APRIL each year: INVEST/DEPOSIT NOT LESS THAN 15% of DEBENTURES MATURING during year ending 31st March of NEXT YEAR in specified instruments (scheduled bank deposits, CG/SG securities, unencumbered bonds); amount NOT to be used except for redemption of maturing debentures; amount in DRR SHALL NOT be utilised EXCEPT FOR REDEMPTION
options.C: DRR must be 25% of debenture amount and must be deposited in fixed deposit
options.D: DRR is optional and companies may choose not to create it

answer_html:
Answer: (A) DRR must be created from any reserve available with the company

Section 71(4): Where DEBENTURES ARE ISSUED, company shall CREATE A DEBENTURE REDEMPTION RESERVE ACCOUNT from PROFITS OF THE COMPANY AVAILABLE FOR PAYMENT OF DIVIDEND. Amount credited to DRR shall NOT be utilised EXCEPT FOR REDEMPTION OF DEBENTURES. Rule 18(7)(c): Company shall ON OR BEFORE 30TH DAY OF APRIL each year INVEST OR DEPOSIT a sum NOT LESS THAN 15% of amount of its DEBENTURES MATURING during year ending 31st March of NEXT YEAR in: (i) Deposits with SCHEDULED BANK (free from charge/lien); (ii) UNENCUMBERED SECURITIES of Central/State Government; (iii) Unencumbered securities under Indian Trusts Act; (iv) Unencumbered bonds of notified company. Amount deposited NOT to be used for any other purpose except redemption.

question_html: Under Section 71(7), which provision in a trust deed relating to debentures is VOID?

options.A: Any provision giving the trustee power to enforce the security
options.B: Any provision setting the rate of interest on debentures
options.C: Any provision EXEMPTING THE TRUSTEE FROM LIABILITY FOR BREACH OF TRUST or INDEMNIFYING HIM against such liability — where he FAILS TO SHOW DEGREE OF CARE AND DUE DILIGENCE required of him; however, exemptions may be agreed upon by MAJORITY holding NOT LESS THAN THREE-FOURTHS in value at a meeting
options.D: Any provision restricting the trustee's right to call for reports

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Any provision setting the rate of interest on debentures

Section 71(7): VOID PROVISION: Any provision in a TRUST DEED or any CONTRACT WITH THE DEBENTURE HOLDERS that has the effect of EXEMPTING A TRUSTEE FROM OR INDEMNIFYING HIM AGAINST ANY LIABILITY FOR BREACH OF TRUST — where he FAILS TO SHOW THE DEGREE OF CARE AND DUE DILIGENCE required of him as trustee, having regard to the provisions of the trust deed conferring on him power, authority, or discretion. EXCEPTION: Liability of trustee shall be subject to EXEMPTIONS AGREED BY A MAJORITY of debenture holders holding NOT LESS THAN THREE-FOURTHS IN VALUE of total debentures at a meeting held for this purpose.

question_html: Under Sections 71(9), (10) and (11), what happens when a company FAILS TO REDEEM debentures or the debenture trustee finds assets INSUFFICIENT?

options.A: Only the holders can file a petition; the trustee has no such right
options.B: Only the company can file a petition with the Tribunal
options.C: If assets INSUFFICIENT: debenture trustee can FILE PETITION BEFORE TRIBUNAL which may impose RESTRICTIONS ON FURTHER LIABILITIES; FAILURE TO REDEEM/PAY INTEREST: Tribunal (on application by debenture holders/trustee) may direct company to REDEEM FORTHWITH with interest; DEFAULT IN COMPLYING WITH TRIBUNAL ORDER: imprisonment up to 3 YEARS or fine RS. 2 LAKHS to RS. 5 LAKHS or BOTH
options.D: The debenture trustee can only report to SEBI — cannot file petition with Tribunal

answer_html:
Answer: (C) If assets INSUFFICIENT: debenture trustee can FILE PETITION BEFORE TRIBUNAL which may impose RESTRICTIONS ON FURTHER LIABILITIES; FAILURE TO REDEEM/PAY INTEREST: Tribunal (on application by debenture holders/trustee) may direct company to REDEEM FORTHWITH with interest; DEFAULT IN COMPLYING WITH TRIBUNAL ORDER: imprisonment up to 3 YEARS or fine RS. 2 LAKHS to RS. 5 LAKHS or BOTH

Section 71(9): Where DEBENTURE TRUSTEE concludes that ASSETS OF THE COMPANY ARE INSUFFICIENT (or likely to become so) to DISCHARGE PRINCIPAL AMOUNT AS DUE — may FILE A PETITION BEFORE THE TRIBUNAL; Tribunal may, after hearing, ORDER RESTRICTIONS ON INCURRING FURTHER LIABILITIES. Section 71(10): Where company FAILS TO REDEEM DEBENTURES ON MATURITY or FAILS TO PAY INTEREST when due — Tribunal may, on APPLICATION by debenture holders or trustee, DIRECT COMPANY TO REDEEM FORTHWITH on PAYMENT OF PRINCIPAL AND INTEREST. Section 71(11): DEFAULT IN COMPLYING WITH TRIBUNAL ORDER: EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER punishable with IMPRISONMENT up to 3 YEARS or fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 2 LAKHS but may extend to RS. 5 LAKHS or BOTH.
topic_text: Section 71(9)(10)(11) — Debenture Trustee Petition & Failure to Redeem

question_html: Under Rule 18, within what period must a TRUST DEED be executed by the company issuing debentures, and what are the inspection rights?

options.A: Within 1 month of closure; only debenture holders can inspect
options.B: Within 6 months of closure; only members can inspect
options.C: Within 3 MONTHS OF CLOSURE OF ISSUE OR OFFER in FORM SH-12; OPEN FOR INSPECTION to any MEMBER OR DEBENTURE HOLDER in the same manner as register of members; COPY forwarded to any member/debenture holder at request WITHIN 7 DAYS on payment of fee
options.D: Within 1 year of closure; only the Board can inspect

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Within 1 month of closure; only debenture holders can inspect

Rule 18: TRUST DEED: executed by company in FORM SH-12 WITHIN 3 MONTHS OF CLOSURE OF THE ISSUE OR OFFER. Shall be OPEN FOR INSPECTION to any MEMBER OR DEBENTURE HOLDER in the SAME MANNER, to the SAME EXTENT and on PAYMENT OF THE SAME FEES as if it were the REGISTER OF MEMBERS of the company. A COPY of the trust deed shall be forwarded to any member or debenture holder at his request WITHIN 7 DAYS of the making, on PAYMENT OF FEE. This ensures transparency and protects the rights of debenture holders.
topic_text: Rule 18 — Trust Deed: Execution and Inspection

question_html: Under Section 71(1), the issue of DEBENTURES WITH AN OPTION TO CONVERT INTO SHARES (wholly or partly at the time of redemption) shall be approved by:

options.A: An ordinary resolution passed at the general meeting
options.B: Board resolution with unanimous approval of all directors
options.C: SEBI's written approval for all companies
options.D: A SPECIAL RESOLUTION at a general meeting; increase of subscribed capital on exercise of such option is NOT deemed FURTHER ISSUE; Government may order conversion even without such option in terms — company may appeal to Tribunal within 60 DAYS if terms not acceptable

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Board resolution with unanimous approval of all directors

Section 71(1): CONVERTIBLE DEBENTURES (option to convert into shares wholly or partly at time of redemption) require SPECIAL RESOLUTION at general meeting. INCREASE OF SUBSCRIBED CAPITAL caused by exercise of conversion option: NOT DEEMED TO BE A FURTHER ISSUE OF SHARE CAPITAL — but subject to condition that terms of issue (containing conversion option) were approved BEFORE ISSUE by a SPECIAL RESOLUTION. GOVERNMENT CONVERSION ORDER: Government may by order direct conversion of debentures/loans into shares (even if terms don't include such option) if it considers it NECESSARY IN THE PUBLIC INTEREST. Company may APPEAL TO TRIBUNAL WITHIN 60 DAYS if terms not acceptable. In determining terms, Government shall have due regard to financial position, rate of interest, and other relevant matters. ACCEPTANCE OF DEPOSITS — SECTIONS 73–76

question_html: Under Section 2(31) and Rule 2(c), which of the following amounts is NOT treated as a 'deposit' under the Companies Act?

options.A: Money received from a general member of the public
options.B: Money received from an individual private investor
options.C: Amount received from a relative of a director as a loan
options.D: Amount received from another COMPANY; from BANKS as loan; from CENTRAL/STATE GOVERNMENT; from DIRECTORS of the company; towards OFFER OF SECURITIES (unless securities not allotted and amount not refunded within 60 days); amounts by PROMOTERS; amounts by NIDHI company

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Amount received from a relative of a director as a loan

Section 2(31): DEPOSIT includes any receipt of money by way of DEPOSIT OR LOAN or in any other form by a company. Rule 2(c) EXCLUSIONS from deposit: (1) Amount from CENTRAL/STATE GOVERNMENT or guaranteed by them; (2) Amount from LOCAL/STATUTORY AUTHORITY; (3) Amount from FOREIGN GOVERNMENTS/INTERNATIONAL BANKS/MULTILATERAL INSTITUTIONS etc. (per FEMA); (4) Amount as LOAN OR FACILITY FROM ANY BANK; (5) Loan from PUBLIC FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS; (6) Amount from ANOTHER COMPANY; (7) Amount received towards OFFER OF SECURITIES (unless securities not allotted and amount not refunded within 60 days — becomes deposit); (8) From a DIRECTOR; (9) By issue of BOND OR DEBENTURE; (10) EMPLOYEE security deposit (non-interest bearing); (11) Non-interest bearing amount held in trust; (12) Amounts in COURSE OF BUSINESS; (13) Amount from PROMOTERS; (14) Amounts accepted by NIDHI COMPANY.

question_html: Under Section 73(2), a company may accept deposits from its MEMBERS after fulfilling which conditions?

options.A: Only board resolution required; circular to all members
options.B: PASSING OF RESOLUTION IN GENERAL MEETING; CIRCULAR TO MEMBERS containing financial position, credit rating, depositor info, and deposit dues; file copy with Registrar WITHIN 30 DAYS before issue; DEPOSIT NOT LESS THAN 20% of deposits MATURING DURING FOLLOWING FINANCIAL YEAR in DEPOSIT REPAYMENT RESERVE ACCOUNT in scheduled bank by 30TH APRIL each year; certify NO DEFAULT in repayment or 5 YEARS ELAPSED since making good
options.C: Only SEBI approval is required; no reserve fund needed
options.D: Only ROC filing is needed; no circular to members

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only board resolution required; circular to all members

Section 73(2): ACCEPTANCE OF DEPOSITS FROM MEMBERS conditions: (a) PASSING OF RESOLUTION IN GENERAL MEETING; (b) CIRCULAR TO MEMBERS including: FINANCIAL POSITION, CREDIT RATING OBTAINED, TOTAL NUMBER OF DEPOSITORS, AMOUNT DUE TOWARDS DEPOSITS from previous deposits, and other prescribed particulars; (c) FILE COPY OF CIRCULAR with Registrar WITHIN 30 DAYS BEFORE DATE OF ISSUE; (d) DEPOSIT NOT LESS THAN 20% of amount of deposits MATURING DURING FOLLOWING FINANCIAL YEAR in DEPOSIT REPAYMENT RESERVE ACCOUNT in SCHEDULED BANK by 30TH APRIL each year; (e) CERTIFY NO DEFAULT in repayment of deposits or interest; if default occurred — company made good the default and 5 YEARS ELAPSED; (f) Provide SECURITY if any for repayment.
topic_text: Section 73(2) — Acceptance of Deposits from Members

question_html: Under Section 76(1), which public companies qualify as 'ELIGIBLE COMPANIES' to accept deposits from persons other than members?

options.A: Any public company regardless of net worth or turnover
options.B: Only listed public companies that have obtained SEBI approval
options.C: PUBLIC COMPANY having NET WORTH NOT LESS THAN RS. 100 CRORE OR TURNOVER NOT LESS THAN RS. 500 CRORES; prior consent by SPECIAL RESOLUTION in general meeting; filed resolution with Registrar before making invitation; RATING from recognized agency disclosing adequate safety every year; CHARGE on assets within 30 DAYS of acceptance of secured deposits
options.D: All public companies with paid-up capital above Rs. 50 crores

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Only listed public companies that have obtained SEBI approval

Rule 2(e): ELIGIBLE COMPANY = PUBLIC COMPANY having NET WORTH NOT LESS THAN RS. 100 CRORE OR TURNOVER NOT LESS THAN RS. 500 CRORES which has obtained PRIOR CONSENT OF COMPANY by SPECIAL RESOLUTION in general meeting AND FILED the said resolution with Registrar BEFORE MAKING ANY INVITATION. Exception: An eligible company accepting deposits within limits under Section 180(1)(c) may accept by ORDINARY RESOLUTION. Section 76: Must obtain RATING from RECOGNIZED RATING AGENCY ensuring ADEQUATE SAFETY for every year during tenure of deposits. SECURED DEPOSITS: Create CHARGE on assets within 30 DAYS of acceptance of secured deposits.

question_html: Under Section 74(3), if a company fails to repay deposits accepted BEFORE COMMENCEMENT of the Companies Act, 2013 within the specified/extended time, the penalty is:

options.A: Fine up to Rs. 1 lakh; officers: fine up to Rs. 10,000
options.B: Fine up to Rs. 5 lakhs; officers: imprisonment up to 1 year
options.C: Fine up to Rs. 10 lakhs; officers: imprisonment up to 3 years
options.D: COMPANY: fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 1 CRORE but may extend to RS. 10 CRORES (in addition to repayment); EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER: imprisonment up to 7 YEARS or fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25 LAKHS but may extend to RS. 2 CRORES or BOTH

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Fine up to Rs. 10 lakhs; officers: imprisonment up to 3 years

Section 74: REPAYMENT OF DEPOSITS ACCEPTED BEFORE COMMENCEMENT OF ACT: Company must FILE STATEMENT with Registrar within 3 MONTHS from commencement showing deposits accepted and arrangements for repayment; REPAY WITHIN 3 YEARS from commencement or on/before expiry of period for which accepted — WHICHEVER IS EARLIER. Tribunal may allow further time. Section 74(3) PENALTY for failure to repay: COMPANY = fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 1 CRORE but may extend to RS. 10 CRORES (IN ADDITION TO REPAYMENT OF DEPOSIT AMOUNT); EVERY DEFAULTING OFFICER = imprisonment up to 7 YEARS or fine NOT LESS THAN RS. 25 LAKHS but may extend to RS. 2 CRORES or BOTH.
topic_text: Section 74(3) — Repayment of Old Deposits: Penalty

question_html: Under Section 75, when it is proved that deposits had been accepted with INTENT TO DEFRAUD depositors, which special consequence follows?

options.A: Only the company is liable; officers are shielded by limited liability
options.B: All shareholders of the company become personally liable
options.C: All directors and officers AT TIME OF ACCEPTANCE shall be JOINTLY AND SEVERALLY LIABLE TO REPAY deposits (including interest); each shall be PERSONALLY RESPONSIBLE WITHOUT LIMITATION OF LIABILITY — this cannot be overridden by any contract or arrangement
options.D: Only the managing director is personally liable for fraudulent deposits

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Only the company is liable; officers are shielded by limited liability

Section 75 DAMAGES FOR FRAUD: Where a company fails to repay deposits and it is PROVED THAT THE DEPOSITS HAD BEEN ACCEPTED WITH INTENT TO DEFRAUD THE DEPOSITORS or for any FRAUDULENT PURPOSE — every DIRECTOR OR OFFICER OF THE COMPANY WHO WAS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE ACCEPTANCE OF SUCH DEPOSIT shall JOINTLY AND SEVERALLY BE LIABLE: (a) for REPAYMENT of deposits (including interest); (b) Shall be PERSONALLY RESPONSIBLE, WITHOUT LIMITATION OF LIABILITY, for all losses and damages incurred by the depositors. This CANNOT BE OVERRIDDEN by any contract or arrangement between company and officer.
topic_text: Section 75 — Damages for Fraud in Deposits

question_html: Under Section 73(1), no company shall invite, accept or renew deposits from the PUBLIC except in the manner provided under Chapter V. Which companies are EXEMPT from this prohibition?

options.A: Only private companies are exempt
options.B: BANKING COMPANIES and NON-BANKING FINANCIAL COMPANIES (as defined under RBI Act, 1934) and such other companies as the Central Government may specify after consultation with RBI — NOT subject to Section 73(1)
options.C: Only government companies are exempt
options.D: Only companies with net worth above Rs. 500 crores are exempt

answer_html:
Answer: (B) BANKING COMPANIES and NON-BANKING FINANCIAL COMPANIES (as defined under RBI Act, 1934) and such other companies as the Central Government may specify after consultation with RBI — NOT subject to Section 73(1)

Section 73(1): On and after commencement of this Act, NO COMPANY shall INVITE, ACCEPT OR RENEW DEPOSITS from the public except in a manner provided under CHAPTER V (Acceptance of Deposits). Section 73(1) proviso: NOT APPLICABLE to: (1) A BANKING COMPANY; (2) A NON-BANKING FINANCIAL COMPANY as defined under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934; and (3) SUCH OTHER COMPANY as the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT MAY, AFTER CONSULTATION WITH THE RBI, SPECIFY. These categories of companies are regulated separately under RBI/banking regulations. MISCELLANEOUS PENALTIES & KEY COMPARISONS

question_html: Which of the following correctly matches the PENALTY under the specified sections of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Section 53 (shares at discount): Company and officers — fine up to Rs. 1 lakh only
options.B: SEC.48(5): Company Rs. 25K–5L; Officer 6 months/Rs. 25K–5L; SEC.53(3): Company Rs. 1L–5L; Officer 6 months/Rs. 1L–5L; SEC.56(6): Company Rs. 25K–5L; Officer Rs. 10K–1L; SEC.57: Imprisonment 1–3 YEARS AND fine Rs. 1L–5L; SEC.68(11): Company Rs. 1L–3L; Officer 3 years/Rs. 1L–3L
options.C: Section 57 (personation): only civil penalty — no imprisonment
options.D: All sections have uniform penalty of Rs. 1 lakh fine

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Section 57 (personation): only civil penalty — no imprisonment

PENALTY COMPARISON: SEC.48(5) VARIATION OF RIGHTS: Company Rs. 25,000–5 LAKHS; Officer: 6 months or Rs. 25,000–5 LAKHS or both. SEC.53(3) SHARES AT DISCOUNT: Company Rs. 1 LAKH–5 LAKHS; Officer: 6 months or Rs. 1 LAKH–5 LAKHS or both. SEC.56(6) TRANSFER DEFAULT: Company Rs. 25,000–5 LAKHS; Officer: Rs. 10,000–1 LAKH. SEC.57 PERSONATION: Imprisonment 1 YEAR (min) to 3 YEARS AND fine Rs. 1 LAKH–5 LAKHS. SEC.58 CONTRAVENING TRIBUNAL ORDER: Imprisonment up to 3 YEARS and fine Rs. 1 LAKH–5 LAKHS. SEC.59(5) REGISTER RECTIFICATION DEFAULT: Company Rs. 1 LAKH–5 LAKHS; Officer: 1 year or Rs. 1 LAKH–3 LAKHS or both. SEC.64 ALTERATION NOTICE DEFAULT: Rs. 1,000/day or Rs. 5 LAKHS (less). SEC.68(11) BUYBACK DEFAULT: Company Rs. 1 LAKH–3 LAKHS; Officer: 3 years or Rs. 1 LAKH–3 LAKHS or both. SEC.71(11) DEBENTURE/TRIBUNAL DEFAULT: 3 years or Rs. 2 LAKHS–5 LAKHS or both.
topic_text: Penalty Comparison: Sec.48 vs Sec.53 vs Sec.56 vs Sec.57 vs Sec.68

question_html: Under Section 68(2), when can a company buy back its own shares with only a BOARD RESOLUTION (without special resolution)?

options.A: When the buy-back is 25% or less of total paid-up capital
options.B: WHEN BUY-BACK IS 10% OR LESS OF TOTAL PAID-UP EQUITY CAPITAL AND FREE RESERVES; AND authorized by BOARD RESOLUTION at its meeting — no special shareholder resolution needed
options.C: When the company has fewer than 50 shareholders
options.D: When buy-back is from open market only

answer_html:
Answer: (A) When the buy-back is 25% or less of total paid-up capital

Section 68(2): SPECIAL RESOLUTION required for buy-back EXCEPT when: (1) The buy-back is 10% OR LESS of the TOTAL PAID-UP EQUITY CAPITAL AND FREE RESERVES; AND (2) Such buy-back has been AUTHORIZED BY THE BOARD BY MEANS OF A RESOLUTION PASSED AT ITS MEETING. In this case, a BOARD RESOLUTION ALONE SUFFICES — no special shareholder resolution needed. For all buy-backs exceeding 10% of total paid-up equity capital and free reserves: SPECIAL RESOLUTION is mandatory. Also: buy-back ≤ 25% of AGGREGATE PAID-UP CAPITAL AND FREE RESERVES is the OVERALL CEILING.
topic_text: Section 68 — Buy-Back: Board Resolution vs Special Resolution

question_html: Under Section 61, cancellation of shares not taken is described as 'DIMINUTION' of share capital — NOT reduction. What is the KEY SIGNIFICANCE of this distinction?

options.A: Diminution requires Tribunal confirmation like reduction
options.B: CANCELLATION OF SHARES NOT TAKEN (Section 61(e)) is NOT DEEMED TO BE REDUCTION OF SHARE CAPITAL — therefore does NOT require Tribunal confirmation under Section 66; it only cancels shares never subscribed; whereas REDUCTION OF SHARE CAPITAL (Section 66) requires SPECIAL RESOLUTION and TRIBUNAL CONFIRMATION
options.C: Diminution and reduction are identical — both require Tribunal approval
options.D: Diminution requires SEBI approval but not Tribunal confirmation

answer_html:
Answer: (B) CANCELLATION OF SHARES NOT TAKEN (Section 61(e)) is NOT DEEMED TO BE REDUCTION OF SHARE CAPITAL — therefore does NOT require Tribunal confirmation under Section 66; it only cancels shares never subscribed; whereas REDUCTION OF SHARE CAPITAL (Section 66) requires SPECIAL RESOLUTION and TRIBUNAL CONFIRMATION

DISTINCTION: Section 61(e): CANCELLATION OF SHARES NOT TAKEN — the cancellation of shares which have NOT BEEN TAKEN OR AGREED TO BE TAKEN by any person at the date of the resolution passing. This is declared by Section 61 to DIMINISH (reduce the amount of authorized capital) BUT IS NOT DEEMED TO BE A REDUCTION OF SHARE CAPITAL under Section 66. Therefore: (a) NO TRIBUNAL CONFIRMATION required; (b) Only general meeting resolution + notice to Registrar in FORM SH-7 within 30 days. REDUCTION OF SHARE CAPITAL (Section 66): Requires SPECIAL RESOLUTION + TRIBUNAL CONFIRMATION + notice to CG/Registrar/SEBI/creditors + auditor's certificate.

question_html: Which of the following CORRECTLY states a key distinction between DEBENTURES and EQUITY SHARES under the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Debentures carry voting rights; shares do not
options.B: Both debentures and shares carry identical voting rights
options.C: DEBENTURES: evidences a DEBT; NO VOTING RIGHTS [Sec.71(2)]; holders are CREDITORS; MOVEABLE PROPERTY; may be secured; DRR required; trust deed within 3 months; debenture trustee before issue; EQUITY SHARES: evidences OWNERSHIP; VOTING RIGHTS on every resolution [Sec.47(1)]; shareholders are OWNERS; convertible debentures require SPECIAL RESOLUTION for conversion option
options.D: Debentures are always secured; shares are always unsecured

answer_html:
Answer: (C) DEBENTURES: evidences a DEBT; NO VOTING RIGHTS [Sec.71(2)]; holders are CREDITORS; MOVEABLE PROPERTY; may be secured; DRR required; trust deed within 3 months; debenture trustee before issue; EQUITY SHARES: evidences OWNERSHIP; VOTING RIGHTS on every resolution [Sec.47(1)]; shareholders are OWNERS; convertible debentures require SPECIAL RESOLUTION for conversion option

DEBENTURES vs EQUITY SHARES: (1) NATURE: Debenture = DEBT INSTRUMENT; Share = OWNERSHIP INSTRUMENT; (2) VOTING RIGHTS: Debentures = NO VOTING RIGHTS [Sec.71(2)]; Equity shares = VOTING RIGHTS ON EVERY RESOLUTION [Sec.47(1)]; (3) STATUS: Debenture holders = CREDITORS; Equity shareholders = OWNERS; (4) SECURITY: Debentures may be SECURED (by charge) or UNSECURED; shares are never 'secured'; (5) RETURN: Debentures carry INTEREST (fixed); Equity shares carry DIVIDEND (variable); (6) PRIORITY ON WINDING UP: Debenture holders have PRIORITY OVER SHAREHOLDERS; (7) CONVERSION: Convertible debentures → shares requires SPECIAL RESOLUTION [Sec.71(1)]; (8) STATUTORY REQUIREMENTS: DRR, Debenture Trustee, Trust Deed (Form SH-12 within 3 months) — all apply to debentures.
